label: children
translation:
Swallow of Piiri-pääri  
Where is your golden nest?  
"On the dry spruce top in the forest."  
Where did the dry spruce come from?  
"An old man cut it down."  
Where did the old man come from?  
"He crawled into the field garden."  
Where did the field garden come from?  
"Driven oxen plowed it up."  
Where did those driven oxen come from?  
"A German shot them down."  
Where did that German come from?  
"The German went to town."  
Where did that town come from?  
"The town burned down."  
Where did the town ashes go?  
"The wind blew them into the sea."  
Where did the sea come from?  
"A black rooster drank up the sea."  
Where did that black rooster come from?  
"The black rooster flew to the sky."  
Where did the sky come from?  
"The sky fell down."  
Where did the earth come from?  
"The earth sank down."  
Where did the bottom come from?  
"A goose ate up the bottom."  
Where did the goose come from?  
"A pig ate up the goose."  
Where did the pig come from?  
"A knife killed the pig."  
Where did the knife come from?  
"The knife disappeared by itself."

label: children
translation:
The mouse, however, walked the ipsu path,  
Ipsu path, apsu path,  
With the crab’s carts behind.  
"Where are you going, little mouse?"  
"To the manor lord to drink,  
From the pantry to eat bread,  
From the cellar to catch fish,  
To lick the frying pan.  
The lady gives me porridge,  
The cook makes cream sauce for me.  
The maid is cooking blood sausage;  
I myself eat pork,  
I try fish bones.  
From the manor I got war news:  
Father went to the hayfield,  
The maid gave a slap,  
Then I got to run away from the town."  
"Where are you going, little mouse?"  
"I'm going to thresh the grain;  
Maybe a tree will fall on my head,  
Then I will run to its roots."  
"Roots will make your teeth rusty,  
Your eye sockets moldy."  
"I will wash with water;  
If the water chills me,  
I will swell with fire.  
If the fire burns me;  
I will smear with butter!"  
"Where does the mouse get butter?"  
"From the mistress’s pot,  
From the free woman’s dish."

label: children
translation:
Lõõri-lõõri, little bird,
Piiri-pääri, little swallow,
Where did your golden nest get made?
"Behind the oak tree."
Where did the oak get made?
"An old man cut down the oak."
Where did that old man get made?
"He was placed under the field bed."
Where did that field bed get made?
"Hitched oxen plowed the bed."
Where did those hitched oxen get made?
"A bear broke the hitched oxen."
Where did that bear get made?
"The bear went into the tall reed."
Where did that tall reed get made?
"A sickle mowed the reed down."
Where did that sickle get made?
"Hard"
Where did that hard get made?
"A hen scratched the manure."
Where did that hen get made?
"It was taken to the town, eaten away."
Where did that town get made?
"Fire burned the town down."
Where did that fire get made?
"Water put out the fire."
Where did that water get made?
"Water sank beneath the earth."
Where did that earth get made?
"The earth is for us to stand on,
To stand on, to remain on."

label: children
translation:
Hello, hello, Tepermann  
From Tepermann I got madara  
From madara I got madlipilli  
From madlipilli I got peburi  
From peburi I got Peteriku  
From Peterik I got Riivaku  
From Riivak I got Riiven salt  
From Riiven salt I got sobina  
From sobina I got salt box  
From salt box I got vadin  
From vadin I got barrel of vodka  
From barrel of vodka I got rainbow  
From rainbow I got whip forest  
From whip forest I got big islands  
Big islands, wide plains  
Under the berry pine forest  
Under the golden spruce  
There the buns were eaten  
Vodka mugs were carried  
Bottled beers were drunk.

label: children
translation:
Oh, poor little bird of Virbel,
Virbel bird, Virbel bird,
Where shall I make my nest?
In the haystack of the family,
In the wise buildings of the farm.
The family’s daughter, a young maiden,
Went to fetch wood from the haystack.
She knocked down my nest from the haystack,
From the wise buildings of the farm.
Oh, poor little bird of Virbel,
Virbel bird, Virbel bird,
Where shall I make my nest,
To lay my eggs in,
To hatch my chicks under?
On the dry spruce in the forest,
Behind the room, on the oak branch.
Where did that dry spruce come from?
The old man cut down the spruce.
Where did that old man come from?
He was buried on the field of the peasants.
Where did that peasants’ field come from?
The oxen from the village plowed the field.
Where did those village oxen come from?
A bear killed the village oxen.
Where did that bear come from?
The Saxon shot the bear.
Where did that Saxon come from?
The Saxon went to the town.
Where did that town come from?
The town burned down.
Where did the ashes of the town go?
Under the streets of the new town,
Beneath the ramparts of the old town.

label: children
translation:
Sleep, sleep, tumbleweed,  
The chilly one did a somersault,  
The key to the sausage chamber got lost,  
The butter pot tipped over.

label: children
translation:
Liiri-lõõri sparrow,  
piiri-pääri swallow,  
where was your golden nest?  
In the forest on top of a dry spruce.  
Where did that dry spruce come from?  
An old man cut it down.  
Where did that old man’s father come from?  
The old man died.  
Where was that old man’s grave?  
In the long field’s garden.  
Where did the long field’s garden come from?  
Driven oxen plowed it up.  
Where did those driven oxen come from?  
A bear tore the driven oxen apart.  
Where did that bear’s father come from?  
The bear ran into the reeds.  
Where did those reeds come from?  
The sickle whistled down.  
Where did that sickle come from?  
It wore out its blade.  
Where did that blade come from?  
A hen rummaged in the dung.  
Where did that hen come from?  
A kite carried the hen over the sea.  
Where did that kite come from?  
The kite went to town.  
Where did that town come from?  
The town burned down.  
Where did the town’s ashes go?  
The wind blew them away.

label: children
translation:
Hello, hello, little mouse!  
Oh my, little kitty!  
Where are you going, little mouse?  
I am going to chop wood.  
What if this wood falls on your head?  
I will run to the roots.  
What if you get hungry?  
I will start peeling birch bark.  
What if that bark gets stuck in your throat?  
I will cut it with a knife.  
What if blood comes out?  
I will wash it with water.  
What if those hairs get wet?  
I will dry them with fire.  
What if those hairs get singed?  
I will butter them with butter.  
Where do you get the butter?  
From the old woman's chamber pot.  
Where does the old woman get it?  
From the black blueberry seed.  
Where did the black blueberry get it?  
It drank from our lake water,  
tasted our well water,  
smelled the spring water,  
and sampled our sea water.

label: children
translation:
Liiri-lõõri song,  
where is your darling’s nest?  
In the forest, on a dry spruce.  
Where did that spruce itself come from?  
An old man cut it down.  
Where did that old man himself come from?  
The old man died.  
Where was he buried?  
In the long vegetable garden.  
Where did that vegetable garden come from?  
Brown oxen plowed it up.  
Where did those brown oxen come from?  
A bear tore the brown oxen apart.  
Where did that bear itself come from?  
The bear tricked the reeds.  
Where did those reeds themselves come from?  
A scythe whistled by the reeds.  
Where did that scythe itself come from?  
The sly one deceived the scythes.  
Where did that sly one itself come from?  
A hen scurried into the sly one’s manure.  
Where did that hen itself come from?  
An eagle tore the hen apart.  
Where did that eagle itself come from?  
A spark burned the eagle down.  
Where did that spark itself come from?  
The spark went out in the ashes.  
Where did those ashes themselves come from?  
The wind blew the ashes under the sky.

label: children
translation:
Äia-tuia,  
Let the swing go  
Towards the sea, into the forest,  
To the top of a dry spruce.  
Others eat bread rolls  
We eat rye bread  
Bang! bang! they buried  
Gypsy Manni  
The stone bell was struck  
Sauce was eaten with bread.

label: children
translation:
Liiri, lõõri, little bird  
Where is your golden nest?  
In the forest on a dry spruce tree.  
Where has that dry spruce remained?  
An old man cut it down.  
Where is that old man's gold?  
The old man has died.  
Buried in the garden bed.  
Where is that golden garden bed?  
Draft oxen plowed it up.  
White oxen chased the calves.  
Where have those oxen gone?  
They crawled into the reed thicket.  
Where is that golden reed thicket?  
A sickle mowed it down.  
Where is that little sickle?  
The scythe blade wore it out.  
Where is that golden blade?  
The hen was scratching in the manure.  
Where is that little hen?  
A hawk took it away.  
Where is that little hawk?  
It shot the village tomcat.  
Where is that little village tomcat?  
Sitting at the edge of the tavern table,  
With a shot glass between its fingers,  
And a beer mug under its arm.

label: children
translation:
From sõmeru I got fingerless gloves,  
Fingerless gloves into a bundle.  
Bundle and jug.  
From the jug I got the market thumb,  
From the market thumb a curious one.  
From the curious thumb a cross,  
From the cross to the rimal.  
From the rimal I got a clasp for the chest,  
From the clasp for the chest I got sõmeru.  
From sõmeru I got fingerless gloves,  
Fingerless gloves into a bundle,  
Bundle and jug.

label: children
translation:
Liiri-lõõri, swallow,  
Piiri-pääri, little swallow,  
Where is your golden little nest?  
In the forest, on the dry spruce.  
Where did that dry spruce stay?  
An old man cut the spruce down.  
Where did that old man himself go?  
The old man died.  
Where was the old man buried?  
Under the long garden bed.  
Where did that garden bed remain?  
Spotted bulls plowed it up.  
Where did those spotted bulls stay?  
A bear tore the bulls down.  
Where did that bear itself go?  
The bear jumped into the reeds.  
Where did those reeds remain then?  
The sickle whistled it down.  
Where did that sickle stay again?  
The sled wore it out.  
Where did that sled go?  
The sled splashed into the lake.  
Where did that lake remain again?  
The rainbow drank the lake empty.

label: children
translation:
Hello, hello Teppelmann.  
Teppelmann became a maraka,  
The maraka became a maanipill,  
The maanipill became a piburi,  
The piburi became a piitsarikki,  
The piitsarikki became a rimakas,  
The rimakas became a breastpin,  
The breastpin became a fleshy one,  
The fleshy one became a salt container,  
The salt container became a formula,  
The formula became a rainbow,  
The rainbow became a kavak,  
From the kavak came dear forests.  
Those forests, honeyed forests.  
From an apple tree came a beer cupboard,  
From rowan came milk bottles,  
From juniper came rock jugs.

label: children
translation:
Of fineness and brittleness.
From brittleness came nettle thumb,
From nettle thumb came the mitten,
From the mitten came the thumb-cross,
From the thumb-cross came the ribbed wale,
From the ribbed wale came the ring channel,
From the ring channel came the coarse wale,
From the coarse wale and the mitten.....

label: children
translation:
Titmouse-lark lark,  
Where is your golden nest,  
Behind the room in the oak grove,  
Under the elm by the yard,  
Where did that oak itself come from?  
The bear scratched up the stump,  
Where did that bear itself come from?  
The bear went long ago to other lands,  
Left footprints on this land.  
The cat went to see the bear off,  
Fell into the village well,  
From under the belly came tall boots,  
From the nose the girl got boots,  
From the tail came the ox’s saddle.

label: children
translation:
Border swallow,  
Where is your golden nest?  
On a dry spruce in the forest.  
Where is that golden dry spruce?  
An old man has knocked it down,  
Where is that golden old man?  
He has buried it in the edge of the field,  
Where is that golden field edge?  
The furrows have been plowed up.  
Where are those golden furrows?  
A bear has trampled the furrows,  
Where is that golden little bear?  
The hunter has shot the bear down.

label: children
translation:
Mamsel cooked jam,  
I tasted the jam.  
Mamsel hit me with a ladle,  
I hit with a fire striker;  
Mamsel fell down,  
I went behind the cupboard.  
The clock had not struck twelve,  
The stallions were not fed in the stable.

label: children
translation:
Liiri, bird, swallows,  
Piiri, sparrow, swallow,  
Where is your golden nest?  
In the forest, on top of a dry spruce.  
Where did that spruce itself come from?  
An old man cut the spruce down.  
Where did that old man himself come from?  
The old man died.  
Where was he buried?  
At the edge of a long field.  
Where did that field edge come from?  
The farmers plowed it up.  
Where did those farmers come from?  
But a bear broke the farmers.  
Where did that bear itself come from?  
The bear hid in the reeds.  
Where did those reeds come from?  
The sickle whistled through the reeds.  
Where did that sickle itself come from?  
A cheat cheated the sickles.  
Where did that cheat himself come from?  
I put the cheat on the window of the sauna,  
The hen scratched in the dung.  
Where did that hen itself come from?  
The eagle broke the hen.  
Where did that eagle itself come from?  
The eagle flew under the sky.

label: children
translation:
Sleep came in through the door  
aimed at the child's eye  
fell onto the child's eyebrow  
stared at the child's shadow.

label: children
translation:
The lark sings on the tile  
The swallow at the edge of the border  
Where is your darling’s nest?  
In the forest on top of a dry spruce.  
Which spruce?  
An old man cut the spruce.  
Which old man?  
The old man died.  
When was he buried?  
In the long field’s garden bed.  
Which garden bed?  
A hen scratched the garden bed.  
Which hen?  
The hen flew into the grass.  
What grass?  
A sickle mowed the grass.  
Which sickle?  
The sickle’s edge is worn.  
Which edge?  
A bear gnawed the edge.  
Which bear?  
The bear swam across the sea.  
Which sea?  
A black bull drank from the sea.  
Wh-  
The black bull went to the barn.  
Which barn?  
The fire burned in the barn.  
Which fire?  
The fire went to the sky,  
With pots, pans,  
Spatulas, spoons.

label: children
translation:
Lyre, bellows, chatter,  
border, brocade, swallow,  
where is your golden nest?  
On the dry spruce tree in the forest.  
Where did the dry spruce come from?  
An old man cut the spruce down.  
Where did the old man himself come from?  
He was buried under the garden patch.  
Where did the garden patch come from?  
The oxen plowed it up.  
Where did the oxen themselves come from?  
The wolf had eaten the oxen.  
Where did the wolf itself come from?  
The wolf had gone into the deep forest.

label: children
translation:
A thousand-thousand, a hundred-hundred
You go along the rye bridge
To fight in the Iron City,
From the Iron City to the wooden block,
From the wooden block to the sliding gate,
From the sliding gate to the leather pouch,
From the leather pouch to the manure mound,
From the manure mound to the pig mound.

label: children
translation:
Liiri, lõõri, Swallow,  
border, Pääri, little swallow,  
tell me, where is your golden nest?  
In the forest, on the branch of a dry spruce.  
Where did that dry spruce come from?  
An old man cut the spruce down.  
Where did that old man come from?  
The old man died himself.  
Where was that old man buried?  
In the bed of a long field.  
Where did the bed of the long field come from?  
Farmers plowed it up.  
Where did those farmers come from?  
A bear tore them apart and ate them.  
Where did that bear come from?  
The bear went into tall reed.  
Where did that reed come from?  
A sickle cut it down.  
Where did that sickle come from?  
A rake wore it down.  
Where did that rake come from?  
It got lost in the sleigh’s dung.  
Where did that sleigh’s dung come from?  
A white hen was running about.  
Where did that white hen come from?  
A hawk ate it.  
Where did that hawk come from?  
A hunter shot it down.

label: children
translation:
Lõõri, lõõri, little lark,  
Piari, piari, little girl,  
Where is my golden peach?  
The peach is on a wet pine tree.  
Where is that wet pine?  
In the forest grew the wet pine.  
Where did the forest grow?  
Fire burned the forest down.  
Where did the fire come from?  
Water extinguished the fire.  
Where did the water come from?  
A black bear drank the water.  
Where is that black bear?  
A bear broke the black bear.  
Where did that bear come from?  
A rifle shot the bear down.  
Where did the rifle come from?  
The rifle is in the reed in the forest.  
Where is that reed?  
A sickle whistled on the reed.  
Where did the sickle come from?  
The whetstone sharpened the sickle.  
Where did that whetstone come from?  
The whetstone was in cow dung.  
Where is that cow dung?  
A hen scratched in cow dung.  
Where did that hen come from?  
An eagle took the hen away.  
Where did that eagle come from?  
The eagle went over the sea and the forest itself.

label: children
translation:
Monday - oats were brought,  
Tuesday - flax was processed,  
Wednesday - the dog was sent to the store,  
Thursday - the hide was taken,  
Friday - bread was prepared,  
Saturday - it was put in the oven,  
Sunday - yes, today is Sunday!

label: children
translation:
Our cat has scratched eyes,  
Sat on a stump in the forest.  
A pipe was in its mouth and a stick in its hand,  
Called children to read,  
Those who could not read,  
Were sent off to take a nap.

label: children
translation:
Lõõri-lõõri swallows.  
Piiri-pääri swallows,  
where is your golden nest?  
In the forest, on a dry spruce branch.  
Where did that dry spruce come from?  
An old man cut it down.  
Where did that old man come from?  
The old man died.  
Where was he buried?  
On the bed of a long field.  
Where did that bed of the long field come from?  
Peasant lads plowed it up.  
Where did those peasant lads come from?  
A bear broke them up.  
Where did that bear come from?  
The bear jumped into the reeds.  
Where did those reeds come from?  
A sickle whistled down.  
Where did that sickle come from?  
A scythe wore out.  
Where did that scythe come from?  
A hen pecked in the dung.  
Where did that hen come from?  
The gold broke.  
Where did that gold come from?  
The gold flew to the town.  
Where did that town come from?  
The town burned down.  
Where did the town's ashes go?  
The wind scattered them across the meadow.

label: children
translation:
Six, six, little darling,  
kitten, spotted little bird,  
lark, lark, skylark,  
where is your golden nest?  
The nest is in the vegetable patch.  
Where did the vegetable patch come from?  
The hired farmers plowed it up.  
Where did the hired farmers come from?  
The bear broke the hired farmers.  
Where did the bear's father come from?  
The bear went to the top of the spruce in the forest.  
Where did that spruce come from?  
An old man cut down the spruce.

label: children
translation:
Piece of cake, piece of cake,  
slice of raw meat,  
dip it in egg,  
roll, roll, roll - jump into the oven!

label: children
translation:
Border-border, little swallow,  
lilt-lilt, little swallow,  
where is your golden nest?  
In the forest on a dry spruce.  
Where is that dry spruce left?  
An old man cut down the spruce.  
Where is that old man?  
He went to the garden patch.  
Where are those old garden patches?  
Servants plowed them up.  
Where are those old servants?  
I sent them down to the reeds.  
Where are those old reeds?  
The scythe mowed the reeds.  
Where is that old little scythe?  
The weasel sneaked, alarmed loudly.  
Where is that old little weasel?  
A hen scratched in the manure.  
Where is that old little hen?  
A hawk took it to the forest stump.  
Where is that old little stump?  
A bear scratched the little stump.  
Where is that old little bear?  
He crossed over two forests,  
jumped over eight forests,  
his head showed above the forest,  
his body twisted in the middle of the forest,  
his legs were hidden under the forest.

label: children
translation:
Come here, pig Jaan,  
shut Kusti’s eyes,  
eyes shut, mouth closed,  
nose to the little piggy,  
ears to Kiki-Koki,  
tail to the little dill-fool.

label: children
translation:
Liiri-lõõri, skylark,  
piiri-pääri, swallow,  
where is your golden nest?  
In the forest, on the dry spruce.  
Where did the dry spruce come from?  
An old man has cut it down.  
Where did the old man come from?  
He crept into the reed bed in the forest.  
Where did the reed bed come from?  
A sickle has swished.  
Where did the sickle come from?  
A blade has worn out.  
Where did the blade itself come from?  
A hen has scratched in the manure.  
Where did the little hen come from?  
A hawk took the hen away  
to the field’s edge outside,  
to the back of the field in the buckwheat,  
in the middle of the field of boiling oats,  
across the sea, onto a tree stump.

label: children
translation:
A goat kid for the herd,  
take the son behind,  
make a fence from there.  
I make a fence for the cow,  
the cow gives me milk.  
I give the milk to the piglet,  
the piglet gives me a mate.  
I give the mate to the mother-in-law,  
the mother-in-law gives me a cake.  
I give the cake to Kalev,  
Kalev gives me iron.  
I give the iron to the reaper,  
the reaper gives me gold.  
I give the gold to the oak,  
the oak gives me a leaf.  
I give the leaf to the sheep,  
the sheep gives me wool.  
I give the wool to the spinner,  
the spinner makes me a new hood.

label: children
translation:
Sleep comes with a yawn  
through the forests and groves,  
brings a little hay with it,  
two stalks of straw it carries.  
Sleep comes in through the door,  
falls upon the child's cheeks,  
upon the edges of the child's cheeks,  
falls upon the child's eyebrows,  
falls upon the child's eyelids,  
closes the big eyes.

label: children
translation:
Lyre-flute, lark,  
border-edge, swallow,  
until your nest?  
In the forest, on the dry spruce.  
Until the little spruce?  
An old man carved the little spruce.  
Until that old man?  
The old man died.  
Where was he buried?  
By the edge of the long field.  
Where did he remain there?  
The hen’s tail sticks out.  
Where is that little hen?  
The hen flew to the barn.  
Where is that barn?  
The sickle reaped the barn.  
Where is that little sickle?  
The sickle sits in the basket.  
Until that little stump?  
The bear scratched the stump.  
Until that little bear?  
The bear rolled into the water.  
Until that little one?  
The black bull drank water.  
Until that black bull?  
The black bull went to the cowshed.  
Until that little cowshed?  
Fire burned the cowshed.  
Until that little fire?  
The fire went up to the sky.  
Who will go there after?  
With tin, with copper,  
with sledges, with spoons,  
and with pots, with pans.

label: children
translation:
Where did the bear itself come from?  
The bear went to the reed.  
Where did the reed itself come from?  
The sickle cut it down.  
Where did the sickle itself come from?  
The scythe wore it out.  
Where did the scythe itself come from?  
It disappeared on the sauna manure heap.  
Where did the sauna manure come from?  
The white hen scattered it.  
Where did the white hen come from?  
The eagle ate it.  
Where did the eagle itself come from?  
The falcon shot it down.

label: children
translation:
Ride, ride along,  
from there we can eat.  
Ride, ride to Riga,  
a cup to Tallinn,  
beer to Petersburg,  
and a tail to the German shore.

label: children
translation:
Ott, ott, ott, ott, Otike  
Where is my little neck pouch?  
/:The pouch is on a stump in the forest:/  
Where did the stump itself come from?  
An old man cut down that stump.  
Where did the old man himself go?  
The old man died.  
Where was he buried?  
In the garden of a long field.  
Where did those gardens themselves come from?  
Draft oxen plowed them up.  
Where did those oxen themselves go?  
A bear tore them apart.  
Where did that bear itself go?  
The bear ran to town.  
Where did that town itself go?  
The town burned down.  
The bear disappeared, the town burned down,  
The wind scattered the ashes.

label: children
translation:
Loori loori loorke,  
pairi pairi swallow  
Where is your golden nest?  
In the dry spruce in the forest.  
Where did the dry spruce come from?  
An old man cut it down.  
Where did the old man come from?  
The old man died.  
Where was he buried?  
In the border of the long field.  
Where did the border of the long field come from?  
The peasants plowed it up.  
Where did those peasants come from?  
A bear broke the peasants.  
- - - - - - - - - - - -  
Fire under the ash sky  
Around Alli Krans’s neck,

label: children
translation:
Lark, pipe, skylark,  
Border, gate, swallow,  
Where is your darling’s nest?  
In the forest on a dry spruce branch.  
Where is that darling spruce?  
An old man has cut it down.  
Where is that darling old man?  
He crept into a long garden bed.  
Where is that darling garden bed?  
Oxen that have been yoked plowed it up.  
Where are those darling yoked oxen?  
A bear killed the yoked oxen.  
Where is that darling little bear?  
He crept into a long reed bed.  
Where is that darling long reed?  
The sickle whistled as it cut down.  
Where is that darling little sickle?  
It has worn out completely.  
Where is that darling little hard one?  
A chicken scurried into the manure.  
Where is that darling little chicken?  
A hawk has killed the chicken.  
Where is that darling little hawk?  
The hawk has flown over the town.  
Where is that darling little town?  
The town has burned down.  
What is left of that town?  
A pig with seven piglets,  
A horse with its foal,  
A hen with two chicks.

label: children
translation:
Lira, pipe, lark  
Border, pennant, swallow  
Where is your dear little nest?  
In the forest on a dry spruce  
In the meadow on a broad alder.  
Where has that dry spruce gone?  
Where has that broad alder gone?  
The old man has cut it down.  
Where has that old man gone?  
The old man has died.  
Where was he buried?  
In a long garden bed.  
Where has that garden bed gone?  
Oxen that were yoked plowed it up.  
Where have those yoked oxen gone?  
A bear broke the yoked oxen.  
Where has that bear itself gone?  
The bear ran into the reed.  
Where has that reed gone?  
The scythe sang on it —  
It has worn it down hard.  
Where has that hard place gone?  
On a dry stumptop in the forest.  
Where has that dry stump gone?  
Roosters and hens have scurried up.  
Where have those roosters and hens gone?  
The eagle has eaten the roosters and hens.  
Where has that eagle itself gone?  
The eagle has flown under the sky.  
Men, brothers, let's make stairs,  
So we could catch the eagle.

label: children
translation:
Tit, tit, the titmouse,  
look, look, the sparrow.

label: children
translation:
The dog went to the herd company group,  
its tail curled, its leg bent,  
from the herd home it moved along,  
tiptap tiptap tiptap.

label: children
translation:
Chirp chirp titmouse,  
watch watch sparrow  
jump over the pea field  
leap over the cabbage patch  
whiz through the forest.

label: children
translation:
The dog went with the herd's gang  
tail tucked, snout in the ditch.  
From the herd to home, swift and nimble.

label: children
translation:
A goat in a herd of sheep  
Across the sea, a berry  
Bring me hay  
I will give hay to the cow  
The cow will give me milk  
I will give the milk to the baker  
The baker will give me bread,  
I will give the bread to the shoemaker  
The shoemaker will give me boots  
I will give the boots to the tailor  
The tailor will give me clothes.

label: children
translation:
Tit, tit chickadee,  
look, look sparrow.

label: children
translation:
The dog went to the herd in a group,  
tail drooping, the foot in a rut.  
From the herd home, carefully winding.

label: children
translation:
Liiri’s flute is a nightingale  
the border is a swallow  
jump over the bean field  
hop over the cabbage patch  
over the forest, whirl.

label: children
translation:
The dog went to the herd:  
in a group.  
Tail drooping  
head down low,  
from the herd home  
tugging pulling jerking  
shuffling stamping stirring.

label: children
translation:
Liiri's pipe tune,  
the swallow at the edge of the border  
jump over the oat field fence  
leap over the cabbage patch  
whiz over the forest.

label: children
translation:
Chirp chirp chickadee,  
look look sparrow  
flew over the pea garden  
jumped over the cabbage patch,  
over the forest a horn.

label: children
translation:
The lira's warbler,
the border's swallow
flies over the oat field
jumps over the cabbage field
over the forest the horn.

label: children
translation:
A swallow flying around the border,  
a meadowlark trilling,  
flew over the oat field.

label: children
translation:
Liiri, pipe skylark,  
border's edge swallow.

label: children
translation:
Tit, tit, titmouse,  
see, see, sparrow,  
fly over the pea field,  
jump over the cabbage patch,  
buzz over the forest.

label: children
translation:
The dog went to the herd compa-kapa
tail drooping in the hollow.
From the herd home twisting turning twisting,
timpa tampa tirdi.

label: children
translation:
Tit, tit chickadee,  
look, look sparrow.

label: children
translation:
Roll the cake, roll the cake  
put it in the oven, take it out  
eat it all up!

label: children
translation:
The goat carries the herd,  
over the sea the berry,  
bring me hay,  
I will give the hay to the lamb,  
the lamb gives me wool,  
I give the wool to Kalev,  
Kalev gives me iron,  
I give the iron to the blacksmith.

label: children
translation:
Liiri, lõõri, skylark,  
border, edge, swallow  
jump over the bean field fence,  
leap over the cabbage patch,  
over the forest vroom!

label: children
translation:
Tit tit chickadee,  
look, look sparrow.

label: children
translation:
The dog went to the herd: quick quick
tail wagging, nose in the valley,
from the herd home twist turn.

label: children
translation:
The dog went to the herd, the group, the company.  
It came back with a winch, a crank, a whir  
and tipa tapa tirr.

label: children
translation:
Kurr karr, where are you going,  
purr, I’m going to the corner.  
Pirr, parr to the parsnip.  
Mirr, märr what’s there.  
Nirr norr to catch mice.

label: children
translation:
Liiri, little skylark of the flute,  
little swallow on the border,  
jump over the oat field fence,  
leap over the cabbage patch,  
over the forest run.

label: children
translation:
Purr, fool into the corner,  
pirr parr to Parsile.  
Mirr, marr what’s there,  
sirr, sorr to eat mice.

label: children
translation:
A goat, a cat, a herd  
across the sea with berries  
bring me hay,  
I bring hay to the cow,  
the cow brings me milk,  
I bring milk to the piglet,  
the piglet brings me meat,  
I bring meat to the chicken,  
the chicken brings me an egg,  
I bring the egg to the buyer,  
the buyer gives me money.

label: children
translation:
Liiri, little swallow of the pipe,  
swallow of the border edge,  
jump over the oat field fence,  
leap over the cabbage patch,  
over the forest vroom.

label: children
translation:
Prigadi pragadi where did you go.
Prigadi pragadi I went to the forest.
Prigadi pragadi what did you see.
Prigadi pragadi I saw a boy.
Prigadi pragadi what did he ask,
prigadi pragadi he asked for a kiss,
prigadi pragadi did you give,
prigadi pragadi no I did not give
prigadi pragadi why didn’t you give,
prigadi, pragadi his mouth was scabby.

label: children
translation:
Liiri, the lark of the pipe,
piiri, pääri, the swallow,
jump over the oat field fence,
leap over the cabbage patch,
over the forest vroom...

label: children
translation:
A goat leads a herd,
over the sea of berries,
bring me hay;
I give hay to the cow,
the cow gives me milk,
I give milk to the piglet;
the piglet gives me meat,
I give meat to the chicken,
the chicken gives me an egg,
I give the egg to the buyer,
the buyer gives me money,
I take the money to the store,
from the store I get goods.

label: children
translation:
Liiri, pipe, skylark,  
border, end, swallow  
jump over the bean field fence  
hop over the cabbage patch,  
over the forest, dart.

label: children
translation:
The dog went to the herd: in a group, in a pack,  
tail drooping, nose down  
from the herd home, twisting, turning, stirring  
hustle, bustle, rustle.

label: children
translation:
Liiri, little swallow,
border swift swallow
jump over the oat field fence
hop over the cabbage patch,
over the forest ridge.

label: children
translation:
Tii, tii titmouse  
look look sparrow  
flew over the pea garden  
jumped over the cabbage garden  
over the forest, off it goes.

label: children
translation:
The song of the nightingale in the linden tree  
Where is your nest  
nest on the dry spruce top?  
where is that dry spruce  
the old man cut it down  
where is that old man  
the old man died  
where was he buried  
under a long garden bed  
where is that long garden bed  
the serfs plowed it up.

label: children
translation:
Tit, tit chickadee  
caw-caw sparrow.

label: children
translation:
Tit, tit titmouse  
caw-caw sparrow.

label: children
translation:
The dog went to the herd kompa-kompa,  
its paw drooped, tail dragged,  
came home, vinta-vanta virrdi,  
timpa tampa tirrdi.

label: children
translation:
Liiri, lõõri, swallow.
Border chief swallow,
where is your dear nest?

label: children
translation:
The dog goes to the herd: in a group, in a bunch,  
tail tucked, lost on the hill.  
From the herd home: sling, sling the skirting.

label: children
translation:
Tit, tit, the titmouse,  
look, look, the sparrow  
flew over the bean field,  
jumped over the cabbage patch,  
over the forest, off it goes!

label: children
translation:
The dog went to the herd's timpa tompa,  
its tail was in a ditch, its tail was crooked,  
from the herd to home with a twist and turn,  
timpa, tampa, tirdi.

label: children
translation:
The dog went to the herd: in a group together,  
tail wagging at the riverbank,  
from the herd home: twist, turn, spin,  
tip-tap, tip-tap.

label: children
translation:
Where are you going, capercaillie?
I am going to the black grouse's feast,
who will kill the black grouse?
A billy goat with a prong,
a sheep with a paw,
a goat with a kid.

label: children
translation:
Tit, tit titmouse,  
look, look sparrow  
flew over the pea garden  
jumped over the cabbage patch  
over the forest ran a squirrel.

label: children
translation:
Tit, tit, titmouse,  
chick, chick, sparrow,  
fly over the pea garden,  
jump over the cabbage patch,  
over the forest whoosh!

label: children
translation:
The dog went with the herd, in a group,
tail tucked, horn crooked,
from the herd to home, twist and turn,
swish, swash, twirl.

label: children
translation:
Tit, tit, the titmouse,  
vaa, vaa, the sparrow,  
fly over the oat field fence,  
jump over the cabbage garden  
over the forest whistle -.

label: children
translation:
Tit, tit titmouse,  
look, look sparrow,  
fly over the bean field;  
jump over the cabbage patch,  
over the forest, whir!

label: children
translation:
Tii tii titmouse  
vaa vaa sparrow  
fly over the fence  
jump over the cabbage patch  
whizz over the forest.

label: children
translation:
It was beautiful to skip as a girl  
It was costly to raise a girl  
Even better to marry her off  
But she takes the milkmaid’s cow  
From Laugu stallion’s stable.

label: children
translation:
Swallow, swallow swallow,  
Swallow, swallow swallow.  
Where is your golden nest?  
In the forest on a dry spruce.  
Did that dry spruce grow?  
An old man cut it down,  
Where did that old man get it?  
Oxen plowed it down.  
Where did those oxen come from?  
A bear tore them down.  
Where did that bear come from?  
A German shot him down.  
Where did that German come from?  
The German went to town for a walk.  
Where did that town come from?  
The town burned to ashes.  
Where are those ashes and burnt soil?  
But the wind whistled through the reeds—  
Where did those reeds come from?  
The sickle whistled through the reeds!  
Where did that sickle come from?  
That is not known.

label: children
translation:
Oh, poor me, where is my wife?  
In the forest of Kihlevere with the goat herd.  
What is she doing there?  
Sitting on a new chair,  
sewing a new coat,  
patching an old sheepskin coat,  
with silk and thread,  
old woolen yarn.

label: children
translation:
Swallow on the border edge,  
lark in the field, skylark,  
where is your dear little nest?  
In the forest, on a dry spruce branch.  
Where is that dear dry spruce?  
The old man has cut it down.  
Where is that dear old man?  
He went to the garden patch.  
Where is that dear garden patch?  
Oxen have plowed it up.  
Where are those dear oxen?  
A bear had broken the oxen.  
Where is that dear little bear?  
In the front field is rye,  
in the back field is buckwheat,  
and in the middle field is a swirl of oats.

label: children
translation:
Sleep, sleep Maalu, weigh:
I have shut the fleas,
counted the bedbugs;
I put the mosquitoes in tongs.
The child can sleep quietly.

label: children
translation:
Ptruu, go to Riga,  
then back to Tallinn.  
Bring bread for the child:  
horn-shaped loaves,  
double-crust buns,  
flavored honey breads,  
sour breads with holes,  
the better the more adorned.

label: children
translation:
:,: Sleep, sleep little heartbeat,  
Sleep little baby bundle. :,:
Mother went to the forest to get the baby,  
Set the cuckoo to rock,  
Set the summer bird to move.  
There the cuckoo fell asleep  
Because the summer bird sang too much.

label: children
translation:
Susu, susu sugar egg.  
Mom went to the forest to get mammu.  
Started swinging the cradle,  
Moving the summer bird.  
There the cuckoo called out loud,  
The summer bird sang too much.

label: children
translation:
Make a cake, dip the bread,  
Lean pork,  
Dip in egg,  
Put a dollop of butter on top,  
Roll, roll, fall – quickly eat the bread!

label: children
translation:
Liiri, little swallow,  
Where is your darling’s nest?  
In the forest on a wet pine,  
At home on the dry spruce.  
Where did that dry spruce come from?  
An old man cut it down.  
Where did that old man go?  
He crawled under the garden bed.  
Where did that garden bed come from?  
Draft oxen plowed it up.  
Where did those draft oxen come from?  
A bear tore them down.  
Where did that bear come from?  
A German shot it.  
Where did that German come from?  
The German went to the sauna, stuck his head in the bundling of birch twigs,  
The door locked, the cuckoo went cuckoo!

label: children
translation:
Son, ride to town,  
old man to Tallinn.  
Bring an apple, horse,  
bring a roll, tail.

label: children
translation:
A goat goes to the herd,  
over the sea to the berry,  
bring me some hay.  
I give the hay to the sheep:  
the sheep gives me wool.  
I give the wool to my mother,  
mother makes me a warm knitted jacket  
for going to the herd.

label: children
translation:
Swallow at the edge of the border,  
flute at the end of the hornpipe,  
where is your dear nest  
behind the room on the oak branch?  
Where did that oak remain?  
The old man cut it down.  
Where did that old man remain?  
The old man died.  
Where did that death remain?  
Death went to hell.  
Where did that hell remain?  
Hell burned down.  
Where did that fire remain?  
The fire went out.  
Where did that stump remain?  
The bear tore the stump.  
Where did that bear remain?  
The bear went across the sea to Sweden.  
How can one get there?  
With nails, with nails,  
on old iron wheels,  
with pointed stakes.

label: children
translation:
Ptruu is going on a trip to Riga  
to the city of Tartu  
to bring tobacco for her father  
and some candy for her mother.

label: children
translation:
Hey little bee, sleepy mood,  
sleep long, grow big.  
Aidel as a haycutter,  
Taadi as an oak harvester,  
a hard wood clatterer.  
A long fart puller.  
A wide hem splitter.

label: children
translation:
Tit, tit chickadee,  
look, look, sparrow,  
Liri, lõõri, swallow,  
piiri, pääri, swallow,  
jump over the oat field,  
hop over the cabbage patch,  
over the forest - whir.

label: children
translation:
The dog went to the herd's company group  
tail drooping, head down  
from the herd home, pulling, tugging, twisting  
clumsy, awkward, stumbling.

label: children
translation:
A goat brought the village's herd,  
across the sea, berries,  
brought me hay,  
I gave the hay to the cow.  
The cow gave me milk,  
I gave the milk to the piglet,  
The piglet gave me a side (cut of meat),  
I gave the side to the village.  
The village gave me cake,  
I gave the cake to Kalev.  
Kalev gave me iron,  
I gave the iron to the sled.  
The sled gave me gold,  
I gave the gold to the oak.  
The oak gave me leaves,  
I gave the leaves to the sheep.  
The sheep gave me wool,  
I gave the wool to Veerik,  
Veerik gave me a pike (fish),  
Kalev’s neckerchief.

label: children
translation:
Tit tit chickadee,  
Look, look sparrow,  
Lieri looli lark,  
border prince swallow,  
jump over the bean field,  
hop over the cabbage patch,  
over the forest – whizz!

label: children
translation:
A goat is a herd of goats,  
berries across the sea.  
Bring me hay,  
I will give wool to the sheep,  
the sheep will give me wool,  
I will give the wool to the little twig  
for the shepherd’s shoes,  
to the servant big socks,  
to the master long trousers,  
to the groom a spruce hat.

label: children
translation:
The raven, a gentle little bird,  
flew to the town's street.  
From there it flew to the tavern,  
to the innkeeper's funeral.  
The raven made a gathering call,  
called together the sad birds.  
He did not call the eagle, -  
the eagle was a fierce predator.  
The woman made trousers, the old man made trousers,  
he himself already had trousers.  
Then three pairs of trousers came together,  
three new pairs of trousers in total.  
The blue ones were bridge-trousers,  
the red ones were wedding trousers,  
the yellow ones were suitor trousers,  
the white ones were raven trousers.

label: children
translation:
Ut-tut-utt - come to us!  
Our girl is coming to you tomorrow,  
bringing you bread  
and a tall bottle of milk.

label: children
translation:
Swing, swing little goat kid,  
Laala, laala little lamb!

label: children
translation:
Oh, poor me, where is my wife?  
In the goat herd at Kirevere manor!

label: children
translation:
A goat leads the herd  
over the sea of berries.  
Bring me some hay,  
I will give it to the sheep,  
the sheep gives me wool,  
I give the wool to the spinner,  
to the shepherd, clogs,  
to the servant, large socks,  
to the master, long trousers,  
to the groom, a spruce hat!

label: children
translation:
Border-swallow swallow,  
lyre-lark lark,  
where is your darling's nest?  
Behind the room, on the oak tree.  
Where is that oak?  
The old man cut it down!  
Where is that old man?  
The old man died.  
Where is that death?  
Death went to hell.  
Where is that hell?  
Hell burned down.  
Where is that fire?  
The fire went out.  
Where is that stump?  
The bear tore the stump apart.  
Where is that bear?  
The bear went across the sea to Sweden.  
How can you follow there?  
With pegs, with pegs,  
old iron wheels,  
sharp-pointed poles!

label: children
translation:
Toot, toot toot come to us,  
our girl is coming to you tomorrow.  
Today we have a Swedish dance,  
the two-egg dance.  
The girl dances, the old man dances,  
I with Miku-Mari,  
the sexton in the kitchen with Triin,  
the gentleman with his lady!

label: children
translation:
Lullaby, lullaby, hush-hush  
Hush, little child,  
sleep for a long time, grow up big,  
grow up to be our shepherd.

label: children
translation:
The man went to the sauna  
put his head in the sauna stove  
The knife went up his ass  
Let out a stinky fart  
The sauna caught fire,  
Where did the sauna ashes go?  
The wind carried them to the sea  
Where did the sea come from?  
A black ox drank it all up  
Where did the black ox come from?  
It ran into the forest reeds  
Where did the reeds come from?  
A sickle whistled down  
Where did the sickle come from?  
The sickle broke into five pieces  
Where did those sickle pieces go?  
The grindstone wore them down  
Where did the grindstone come from?  
A chicken scratched on the manure  
Where did the chicken come from?  
The eagle ate the chicken  
Where did the eagle come from?  
The old man shot it down  
Where did the old man come from?  
The man went to war to fight  
There his head was cut off  
And his blood was shed

label: children
translation:
Oh, poor me, where is my wife?  
In the Tärivere forest with the goat herd.  
She sits on a golden chair  
on a silver-framed bucket,  
with silk, with thread,  
with double gold.

label: children
translation:
Border swallow  
where is your nest?  
Liiri, the lark  
where is your nest?  
Behind the room, on the oak tree  
Where is that oak?  
An old man cut the oak down.  
Where is that old man?  
The old man is under the garden bed.  
Where is that garden bed?  
The oxen plowed the garden bed.  
Where are those oxen?  
Bears broke the oxen.  
Where are those bears?  
Guns knocked the bears down.  
Where are those guns?  
Fire burned the guns.  
Where is that fire?  
Water extinguished the fire.  
Where is that water?  
The water is in the sea now.

label: children
translation:
Liiri-lõõri, lõuke,  
Pääri-pääri, swallow!  
Where was your golden nest?  
In the forest on a dry spruce.  
Where did that dry spruce come from?  
An old man cut down the spruce.  
Where did that old man come from?  
The old man died.  
Where was he buried?  
In the flower bed of Pikapõllu.  
Where did the flower bed of Pikapõllu come from?  
Cursed swine plowed it up.  
Where did those cursed swine come from?  
They went on a long road.  
Where did that long road come from?  
Grass grew over the clearing.  
Where did the grass on the clearing come from?  
Ani ate the grass down.  
Where did Ani come from?  
Ani flew into the sky  
into the blue cloud,  
and the red cloud’s wedding,  
and the white cloud’s branch.

label: children
translation:
Lõõri-lõõri, lõuke,  
pääri-pääri, swallow,  
where was your golden nest?  
In the forest on a dry spruce.  
Where did that dry spruce come from?  
An old man cut the spruce down.  
Where did that old man come from?  
The old man died.  
Where was he buried?  
In the garden of a long field.  
Where did that field garden come from?  
Servants plowed it up.  
Where did those servants come from?  
A bear broke the servants.  
Where did that bear come from?  
The bear jumped into the reeds.  
Where did those reeds come from?  
A sickle cut the reeds.  
Where did that sickle come from?  
A trickster tricked the sickles.  
Where did that trickster come from?  
A hen stirred in the manure.  
Where did that hen come from?  
A hawk took the hen away.  
Where did that hawk come from?  
The hawk flew to the town,  
to the blue eye,  
to the red wedding,  
to the white post,  
to the black funeral.

label: children
translation:
Lõõri-lõõri, little bird,  
pääri-pääri, little swallow,  
where was your golden nest?  
On a dry spruce in the forest.  
Where did that dry spruce come from?  
An old man cut down the dry spruce.  
Where did that old man come from?  
A bear broke the old man.  
Where did that bear come from?  
The bear chewed the reed.  
Where did that reed come from?  
The sickle whistled it down.

label: children
translation:
Liiri-lõõri, swallow,  
where is your dear little nest.

label: children
translation:
Lilac, let the lilac be,
Let the cuckoo be.

label: children
translation:
Liiri-lõõri swallow,  
Piiri-pääri swallow!  
Where is your golden nest?  
- In the forest, at the top of a dry fir.  
Where did that fir come from?  
- The village boy cut it down.  
Where did that village boy come from?  
- A bear tore him apart.  
Where did that bear come from?  
- The bear is in the tall reed.  
Where did that reed come from?  
- The sickle whistled it down.  
Where did that sickle come from?  
- The whetstone wore it out.  
Where did that whetstone come from?  
- The eagle broke it.  
Where did that eagle come from?  
- The eagle has flown to the town.  
Where did that town come from?  
- The town has burned down.  
Where has that town's ash gone?  
- The wind has blown the ash to the sky.

label: children
translation:
Tui, tui, tui, tui, tui, tui, come to us,  
Our lady is coming, our lady is coming to you tomorrow,  
Wearing a skirt made of sackcloth,  
With a headscarf made of corduroy.

label: children
children
translation:
Liiri-lõõri swallow,  
Piiri-pääri swallow!  
Where is your golden nest?  
In the forest, on the dry spruce branch.  
Where is that dry little spruce?  
The old man cut it down.  
Where is that old little man?  
Into the piece of garden field.  
Where is that old garden field?  
The yoked oxen plowed it up,  
The gray oxen drove it up,  
The black oxen pulled it up.  
Where are those old yoked oxen?  
I sent them down to the reed.  
Where is that old reed?  
The scythe mowed the reed.  
Where is that old little scythe?  
The (little) salamander crept, crawled hard.  
Where is that old little salamander?  
The hen scurried into the dung.  
Where is that old little hen?  
The hawk took it to the stump in the forest.  
Where is that old little stump?  
The bear scratched the little stump.  
Where is that old little bear?  
He jumped over nine forests,  
He jumped over eight forests.  
His head was visible above the forest,  
His feet were visible beneath the forest,  
His body twisted through the middle of the forest.

label: children
translation:
Come home, dear father,  
Come home, dear mother.  
Come home from the windy place,  
From the wide field,  
From the church tower.  
Bring me the wide-horned ones,  
The honey bears with honey,  
The best blacksmiths.  
But be quiet, little child,  
It seems they are already coming.  
The head appears above the forest,  
The feet rarely through the forest,  
The middle twisting over the forest.

label: children
translation:
Sleep, sleep little pulse
Sleep, little berry twig
Breathe gentle little leaf
Rest little lingonberry flower
A child will grow into a little lamb
A little lamb, a herdsman,
Brings me a basket of strawberries
A handful of cranberries
A sieve full of currants
Half a measure of lingonberries
A full measure of raspberries.

label: children
translation:
Lõõri-lõõri little lark  
Piiri-pääri little swallow  
Where is your dear little nest  
In the forest grove, on top of the spruce  
Where did that spruce then go  
An old man chopped it down  
Where did that old man then go  
He crawled into the garden bed  
Where did the garden bed come from  
Oxen yoked plowed it up  
Where did those yoked oxen come from  
The bear yoked ate them up.  
Where did that bear itself come from  
The bear limped into the reed bed  
Where did that reed then come from  
The scythe hissed down  
Where did that scythe itself come from  
It wore itself out  
Where did that itself come from  
The hen scurried into the manure  
Where did that hen itself come from  
The hawk ate the hen.  
Where did that hawk itself come from  
The hawk flew into the sky  
Where did that hawk reach the sky  
Along a blue silk ribbon  
Along a red braided ribbon.

label: children
translation:
Sleep come in through the door  
Knock on the child's eyebrow  
Let it rest on the child's table  
For the child to take time  
To linger at twilight  
To whistle during the smoke.

label: children
translation:
Äia-tuia, let the swing go  
Kibi-käbi-nuia  
To cross the sea  
To fly over the forest  
To the forest folk’s wedding  
To old Villu's yard.

label: children
translation:
Liiri-lõõri little flute  
Piiri-pääri little swallow  
Where is your golden nest?  
In the forest on a dry fir tree  
Where did that dry fir come from?  
An old man cut the fir down  
Where did that old man come from?  
The old man died  
Where was he buried?  
In the long bed of the field  
Where did that field bed come from?  
Oxen plowed it up  
Where did those oxen come from?  
A bear broke them down  
Where did that bear come from?  
The bear went to the long reeds  
Where did those reeds come from?  
A sickle mowed them down  
Where did that sickle come from?  
A hoe chopped it down  
Where did that hoe come from?  
A hen scratched in the manure  
Where did that hen come from?  
A hawk broke it down  
Where did that hawk come from?  
A Saxon shot it down  
Where did that Saxon come from?  
The Saxon went to town  
Where did that town come from?  
The town burned down  
Where did that fire come from?  
Water put it out  
Where did that water come from?  
The water ran into the sea  
Where did that sea come from?  
The sea grew into black land.

label: children
translation:
Sleep, sleep, father-in-law, garden  
Sleep comes hooting  
Roaring over the mountain  
Come, sleep, through the door  
Step in through the window  
Roll onto the child's bow  
Go onto the child's head.

label: children
translation:
Sleep, come in through the door  
Step onto the child's eye  
Walk onto the child's nest.

label: children
translation:
Grandfather, grandfather, let the swing go  
I sing to the child  
Just like a lamb to a lambkin  
To a mother grouse’s tender one  
To a little duckling.

label: children
translation:
Mood, mood from the wind's ridge  
Let loose wide from the ridge  
Spin from the church's ridge  
You bring horned rolls  
Honeyed breads delightful  
Triangular cakes  
Aspen leaves even better.

label: children
translation:
Swing, move little cradle  
Endure until autumn for me  
Let me go to Riga city  
From there I will bring you a braided ribbon  
A braided ribbon, a throat ribbon.

label: children
translation:
Sleep, sleep, little one  
Stump-stump, stick  
Let the cradle rock  
On top of the big stone  
Sleep come through the door  
Cuckoo on the child's eyebrow.

label: children
translation:
A goat herds the flock,  
Over the sea, the berry.  
Bring me hay,  
I bring hay to the cow,  
The cow gives me milk,  
I give the milk to the piglet,  
The piglet gives me the lice,  
I give the lice to the mother-in-law,  
The mother-in-law gives me wool,  
I give the wool to the calf,  
For myself a good hat,  
For the master long pants,  
For the servant big socks,  
For the shepherd boy clogs.

label: children
translation:
Where did that old man come from?  
The old man died.  
Where was he buried?  
Between the garden plots.  
What happened to those garden plots?  
Speckled bulls plowed them up.  
Where did those speckled bulls come from?  
Bears broke the bulls.  
Where did those black bears come from?  
The old man killed the bear.  
Where did that old man come from?  
The old man died.

label: children
translation:
Äia-tuia, kibi-käbi club,  
Let the swing go  
Over the door into the yard  
Out the back end  
A somersault into the ditch.

label: children
translation:
Father-in-law, mother-in-law, club and stick,  
let the swing go.  
Over the door, out into the yard,  
to the end of the field,  
a somersault into the ditch.

label: children
translation:
Sleep, sleep, little Matsikene  
Sweet sleep to Mats  
Drink, drink, little Juku  
Juku's decorated little jug  
Play the pipe, little Peedu  
Peedu has delicate little fingers.

label: children
translation:
Taita  
Come, come from the top of the wind  
Let, let from the top of the flames  
Spin from in front of the church  
Bring hundreds of horned ones  
Honey cakes delightful  
Pies with two crusts.

label: children
translation:
Häia-tuia,  
Kibi-käbi stick  
Let the swing go  
Over the Kingu forest back, to the edge.

label: children
translation:
Swing, swing, little goat kid  
Sing, sing, little lamb  
The little goat kid has scratched eyes  
The little lamb has sores on its ears.

label: children
translation:
Sleep, sleep, little heartbeat  
Sleep, little teddy bear  
Sleep, sleep, little one  
Quickly, quickly, hurry  
Let the swing go  
Out the door and window  
Sleep come in through the door  
Come in through the door and window  
Come into the child's eye  
Go before the child's hands  
Sit on the child's eyebrow  
Let it rest on the child's table.

label: children
translation:
Hello, hello, Tepermann!  
From Tepermann came a maruna,  
From maruna came Mari's pipe,  
From Mari's pipe came a pibun,  
From pibun came a baker,  
From baker came a salt box,  
From salt box came a tremor,  
From tremor came a rainbow,  
From rainbow came a cab,  
From cab came a beautiful forest.  
In that forest, people drank mead,  
Silver mugs were cherished,  
Tin dishes well respected;  
Wooden utensils, clothèries,  
Inside five kinds of oak,  
Brass on the wall.

label: children
translation:
Lõõri-lõõri little cuckoo  
Piiri-pääri little swallow  
Where is your darling's nest?  
In the field under a big stone  
Where is the stone from the field?  
A black bull plowed that stone  
Where is the black bull from?  
A bear killed the black bull  
Where did that bear come from?  
The bear went across the sea to Sweden  
It won't come out before  
Bridges are built across the Baltic Sea

label: children
translation:
Cuckoo, cuckoo, little cuckoo  
Where did you get your golden nest?  
In the forest, on top of a dry spruce  
Where did that dry spruce come from?  
An old man chopped it down  
Where did that old man come from?  
He sits on the garden bed  
Where did that garden bed come from?  
Oxen plowed it up  
Where did those oxen come from?  
A bear killed the oxen  
Where did that bear come from?  
The bear jumped into the reeds  
Where did those reeds come from?  
He whistled down the scythe  
Where did that scythe come from?  
Luisku lied about the scythe  
Where did that Luisku come from?  
A hen scratched in the manure  
Where did that hen come from?  
The cuckoo took the hen to the sky.

label: children
translation:
Fingerless gloves in a bundle,  
A bundle and a lamp,  
A lamp and a mitten;  
From a mitten came a market thumb,  
From a market thumb came a pebble,  
From a pebble came a cross peider,  
From a peider came rinulad,  
From rinula came a breast pin,  
From a breast pin came porous ones,  
From porous ones came fingerless gloves.  
Fingerless gloves in a bundle,  
A bundle and a lamp,  
A lamp and a mitten.

label: children
translation:
Let the rye grow taller,
Let it grow stronger,
Let it grow a bit longer,
Higher than a straw,
Heavier than a crumb of bread,
Smarter than a grain of buckwheat,
By sliding, your socks became big,
By swinging, your shoes became new.

label: children
translation:
Loori-loori, little loon  
Piiri-paari, little headband  
Where is your precious little nest?  
In the forest on a dry spruce branch  
Where did that dry spruce come from?  
An old man chopped it down  
Where did that old man go?  
The old man died  
Where was he buried?  
In a long field bed  
Where did that bed come from?  
Oxen plowed it up  
Where did those oxen come from?  
A bear tore the oxen  
Where did that bear come from?  
A gun shot the bear down  
Where did that gun come from?  
Fire burned the gun down  
Where did that fire come from?  
Water extinguished the fire  
Where did that water come from?  
A black bull drank it up  
Where did that bull come from?  
Jumped into the river, plunged into the river  
Where did that river come from?  
Reeds grew on it  
Where did those reeds come from?  
A sickle rang down  
Who sharpened the sickle?  
A glint sharpened the sickle  
Where did that glint come from?  
A hen was scratching in the manure  
Where did that hen come from?  
A hawk ate the hen  
Where did that hawk come from?  
The hawk disappeared.

label: children
translation:
Breast, breast little child,  
Breast, breast for the older one,  
A drop of milk for fullness,  
For the height of the cream pitcher.

label: children
translation:
Purr-narr to the corner
Pirr-parr to the duck
Great tit to the gate
Finch to the stake.

label: children
translation:
Kuissu-kuissu, dear children,  
Häia-häia, good children.  
Suisu-suisu, winter child  
Grow into a winter chicken,  
A hay-season duck,  
A rye-slice little bird.  
I take care of the servant’s child.  
I care for the servant boy.  
I take care of the servant’s child,  
The winter boy at the oven.  
The lazy mistress’s child.  
This is my winter knitting needle,  
This is my winter spindle spun cone,  
Spring carding.  
Autumn yarn bundle.  
Spring’s precious fabric bundle.  
Weekday pastime,  
Sunday’s little toy:  
Here the mitten swings,  
Weakly it sways while being pulled,  
Hugged with two hands,  
Carefully held here.  
So that the wind doesn’t come,  
Nor the sun shine,  
So that the rain showers don’t roll,  
Nor hailstones fall.

label: children
translation:
Lõõri-lõõri little bird,  
Pääri-pääri little swallow,  
Where is your golden nest?  
In the forest on a dry spruce.  
Where did the dry spruce come from?  
An old man cut the dry spruce.  
Where did the old man come from?  
The old man died.  
Where was he buried?  
In a long field garden,  
Where did the field garden come from?  
Plowing bulls plowed it up.  
Where did the plowing bulls come from?  
A bear tore the plowing bulls apart.  
Where did the bear come from?  
The bear crawled into the reeds.  
Where did the reeds come from?  
A sickle mowed the reeds.  
Where did the sickle come from?  
A blade wore down the sickle.  
Where did the blade come from?  
A hen scratched in the manure.  
Where did the hen come from?  
A hawk snatched the hen away.  
Where did the hawk come from?  
The hawk flew over the sea.

label: children
translation:
Tune, tune, little lark,  
Fly, fly, little swallow,  
Where is the golden nest?  
In the forest on the dry spruce tip  
Where the dry spruce has grown.  
The old man has cleared it away.  
Where has the old man gone?  
He has gone to the garden patch.  
Where is the garden patch?  
The worked oxen.  
Where are the worked oxen?  
The bear has broken the worked oxen.  
Where is the little bear?  
The bear has gone into the reeds.  
Where are the reeds?  
They have been cut down with a sickle.  
Where is the sickle?  
It has been worn out hard.  
Where has it gone?  
The hen has scratched in the dung,  
Where is the little hen?  
The hawk has taken the little hen.  
Where is the little hawk?  
The hawk has flown under the sky.  
How did he get there?  
Along the red store ribbon,  
Along the blue silk strap,  
Along the silver chain,  
Through the magnificent mist,  
Through five rainbows,  
Between white clouds,  
Into the blue cloud.

label: children
translation:
Make a cake, dip the bread  
Put a lot of butter on it  
Smooth it with pork  
Roll it with an egg  
Put it in the oven, take it out  
Someone? – zap the cake!

label: children
translation:
The dog went to the herd in a group  
Came home quickly.

label: children
translation:
Wander, wander, little granny  
Come to us, little wanderer  
Bring bread a hundred ways  
Village bread in the dawn’s manner  
Old bread in the grave’s manner  
In the field in the plow’s manner  
Honey bread from the honey maker  
Black bread from the baker  
Blue as the sea’s edge  
Fancy Perch from Peipus  
Praised herrings from Arju  
Big herrings from Finland  
Cowslips from the alder grove  
Stumps with burnt mushrooms  
Raisin-like small mushrooms  
To buy clothes with money in advance  
With a penny and two in advance  
Half a penny and a half in advance  
Ten pennies and a die in advance.

label: children
translation:
Grandfather, grandfather,  
Fir cone, club,  
Over the door, outside,  
To the edge of the clearing,  
A somersault into the ditch.

label: children
translation:
A ride, a ride there:  
From there a loaf of bread,  
A long bottle of milk,  
A wide, flat loaf of bread.

label: children
translation:
Come, come little sleep,
Fall upon the child's eyelids,
Narrow the eyes little by little.

label: children
translation:
One does not make one,  
Two do not attack the sofa,  
Three not at once.

label: children
translation:
Liiri-lõõri swallow  
Piiri-peari small chick  
Where is the golden little boy?  
In the forest, on the tip of a dry spruce.  
Where has the dry spruce stayed?  
The old man cut down the dry spruce!  
Where has the old man remained?  
The old man has died!  
Where was he buried?  
Under the long field garden!  
Where has the field garden stayed?  
The oxen have plowed it up!  
Where have those oxen gone?  
The bears have eaten the plowed oxen!  
Where have those bears remained?  
The bears have gone to the reeds!  
Where have those reeds gone?  
The sickle has mowed the reeds!  
Where has the sickle itself stayed?  
The scythe was lying near the sickle!  
Where has the scythe itself stayed?  
The black rooster ran to the manure!  
Where has that manure stayed?  
The manure was taken to the field!  
Where has that black rooster stayed?  
The hawk flew to the black rooster!  
Where has that hawk itself stayed?  
The hawk flew under the sky!  
How did he get there?  
Along the red shoelace  
Along the blue thread!  
Where did he go from under the sky?  
From under the sky, he went to Rootsimoa!  
Where has Rootsimoa stayed?  
Rootsimoa has burned down!  
Who put it out?  
The water put it out!  
Where has that water itself gone?  
The water flowed into the sea!  
The sea came under our yard  
A little swamp is in the middle  
What is on this swamp?  
A pillar is on this swamp.  
What is on top of this pillar?  
A sieve is on top of this pillar!  
What is inside the sieve?  
Seven children are inside the sieve:  
They all govern the weather  
They guide the sea wind.

label: children
translation:
Ride, ride, to town,  
What to go there for?  
To bring bread from there.  
The horse brings the sheep,  
The tail brings the bread,  
The anus brings onions,  
A tuft to the fiery nose,  
A lick for the child’s whip.

label: children
translation:
Mother-in-law, spruce,
a twig, cone, and club.
Start the swing,
Throw the bow aside.
Horse, go to Riga,
Behind to Tallinn;
The horse brings apples,
The tail brings bread rolls,
The flange brings bread,
The poop hole brings onions.

label: children
translation:
Lyre’s tune, little flame  
Border’s edge, little stone  
Where is your dear little nest?  
In the forest, on top of a dry spruce.  
Where is that dear dry spruce?  
An old man has whistled it down.  
Where is that dear old man?  
The old man has died.  
Where is his dear little grave?  
Outside, under the field’s edge.  
Where is that dear field’s edge?  
Working oxen have plowed it up.  
Where are those dear working oxen?  
A bear has killed the working oxen.  
Where is that dear little bear?  
The bear has hidden in the reed.  
Where is that dear reed?  
The scythe has whistled it down.  
Where is that dear little scythe?  
It has worn itself out thoroughly.  
Where is that dear worn one?  
A hen has shuffled into the manure.  
Where is that dear little hen?  
The gold has killed the hen.  
Out in the field is the pea,  
In the middle are the nice wheats,  
At the back is the barley.  
Where is that dear little gold?  
A hunter has shot the gold down.  
Where is that dear little hunter?  
God has killed the hunter.  
Where is that dear God?  
God is now in heaven.

label: children
translation:
Lõõri lõõri little lark
Where is your dear nest
In the forest on a dry spruce top
Where is that dear dry spruce
The old man cut it down
Where is that dear old man
Resting on the field edge
Where is that dear field edge
The variegated oxen plowed it up
Where are those dear variegated oxen
A bear tore the variegated oxen
Where is that dear bear
In the forest in tall reed grass
Where is that dear reed grass
The sickle whistled it down
Loudly clanged it down
Where is that dear sickle
I placed a lid outside
Where is that dear lid
The hen flew off the lid
Where is that dear hen
The hawk took the hen over the sea
Over the sea into the hands of men
Over the island into the hands of Saxons
Into the hands of small boys.

label: children
translation:
Grandfather Tuia, stick and club,
Let the hand go!
Spruce and juniper on the edge,
A pile of wood and a bundle of twigs,
Two ells of Robuska,
Five old sheep,
Ten lambs.

label: children
translation:
Hello, hello Teppermann  
From Teppermann I became a mammoth  
From mammoth I became a string instrument  
From string instrument I became a pipe  
From pipe I became a fiddler  
From fiddler I became Sõmer  
From Sõmer I became a saltbox  
From saltbox I became a hammer  
From hammer I became a winnowing rope  
From winnowing rope I became a hat  
From hat I became a hunter,  
The hunter went to the forest to hunt  
On Sunday morning,  
On weekdays in the evening.  
What did he find in the forest?  
He found a child lying down  
Among the dogwood bushes.  
He took the child on his lap  
Wrapped the child in swaddling clothes  
Took her to the girls’ room  
To the center of the wreath-hedged room  
Asked and listened  
Whose child this was.  
One swore, another swore  
Quarreling, shouting, maiden  
She swore she was the old woman;  
He took the child on his lap  
Took her to the bridegroom’s room  
To the center of the hats.  
Asked and listened  
Whose child this was.  
Hannus, a great German man  
He swore he was the old strong one:  
He must be thrown into the water  
God gave Märta a blue apron.  
He must be thrown into the fire  
God gave Hannus a red hat,  
He must be pushed into the flames  
God loosened the child’s tongue.  
The child began to speak.  
Then they asked and listened  
Who was your father?  
Hannus, a great German man  
He was my father.  
Quarreling, shouting, maiden,  
She was my mother.

label: children
translation:
Lõõri lõõri little swallow  
pääri pääri little swallow  
where is the golden nest  
in the forest on the dry spruce top  
where has the dry spruce gone  
the old man has cut it down  
where has the old man gone  
to the edge of the field  
where has the field’s edge gone  
oxen have plowed the land  
where have the oxen gone  
the bear has broken the oxen’s yoke  
where has the little bear gone  
the bear has crouched in the reed  
where is the reed for the pipe  
the sickle has rusted down  
where is the sickle  
worn out hard  
where have the hard ones gone  
the chicken pecked at the dung  
where has the chicken gone  
when it flew under the sky  
how did you say it  
along silver strings  
along red ribbon shops  
along blue silk straps.

label: children
translation:
Lõõri lõõri little swallow  
pärri pärri sweet little bird  
where is the golden little nest  
In the forest on the dry spruce top  
where did the dry spruce go  
an old man has cut it down  
where did the old man go  
he plowed the field’s fine soil  
where did the field's edge go  
oxen have plowed the field  
where have the oxen gone  
a bear has broken the oxen  
where has the little bear gone  
the bear has eaten the green grass  
where has the green grass gone  
the sickle has been whistled down  
where did the sickle go  
it has worn away sharply  
where did the sharpness go  
a chicken was fluttering in the dung heap  
where did the little chicken go  
it has gone beneath the sky  
where has it gone and how  
along silver paths  
along a red ribbon’s edge  
along a blue silk strap.

label: marriage
translation:
Last year I took a young wife  
The year before, another partner  
She was plump and red  
She was pale and sickly  
She was healthy and sharp  
I took her to the tender hayfield  
To the dry, golden meadow  
She mowed hay, rustled the forest  
Took the swath, caught in the forest  
Took the bow, took the two  
Slept on the third  
Put her apron under her head;  
The apron strings as a pillow  
The apron straps as bedding  
I went home crying:  
Under the stable yard  
The woman came out to meet me, the old man came out to meet me  
Immediately asking me:  
Why do you cry, young lad?  
Why should I cry, old lady?  
Or why should I cry, old man?  
I answered, I told:  
Last year I took a young wife  
The year before, another partner  
She was plump and red  
She was pale and sickly  
She was healthy and sharp  
I took her to the tender hayfield  
To the dry, golden meadow  
She mowed hay, rustled the forest  
Took the swath, caught in the forest  
Took the bow, took the two  
Slept on the third  
Put her apron under her head  
The apron strings as a pillow  
The apron straps as bedding  
She began to limp!  
From the pig seller to sleep  
From the shoelace to shrivel  
From the sole to fall  
The old woman replied, answering:  
Oh, you crazy young lad!  
Oh, you crazy and foolish  
Throw the city girls away  
Barley rolled directly  
Oats following in pairs  
Do one deed without alcohol  
Half a vat of moonshine;  
Five vats of beer  
Oh, woman is ale’s delight:  
Sharp woman is beer’s joy,  
Plague woman is beer barrel’s pleasure;  
Then the woman will be healthy!  
Like other women. -

label: marriage
translation:
When can I go to my father!
When can I go to my mother?
When will I roll to my brothers;
When will I reach out to my sister?
In autumn the rivers are deep;
In spring the waves are wide.
Night’s glance and darkness
The field is broad and open!
Willow
Thick and full of water.
The apple falls into the brook
Amongst the mossy hummocks;
Into the chariot of the horse,
In the bend of the gray time;
Into the wave of the clear lake!

label: marriage
translation:
When I was growing up at father's home  
When I was growing up at mother's home!  
I used to scold my brother in the yard  
Sometimes I got to eat in the barn  
Even more in the living room  
With a share in the chamber.  
Indeed, I got to eat in the kitchen too  
Secretly eat in the sauna too  
Now I can cry in the corner  
Sometimes cry in the barn too  
Even more in the living room  
With a share in the chamber.  
Indeed, I can cry in the kitchen too  
Secretly cry in the sauna too  
I cry with harsh words  
I shout demanding order  
The den of the bloodhound

label: marriage
translation:
My fiancé is a musical instrument maker  
Along with a kannel maker  
He takes me to bed with an instrument  
With a kannel to the chamber  
Puts the instrument’s head below  
Between the kannel’s ceiling  
Rises with the morning  
If I don’t hear, he wakes me  
Takes the instrument from under its head  
From between the kannel’s ceiling  
Lets the instrument call to me  
My kannels announce:  
"Rise, bird, milk the cow,  
Rise, hen, send the herd."  
Your fiancé is a whip maker  
Along with a wooden rod maker  
He takes you to bed with a whip  
With a wooden rod to the chamber  
Puts the whip’s head below,  
Between the wooden rod’s ceiling  
Rises with the morning  
If you don’t hear, he wakes you  
Takes the whip from under its head  
From between the wooden rod’s ceiling  
Lets the whip call to you  
Your wooden rods announce:  
"Rise, lazy one, milk the cow!  
Rise, herder, send the herd."

label: marriage
translation:
Oh, my dear God!
Why did you let me sleep?
If this had been followed through
Men would have been mixed without seed.
Other fellows gave donations
Wore pretty neckwear
I was given black and foolish
A tar stump and a sick one.
Where to go away with the black;
To hasten with the sick,
To rush with the foolish?
Where there is a pond, I shake there
Where there is water, I splash there.
A bar of soap on my wall,
A white towel on the rack;
Why do I wash the pergelida
With a scanty rasp of raspberry?!

label: marriage
translation:
O, God, dear God!  
Why did you leave me sleeping  
When the feast was held  
And the drink was being passed  
Men’s seed was mixed  
The gift of a man's happiness.  
Others got handsome ones, all nice  
I got a black and foolish one  
A charred stump and a sickly one  
Where should I go with the black  
Hurrying with the foolish one  
Facing the sickly one  
Rolling with the angry one.  
Where there is water, there I splash  
Where there is food, there I swim  
Where there is a puddle, I rinse.  
I have a piece of soap on the wall  
A white towel on the rod:  
So I can make the man clean  
Clean, fine  
Fashionable among others  
White among the crowd.  
Now, in spite, they tease me  
Laughing through jokes.  
In spite, the lords tease me  
In spite, the ladies tease me  
The Germans laugh through jokes.  
They do not think to understand  
Do not know the stars  
Do not guess the signs  
I understand, why they do not understand.  
I know the stars in the sky  
Guess the eels in the sea  
Count the burbots in the waves  
So why, in spite, is the teasing  
The laughing through jokes.  
I am not laughed at by a wise woman  
Nor by the diligent young girl  
I am laughed at by a lazy woman  
By a spiteful girl  
Called a dung heap  
Slandered as a sleeper of pawns  
A skater at the pub doors  
A mover of ribbons and ties.

label: marriage
translation:
I was at home, paid for gold  
Father’s crooked yard  
The copper brother’s scent  
The tin brother’s path.  
I roll like an egg on the grass  
Twist like a ball on the field  
A German apple in the yard.  
Now Mari got others’ homes  
The goose got others’ springs  
The duck got others’ places  
The grouse other waters.  
Now you shouldn’t pay attention to the land  
That is under the goose’s wing  
The color between the toes  
The feather of a bird’s wing.  
Now a dog boy courts me  
A starving servant bites  
A bear’s keeper washes.

label: marriage
translation:
I have already been waiting for it,  
I have been watching for it,  
I patiently endured,  
My shoes tore from it,  
My laces begged for it,  
The bull’s hide groaned:  
The last servant of Viru,  
The continued hat of Järva,  
The bad shepherd boy of Harju.

label: marriage
translation:
Clean the straw, rinse the straw
Wash the straw finely,
Beat the straw to whiteness
The straw comes from the straw house
It starts knocking on the door
Swearing at the manure
Throws socks onto the manure,
Shoes onto the midden heap.
Surely Maie will take the land
Anne to the oven and the barn,
Kai will carry to the chamber,
If Mai does not take the land,
Anne will not take to the oven or barn,
Kai will not carry to the chamber:
Surely Matar will take the land,
Kansik will carry to the chamber.
I do not look at the calf sheds,
Stopping at the pigsties
There I curse the farmhand,
Scolding the courier.

label: marriage
translation:
Village maids, language maids,  
Parish maids, liars:  
They said under the apron is better,  
More honest under the hem.  
I was eager to believe,  
Foolish to take advice,  
Immediately I jumped to test it!  
Let them take the apron’s hem,  
Under the hem of the hem, -  
You can suffer a lot on the apron,  
You can be sick under the hem! -

label: marriage
translation:
Called to be a son-in-law,  
A family daughter’s husband,  
Chosen as the owner of a silver ring,  
Listener to a golden necklace,  
Observer of a copper necklace,  
Time came, the day rolled by,  
The night was spent asleep,  
Two nights were yoked together.  
The father-in-law began to bark,  
The mother-in-law began to bark!  
"What did you have when you came to the fire?  
You didn’t have fire when you came,  
The iron of the sled behind you,  
The little whip of reed,  
The pike tail of the sled."  
I heard, answered back:  
"What did you have to show off with,  
By the name of the maiden;  
"One was a glove in the coffin,  
That too was foolish without fingers,  
Blind without a groom.  
"The father got one sock,  
"The best man got half a ribbon,
