"The bride’s rider got a glove finger—  
That was your boasting,  
By the name of the maiden." -

label: marriage
translation:
What use is a tall man,  
Too proud of his height:  
The proud one wants to go to the tavern,  
Politely count money,  
Sits at the edge of the tavern table,  
Beer mug on his knee,  
Another tankard in hand,  
Money on the tavern table;  
Comes home in the evening  
In a drunken stupor,  
Comes inside, takes off his shoes,  
Throws the shoes askew,  
Socks near the big door,  
He himself looking sideways  
Whether the woman will take young men  
Or gather the household’s work.  
If the woman does not take young men,  
Nor gather the household’s work,  
He takes a whip off the bench,  
From the ruffian’s pocket too,  
Drags the woman’s skin along,  
Hits the little one hard;  
The woman jumps into the room,  
Across the yard to the storehouse,  
Starts swearing loudly,  
Cursing the scoundrels,  
Where are my beautiful ribbons?  
Or my proper ties?  
Where is my beautiful quilt?  
My aching beautiful carpet?  
Could have made the home shabby,  
Helped father to gray it,  
Made mushrooms grow on the wall edge  
Before wasting on the bad one,  
Murmuring to the cruel one,  
Whispering to the evil one,  
Wandering steamily around.

label: marriage
translation:
Called a servant  
To help the father- and mother-in-law  
To endure the blows from the father- and mother-in-law,  
To be the feeder of the father- and mother-in-law.  
I do not want this  
To become a servant.  
This is fastened tightly  
To the sled of a bright horse.  
Not suitable to be a servant.  
Let me buy a new horse  
A bright-horse sled.  
I will nail silver shoes underneath  
I will cover it with a red blanket  
More dear, woven by a weaver.  
I will put ruble pieces on the runners.  
Then I will go to find my own  
To feel my dear one  
To claim my girl.  
Then the room will be free of wind  
The house will be on a good site  
I will find the house in the forest  
I will find the cottage in the woods.  
I went inside to look  
In front were polished walls  
At the back were hewn boards  
Three were gold on the table  
One was the groom, the other the girl  
The third the handsome master's wife  
The fourth the dear companion wife.  
Wait, master's wife  
Be patient, companion wife  
Hold on, young man  
Let me teach the sister  
Admonish the young maiden  
If you found a place for bread  
And you got a place for rolls  
You knew a place for sprouting grain.  
Listen then, dear maiden, to the talks  
Of the young man's teasing  
The man is angry, you be sad  
Soften your heart  
Walk with a wise mind  
Then you will be praised well.  
A good girl has learned well  
A wise girl has been taught to dance  
Has brought the best to her husband.

label: marriage
translation:
Little sister, darling  
I have a groom, you have a groom  
My groom is a piper  
Dear kannel player  
Takes my piper to sleep  
Takes the kannel player to the chamber  
Helps my piper up  
From the kannel player's chamber  
Your groom is a whip maker  
Dear whip wielder  
Takes your whip to sleep  
Takes the whip to the chamber  
Drives the whip up  
From the whip wielder’s chamber  
Get up, heifer, milk the cow  
Old heifer, feed the calf

label: marriage
translation:
Oh, my dear honey man  
Made from fish bones  
From the other side of the partridge bones  
Does not take away the wool nail  
Does not carry the thistle nail  
Jumps on the hop nail  
Does not beat with one stroke  
Scolds with two strokes  
Let me make six strokes crisp  
A chick eats eight  
Then makes a little whip from thread  
A little stem from oat straw  
Then starts beating the crisp  
Punishing the chick.

label: marriage
translation:
Wait, wait, my dear ones  
Be patient, dear clans  
Let autumn come  
Step, lovely little time  
I will lay down a big feather  
I will kill the winter bull  
Valleys flowing with beer  
Mountains playing hide and seek  
When I go to meet my own  
And I reach the sister hill  
I bake moon cakes  
Day-child’s loaves  
I wash the season’s year  
I found my father on the meadow  
My brother on the meadow’s edge  
There my horse neighs  
Father’s harm is a pike (uncertainty in metaphor)  
Opposite me came a dear brother  
Opposite bloom sisters  
In the dark my brother’s servants  
Many my brother’s paid ones.  
One there quarreled on the heart’s bridge  
Another fought, knocked on the bridge  
A third tapped on the shoulder  
The fourth held the reins of oxen  
I came to the Viru brothers  
To the sister hill in Saaremaa  
Mother went quickly to cook food  
Father went quickly to kill the bull  
Sister went quickly to knead sourdough  
Brother went to bring fresh spirits  
Mother dear, darling  
Do not go quickly to cook food  
Do not go quickly to kill the bull  
I am not coming because of food  
I am not coming because of drink  
I came to see my own  
To visit my dear ones  
I came to the Viru brothers  
To the sister hill in Saaremaa.

label: marriage
translation:
Neither fieldwork tires me
Nor outdoor work exhausts me
Nor the pain in my thigh.
Break me with a well-digger’s hoe
Tire me with empty talks
Trouble me with false tongues.
Stories ran, I did not run
Speeches happened, I did not go
Stories flowed without drinking
Speeches without ever entering the tavern
Because I happened upon a drinking companion
Right away a tavern-goer
The drinker has no money
The tavern-goer has a few coins.

label: marriage
translation:
Brother, little brother  
I am going to Narva to bring a wife  
From across the other side of Petersburg  
Do not go dressed as a man  
With an old ploughman's hat  
Skip down to the cellar  
Step down to the barns  
Take new clothes from the barn  
White shirts from the clothes rod  
Then go to Narva to bring a wife  
From across the other side of Petersburg  
Go through Lihula  
The little tin bell is ticking  
The iron cart is rattling  
The fire sings a tune below  
On the other side of the black grouse's perch  
A cuckoo behind in the sleigh basket  
A bunch of girls came in front of the carriage  
The maiden, however, behind the sleigh  
Whose handsome boy is that  
Whose sweet lad  
Whose fire sings a tune below  
On the other side of the black grouse's perch  
A cuckoo behind in the sleigh basket.

label: marriage
translation:
Yesterday the weddings began  
And today the lunch ended.  
My wife very ill  
Very ill in bed  
Old women at the bedside  
I stand and watch  
God knows what to do about it  
War is sad and the mood is bleak  
Old grandmothers argue  
Go outside, young man  
Go outside, kill time  
Sharpening the stick shed  
Breaking the branch shed.  
I went outside, killing time  
I did not sharpen the stick shed  
Nor break the branch shed  
I came back inside  
Found a moth under the apron  
A little under the rag  
A lump under the six edges  
I was very startled  
It is not my fault  
It is the blacksmith apprentice’s fault  
The labor of the tailor boys  
I begin to bark at the woman  
To corner the young woman  
You could have made noise in the forest  
You could have shouted in the grove  
Could have flown in the poplar grove  
That came into our chamber  
Old grandmothers quiet down  
Be quiet, young men  
You are growing up to be herdsmen  
Growing up to be feeder men  
Adding up to broth makers

label: marriage
translation:
Last year I took my young wife  
The year before last, the other half  
I took her to a tender hayfield  
Down to the village meadow  
She mowed hay, jingled in the forest  
Took a breath, caught in the forest  
The willow branch cracked  
Mowed a meadow, mowed two  
Started the third mowing place  
She immediately began to wilt  
Her eyes began to wither  
Started to ache in the knees  
To lie down like a sick sow  
Lost her shoelaces  
Complained about her heels  
I went to the old woman's prayer  
Oh, my dear old woman  
The wife became sweetly ill  
Started aching in the knees  
To lie down like a sick sow  
Lost her shoelaces  
So look after, young lad  
Take the barley to the threshing floor  
Carry the oats to the barn  
The rye to the flax field  
Then we will slaughter the lambs  
Then we will fry the ducklings  
We will put the firewood by the stove  
Strike the blows on the thigh  
Between the white horns.

label: marriage
translation:
Oh, God, beyond strength,  
Beyond the hill’s summit,  
Who left me sleeping,  
Lulled me in your lap.  
When strength was pursued,  
Man’s seed was mixed,  
Boy’s luck was burned out,  
Others got mules, all got horses,  
The others became strong men.  
I got black and foolish,  
A tar stump and a sickly one.  
Where must I go with the black one,  
Rush with the foolish one,  
Face the sickly one?  
Others do a piece of work,  
A piece of work, on dark soil,  
Weaving coarse fabric,  
I must cultivate grayness,  
Nurture without bathing,  
I hammer on muddy water,  
Wash in muddy puddles,  
Carry the plows without rest,  
Old bones from the ancestral land.  
The plow is before me,  
A man is behind it,  
The broom doesn’t end at the corner,  
The bar of soap doesn’t sit on the wall,  
The white towel on the rod.  
Come now, boo, to the chamber,  
Step up, stench, to your place,  
Secretly come to the bed,  
To the jointless ears,  
Whether from earth or man wooed,  
I will not call you as a companion,  
Nor consider you a dog,  
Yet I will still be a father.

label: marriage
translation:
If I had known, could have known  
If I had seen even in a dream  
Brought to me while dozing  
I would think of heating the stove  
That I got an evil companion  
An evil companion, a loud man  
Of a cheerful other half  
Of a gloomy young man  
If the six-stringed were struck together  
The edges of the carpet in the middle  
Thin slices of bread   
Before wasting on the wicked  
On the cruel to scold  
An angry man wastes six  
A strong man ages his wife  
A bitter man spoils the other half  
Of a worried young woman.

label: marriage
translation:
You gave me, grandmother  
You gave me a shoemaker's place  
You found me a bread place  
You knew a plowing place  
You gave me, grandmother  
You gave me a sandy place  
You knew a thorn place  
Do not let my fingers die  
Do not let my nails wear out  
When searching for thorns  
When picking crowberries  
Thorns are slave berries  
Crowberries are heath berries.

label: marriage
translation:
An old woman’s skin journey:  
She offers a piece to her daughter,  
Offers a little straw to sleep on;  
Where should I put the straw,  
Where to sit the dear one?  
The straw takes up much space.  
Let me call out again,  
Let me sing back again:  
Dear one, little brother,  
You cannot marry from this land,  
Nor visit maidens from there.  
You go to marry a thief  
From the church to snatch,  
From the chapel to dig,  
From the grave to raise up.  
You bring to the house the schools,  
Bring inside the grumbling,  
Give to the stove the smoking,  
Show the leash to the spinning wheel.  
Father-in-law starts to say,  
Mother-in-law starts to say:  
"Our boys, little boys,  
Bring the ladder to the room,  
Pull near the stove,  
Bring the tobacco bag from outside,  
Steam bag from atop the stove;  
Bring from outside the grumbling,  
From atop the stove the smoking,  
From the spinning wheel the showing of the leash,  
From the bench the cracking of teeth."

label: marriage
translation:
They were called and listened to,  
Searched for and waited.  
Called to be home guards,  
A family daughter as a wife,  
Promised to give a horse  
To the iron plow handle.  
Silver sleigh harnesses,  
The cuckoo crows at the watermill,  
The grey bird at the trading place,  
The swallow at the headgear,  
The white bird at the harness,  
The iron rack at the stocks.  
I want Anne, I don't want Kaie,  
Anne has few teeth,  
Kaie has broken limbs,  
I want maidens from the farm.

label: marriage
translation:
Other men go to the sea,  
Other women go fishing,  
My man dozes at home,  
Sits under the stove,  
With a pipe in his mouth,  
A poker in his hand,  
But reads bread crumbs,  
Thinks about soot in the oven.  
I send my man to the sea,  
I send my wife to fish.  
The man comes home lying:  
Says the fish were caught earlier,  
The pikes have been driven to the end.  
Oh, poor little wife of mine,  
What am I to do?  
I will start heating the oven,  
I will drive my man away.  
The man, upon my prayer,  
I will add steam,  
Close the sauna door,  
So it finally comes to an end.  
Oh, poor little wife of mine,  
Then I dress for bed:  
In the middle, a patchwork quilt,  
On top, a big quilt.  
What was I supposed to do then?  
The man was a drunk:  
He drank bulls and horses dry,  
He drank sheep even from the barn,  
He drank cows dry without milking.  
So I got rid of my drunken man,  
A drunkard and a rake—  
Then I went to the sea myself,  
I went fishing myself,  
To see if fish were caught earlier.  
I went, a little one,  
Along the road, tiny,  
Along the land, small,  
But the road did not tire me,  
I went boldly to find my fortune.

label: marriage
translation:
O little god of God  
Why did you let me sleep  
When it was time for men to get together  
Everyone got girls, everyone got kisses  
I got black and foolish  
A burnt stump and a sickly one  
A birch stump, a miserable one  
A spruce stump, ugly  
Others had beautiful and nicer ones  
I had cold and rough  
They rode in pairs to church  
I was hunched over my man  
The field was outside on the edge  
The man was inside, on the back edge  
The handkerchief stood on the corner  
The soap bar was on the wall  
The white narcissus was on the rod  
Then I took between the white ones  
Among the nicer ones' middles  
Still it was black as a mole  
Still it was gray as a rat.

label: marriage
translation:
Last year I took a young wife  
The year before, another half  
I took a whole and sound one  
I took a plump and red one  
Very pale and fragile  
I took her to the gentle meadow  
To the golden hay arcs  
She mowed the beautiful hay  
Made a lovely arc  
Did not let the ribbon flutter  
Nor the dewy grass grow  
She began to suffer from her knees  
Her soles became weak  
Her apron strings stretched  
She became sick from under the belt  
I, the man, sought advice  
At the village women’s plea  
The women understood and replied:  
Oh, you foolish young man  
You didn’t want to be without nights  
Could not endure two moons  
Pinched weeks  
Now go quickly home  
Then put your little chickens to bed  
Let the barley lie straight  
Then you’ll have a healthy wife  
Healthy and light  
Like other women.

label: marriage
translation:
Little sister, dear one,  
You got a passionate husband,  
A loving spouse,  
Who leads you to bed with skirts,  
And a grain sack to the chamber.  
He rises in the morning:  
"Rise, bird, milk the cow,  
Herd dear, send the herd;  
The other herd is far away,  
Our herd is in the yard."  

Little sister, dear one,  
You got a man, an angry man,  
Who leads you to bed with a whip,  
And a rod to the chamber.  
He rises in the morning:  
"Rise, servant, milk the cow,  
Herd mare, send the herd;  
The other herd is far away,  
Our herd is in the yard."

label: marriage
translation:
Do you know what a family salary is?  
You have a lock in the room,  
You have water in the well without a key,  
The door to the pigs' pen is open,  
The butter churn has a key in front,  
The cream jar has three locks,  
The old bottle has a lid in front.  
But be diligent in the morning,  
Go through the cowsheds,  
Cowsheds, sheep sheds,  
You will find a calf with the cow,  
A lamb in the sheepfold.  
Then go inside to tell  
By the midwife’s bed,  
To cheer up the midwife.  
If the child is in your arms,  
The child is lying in your lap,  
Go on by, do your work,  
Put the child to swing,  
The child is on the stove,  
Or take a buttered bread in your hand,  
Then you will be called bad,  
Called the old woman’s daughter,  
Called an old man’s child.

label: marriage
translation:
Oh God, dear God!
Why did you let me sleep,
When everyone else had their time on earth.
Everyone got the good stuff, others got the leftovers,
I got the black and the foolish,
The tar stump and the sickly,
The wounded and the sparse,
Where there was a hole, I filled it,
Where there was a puddle, I washed it.
Ruu-roa and rallal-la.

label: marriage
translation:
Oh God, master of the afterlife,  
remember the master of the afterlife,  
why did you leave me to sleep –  
where the share was divided,  
where the seed of maidens was mixed  
and the happiness of women given.  
Others get young women,  
I got a black and foolish one,  
a tar stump and a sick one.  
Where must I go with the black one,  
face the sick one,  
hurry with the foolish one.

label: marriage
translation:
Oh, my former life  
Dear furry knee-cover!  
When I was at the old woman's place,  
At the old woman’s, at the old man’s.  
I was the old woman’s little mouse,  
The two-legged little cat.  
I took some butter without lessening,  
I touched the cake without diminishing.  
The old woman never managed to hit me,  
Nor did the old man manage to hit me,  
To rattle the five brothers,  
The nettle was the brother’s rattle,  
The straw was the sister’s rod,  
The old man’s rod was a clump of moss.  
I ate without care, drank without care,  
Slept without care,  
Put care upon the ridgepole,  
Worry upon the black beard.

label: marriage
translation:
Oh my gentle granny,  
Little honey berry granny!  
You nursed, you pampered,  
You raised, you hugged.  
You took me in your lap, gave me food,  
Called me to the root, gave me drink.  
Put me down, played with me.  
You thought you would become a German woman,  
The wife of a lord from Hiiumaa,  
The wife of the king of Courland. -  
Time passed by.  
You did not become a German woman.  
The lady of a Hiiumaa boy.  
In the end, you became a pauper's wife,  
A lifter of the pauper's sack,  
A mender of old shirts.

label: marriage
translation:
Oh my honey man,  
Hug along, dear comrade,  
In the capercaillie’s feathers from the other side.  
He ate a spoonful at noon.  
He hadn’t coughed a third time.  
He hadn’t nibbled a fourth time.  
He gathered five or six spoonsful,  
Lost seven or eight,  
Then made a little whip from a thread,  
A proper handle from a straw.  
Then struck the whip down,  
Along both forearms.  
Despite me, I screamed,  
Out of anger, I whimpered.  
Immediately he began to test me;  
Looked under my forearm:  
Are there whip strikes on the palm?  
Whip strikes on the top of the neck?  
No red marks on the whip,  
No blue marks on the back.  
Oh my honey man,  
Hug along, dear comrade.  
That helped to accomplish the task,  
To move the household’s laundry,  
To disturb the pig from eating.

label: marriage
translation:
Last year I took a young wife  
The year before, a partner  
I brought her to the tender hayfield  
To join that precious golden arch  
She mowed the beautiful hay  
Shaped a lovely arch  
The grass bent beneath her skirt  
Bluebells on her back  
Dewy grasses for the path  
But the woman began to moan  
Moan and groan  
She threw her apron into the bush  
Pearls into the hay arch  
I went home crying  
Put on the black coat  
Between the gray old men  
I went to seek help for my wife  
An old woman came to meet me  
The old woman asked me  
Why do you cry, young man?  
Why do I cry, old woman?  
But the old woman understood and replied  
Go home, young man  
Take the oats to the ditch  
Two handfuls into the wind  
Then prepare your wife without oil  
Then the woman will be healed  
Healed and light  
Like other women  
I went home crying  
But the woman sat on the toilet  
Sought support from the chair  
Help from the stove  
Come Jesus, come Jesus  
And Jesus came into the room  
Two hands, two feet  
Twenty fingers and nails.

label: marriage
translation:
Is this the man meant for me  
Is this the husband for the household  
He comes home drunk,  
The whole room is filled with sorrow  
The house full of angry quarrels  
He throws stockings into the manure  
Shoes in the middle of the floor  
If you don’t take the berries from the field  
You won’t get a gift from the stove.  
He brought in the devil  
A rowan branch under the bench  
A birch twig under the sleigh  
He started hitting along the waist  
Along the waist and shoulders  
Along the shoulder blades,  
Then the calf felt the devil  
The poor maple felt it on its back  
The waist, however, felt the fine willow  
I surely know, dear woman  
I surely feel the waistband of the underwear  
The taste of frying pans still good  
Even though the oven isn’t lit yet.  
The loom hasn’t been tried yet  
The fist quickly came  
The fierce one clenched his hand.  
The bread peel flew.

label: marriage
translation:
The birds sang with a kind tongue  
with a kind tongue and joyful spirit.  
The flowers are blooming wide open  
The blossoms lift sweetly into the air  
I went to tease the woman  
to love the spouse  
The woman did not want to joke  
the spouse did not want to love  
I went to settle in the forest  
to walk into the birch grove  
to step into the meadow  
to march to the berry land  
to look for love herb  
to gather comfort herb  
From the forest, I found the leaf herb  
From the birch grove, I got the comfort herb  
From the meadow, I got the love herb  
From the berry land, the sweet herb  
I gave the woman to sniff  
The spouse to smell  
The woman began to joke  
The spouse began to love me.

label: marriage
translation:
I surely know those slave songs,  
Slave songs, ox songs,  
How a slave should be,  
How a young slave should be,  
A slave must be diligent.  
At the door, one must sleep,  
In the room, one must rest the head,  
Send sleep to the stable,  
Sweep the twisting hall,  
Rake the bad dining table,  
Handle the stingy firewood,  
The most miserable corners.  
A fool does not understand thanks,  
I cried in the corner,  
Secretly I cried in the sauna.  
Over the yard to the granary,  
Even more to the cellar,  
Into the chamber with two doors.  
Oh, my former life,  
Dear foster home.  
In the evening I ate an apple soup,  
At night I ate milk soup,  
At dawn I ate cream cakes.  
In the evening I eat straw soup,  
At dusk water grass,  
At dawn I eat dog food.  
I take flower stalks from the breast,  
From the bluebell alder grove,  
Water to splash in the vessel,  
Still, the red stalks,  
Water to sprinkle power,  
Bluebell’s lushness,  
More famous than dog food.  
It is good to praise a good woman,  
Good is a good companion,  
When one comes home from the tavern,  
Beautifully lifting the door handle,  
From the serious carpet’s edge,  
Gently lifting the edge of the blanket,  
I stubbornly fish for kicks,  
She quietly keeps quiet.  
“Oh, my dear old woman,  
Honeyberry grandma,  
Bring water with a bucket,  
We will take the twigs to whisks,  
To weave the winnowing screen.  
The old woman is frightened,  
But be silent, young son.  
Throw the linseed into the waters,  
Barley straight into the rivers,  
Two oats into the gray field,  
Then the wife will become healthy,  
Healthy while raw,  
Red and plump.”

label: marriage
translation:
So far, I have toiled at pleated shirts  
Two or three wrinkled ones  
Four or five crumpled ones  
When my old lady had her turn.  
When misfortune befell the old lady  
Then I crawled into the sack  
Felled a young tree  
I carry a nail in the pocket  
Another nail in the sheath  
The third in a small pouch.

label: marriage
translation:
It was said at night  
thought and pondered  
some kind of thought arose  
thinking of those left without a husband  
without a partner, struggling,  
I got a husband from among men  
from beyond the boys  
I got a husband mindful  
caring from afar  
a dear companion beloved  
comes like a wren to the barn,  
creeps like a bird into the nest  
lets go like a gull into the bed,  
calls the morning awake  
rise bird to milk the cow  
rise dear to take the herd  
but I understand again, I answer  
I must have a birch to milk the cow  
I must have an aspen to take the herd  
a maple tree waters the calf  
I must have a spruce to strain the milk,  
good folk, good folk sister  
good folk to praise, good to talk.

label: marriage
translation:
When will I rock for the sisters,  
When will I roll for the brothers.  
Not born to go in autumn,  
Not fit to go in spring:  
Rivers are deep in autumn,  
Waves are broad in spring;  
My horse drowns in the brook,  
My stallion in the waves,  
My colt in the high grasses,  
My foal between the tussocks.

label: marriage
translation:
What was under the slave's care  
The domesticated animal had shelter  
The cattle had a place to go  
The fire was without a latch  
The well was uncovered on the hill  
The stable was without a key  
That was under the slave's care  
The domesticated animal had shelter

label: marriage
translation:
Why do you bluster, little wind  
Bang, bad weather  
Today my man is at sea  
Today my companion is fishing  
My boy is on the sail  
Blustering tomorrow, little wind  
Bang, bad weather  
Tomorrow a stranger man at sea  
A stranger companion fishing  
A stranger boy on the sail  
Tomorrow breakers at sea  
Fish slayers fishing

label: marriage
translation:
Last year I took a young wife,  
The year before the other half,  
I took her to a tender meadow,  
She mowed the hay, the forest snapped,  
The willow bushes crackled.  
Her knees began to ache,  
Her calves to ache as well,  
Her apron strings started to swell,  
The man hurried home,  
Over the fence to the mother-in-law’s,  
- Listen, mother-in-law, dear mother-in-law,  
Understand what is wrong with my wife,  
Her knees began to ache,  
Her calves to ache as well,  
Her apron strings started to swell,  
- Oh you crazy young men,  
Oh you young and foolish.  
You should remember last year,  
Recall the year before last,  
What you did under the blanket,  
Quietly under the carpet,  
You haven't gone a night without it,  
You have it six times once,  
Four times a week,  
Five times at dusk,  
Six times before dawn.

label: marriage
translation:
Oh God, dear little god,  
Why did you let me sleep,  
When it was time for hay harvest,  
Everyone became beautiful and smart,  
I became black and stupid,  
I scrubbed my husband,  
The field was in front of the house,  
The man was inside the barn,  
The soap was on the wall,  
The white scarf was on the willows,  
I scrubbed and scrubbed,  
Still was black as a mole,  
Still was gray as a rat.

label: marriage
translation:
Last year I took a young woman,  
The year before last, to the other side.  
I brought her to a tender hayfield,  
I placed a golden arch over it...

label: marriage
translation:
Tiidut, tiidut, the daughter is crying,  
The daughter does not cry for nothing,  
The daughter has troubles coming,  
And the logs are being measured,  
The fire does not go out from the rooms,  
No spark from the bedpost,  
No woman from young clothes,  
No gray from the dun horse's mane.

label: marriage
translation:
I went to the forest to walk  
and to look for a bird's nest.  
And while looking for the bird's nest  
I found a boy under a thicket.  
His underside was covered in mud  
and his upper side was tanned.  
Then I took the boy on my shoulder  
and took him to the Paide river;  
there I washed him with a brush  
and with soap from the Seven Societies.  
Then I took him on my shoulder again  
and took him to the Vändra fair.  
Then I traded him for a colt  
and a stallion with two ears.

label: marriage
translation:
Last year I took a young woman  
The year before last, another half,  
I took her to the other side of the river,  
I carried the dear one.  
Mowed a bow, mowed two,  
Started limping on the knees,  
Bled from the shoelace,  
Tied from the shoelace of a pig’s ear.  
The fire did not end here,  
A spark in the bedpost.  
I gave the woman an incantation,  
To the young one to make her cry...  
If there is no dung in the yard,  
Take fodder from the forest,  
If there is no fodder in the forest,  
Take the bran from the threshing floor,  
If there is no bran on the threshing floor,  
Bring an apple from the house,  
Light its tail on fire.

label: marriage
translation:
You know what the prime minister says:
You have a locked room,
your water is in a well without a key,
the pigsty door is open,
you have the butter churn key with you,
the cream container has three locks,
the old container has a lid in front.
But be diligent with your work,
go through the cowsheds,
the cowsheds, the sheep sheds.
You will find a calf with the cow,
a lamb in the pen,
then go inside and tell grandma,
by the edge of grandma’s bed,
but cheer up grandma’s spirit.
If a child goes into the spider,
the child will come as a destroyer.
You go along, do your work,
push the spider to swing,
the child goes on top of the oven,
butter and bread are to be secured,
then you will be called,
the good old lady's daughter,
the good old man's daughter.

label: marriage
translation:
Last year I took a young wife,  
the year before last, to the other side,  
I took her to Einamaa.  
Einamaa reaped, grazed the forest,  
took the meadow, the grove rustled,  
then began to limp on the knee,  
to sleep in stocking feet,  
to swell from the apron straps.

label: marriage
translation:
Oh God, dear God,  
Why did you let me sleep,  
When it was time for manhood,  
Everyone got prizes, some got treats,  
I got black and foolish,  
A pitch pine and sickly,  
A willow stump and pitiful,  
Everyone else went properly to church,  
But I am stooping with my man,  
The plow was in the front on the ridge,  
The man was behind with the pack,  
The pipe was standing in the corner,  
The soapdish was on the wall,  
A white cloth hung on the rod.  
Still I was black as a mole,  
Still I was gray as a rat.

label: marriage
translation:
What do I fear here while singing
Declaring my voice
I have no fear of the bride
Nor am I afraid of the groom
Nor ashamed of father- or mother-in-law.
My bride from afar
Wears twisted socks to Viljandi
She drinks from the lake's pitcher
Before the lake's mouse-gray
Behind the lake's golden ears
Sometimes blood-red.
But I went to woo a young woman
I took a wife for fun
Across for another's sake
Others got fools and all got rogues
I got the black and the foolish
From Tõrva's corner, sickly
With a squinting eye and angry
Where I had to go with the black one
Confront the sick one
Hurry with the foolish one.

label: marriage
translation:
Last year I took a young wife  
The year before last, across the river  
I took her to a tender hayfield  
Turned her onto a golden arc  
She mowed beautiful hay  
Did it for the joy of the song.  
She made a pretty arc.  
Then she started moaning  
Moaning and wailing  
And digging into her trouble  
From her shoelace to wither  
From her ankle to sleep  
From her stocking band to die.  
From her apron string to swell.  
Neither the doctors of Harju  
Haunted doctors, nor wise women helped there.  
But the porridge pitchers helped there  
Porridge pitchers with cake bags  
Watching over an old woman  
A daughter is needed for the farm  
A child is needed for the plough  
One for the guardian of another  
A third is needed for the herdsman.

label: marriage
translation:
Last year I took a young wife,  
The year before the other half.  
I took her down to the meadow,  
Put a gold ring on her finger.  
She mowed beautiful hay for me,  
Mowed the lovely arch as well.  
Then my knee began to ache,  
My ankle to ache too.  
I went to see the doctor.  
No help from Pärnu doctors,  
Pärnu doctors, Paide doctors.  
Trouble went into the ground,  
Mercy went into the grave,  
The smoker died,  
The cuddler disappeared.  
One cannot die at death’s ear,  
Go to the grave at mercy’s ear.

label: marriage
translation:
When will I go to my father,  
When will I go to my mother,  
When will I roll to my brothers,  
When will I walk to my sisters?  
Autumn is not yet born to go,  
Spring does not yet go to the field.  
The autumn streams are deep,  
Spring has wide waves.  
The apple sinks into my stream  
To the waves of the field’s shore,  
Into the gravel of the timothy grass  
Among the mossy clumps.

label: marriage
translation:
Oh god behind the power!
Why did you let me fall asleep,
when those girls were watched?
Everyone got high,
others got stumps,
I got black and stupid.

label: marriage
translation:
Last year I took a young wife,  
the year before took another half.  
I led her to a tender hayfield,  
placed gold over the arch,  
She mowed beautiful hay for me,  
mowed the lovely arch as well,  
She took to resting as if she were suffocating.  
She began to ache in the knees,  
fell asleep on the shin,  
complained about the heel.  
I tried to treat her,  
tried giving doctoring,  
But no Pärnu doctors helped me,  
Pärnu doctors, Paide healers,  
the worry bearer went to the ground,  
the giver of grace went to the grave,  
the one who soothed died away,  
the one who embraced disappeared.  
One cannot die by the ear of the dead,  
nor go to the grave by the ear of grace.

label: marriage
translation:
Tiidut-tiidut I found a coin,  
found a coin, put it in my pocket,  
with the coin I bought a horse,  
with the horse I harvested oats,  
with the oats I took a wife,  
with the wife I kept a family.

label: marriage
translation:
Last year I took a young wife,  
the year before last, another half,  
I brought her to a tender hayfield,  
placed a golden arch above her.  
She mowed the low meadow,  
cut the smooth stalks.  
She remained limping on her knees,  
fell asleep with aching calves,  
started limping with her shoelace,  
and limped barefoot.

label: marriage
translation:
If I were a man of age,
I would buy an apron with pockets,
A shawl with rye ears;
Because the wicked little wolf -
When he rode to courtship,
He promised to bring a silk hat,
A silk hat, a calico apron,
A dear calico apron;
It came to be, it came to live -
Now the fist is checkered,
The palm is grim,
On the back of the hand is cross-shaped.

label: marriage
translation:
Oh, God, dear God,
A little worry in my mind,
Why did you let me sleep
When it was harvest time.
Everyone went to church
I was scrubbing my man,
The field was in front with soil,
The man was inside with a sack.
The soap was on the wall
A white towel on the pole.
It was always as black as a mole
Always as gray as a rat.

label: marriage
translation:
I already knew what was coming to me!  
It lifts the coal sack,  
Lifts my kettle.  
If only I had known this before,  
Known it before, heard it long ago,  
I would have tied my hands to a stump,  
Rather than to this Jaan.  
Oh, my dear gray blanket,  
Thin foggy shawl!  
I could have kept silent,  
Lurked beneath the moon,  
Before I gave in to the fool.  
He got to sleep in the sheepfold;  
The sheepfold might have become tangled,  
The rider might have circled the shoulders.

label: marriage
translation:
Good was praised a good man.
Good was to live with the good.
He comes like a quiet guest,
Steps like a feather to the nest.
Gently he lifts the edge of the blanket,
Carefully the edge of the carpet:
Fearing to startle the dear one,
So as not to jump out of the bed:
Rise, dear, milk the cow,
Drive our herd afar.
Bad was praised a bad man,
Bad was to live with the bad.
He comes like the devil home,
Steps like a kick to the nest.
From bad he lifts the edge of the stove,
From noise he lifts the edge of the carpet,
Fiercely the edge of the blanket.
Rise, though, fool, milk the cow,
Other calves to the pasture,
Our calves to the mud.

label: marriage
translation:
Oh, my little blue coat,  
And my dear gray blanket,  
A thin layer of fog.  
You could have lain down  
To brood under the cover,  
Before you had to lie down in the sapard,  
You could roam on the rafter.  
In the sapard, you had to lie down quickly,  
On the rafter, you could roam around.

label: marriage
translation:
The old woman came out to the gate  
The old man came out to the street.  
I turn around, step inside.  
Then an old lady came out to meet me.  
She was tiny under the blanket,  
A little bit under the bed,  
A beautiful piece was under the rag,  
A little under the carpets.  
Oh, you foolish young men  
Throw the barley into the mud,  
The oats straight into the sea.  
That's how to treat a woman without oil.  
Then the woman will stay whole  
Like other women.

label: marriage
translation:
Others took black heads,  
The handsome took white heads.  
I was left with the black and the foolish,  
A tar stump and a sickly one.  
Where there is a stream, there I swim,  
I wash the patch of shavings,  
So that I might become as fair  
As once were others' heads.

label: marriage
translation:
When shall I borrow from my father,
When shall I go to my mother,
When shall I run to my sisters,
When shall I roll to my brothers.
Autumn is not for going out;
Autumn has deep rivers.
Spring is not for roaming;
Spring has wide waves.
The road is rocky.
Do not saddle the horse;
It wears out its hooves.
The horse drowns in the creek,
In the boat among the willow shrubs,
In the turf with stone fragments.

label: marriage
translation:
When will I go to my father,  
When will I go to my mother,  
When will I roll to my brothers.  
Autumn does not want to come,  
Spring does not want to go;  
Autumn’s rivers are deep,  
Spring’s waves were wide.  
I take hold and get angry.  
But I put on an apron as a sail,  
And a winnowing basket as a wise barrier,  
Then I go to my father,  
Then I go to my mother.  
Then I roll to my brothers.  
My sister-in-law had daughters under the yard,  
Brother’s daughters at the gate.  
Brother took a horse from the harness,  
Brother’s wife took off her gloves.  
Nadu gave a rocking chair.  
Then the brother began to talk,  
To speak with his wife:  
“Look for food for my sister.”  
The wife took some sips,  
Beloved Käli scolded:  
“What will I give my sister to eat?  
The water is cloudy and gone,  
The scales are cold in the cellar.”

label: marriage
translation:
Oh my honey woman  
Rise, dear, milk the cow  
Rise, darling, send the herd.  
Other bulls to the grass,  
Our bulls to the mud  
Other cows to the alder grove,  
Other herds far away,  
Our cows on the sand.

label: marriage
translation:
When do I sway to the sisters
When do I roll to the brothers.
I was late to go to father
I was late to go to mother.
At last I roll to the brothers,
And I sway to the sisters.
I was not born to go in autumn,
Spring was not suitable to walk;
The autumn rivers are deep,
The spring tides were wide.
My horse drowned in the ditch,
In the wide wave of the meadow,
In the broken stones of the boat,
In the gray turn of age,
In specks of stone.

label: marriage
translation:
I was once at grandmother's home,  
I grew up once at grandfather's home;  
I was like a thistle in bloom  
I grew like a hemp vine,  
Flax fiber, clover,  
Granny was gentle with me like a cat,  
Grandpa handled me with care.  
I don’t know how I walked,  
Head first, feet last.  
A stranger looks at a stranger  
Heart sideways into it.  
Started rattling at the door,  
Beating back to the wall,  
Click-clack on the latch  
There was surely banging on the floor.  
Everyone is angry at me  
The lower garden twigs,  
The upper linden barks.

label: marriage
translation:
I was always miserable,  
So many times my mood was sad.  
Because I was bad, because I was sad,  
Because it was a bad time,  
To the autumn frost,  
To the spring snow cover,  
It began to pour snow,  
To shake hail,  
But snow with a thick layer to the roof,  
Snowdrifts to the ridge roof.  
Autumn does not come to pass,  
Autumn rivers are deep...

label: marriage
translation:
I took the mistress from Võnnu,  
Then from Narva the young maiden.  
I led the tender haymaker,  
Carried the gold on her back.  
She began to swell at the knees,  
To limp on her feet,  
To sleep on her calf muscle.  
She did not mow the tender hay,  
Nor did she take the gold on her back.  
I feared the weeping of the young,  
The bow would be drawn,  
Suddenly there was trouble in the room,  
The bow aimed at the eye.  
It is not he who aims at the father-in-law’s eye,  
The father-in-law’s eye, the mother-in-law’s eye,  
The hunchback’s shepherd’s eye,  
The jesters’ eye,  
The five brothers’ maiden’s eye.

label: marriage
translation:
Last year I took a young woman,
The year before I took another.
I took her to the tender hayfield
And placed a golden arch above.
She mowed the beautiful hay,
She mowed the lovely arch;
She cut the creeping grass,
The dewy grass in the clearing,
The bluebells in the clearing.
She began to suffer from her knees,
Complaining of her heels.
I sought help.
The gray horses went to the doctor,
The linen carts to the town road.

label: marriage
translation:
Oh, my honey man,  
Little bird from the bone.  
Grant me the life of a lady.  
Lady, place me on your lap.  
May the life of the master be yours.  
I have no riffraff among me,  
No scoundrel in my hand.  
My lap is empty for a burden,  
My hands empty for walking.  
Dear sister, gentle one.  
Oh, you poor child captive,  
Child captive, broken bed:  
May your lap be full even for a burden,  
Your hands full for walking.

label: marriage
translation:
Now permission is granted to spy
It is nice to go to the sauna
Beautiful to shout with a turnip
Now the reins are held by the old woman
The bridle is in the brother’s sleeve
The reins are held by my own.
When the reins can be held by the fool
The bridle is held by the madman
The bridle is in the man's sleeve,
Then I ask permission from the cap
To the wise one from six
Whether the cap allows me to the village
Thanks to another household
An apron to another room
A clog to the building
The cap does not allow to the village
Thanks not to another household
An apron not to another room
A clog not to the building
I sneak away like a pig to sleep
Go like a lamb to bed
Pull my knees up to my chest
Elbows to my sides
Fists near the heart
Warmth flows from the knees to the belly
Warmth from the elbows to the sides
Warmth from the fists to the heart
I get up in the morning
Elbow water was under the side,
There was a knob of water on top
Jelly water under the heart
Rolling tear water
Eyebrows in a drop of water
When I grow up at home
I sat in father's room
I sat in mother's room
I looked into the brother's room
I grow like hemp in the ditch
I rise like a strawberry in the house
Long pipe in the corner of the room
Neither the old woman has beaten me enough
Nor the old man beaten me enough
To frolic with the mild brother
A straw was the old woman's rod
A cattail was the old man's rooster
A willow leaf was the brother's twig
I got to a bad man
To a wicked companion
Oh, my unruly hair
Or my honeycomb
Dear golden-haired one
I am beaten with a fist
My bottom is pinched
My palm is clipped.

label: marriage
translation:
I went to Narva to fetch my wife,  
The wife died on the road to Narva,  
I threw my apron into the ditch,  
The shawl into the cattails,  
Beads onto the hayrack,  
The braids onto the pile,  
Rings onto the thicket.

label: marriage
translation:
Last year I took my young wife

"What should I cry for, old woman:  
Last year I took a young wife,  
The year before that, from across the border.  
Her knees began to ache,  
Her shins grew swollen."  
The old woman’s reply could be heard:  
"No Harju doctors can help here,  
Harju doctors, Toompeh’s healers,  
Paide agreement-makers,  
Narva belly-lifters,  
You go, malt brewer,  
Barley crusher to the river.  
Two handfuls of oats afterwards,  
Then the woman will be healthy again."

label: marriage
translation:
Oh God, dear little God!  
You let me sleep for a long time.  
When this residue was left,  
When this seed was mixed.  
Mixed with men's seed,  
Ruined women's luck.  
Everyone else got something, everyone got high:  
I got black and foolish  
A tar stump and sickly.  
Where should I go with the black?  
Then I will start tending my beloved  
To grow chamber raspberries.  
The snuffbox stands on the corner  
A bar of soap on the wall,  
A white headscarf on the end of a rod.  
If I find the way, I will wave,  
If I find the puddle, I will wash,  
If I find the box, I will take again.

label: marriage
translation:
What drives a horse crazy?  
What drives a rifle mad,  
What makes a woman foul?  
A fool is a flirt,  
A home daughter a scamp,  
A family daughter a deceiver,  
A farm daughter a little brat.  

A madman throws a horse into a ditch,  
Chases a greyhound under the hill,  
Lets loose a fox in the forehead,  
Dashes a doe into a stone,  
On top of a tall cliff,  
Into a red tree root,  
Into black mud like a serpent.  

A madman with a rifle bangs:  
Shoots into the soles of the feet,  
Aims between the eyes.  

A naughty woman has no enjoyment:  
With whom can she show tender love,  
Who feeds the domestic bird.  

A slut is naked:  
No rags on her body,  
Nothing on her skin.  

A home daughter is a flirt:  
Does not spare her mouth afterward.  

A deceiver beats the family daughter,  
Hits hard without mercy.  

A bratty farm daughter:  
Swears with crazy words.

label: marriage
translation:
Oh my dear home of gold,  
Love my father’s hearth,  
Berry from grandmother’s land,  
Better place in the room.  
I did not see days of hunger,  
Did not hear harsh words,  
Malicious barking,  
Angry swearing.  
I went to a sensible man,  
A pitiful marriage,  
With an immature partner.  
A partner does not grow,  
A man is not willing to take.  
Now I see days of hunger,  
Now I hear harsh words,  
Father-in-law’s mother’s barking,  
Hiding angry swearing.  
Better to go to the servant’s village,  
Than to endure the master’s mockery,  
The servant goes plowing the field,  
The father-in-law’s son to help,  
The husband’s brother goes to the mill.  
The master snaps at the room,  
Seeks to fight with words,  
Seeks to quarrel with clothes,  
Trim-trim with nonsense.

label: marriage
translation:
A mute little bird  
My sweetheart’s fiddler  
Together the kannel player

To the kannel’s chamber  
Morning rises  
Takes the fiddle under the piano  
From the kannel’s chamber to the end of the yard  
Rise, flower-milking cow  
Rise, dear Anna, to give milk  
Rise, beautiful one, to drive the herd  
Other herds in the cattle yard  
Our herd in the distant field  
Other bulls in the mud  
Our bulls on the grass  
Other cows unmilked  
Our cows in the grove.

label: marriage
translation:
Family daughter, young maiden  
Farm daughter, little plant  
I ask for your hand in visit  
I do not seek advice from another woman  
I take your hands into mine  
Fingers from mittens  
Eyes from silk scarf  
Why do I knead father-in-law’s breads  
Why do I knead mother-in-law’s breads  
Rolling family cloths  
Making new white ones  
I throw old ones to the wool  
Foam jumped into the iron  
Clumps in the comb  
Tears to another family.

label: marriage
translation:
Oh my honey man,

Every Monday has gone fishing.  
Monday brings eels,  
Tuesday brings smelts,  
Wednesday nice fish,  
Thursday mother’s eels,  
Friday Riga roaches,  
Saturday broad burbots,  
Sunday pikeperch.  
Surely the fish will come home,  
Roes are falling by the bed,  
Trouts into the oven to fry,  
Pikes to the smokehouse to cure.

label: marriage
translation:
Prayer birds, sorrowful birds,  
Forest cranes, sad birds,  
Forest ducks, humble birds,  
Go through my homes,  
Pass through my homes,  
Bring word to my father,  
Bring word to my mother,  
Inform the old man:  
How boring life is for me,  
The place of the maiden.  
When I cry for my brother’s face,  
When I cry for my brother’s wreath,  
The whole year passes old position.  
Where I sit, the seat is wet,  
Where I stand, the walls are slippery,  
I desire, but my place is empty,  
I cannot find understanding in the night,  
Home daughters together.  
The home daughter paid with gold,  
In father’s house paid with berries,  
To the copper brother’s widow.  
He demanded, pay the water,  
That flows from under the nail to the nail bed,  
Between the toes.

label: marriage
translation:
I am a drunkard, an old man from Nurme  
A tavern-goer, a little boy  
I still drink at the tavern  
I sing songs on the tavern table  
Alone at night for two  
For four weeks  
For two to three months  
For five quarters  
I drank bulls out of the stable  
I drank stallions out of the harness room  
Cows from the milking place at home  
Still left to grumble  
Hooves left to rustle  
Scraps left to listen  
The nape left to laugh  
Talks remain to tell tales  
I still drink at the tavern  
I sing songs on the tavern table  
I don’t know where my sweetheart is  
Whether she is outside or in the yard  
A young maiden  
Go outside to check  
Look into the tavern yard  
Whether she is outside or in the yard  
Or has been locked in  
Or is in the grasp of the blizzard wind  
A wide stable for the pilot  
Hundreds of big walls  
The maiden understood and replied  
She is neither outside nor in the yard  
Nor is she in the grasp of the blizzard wind  
A wide stable for the pilot  
Hundreds of big walls  
She stands here by the wall  
Hiding among the crows  
A young maiden  
You bring a starry blanket  
Wipe my sweetheart’s dew  
Swish, spread the dust.

label: marriage
translation:
Last year I took a young wife  
The year before last to the other side  
I took her to the gentle hayfield  
And under that golden arch  
She mowed the beautiful hay  
Made a lovely arch  
The grass grew a creeping veil  
Bluebells a strand veil  
Dew grasses a side veil  
But the wife began to groan  
To cry out, to moan  
She threw her apron into the bushes  
Pearls into the hay arch  
I went home even crying  
Crying even out of fear  
I put her in a black coat  
Between gray shoulders  
I went to seek help for my wife  
An old woman came out  
Old woman, old man  
Why do you cry for your young husband  
Or what do you lament for the townsmen  
Why should I cry, little woman  
Or why should I lament, little old man  
Last year I took a young wife  
The year before last to the other side  
I took her to the gentle hayfield  
And under that golden arch  
She mowed the beautiful hay  
Made a lovely arch  
The grass grew a creeping veil  
Bluebells a strand veil  
Dew grasses a side veil  
But the wife began to groan  
To cry out, to moan  
She threw her apron into the bushes  
Pearls into the hay arch  
But the woman understood, the man replied  
Go home, young man  
Take the barley to the ditch  
The oats two by two to the haystack  
Then make the wife oil  
Then the wife will get well  
Quite well, even fully well  
Like other wives  
I went home even crying  
The wife sat by the stove  
Searched for support on the chair  
Ah, from the little oven help  
Come Jesus, come Jesus  
That Jesus had come into the room  
Twenty hands, twenty legs  
Twenty fingers, nails

label: marriage
translation:
I could have been a girl  
A girl, just a girl  
I could have worked as a girl  
Being a servant to my father  
Being a servant to my mother.  
I could have gone out for my brother  
I could have been in the manor for my sister  
If I ended up with a bad man  
A scoundrel of a corpse  
A horse changer  
A hat maker  
A dog collar cutter.

label: marriage
translation:
Village old women, little old women  
Village houses, little rooms  
Help to understand  
Give a little advice  
I took a young wife  
Yesterday the wedding started  
Today is the proper wedding day  
My wife is so sick  
God knows what will happen to her  
Old women by the bed  
But they send me outside  
I turn outside  
But then turn back inside  
A woman came to the door  
Tiny in an apron  
A little in a scarf  
A bit in a kerchief  
But the woman immediately understood and said  
Oh you foolish young man  
You have pinched the wife  
You have stroked under her stomach  
Throw the malt aside  
Barley straight into the river  
Oats after two  
Rye carry quickly to the mill  
Make the wife without oil  
Give the wife some sour whey to drink  
Then the wife will become healthy  
Healthy and strong  
Like other wives  
Oh, if I say it differently again  
I will turn the words upside down  
Other wives make a mess  
My Kärt's little stool  
She does not spoil clothes  
Nor waters the cupboard.

label: marriage
translation:
The woman said, "Take a wife."
The man said, "Be without one."
I took a young wife last year,
The year before last, across the way.
She was plump and red,
She was pale and painful,
She was healthy and sharp.
She began to suffer from her knees,
To die from her garter,
To wither from her shoelace.
I went searching for a doctor,
I rode to the five corners of Viru,
I rode to the twelve corners of Kuura,
I searched thoroughly through Luane.
An old woman came to meet me.
"Go home, young man!
Take some of this whiskey,
And some of this cheap beer!"
Then the woman became healthy,
Healthy and sharp,
Plump and red,
Pale and strong.
Then the old woman came back,
She had a small apron on,
A little rag on,
And a nicely fitted petticoat.

label: marriage
translation:
I went to Veigu’s brother  
And to Veigu’s sister-in-law too  
The indifferent brothers do not know me  
Nor the indifferent sisters-in-law.  
For an hour I stood unknown  
For another hour unrecognized  
I heard I stood by the hut sailing  
During the day a long towel was wiped  
Respect your shoulder  
There is no cloth tearing  
There are no bitter debaters  
By the wreath on the head of the wiper  
Comes my own Ella’s brother  
Comes the sister to talk  
To offer a seat  
For me to sit down  
Veigu’s sister-in-law  
Asks me riddlingly  
Where have you come from  
Have you come from Suaramaa  
Or from across the Russian border?  
Veigu’s sister-in-law  
Asks me puzzlingly  
What will I eat  
What will I drink  
The rat’s intestines without food  
The moor’s juice untaken  
The cat’s fur without scratching  
I will give yesterday’s eastern lient  
Today’s eastern lient  
Three-day-old female lient  
A week’s needle lient  
A bitter ink lient  
A mild broth lient.  
I hear, I answer again  
I understand the verse, I reply again.  
Veigu’s sister-in-law  
I did not come to eat  
I did not come to drink  
I came to talk to my brother  
To greet my sister-in-law.  
At home I ate to my heart’s content  
At home I drank to my fill  
At home I sipped the broth  
I left home with three dishes  
The oven had duckling broth left  
The firepit had bird broth left  
Behind the chamber was sheep broth left  
At home I ate to my heart’s content  
At home I drank to my fill  
Veigu’s sister-in-law  
Let the servant go home  
To the field under the sun  
Surely your inks will be tipped  
The broths will be tasted  
The meat broths tested  
The needle broths sniffed.

label: marriage
translation:
What is a tall man made of
From proud beans,
From white foam;
A man is loud with a white fist.
A head strong with a fist,
Quickly comes the fist's strength,
With harsh fists loud.
A man has a wise mind,
A flour sack whiter,
A grain barn clearer,
A wallet heavier;
It won't hit me to the bone
Nor hit me twice,
If I do the fire dance,
Burn a little fire.
Seven flax seeds to burn -
Then he makes a little whip from thread,
A little handle from straw -
Then he snaps at the woman,
Still he jumps to try
If there is a whip in his hand.
Because I praise my man
As a strong lifter,
A hard carrier of bags;
Look, how strong a lifter,
He lifts a nail like a stick,
Throws a nail like a woolen pin,
A nail on the shoulder like a lump. -
Because I praise my man
As a strong lifter,
A hard carrier of bags. -

label: marriage
translation:
My gender was unwanted,  
The sisters were jealous of the flowers;  
They left me to sleep,  
When there was a men's game with us,  
On the pine forest clearing was a groom’s flock,  
Then the boys got other drinks,  
Others got tough men—  
I got a fool and a fool,  
Pine stump and sickly;  
Where must I go with a black one  
To confront the sickly one,  
To rush with the fool,  
Where I hit water with a bottle,  
Where there is feed, there I diverge,  
Where there is a puddle I wash,  
The switch stands on the corner,  
A white scarf is on the stick,  
A piece of soap is on the wall—  
That’s why I wash the groom,  
Care about my beloved;  
I do not complain nor fear  
That I have become a slave to a servant,  
I have passed the dawn of a servant,  
Above was the luck of a slave,  
The poor child’s foal luck,  
The family son’s pipe luck,  
Pipe luck, whip luck—  
So I do not complain nor fear  
That I have become a slave to a servant.

label: marriage
translation:
Oh my former life  
Beautiful childhood  
When I was growing up at home  
I sat in father's yard  
I grew like hemp fibers  
I rolled like an egg in the grass  
Across the yard, little sister  
Across the fence, little fence  
I did not grow without fish  
Did not grow without pork  
I did get to eat in the kitchen  
Early to eat in the barn  
Secretly ate in the boots  
Even more in lifelessness  
Now is the time of bitter childhood  
Now I must cry in the corner  
Or cry in the barn  
Secretly I can cry  
In a double room  
Even more in lifelessness  
Where I stand, the walls are wet  
Where I cry, the corners are wet  
I do not sleep in the evening  
I rise in the morning  
The floor was covered with water  
An ell of water under the bed!

label: marriage
translation:
I was once my father-in-law’s daughter-in-law  
Father-in-law’s daughter-in-law, mother-in-law’s daughter-in-law  
When I managed to make the bed  
Made the bed, walked softly  
Always did chores  
Then I was left behind in my father-in-law’s mind  
Then I was left behind in my mother-in-law’s mind  
I became ugly in my brother-in-law’s mind  
I became cold in the servants’ mind  
I became a fool in my husband's relatives’ mind  
I started washing clothes  
The servants didn’t allow me to thresh  
Father-in-law didn’t want to help with the kitchen  
Relatives were full of criticism  
Mother-in-law didn’t want to speak with me

translation:
Corner woman, a little weak  
Looks for help from the stove  
Seeks support from the winding  
Cannot get help from the stove  
Seeks support from the winding  
Come inside, little Jesus  
Place your hand on her chest  
Then it will get a little better  
After an hour, stronger.

translation:
Last year I took a young wife  
The year before last on the other side  
I took her to the tender hayfield  
I placed gold upon her head  
He mowed the hay in the nook of the forest  
He took the glade in the trap of the forest

Her soft eyes to sleep  
Her shoelaces to untie  
Her apron strings to ache  
I asked the woman  
Last year I took a young wife  
The year before last on the other side

He took the glade in the trap of the forest  
Then her knees began to ail  
Her soft eyes to sleep  
Her shoelaces to untie  
Her apron strings to ache.  
The woman heard and answered back  
Young men, like her brothers  
Throw city boys into mud  
Barley was lying straight  
Oats into two middens  
Then make good beer  
Taste the sweet mead  
Make a fine brandy  
Knead bread to be tough  
Then the wife will be healthy  
Healthy and strong  
Then the time came for the child to roll  
Then the son came home  
Prepared for his time.

label: marriage
translation:
Village girls, tongue-tied,  
Parish girls, deceitful!  
They said the apron is better,  
More honest under the hem.  
I was diligent in believing,  
Foolish in taking advice!  
Let them take the hem under the apron,  
Under the hem of the apron.  
One can suffer a lot on the apron,  
Under the hem one can be sick!

label: marriage
translation:
Oh God, beyond power,
Great God, beyond the swamp!
Who left me sleeping:
When those women were given,
Necklaces were twisted.
Others got gems, all got heights,
I got black and foolish
A diseased tar stump,
A pea stump: just gray.
Where should I go with the black?
Face the sick?
Where there was water: there I splashed,
Where there was a puddle: there I flapped!
Where the moss was not wet,
No need to flap the puddle:
There I was born to give mouth
Immediately to change into a worm.

label: marriage
translation:
Hello, hello Tedre Rein!  
Did you see Kadaka Rein?  
Asking Rein from Rein:  
"Are you women healthy?"  
The women’s health is unknown,  
Some are healthy during the day, others are sick!  
Mother-in-law is healthy, mother-in-law is sick,  
The sugar mint is dying,  
In the support hut, there is a cold spell.

translation:
Three on the daughter's knee  
The first was Ella’s knee  
That was Ella grandmother’s knee  
The middle one was dear husband’s knee  
That was dear husband’s knee  
The last was the wretched knee  
That was evil husband’s knee  
Sudden father-in-law’s knee  
Sudden mother-in-law’s knee  
Künastu servant’s knee  
Nurjatu midwife’s knee  
The mad man’s knee  
When it was Ella grandmother’s knee  
Then you could run around in a shirt  
You could flutter in linen  
When it was dear husband’s knee  
The middle one was dear husband’s knee  
That was dear husband’s knee  
You could eat in the shed  
Secretly you could eat in the sauna  
Surely you could eat in the kitchen too  
In the double-layered blanket  
Even more in the living room  
Finally, that was evil husband’s knee  
Sudden father-in-law’s knee  
Sudden servant’s knee  
Nurjatu midwife’s knee  
The mad man’s knee  
You could cry in the shed  
You could cry in the sauna  
Surely you could cry in the kitchen too  
In the double-layered blanket  
Even more in the living room  
Everything comes upon  
The pig’s eye falls upon  
Father-in-law came upon, mother-in-law came upon  
Father-in-law came with a bull’s yoke  
Mother-in-law came with a cow-milker  
The midwife on the stove porch roof  
Her husband was a stone fist  
I got from the door to the yard  
Through the gate I got out  
Then I got more on the back  
I didn’t wait, I came out  
I went back quickly  
Then I go back inside  
I throw the chips on the bench  
Already the father-in-law spoke of goodness  
Already the mother-in-law spoke of goodness  
The servant spoke of gold  
Her husband had gone astray  
Already I was at home  
Who went from the door to the yard  
Went out through the gate  
Then began to argue back  
Began to scold the father-in-law  
To speak against misfortune  
To beg my husband  
Be well father-in-law  
Be well mother-in-law  
Teach the son goodness  
Don’t put him to sleep on the patch  
Don’t send him to the stove  
Forced to do heavier work  
Commanded to work faster  
Don’t put him to drink vodka  
Don’t make him want sour wine  
Don’t make him taste bitter beer  
Teach him to drink beer  
Wait, wait, come on, mother-in-law  
Let him go to the tavern a second time  
I dig a hole under the door  
Put chains on the hole  
I throw branches on the floor  
When he comes home from the tavern  
He immediately steps into the hole  
Breaks his neck on the branches.

label: marriage
translation:
Dear bride, do you hear me,
When I come to woo you,
Will you accept me;
Will you accept me with honor,
Or drive me away with shame:
You are black and hairy
And like a furry wreath.
If you accept me with honor,
Then I will give a betrothal gift,
Give a silver ring,
I will bring you a measure of vodka.
Come to me, my darling,
My little sweetheart,
I will set work for the bride:
I will make you give kisses,
Look for a head for the day,
Patch coats for the month,
Make a place for the year.
I will bring a thousand slippers,
A hundred pairs of socks,
I got them as presents for you,
Again, meant for you,
Even a pair of blushed shoes were given,
Those between the bands:
The nose was rubbed and worn,
Tilting and trembling.
There she cries with young eyes,
Her curly hair disheveled:
"This is my lace cap,
This is my silk eye kerchief,
A brightest neck scarf,
It flew here, it flew there,
It flew straight to the chamber,
Legs followed after."
Old man, old devil,
Give me back my honor,
And put on my red robe,
I am going to a new husband,
To be a young bride again.

label: marriage
translation:
Oh God, dear God,  
Great God above!  
Why did you let me sleep,  
When it was time to hunt?  
Others got the hares, all got the high ones,  
I got the black and foolish one,  
The tar stump and the sick one,  
The dead stump and fierce one;  
The birch stump and the hairy one!  
Others here wash their hare,  
Nurturing their lovers -  
I got the gray one,  
The poor furred one!  
Field to the side,  
Hare behind the back,  
Nose at the field corner,  
White scarf on the stick,  
A piece of soap on the wall.  
So I could be like others,  
Like the men of others.  
Then came the blessed evening,  
Dear month-play time.  
Hard then to call grandma,  
It’s sad to call to be a man,  
Come to bed, little toad,  
Step into the gray bed.

label: marriage
translation:
Oh Jüri behind the river  
Oh Mari under the earth  
Why did you leave me sleeping?  
When the maidens were being distributed?  
Others got the fair ones, everyone got the tall ones  
I got the dark and the foolish.  
A tar stump and a sickly one  
Where am I supposed to go with the dark one.  
To come with a tar stump?  
I found a stream, I splashed it  
I found a brook, I splashed it  
I found a pond, I washed in it.  
So that the dark one would have a different color,  
The tar stump a different color.  
Then I got a wife with a hooked nose  
Small and upright.  
Who knew how to handle fire  
To milk a cow without a chandelier  
Surely she kneaded bread clumsily  
And spilled a little flour.

label: marriage
translation:
Last year I took a young wife,  
The year before last – a different one.  
I took a healthy and strong one.  
I took a plump and red one.  
Very white and tender.  
I took her to the hay meadow,  
To the precious hay barn,  
Mowed beautiful hay there,  
Drove the little barn’s beauty.  
Did not leave a ribbon fluttering.  
The dew-hay began to grow,  
Suddenly started to weaken,  
Started to thin from the sole of the foot,  
Swelling from the apron strings,  
Fell ill from under the belt.  
I, the man, was left to ponder:  
To the village women’s prayer.  
The women understood and answered:  
Oh, you foolish young man,  
The night cannot be without weather,  
The moon cannot bear two -  
Weeks cannot be pinched,  
Now go quickly home,  
Put the little birds in the barn,  
Put the oats straight into the water.  
Then your wife will be healthy,  
Healthy – light –  
Like other women.

label: marriage
translation:
Hello farm, hello room  
Hello new doorframes  
Hello little noisy sparrows!  
May I come into the room  
Take care of the yard  
Ride outside on horseback?  
Perhaps you have springs inside  
Secret wells in the chamber  
Linen boards under the bench?  
Perhaps I will spoil the clothes’ edge  
My bride’s ornament edge  
In blue silk stockings?  
Let the speakers come out,  
Old fingers from in front of the stove  
Zippers from in front of the linen bench  
Make room in front of the stove ceiling  
In the hiding place above the bench  
Behind the back wall  
In front of the doorframe?  
A standing place in front of the wall.  
The drum is brought into the room  
A chair is offered on the floor  
Now our midday bread runs out  
Pieces of bread are aging  
Fur mittens are lasting  
Let me make a big bag from a sock  
Make a thief’s bag from a sleeve  
Make a carrying bag from a cupboard  
Where shall I find the pieces  
To carry fur mittens?  
Where shall I find the pieces  
To carry fur mittens?  
The fire is locked inside  
The well is dry at the hill  
The hayloft has no key  
Bread crumbs are in the book  
Milk pails with a lid!

label: marriage
translation:
Among us is a proud girl  
She was a white girl in the parish  
Mareta from Keskküla, the nice one  
She was the village's pride  
Taken out in full bridal attire  
To her mother's wedding.  
Celebrations were held - for the couple  
Then illness began to come  
Hard days started ahead  
Joosep also told Kaie  
Oh, my poor young girl!  
Where should I lay you?!  
You must not be taken before the elders  
You must not be brought before the wise ones  
Not to your father Marjus's house  
Nor to your mother's beloved chamber  
I will send you to the pigsty  
In your clean wedding clothes.  
Joosep asked Kaie,  
Whose own is this?  
Kaie laid her head on the pillow  
Eyes inside the clothes  
Joosep asked a second time  
Oh, my young wife  
Tell your father  
Whose own is this?  
Kaie struck her fist on her chest  
Like a sturdy oak cup  
Nine are your fathers  
The tenth swings Kaie.

label: marriage
translation:
Called a member of the household,  
A son-in-law,  
A husband to the little ring finger,  
A listener to the gold necklace,  
A watcher to the copper necklace.  
Time came, a day rolled by,  
Had slept through the night,  
Endured two nights,  
The father-in-law began to growl,  
The mother-in-law began to growl.  
What was brought into this?  
There was no concern for the newcomer.  
From the iron horse’s back,  
From the whip on the reed horse,  
From the sash of the spotted tail,  
I heard and responded:  
What did you gain in wealth  
By the name of the maiden?  
One had a glove for a mitten,  
Even that one silly without a finger,  
Blind without a veil,  
The father got one stocking,  
The page boy got half a ribbon,  
The bride rider got a glove finger—  
That was what you gained in wealth  
By the name of the maiden.

label: marriage
translation:
I wanted to plant a seedling  
I wanted to plant a seedling  
I plant it in hard soil  
I put it in the cracks of the limestone  
Where no shoot grows  
No head grows.

label: marriage
translation:
Yesterday the wedding began  
And today the lunch ended  
My wife is very sick  
Very sick in bed  
Old women by the bedside.  
I stand and watch  
God knows what will come of it  
The heart is sad and the mind is weary  
The old ladies whisper.  
Go outside, man, young men  
Go outside to pass the time  
To sharpen a staff in the shed  
To break a twig in the shed.  
I went outside to pass the time  
I did not sharpen a staff in the shed  
Nor did I break a twig in the shed  
I came back inside  
Found a blemish beneath my apron  
And a lump under my sixpence,  
I was very startled  
This is not my fault  
This is the blacksmith's fault  
The work of the crippled boys.  
I will start harassing the woman  
Cornering the young woman.  
Surely you could make noise in the forest  
Surely you could shout in the grove  
Fly through the alder thicket.  
Why did you come into our room?  
The old ladies silence them  
Just leave the young men be  
They will grow to be herders  
They will grow to be stable boys  
They will become soup cooks.

label: marriage
translation:
Last year I took a young wife  
The year before, another partner  
I led her to a tender hayfield  
Under the darling into the woods  
She mowed hay, clattered in the forest  
Took the forest trap for hay  
The willow bush snapped  
She mowed a bow, mowed two  
Started the third mowing meadow.  
Immediately she began to wither  
Seeing her eyes, began to wilt  
Started to suffer from knees  
To sleep from lung disease  
To knit from shoelaces  
To complain about the soles of her feet  
I went to ask the old woman.  
Oh, my dear old woman  
The wife remained dear and ill  
Started to suffer from knees  
To sleep from lung disease  
To lose the shoelace.  
And beyond, watch the young son.  
Take the oats scattered  
Carry the barley to the spring  
The rye to the linen  
We will kill the lambs here  
Fry the ducklings here  
We will beat the fibers upon the threshing floor  
A slap to the thigh  
Between the white horns.

label: marriage
translation:
Oh God, beyond the mountain
Beyond the mountain ridge
Who left me to sleep
Lulled me in your lap.
When this ridge was followed.
Men’s seed was mixed
Boy’s happiness was denied
Others got muffs, all got high,
Others became sharp men
I got black and stupid
A tar stump and sickly.

label: marriage
translation:
What is under the care of a slave,  
At the mercy of minnows?  
A fire in an unlocked room,  
A fart in a parson without a net,  
A barn without a key,  
A well without a cover on the hill.  
This is under the care of a slave,  
At the mercy of minnows.

label: marriage
translation:
Other men go to the sea,  
Other husbands go fishing,  
My man rummages at home.  
I sent my man to the sea.  
The man replied deceitfully:  
He said the sea is cold,  
The shore is frozen.  
I went myself, my dear!  
The sea was not cold,  
The shore was not frozen.  
I brought fish, ate fish,  
Counted fish bones for the man.  
The man eats deceitfully.  
I began to heat the stove:  
A warm sauna for myself,  
A hot sauna for the man;  
A leafy whisk for myself,  
A juniper whisk for the man.  
Then I took the man in my arms,  
I took the man to be whisked.  
Then the man began to say a prayer:  
Oh, my humble wife!  
I am born along the heart,  
I go after your hand,  
I let my bare feet follow;  
I give my foot strength,  
Strength to your big toe.

label: marriage
translation:
Two are offered to me:
One is lazy, the other a widow.
Which one do I leave, which one do I take?
I leave the lazy one, I take the widow.
How I go to bed with the old man:
I give my hand like to a stump,
A kiss like to a dead pig,
Shame to call a father-in-law,
Ugly to call a companion,
Frightening to call a father.
Still, I say:
Come to bed, old man!
How do I give the old man my hand?
A hand like to a dry roll,
A kiss like to melting butter.

label: marriage
translation:
I used to be a young man  
I wore pleated shirts,  
I carried rolled-up sleeves. –  
Now I rustle in a sack,  
I wither in the barn.

label: marriage
translation:
Until now, I was Ella Eide's son,
When she had no husband,
I wore slit shirts,
I wore two-hooked ones.
Last year I took a young wife,
The year before last, the other side,
Then I crawled into the sack,
I live from the old horn,
Now I bend at the needle—

label: marriage
translation:
I mowed hay that shimmered in the forest  
I took the loosening sound in the grove  
Started to ache in the knees  
Fell asleep from calf pain  
From the soles of the feet to the thigh  
Then I took it to the tender hayfield  
I called my dear to the arch's end  
Our little brave boys  
Haymakers, wood carriers  
Shakers of the tall forest  
I fell cutting down wet pines  
Wet pines, dry spruces  
I leave the ashes to grow  
Birch branches to be straight  
Branches groan like a father  
Leaves mourn like a mother  
But the trees like sons and daughters

label: marriage
translation:
There was a rye bread to live on
One was a mitten, probably a towel
Also this one was foolish to touch
Blind without a turn
They nursed a girl child
They nursed, raised life
They grew, embraced
A miracle to a righteous, beautiful soul
Grow to a righteous, humble soul
You become the firstborn to the grandmother
A step to the gravedigger
A defender against fire
A water carrier for Virve
The time came, the day arrived
Support was given to one unknown
Help was given to one disregarded
Did not understand to thank angrily
Did not give the beginning to help
So ended up a slave without searching
A bread eater without being found
Who is under the care of a slave
Under the will of daughters-in-law
There came a locked room
Farted in the guest room without a curtain
The well is without a lid
The cowshed is without a lock
These are under the care of a slave
Under the will of daughters-in-law
Under the control of the commander

label: marriage
translation:
Village women are cold-hearted
Parish women are deceitful
They said I would remain without a husband
Live without a spouse
I got a faithful husband
A loving spouse
When he comes home from the tavern
He takes a carpet from the closet
A slippery door handle.
He rises early in the morning
The wife gets up to milk the cow
Dear wife, take the herd.
She makes a small whip from thread
A handle from a straw stalk
She strikes him once, she strikes him twice
Immediately he jumps off the bed
Are there rods on the belt
Tools on the arm.

label: marriage
translation:
A Naughty Youngster  
When you go to the farmhand  
The farmhand goes to sleep  
The grain grows in the field  
This puts the flute to sleep  
The kantele takes it to the chamber  
The morning rises  
Rise, bird, milk the cow  
White bird, give milk to the calf  
Dear bird, join the herd  
The village herd goes to the distant one  
Our herd is to the herd-grass  
When you go to the official  
The official goes to sleep  
The official stands by the wall  
This puts the whip to sleep  
The kantele takes it to the chamber  
The morning rises  
Rise, bitch, milk the cow  
Old bitch, give milk to the calf  
Herd-bitch joins the herd  
Munde’s herd goes to the distant one  
Our herd is to the herd-grass.

label: marriage
translation:
A young corner woman  
Does the farm's stable work  
From morning till evening.  
She goes to bed in the evening.  
She does not feel that hour,  
Nor thinks about the time  
When long troubles  
Start to trouble her.  

The poor woman gets up,  
Already heavy with age  
The old mother's long troubles.  
Pain runs down her back,  
Bites along the hip bone.  
What should I do?  

She rises from the bed,  
Lets herself kneel on the floor,  
Lies on her back against the wall.  
Leans her back against a pillar,  
Seeks support from a chair,  
From the corner cupboard for support.  
Asks for stability from the wall—  
Cannot lean on the chair,  
Cannot get support from the corner cupboard,  
Cannot get stability from the wall.  

Jesus waits in the chamber,  
Mary sleeps in the corner,  
When will help be called?  
What is the poor woman doing now?  
She asks little Jesus for help.  
Come to help, little Jesus.  

Jesus steps in to help now.  
Jesus had two hands,  
One big, one small.  
The big hand for visiting women,  
The small hand for the young corner woman.  

Jesus brings the boy to the room.  
The companion waits in the chamber.  
What do I pay Jesus?  
Jesus does not want money.  
Jesus wants kind hearts.  

What is the poor woman doing now?  
Come to Mary's help!  
Mary steps in to help.  
Mary had two hands,  
One heavy, one light.  

The heavy hand for visiting women,  
The light one for the young corner woman.  
Mary holds her daughter with her scissors,  
The daughter was brought to the room.  
Mary thinks in the chamber,  
What do I pay Mary?  
Mary does not want money,  
She wants kind hearts.  

The young corner woman  
Now you see the long weeks  
Of the old mother's long troubles.

label: marriage
translation:
The birds sang with gentle tongues  
With gentle tongues and joyful spirits  
The flowers just began to bloom  
The blossoms lifted sweetly into the air.  
The wife began to joke  
To love her husband  
The woman did not want to smile  
The husband did not want to love  
I went to the forest to settle things  
To walk into the grove  
To step into the meadow  
To march to the berry fields  
To look for love herb  
To gather affection herb  
From the forest I found nettle herb  
From the grove I got affection herb  
From the meadow I got love herb  
From the berry fields sweet herb  
I gave the woman to sniff  
The husband to smell.  
The woman began to joke  
The husband began to love me.

label: marriage
translation:
Old man with an old devil’s beard  
Hell with the beard  
The old man caught me  
In his gray love  
From under the moonlit day,  
Through the wooden gate.  
Over the yard with apple trees  
Over a pile of rowan trees.  
I stoked the stove with kindling  
Set the sauna for the horse’s tail (sauna whisk)  
I took the whisk poorly  
On a cowardly donkey upwards.  
With a broom twig, I lit the stove.  
Then I added steam  
More miserably I endured  
The old man begged me:
