Along the wide shore of the island.  
There the woodpecker pecks wood.  
Blue feathers for the head,  
Old copper for the line.  
They build new houses,  
Create dear chambers,  
New storehouses are thatched,  
The starling makes the roof,  
The woodpecker smooths the walls,  
The ptarmigan makes the lintel,  
The sparrow the bare ceilings,  
The magpie makes the stove,  
The cranes make the beams,  
The duck pats the lintel.  
They nail in iron crosses,  
Silver buttons on the corners.  
Line them with meatskin,  
Hinges made of eggshells.

label: entertainment
translation:
This is how it is in our country,  
This happens in our farm:  
A pig was plowing, a dog was biting the stake,  
A sheep was biting a wolf,  
A chicken was pecking a golden ring,  
A pig was wearing a brooch on its chest,  
A dog was walking with a crown on its head,  
A goat had bindings on its legs,  
A sheep had wide hoofs.

label: entertainment
translation:
Now I go singing to the threshing floor  
Head twisted to the father-in-law  
Sister boiled apple broth,  
Father-in-law made fresh Baltic herring broth.  
Mother-in-law baked fish,  
Brother-in-law drank brandy.

label: entertainment
translation:
I watch over the old woman’s sheep,  
I protect the old man’s herd.  
The old woman makes a new cozy hut for me,  
From blue wool,  
From blue she makes a standing hut,  
From white wool a warm hut,  
From gray wool a rough hut,  
From black wool another hut.  
From red she makes a wedding hut.  
A little wolf comes,  
Takes the child and the sheep to the forest,  
Pulls the grandmother into trouble.

label: entertainment
translation:
Upon the great clans,  
Proud of the fathers,  
Proud of the mothers,  
Dignified of the five brothers,  
Noble of the six sisters,  
On whom does the poor child rely?  
I am proud of myself,  
Dignified on the five fingers,  
Noble on the two hands.  
I have no clan here on this land,  
No sister in my village,  
No aunt in this people’s place;  
All my kin are in Finland,  
Father’s brothers in Hiiumaa,  
Half the brothers in Pohja Land,  
Sisters at the edge of Laiuse.  
Kin speaks Finnish language,  
Father’s brothers speak Hiiumaa language,  
Half the brothers speak Pohja language,  
Sisters speak Laiuse dialect.  
All my kin in foreign places,  
Sisters in closed shoes,  
But I alone am five-legged,  
Five-legged, wearing a buckskin shoe,  
Keeper of the willow slippers;  
God grant willow offshoots,  
So all the birch calves could grow,  
From which poor children get shoes,  
Footwear for the poor child.  
My father the miracle worker:  
Made me a wondrous coat,  
Made a spotted tipi,  
A goatskin on a birch,  
I am not born among the great,  
Nor fit in the house of the rich,  
Noble among the ear-seaters.  
I sit particularly  
Among other weary ones,  
In the midst of beggars.

label: entertainment
translation:
Let's leave this countryside,  
Let's go to Finland for the summer,  
For half the summer to the land of cranberries,  
For a little while to the town of Narva.  
There is no hay cutting,  
Nor meadow mowing,  
But there someone mows the hay poorly,  
The scythe takes the meadow,  
The cuckoo calls from the hills,  
Who brought here  
Who brought the red ribbon?  
Who brought the rose-colored cloth?  
Father brought the blue here,  
Mother brought the red ribbon,  
Brother brought the rose-colored cloth.  
I myself am weaving a Kalev's belt,  
With big, wide heddles,  
With big heddles made by my father-in-law,  
Wide heddles made by my mother-in-law,  
With loom feet made along.

label: entertainment
translation:
If we had a whole yard full of us  
Oh, if we had a whole sled full of us,  
A brother’s lap full of warmth,  
A valley full of white boys,  
Then we would know what to do:  
We would build a barn on the wind,  
At the other edge of the barn –  
Behind the barn, a small stable,  
Inside the stable, a gray mare,  
A good saddle for the mare,  
A German boy for the saddle –  
A golden belt for the German boy,  
A weaver for the golden belt...

label: entertainment
translation:
Oh you little hop madman  
A tiny drop of poison  
Took the minds from men's heads,  
Half the minds from boys' heads,  
The temples in front of women's faces.  
Men roar without hats  
Women dance without skirts  
What else do we drink beer for  
If not to glorify beer,  
Little hop bear in a new cap  
I drink beer, rattling the jug  
I cast the whips into the whip bag  
Legboards from the brushwood.

label: entertainment
translation:
I guard grandma’s ewe,  
Protect grandpa’s large herd;  
From the swamp came great wolves,  
From the forest behind, wide paws,  
Broke down the black ewe,  
Tore away the speckled bull.

label: entertainment
translation:
Let the brewers be healthy,  
Brewers, pourers,  
Who have put together six.  
First, water, which is liquid,  
Second, fire full of strength,  
Third, dear junipers,  
Fourth, malt sweet,  
Fifth, bitter hops,  
Sixth, those hot stones,  
Seventh, yeast added on top.

label: entertainment
translation:
Morning squirrel fur  
Daytime raccoon fur  
Noon skylark fur  
Evening rye flower fur  
"He went under our yard  
Ate a heap of our hay  
Reduced our rye in the field."

label: entertainment
translation:
Six little gold pieces  
A colorful little bird  
I will not give my hen  
I feed it with sugar  
In winter with buckwheat groats.

label: entertainment
translation:
I had a wealthy godmother  
She gave me a little goat,  
A little bell on the goat’s neck.  
The goat went into the forest bleating,  
The bell on its neck tinkling;  
The goat went to the village herd,  
Across the sea and forest.  
The goat brings me hay,  
I give the hay to the cow;  
The cow gives me milk,  
I give the milk to the piglet;  
The piglet gives me a son-in-law,  
I give the son-in-law to my mother-in-law,  
The mother-in-law gives me a cake.  
I give the cake to my father-in-law,  
The father-in-law gives me iron.  
I give the iron to the smith,  
The smith gives me a horse collar,  
I give the horse collar to the oak tree.  
The oak tree gives me leaves,  
I give the leaves to the sheep  
The sheep gives me a lamb,  
The lamb gives me wool,  
I give the wool to the spinner.

label: entertainment
translation:
Sisters, dear ones,  
did you see my horse  
wandering in the street,  
dancing in the street?  
What color is your horse?  
Morning squirrel color,  
noon flame color,  
and midday gosling color.  
It passed through our yard,  
its tail was tied with silk,  
its mane was braided with thread,  
its head was placed in a braid. -  
It tasted our seawater,  
tried our well water,  
pulled tar from the tar bucket. -

label: entertainment
translation:
Row the swing, row the swing,  
row the swing to the sunny land,  
where the spruces yellow,  
the firs bow wisely,  
the straight alders turn blue,  
the snakes are long and red;  
where the roosters eat gold,  
the hens drink fear,  
the geese cluck silver,  
the crows old copper,  
the small birds  
the tits tin pieces...

label: entertainment
translation:
Neigh, neigh, grey stallion  
Try to jump out into the yard.  
If you get out, you will get barley;  
if you stay inside, you will go without.

label: entertainment
translation:
I make a tua (thatched roof) for the wind,  
a branch from the saana tree.  
I make a roof from feathers of a grebe,  
a room from a hen's egg.  
Inside I make the walls blue,  
on top I put red beams.  
Then the fire came to see,  
the parish came to listen.  
Every head went to Pärnu's Saxons,  
the Palve Fridays to Paide Saxons,  
every month kings would come.  
They wondered about the town of Lihula,  
was it Rahula's shore,  
or was it the emperor's church?  
But I listen and answer:  
"This is Halva Anne's sauna."

label: entertainment
translation:
Sleepy, sleepy little one.  
The wolf pulls the old woman's beard.  
The old woman makes me a new hat,  
The old man makes a winter coat for her,  
from flags and patches  
and the fur of an old bear.  
"Have you seen my sheep?  
They passed by here, I threw leaves in front of them.  
But why is your mouth red?  
I ate strawberries.  
What is behind your back?  
Stones, stumps, brooms, shovels.  
May I come out to play?  
Certainly.

label: entertainment
translation:
I traveled a bit in Turkey,  
A hundred versts in Germany,  
A little on the Narva road,  
Half a verst in Poland.  
I have never seen the miracle  
That I saw in Näuküla:  
Bulls were barking, dogs were plowing,  
Cats were weaving cloth,  
The pig went to work, the sickle was at its waist,  
The fox stood with reins around its neck.  
The horse brought a bull-calf,  
The cow brought a little washbasin,  
The sheep went to lay eggs in the barn,  
The hen brought two lambs.  
Girls were busy spinning,  
Women were carding wool,  
Men were walking the tavern road.

label: entertainment
translation:
Hans was from Harju,  
Jaan was from Järva,  
There was a cook's boy from Kohala.  
Hans was a man from Harju, lowborn,  
Strong from Tinatupe.  
He bought a horse from Harju,  
A saddle from a Saare German,  
A little whip from his own cooper,  
Then he set off on a journey to Riga.  
The Germans in Riga were thinking.  
They thought, they watched:  
Look, there he rides without a master,  
Without a master, the king of the land.  
I heard this and responded,  
Answering the verses, I said:  
I am not without a master,  
Without a master, the king of the land.  
I am another man's servant.  
In summer, I walk carrying sacks,  
In winter, a tapper in the blacksmith's shop.

label: entertainment
translation:
The shepherd herded the flock;
Drove me out to search.
In the misty morning,
In the early dawn,
Along the made paths,
Along the carved trails,
Where before the slaves had walked,
Slaves had walked, oxen had walked.
Early went the poor children.
Late wandered the latecomers.
Before dawn, the orderly ones.
After the day, the day workers.

label: entertainment
translation:
I began to patch the pastels,  
To mend the gift’s binding.  
The manor’s black cat came,  
It took away the patch from my right pastel.  
I went after the cat,  
The cat also went into the well’s shelter.  
Its tail remained as a long escape.  
A pity for the cat, a pity for the well.  
A pity for the village’s cold water.  
I went to the village to get rope.  
Rope from the village, man from the household.  
Two ropes from the thief.  
From Nigul I brought linden rope.  
From Tooma-Jaan, tar string,  
From Andres, I brought only new;  
Couldn’t get the cat out of the well,  
I made five ribbons of five stripes,  
Then I got the cat out of the well.

label: entertainment
translation:
Who here rides along the road,  
Gallops along the paths?  
The horse is silver in front.  
The wagon is copper behind.  
The wheel shakes coins,  
The rims clink ruble pieces,  
The spokes chime pennies,  
The horse in front like the stove,  
The head itself like the day,  
The hat like the moon’s servant,  
The belt like a rain rainbow.  
Master, little master!  
Here someone rides along the road,  
Gallops along the paths.

label: entertainment
translation:
A little beer, a little beauty,  
A little ale, a little darling,  
From your face, you are the handsome one,  
From your stomach, you are the sweet one.  
You walk along my stomach,  
March along my belly,  
Stretch along the spine.  
Be healthy, brewers!  
Who made good beer,  
Often went to the tavern,  
Sometimes went to the well.  
But I sip along with my mind,  
I try along the edge of the pitcher.  
The hop calls in the stream,  
The cone crackles in the bush:  
Come, come young men,  
Pick me into your sack,  
Take me out for the work in the field,  
Put me on the bench edge,  
Carry me to the kitchen stove!  
Then I rise onto the loft,  
I swell along the long gutter.  
Then I take the minds of men,  
Half the minds of the boys' heads,  
The temples from the women's foreheads.  
Men make noise without hats,  
Women dance without shoes,  
Boys half kneeling.  
The beer was wild and the bottle was smart,  
Ale was very sly.  
Oh, you proud barley water,  
Oh, you wrathful grain water,  
Though you surely bring me down,  
Still, I take you inside me.

label: entertainment
translation:
Crazy are those hops,  
mighty are the killer vines!  
They take the minds from men's heads,  
have stolen them from wise women's heads!

label: entertainment
translation:
The song ended, the child went to the barn.  
I quickly went out the door.  
There I saw seven jokes.  
The girl milked an ox by the shoulders,  
The pig sang on a penny.  
The hen brought two lambs,  
The cow hit the leaf of the field with a stallion.  
The horse is a Dutch calf.  
Huhuhu and hahahaa  
The child went to the barn with the song.

label: entertainment
translation:
Tiidut-tiidut, the road was crooked  
The road was crooked, the ground was crooked.  
The wrinkled leg was crooked  
The distiller poured crooked brandy  
The slope brought ointments.

label: entertainment
translation:
Let's get going, men,  
Light the pipes,  
Little ones rushing  
Smoke pipes smoking,  
And steam pipes steaming.

label: entertainment
translation:
I am a drunkard, an old man from Nurme  
A tavern boy  
I still drink in the tavern  
I also sing tavern songs  
Alone I waited for two heads  
Weeks in groups of four  
Months in twos and threes  
Years in groups of five  
I drank away the yoke from the oxen  
The cows from the milking pail  
Still there was grumbling  
The sawdust kept buzzing  
The pinecone remained listening  
The navel stalk kept laughing  
The youth kept talking endlessly  
I still drank in the tavern  
I sang tavern songs  
I don't know where my horse is  
Whether it is outside or in the yard  
A young maiden  
Go outside to check  
See for yourself  
Whether it is outside or in the yard  
Or has it been let loose  
Or caught in a snowstorm wind  
To a wide plank floor  
Rain leans against the big wall  
Stands here by the wall  
Gets caught between the toes  
A young maiden  
Bring a blanket to the bed  
Wipe my beard from the mist  
Dirty the steps of the mother-in-law.

label: entertainment
translation:
Little Jüri, a little rascal  
But a rich boy with money  
Jüri made a room out in the wind  
A sauna on the big island  
He made doors from wolf bones  
And covers from bear bones  
Antler clusters from moose antlers  
Jüri, God's servant  
The Creator’s storyteller  
But Jüri cruelly killed a cat  
Made a coat for Kaie  
A base cloak for Anne  
A full cloak for Maie  
Because Anne loved  
Kaie dearly  
Maie was her love  
Liisu long ago was her torment.

label: entertainment
translation:
But I went on the wedding path  
On the wedding path of Black Mats  
An ox was slaughtered at Mats'  
But I was called a cook  
I put the meat to cook  
And the roast to stew  
Then came the cat with quick eyes  
Ate the meat before it was cooked  
Before the roast was stewed  
I went to catch the cat  
The cat went into a crack in the wall  
I went to find a rope  
Tõnu brought a tarred rope  
From the linden tree I brought a hemp rope  
From the birch tree a hemp rope  
Then I went to catch the cat  
The hemp ropes got tangled  
The linden rope pulled out  
The mice laughed in the corner  
Ast ast ast ast little kitty  
Where is my golden son of the spruce  
Everything is up the cat's ass  
In Black Mats' stomach.

label: entertainment
translation:
Liisakene little ribbon  
Snap as soon as you see the eye  
Tap as soon as you hear the ear  
An old sneaker in the shadow  
Liisu heard the sound of an instrument  
She went outside, flashing  
The floor beneath was beating  
Tapping on the boy's ear  
Liisu heard the sound of a shoe  
Clicking sounds against the codes  
Immediately as the store falls  
Click, run away.

label: entertainment
translation:
I rode, I rode, little brother  
I rode through a piece of Turkey  
Half of the world, the land of the bog  
A bit of Narva land  
I didn’t see the miracle  
That I saw inside the house  
Oxen yoked, dogs plowed.  
Girls made sledges  
Women chopped wheelwood  
Father chopped oxwood  
Old wise man cut timber  
They knocked on spoke wood,  
Men walked on straw roads  
Brandy flasks inside  
Beer jugs at the door.  
They bloomed on straw beer  
Sang on the straw table.

label: entertainment
translation:
The family daughter, a young maiden  
When she hears the fiddle player  
The fiddle player, the fine player  
Then she lifts her forehead  
Steps out from the thicket  
Her chest swells openly  
Now to the oak to dance  
The young spruces to bend  
To the apple trees to sway  
The tumpet to beat  
When I hear the drum player  
The drum player, loud and clear  
Then I head towards the bed  
Step towards the thicket  
Hopping towards the table  
There I sleep, my darling  
My beautiful blossom  
Resting, a bride at the wedding.

label: entertainment
translation:
Uiu Tuiu, a hunter’s bundle  
A ghost’s bundle behind the room  
An evil lord’s gold bundle  
A poor people’s pain bundle  
The laborers have much work  
In the large hall are many lazy ones  
On the family platform much farting  
In the room’s corner much shouting.

label: entertainment
translation:
Be healthy, brewers  
Who put these three together  
First, water is liquid  
Second, that malt is sweet  
Third, you hate fools.  
This took the minds from men's heads  
Half the minds from boys' heads  
Thanks to the wise women's heads.  
Men break into smoking  
Women dance without thanks  
Boys halfway to drunkenness.

label: entertainment
translation:
I had the thought to go on a journey,  
To go on a journey, to travel to the countryside.  
When I set off, it started drizzling,  
When I reached the countryside, it began to hail.  
The shutters were struck by sleet,  
The beams were rattled and shaken.  
Then more wind came, raising a storm,  
It lifted my grey oars upright.  
So I went against the night,  
Against the night, against the moon,  
Against the white dawn,  
Against the dark clouds.

label: entertainment
translation:
In the meadow, a skate was skating inside me,  
The claw pointed into the bush:  
"Bring here some young men,  
Take me home with a sack,  
Take me into the house with a mat,  
Put me on the edge of the board,  
Boil me in the kettle,  
Lift me onto the edge of the threshing floor,  
From there I sneak into the barrel,  
Into the half-full beer,  
Between the sticks of the cask."  
There was beer for the wild, and the bottle was wise,  
It took the senses from the heads of men,  
The sense from the heads of women.  
Men made noise without hats,  
Women danced without senses,  
Boys halfway on their knees,  
Girls on all fours,  
Dancing on their heels and toes.

label: entertainment
translation:
Vaida, the Vaida factory is visible,  
The citizen's chimney is smoking.  
The city brooms are turning green,  
The Toompea towers are gleaming.

label: entertainment
translation:
Let us drink, let us drink, dear brothers!
Let us drink, dear good fellows.
We drink vodka when we can,
We live the master's way,
We work the wise way.

label: entertainment
translation:
The horse runs because of the reins  
It beats its head because of the whip  
It leaps because of the herd’s whip.  
It steps because of the dry hay  
Then the horse curls up in the shed  
In the grey garden corner.  
Milla comes to the drunkard’s doorstep and  
To the ear of the stalk-walker  
To raise the slanted cloak  
The family’s maiden  
The farm girl, the little plant  
You bring the striped blanket  
The woolen, patterned rug.  
Wipe my horse from the mist.  
Wipe the rain from the hooves  
From the wide-lipped stable floor.

label: entertainment
translation:
Whose litter, whose litter, paid for a cow,  
Whose boat :,: a pair of oxen?  
Whose buckle :,: of the large parish,  
Whose wreath for the town of Pärnu.  
Mari’s litter :,: paid for a cow  
Mari’s boat Mari’s boat a pair of oxen  
Mari’s buckle :,: of the large parish  
Mari’s wreath :,: for the town of Pärnu  
Mari herself :,: without all  
Kis Siidi :,: take on your lap  
Kis Armas :,: start turning  
Siidisammet :,: take on your lap  
Mari Armas :,: start turning  
Mari Siidi :,: take on your lap  
Mari dear :,: jump on the neck  
Exchange :,: a good husband  
Juuli Armas :,: start turning  
Juuli dear :,: jump on the neck  
Juuli Siidi :,: take on your lap,

label: entertainment
translation:
Oh, our golden king!  
Rich young gentleman of Riga,  
A true boy from Pärnu.  
Why didn’t you come to us last year,  
When the rivers ran without oil,  
And the springs bubbled below;  
When the surface swirled in whirlpools,  
Now you have come at the beginning of time,  
At the light springtime;  
At the rustling autumn,  
At the snowy snowfall of winter.  
Now you strip off your clothes:  
Rip off your collars,  
Take off your wreath from your head!  
Oh, our golden king!  
Rich young gentleman of Riga,  
A true boy from Pärnu,  
Give me some poor gold;  
Cast away the troublesome silver!  
Last year the master bought a press.  
The mistress got a little burden;  
I myself got a shawl’s worth;  
The press I got from beating the thigh,  
The broth I got from boiling the soup,  
From kneading the bread with a clasp.

label: entertainment
translation:
Cross dance, cross dance, let’s dance  
Our dance, our dance, let’s keep  
Järva dance:,: let’s leave  
Viru dance:,: let’s lead  
Dear dance:,: beloved dance  
Dance of the threshing floor:,: the king  
Roll, little one:,: from the manor  
Blue rises:,: grows from the swamp  
Grows from the swamp:,: from the borders of the land  
Circle of dancers:,: between  
Turning of the shoe:,: from the snakes.

label: entertainment
translation:
Belly of the drum, belly of the drum, reed berry!
Over the twig, over the twig, clover stem.
Who went yesterday :,: to the hayfield?
It was Mari, :,: the young maiden;
That she :,: cut her finger!
Poor toe :,: in the haystack.
Who jumped up :,: to check?
It was her fiancé :,: the young man,
Tied up :,: that finger;
Wrapped it up, a wet bandage.
Where did she get :,: the scarf?
She took it from her neck :,: the neckerchief.
Where did she get :,: the ribbon?
She took it from the belt :,: the belt ribbon.

label: entertainment
translation:
Hops called me into the ditch,  
Cone creaked into the corner stove  
Come here, young men,  
Take me to the hut of the bear,  
Make me a steed for the stag,  
Put me to dry on the railing.  
From there I go to the barn,  
Slip into the half-pint of beer,  
Roll between the twigs;  
Then I take the senses from men's heads,  
Half the senses from boys' heads,  
Thanks from wise women's heads;  
Men roar without hats,  
Women dance without the ground,  
Boys half without boots,  
Girls without belts.

label: entertainment
translation:
Let's go along the paths made  
Along the trails forged  
Where before slaves have walked  
Slaves walked, oxen went  
Early went poor children  
Late came the wolves  
Before dawn the orderly ones  
After day the daytime ones

label: entertainment
translation:
Daughters of Viru are sisters  
Maids of Harju are single  
We join three bodies together  
We consult with four bodies  
We go to Riga to spoil  
To kill in Tallinn  
To burn Põltsamaa  
A German shouted from the hall  
A citizen from the threshold of a stable  
A shop boy in front of the shop  
I say again, back  
Daughters of Viru are sisters  
Maids of Harju are single  
Leave Riga unspoiled  
Do not kill in Tallinn  
Do not burn Põltsamaa  
Leave Riga to bring salt  
Tallinn to strike money  
From Põltsamaa bring flaxen clothes for the women  
Bring tools for the boys  
For the girls, empty things

label: entertainment
translation:
Brewers and necksmiths,  
Passibo pot washers,  
Who made the beer little by little  
In their proud home  
From the long field's harvest.  
It took the minds from the men's heads  
Half the minds from the boys' heads.  
Men roar without hats,  
Women dance without a ribbon,  
Boys with half boots on.  
Wait, wait, Annekene,  
Endure, Kaiekene,  
Surely you have time to give  
To spin the wheel sock.  
To train the wooden shoe.  
Jaan drinks by the riverbank.  
Between five and six o'clock in the morning  
At the break of dawn.

label: entertainment
translation:
It was the right time to go to Paide,  
Joy was to lay out for the fair,  
Oh that barley mash,  
Dear little sack of oats.  
Taught me to make beer,  
To distill vinegar,  
But I started to go wild,  
Moving my feet in the town.  
The Jews reach even the tavern,  
I am lively in the ear,  
In the morning I drank a new six,  
On Tuesday I drank a whole shirt.  
On Thursday I drank among them,  
On Friday I drank clothes off,  
On Saturday I drank a wide belt.  
On Sunday I drank the pants off,  
Then I was finally finished,  
Then I rode to the church with a flea,  
Right onto the donkey over the choir,  
The choir Germans were startled,  
The sexton ran to the kitchen,  
The vicar to the coach,  
Then the benches stayed to be sealed by me,  
The altars to be driven by me,  
The pulpits to be torn by me.

label: entertainment
translation:
Oh wonder, oh wonder  
What did I see, oh wonder  
What did I see in Näo village?  
Two women were fighting,  
Two old ladies' daughters,  
Anne had a stick,  
Kaie a broom  
Maie had a rowan tree on her shoulder,  
Leenu had a little soup ladle.

label: entertainment
translation:
Little musical instrument, little boy  
Dear kannel, little toy,  
Neither instrument nor sustenance without a family,  
The kannel needs a companion to live.  
The instrument walks to taverns,  
Seeks beer houses,  
Trips into the liquor chamber.  
If only my old sounds  
The old sounds in brass,  
Tin sounds in tals (coins).  
I would not hide the instrument’s sounds,  
Nor the German horn sounds,  
Would not let the kannel’s tone be lost.  
I would make the instruments squeak,  
Rooster crows crow,  
The young horn cry.

label: entertainment
translation:
Sister dear, I have told you,  
Dear sibling, I forbid you:  
Do not run to the drunkard,  
To the wanderer of two taverns,  
A drunkard has no sense,  
A tavern-goer has a hangover,  
A lackey dog has a scab,  
He ties you to the tavern wall,  
He watches you by the tavern ropes.

translation:

label: entertainment
translation:
I make a fence, sharpen a stake,  
so that a dream cannot slip over,  
nor a bear over leap,  
nor a snake crawl through.  
Here I leave a knot and  
go to eat tangupuuro (a type of porridge) and drink milk.

label: entertainment
translation:
Sleep, sleep, little one  
The grandmother will make you a new hood,  
The old man will make a winter coat,  
From flags and patches  
And the old bear’s fur.

label: entertainment
translation:
Let's go make this path,  
This carved trail,  
Where God has walked before,  
Where Mary has come to earth,  
A holy cross worn on the chest,  
Worn on the chest, worn on the shoulder,  
Risking the chest wearing,  
Enduring the shoulder wearing.  
What could be left on the trail,  
Or fallen on the step from there?  
Gold left on the trail,  
Silver fallen on the step.  
Who foolishly took the gold?  
Who wickedly took the silver?  
I, the foolish Marnikene,  
I, the foolish one, took the gold,  
I, the wicked one, took the silver,  
I took it to my brother's house,  
I took it to my brother's wife,  
I placed it on my brother's table,  
On a nice jug with a lid,  
I tapped a mug for my brother,  
A tin jug with a lid,  
Katik struck the jug's lid,  
Katik, my brother’s wide table,  
Brother dear, little brother dear,  
Take your horse from the yard,  
Don’t complain about the crane's neck.  
Let's take the gold to Viljandi,  
Carry the silver to Tarvastu,  
Viljandi has a skilled blacksmith,  
Tarvastu has a wise smith,  
Let's make wedding rings,  
A pearl necklace for mother’s child.

label: entertainment
translation:

Six on the locks.
Go to that farm
Where there is a chicken on the threshing floor,
On the dry straw of the rooster.
“Hello, hello man, what are you doing here?”
“I am digging a hole.”
“What will you do with that hole?”
“I will draw in charcoal.”
“What will you do with that charcoal?”
“I will put a pot on it.”
“What will you do with that pot?”
“I will put water in it.”
“What will you do with that water?”
“I will take the feathers of the hen and the rooster.”
“What wrong did the hen and the rooster do?”
“The lord’s trench was plowed,
and the maiden took the peas away.”
“Where were you earlier?”
“Down the hill I built a fence.”
“Where were the women and children?”
“They were carrying wood and reeds.”
“How long was the fence?”
“As high as the sky.
How wide?
As wide as the blade of an axe.
How thick?
Like a sieve for oats.”

From here, the calm

took the wife, the bell stayed with me.

Whose building could this be

This is my little sauna  
A refuge for poor children

The walls of elk shin bones

The benches of pork meat

Going to the tavern, drinking vodka  
When my father-in-law was very rich  
And my mother-in-law was very rich  
They gave me a little goat  
A bell for the goat’s neck  
The wolf ate the goat, the bell remained with me  
I went to the Jaanipää church  
I put the bell on the woman’s neck  
The woman was angry, stomping  
The bell was loud, clanging  
Those who saw me, laughed at me  
Those who knew me, scolded me  
Oh, you crazy and foolish one  
Bring the bell back to the woman’s neck.

label: entertainment
translation:
The pig died for us, the junker was born  
Calves were watching out the window  
Dogs were clattering, boots on feet  
The gentleman was honored at the edge of the snowdrift  
The lady went to the field to plow  
The young men were going to the swamp  
The children were going to pick twigs  
The sister village’s role is that of a rascal  
I am such a rogue  
The rogue has a fine horse  
The mare has a slippery stallion  
The prostitute has a proud stallion  
The rogue went with the beauty to church  
The fool went to bed with the woman  
The prostitute went to the town to bring bread

label: entertainment
translation:
I smoked a long pipe  
I let the smoke fly straight  
Blue smoke rose from my mouth  
A four-twist from my nose  
But some thought it was manor smoke  
It was pipe smoke from a poppy

label: entertainment
translation:
When I left the tavern  
I saw seven jokes  
A pig sang on a penny  
A rooster rummaged in the garden there  
Ani ate hay from the heap  
A sheep took lovers from Vahva  
A cow plowed the field angrily  
A girl milked an ox from the back.

label: entertainment
translation:
Rowing, rocking, rowing, rocking  
To the heights, to the distance  
Over the marsh, over the bogs  
Over the long Lake Peipus.  
Rowing, rocking to that land,  
Where the spruces turn yellow  
The young birches turn green  
The straight alders gleam blue  
Where the roosters eat gold  
Roosters gold, hens beware  
The ducks green silver  
The crows old copper.

label: entertainment
translation:
Let's get going, men  
Let's light the pipes  
Let the smoking noses smoke.

label: entertainment
translation:
Droplet, droplet little needle,  
Droplet little needle eye  
The needle didn’t get lost while playing  
While playing, while messing about  
It got lost while working  
Sewing a dowry sheet  
Mending children's clothes  
Trimming the young man's shirt  
Jump needle, jump needle  
Spark spark needle  
Buzzing little girl’s needle  
Jump into Udri's barley  
Into the shepherd boy's turnip garden.

label: entertainment
translation:
Kuos-kuos little goldfinch  
Kuos goldfinock  
What is the goldfinch looking for us?  
The goldfinch is looking for the ram's barn  
Through the straw pigsty  
Through the chicken coop door  
Through the market sheep's barn.

label: entertainment
translation:
Sifting-sifting, little sieve  
Bottom of the sieve  
Lend me the sieve, lambkin  
Cannot lend, lambkin  
You have stern servants  
Stubborn flatterers  
They take the sieve to the dung heap  
The pig eats the bottom of the sieve  
The male goat eats the skeleton’s bottom  
The little foal eats the fodder bottom  
Lend it, lambkin

label: entertainment
translation:
If only I knew what I would do,
I would put the room to the wind,
The sauna on a big island,
The city on a grain of sand.

label: entertainment
translation:
The hazel jumps out of the forest,  
The cone cracks out of the pocket;  
"Come here today, young men,  
Come pick me today,  
Take me to Kotila's home,  
To Matila's father's house!"  
Put the ducks out to dry,  
From there I roll into the rye field,  
I put it into the half barrel of beer,  
Between the stave hoops.  
But I take the senses from the men's heads,  
The wits from the wise women's heads;  
Then the men made noise without hats,  
The women danced without wits,  
Boys with half a boot on,  
Girls with wreaths on their heads.

label: entertainment
translation:
The flanks of the mares strike fire,
The shanks of the alder strike sparks,
The hooves of the colt strike lightning
On the rough village ground,
At the threshing floor of Esna parish.

label: entertainment
entertainment
translation:
I make tales for a drunkard,
I make calls at the tavern counter:
Tavern manners are filthy manners,
No vodka given without money;
No beer without buying,
No small beer without trading,
No mead without thinking.
Tavern manners are filthy manners.

label: entertainment
translation:
Snort-snort, pub landlady,  
Take care of your beauty, Anna  
Don’t let your reputation go  
The tavern dogs roam around  
Uninvited mischief boys  
They cause stomach troubles  
Make you sick below the navel.  
If you lock up the town, lock it tight  
Give the key to Ottu  
Or maybe also to little Vestu.

label: entertainment
translation:
My father is a miracle worker,  
My mother is a miracle worker,  
They made me a wonderful coat,  
From patches and patches  
Of pigskin spikes,  
Of catskin legs,  
At the top was squirrel fur,  
In the middle patchy dog skin,  
At the back wore cat skin.

label: entertainment
translation:
Now the meals have been eaten,  
Now the drinks have been drunk.  
Only the songs remain unsung,  
Tunes remain unplayed;  
The cook's honor unacknowledged,  
The cook has diligently prepared the broth:  
Just the right amount of salt added.  
He brought herbs from Sweden,  
Salads brought from Germany,  
Onions from across the sea. -  
What I ate at the meal,  
I ate up all the food,  
And what I drank at the drink,  
I drank up the barrel of beer  
What was left of the food from the meal  
The bone is down, the skin is above,  
A piece of tender meat. -  
What remained after the food:  
The tail and the horns remained,  
The tail remained to sweep the sheathe.  
The horns remained to be pondered,  
The head remained to be carried home. -  
What remained from the barrel of drink  
The yeast settled below, the foam was above,  
The seed without clear beer.

label: entertainment
translation:
On its own proud bush branch,  
Hangs on a high rod.  
It bends the row of nails on the house,  
Asks at the family door's threshold:  
Help me onto the oven,  
Put me on the stove board,  
Lift me on the bottom of the stove’s smoke plate.  
From there I will roll to the vat,  
Slip into the halfway beer barrel.  
Oh, beers, bubble up,  
Beer crates rise up,  
Vats sputter and bubble.

label: entertainment
translation:
I walk through the rustling forest.  
I dress in the eerie street,  
I think the path is ticking,  
The trails are cracking.  
But the little path does not tick.  
Neither do the little trails crack.  
My tin path ticks to you.  
The quiet rods crack.  
A pearly horse lives.

label: entertainment
translation:
Oh, oh crazy one, where does the joke come from,  
From barley you can always make kvass  
Oh that barley mold,  
Dear old woman of oats,  
Taught to make beer,  
Drives anger into vodka.  
At home, a spindle is whirling  
A cone is bobbing in the bush  
It makes the men roar  
The girls dance without shoes  
The boys into half boots.

label: entertainment
translation:
Aidu-vaidu old pants  
I had three pairs of trousers at home  
Mother made the trousers, father made the trousers  
I had trousers before myself,  
Then there were three pairs of trousers in total  
One pair were clean wedding trousers  
The others were white leg trousers  
The third were worn courting trousers.

label: entertainment
translation:
I sing, why don’t I sing
I sing a song about a horse,
A saddleless steed
With a walnut for a head
Eyes made of stars in the sky
Eyelids made of dragon trees
Ears made of hemp leaves
Hooves made of birch sponges
A tail made of oats
A body made of hay shavings.
Then I go on a journey to Finland
I snap the Finnish bridge
I knock on the foundation beams
This horse doesn’t run because of the reins
Because of the thin whip
The horse runs because of the barley
It leaps because of the oats’ sheaf.

label: entertainment
translation:
Let us begin to go  
All the people will start to move  
All those young ones will falter  
We cause trouble within the family  
We waste money  
We eat up the bull’s feed  
We drink up the bull’s drink  
I hear and respond  
I will not leave here before  
I separate the tufts  
I take the wall beams on my back  
The shutters for the doorframe  
Reed ropes on the shoulder  
I devour the stove’s warmth  
Then I will start to go  
Then I will mark the mound  
The scar into the teiup  
The cross into the Riga rope  
Whoever wants to chase behind  
May take the mark from the mound  
The scar from the teiup  
The cross from the Riga rope  
Below I go down without  
Above I go under the red day  
Between I go the path of the five rainbows  
At six, at the break of dawn.

label: entertainment
translation:
Let's go, let's go, let's walk, let's walk  
Let's walk to the hilltop  
The land covered in liverwort  
Green, pink  
When will we arrive there  
Where we have long been awaited  
Long awaited  
There is no sound of a rooster's crow  
No rooster's crow, no hen's clucking  
No weak child's crying  
No mourning of widows. -  
Let's go, let's go, let's walk, let's walk  
Let's walk to the hilltop  
The land covered in liverwort  
Green, pink  
When will we arrive there  
Where the wind has made a room  
Water has rolled logs  
Rain has mossed the walls  
Fog has made new doors.

label: entertainment
translation:
Let's go chest to chest, let's go ear to ear  
Let's go chest to Riga  
Quietly towards Tallinn  
Let's go to Riga to spoil  
To Tallinn to kill  
The guard calls from the rampart  
The houseboy from the doorstep  
The little boy at the shop door  
Do not spoil little Riga  
Kill little Tallinn  
Let them bring salt to Riga  
Let them hammer money for Tallinn  
Boys to bring a headdress  
Women to wear patterned shawls  
Girls to carry the blue veil.

label: entertainment
translation:
Let's start our journey  
Our home is far away  
Five is to change a fence  
Six is for the river to dry up  
Seven is bitter soda  
Eight is a clever vow  
Nine is the Emajõgi River  
Ten is cold springs

label: entertainment
translation:
Where do we go against the night  
Against the night, against the water  
Against the gaze of darkness  
Against the shining of dawn  
Against the golden moon  
Perhaps we drown in the brook  
Perhaps we disappear on the shore  
Who searches for us in the brook  
Or who tries on the shore  
God searches in the brook  
Mary tries on the shore.

label: entertainment
translation:
I had a rich godfather  
He gave me a goat  
A little strap around the goat’s neck  
The wolf ate the goat, the strap stayed with me  
I put the strap around Kaie’s neck  
Kaie was eager to dance  
The strap broke, the pants tore  
The pants tore, the money ran out  
Then I took them to the smith in Viira  
To the smith in Viira, Ella’s brother  
“Take my straps and fix them  
Fix the torn pants  
Patch the money holes”

label: entertainment
translation:
A little bottle of vodka, little brother  
A little red-necked punch  
When I took you in  
You shoved me down  
A little beer, little ale  
A little fish, little neighbor  
The gentlemen of Viru drank vodka  
The women of Salla ate bread  
The forest maidens drank honey  
The wives of the men from Kal´la  
That's why I drank, little man  
Little boy

label: entertainment
translation:
What else do we drink but beer  
If you don’t decorate the path to beer  
Use the pitcher  
Throw the whips into the wild  
Throw the boards into the grove

label: entertainment
translation:
Row the swing, pull the swing  
Pull the swing to the field of bulls  
Where roosters eat gold  
And hens reach the yard  
Ducks have silver wings.

label: entertainment
translation:
A little vodka, a little winch  
A little beer, a little smoke  
A little darling, my dear;  
The beer warms me  
I make the beer hot,  
I heat a coat for the jug  
And a new coat for myself.  
But I started to feel unwell myself,  
Killed the little lark  
Why do you give me ugly drinks,  
Why bring joyless tobacco?  
Why not make the beer pretty,  
Heat a coat for the jug— – –

label: entertainment
translation:
I was called by the spring well,  
Kai shouted to me from the echo path:  
Run, boy, the horse needs watering,  
Servant boy, put on the saddle.  
I am going to Finland for a visit.  
Crossing the Finnish bridge,  
Knocking on the plank foundation,  
I am going to my father-in-law’s door,  
I am going to my mother-in-law’s door;  
Hello father-in-law, hello mother-in-law:  
May I come inside the room,  
To take care of the horse,  
Not to tie the foal to the fence.  
Father-in-law heard, mother-in-law heard,  
Soon they answered:  
Ride into my house,  
Here is my little daughter,  
The household girl, the maiden,  
Take a blanket, carry a carpet,  
Wipe my apples from the branches,  
Wipe the dust from my back,  
Spread the grips by the boards.

label: entertainment
translation:
What is wrong with the boys from Vinnu,  
Or is it the fault of the boys from Äntu;  
The wheels run without money,  
The spokes are broken off,  
The hubs are in pieces.

label: entertainment
translation:
Little instrument, little joy,
Dear kannel, little playmate,
An instrument cannot feed alone,
A kannel cannot live without a companion.
The instrument walks the tavern road
Looking for a beer girl,
Trying the vodka chamber,
Let's go singing through the forest
Whose voice then carries far,
That one the groom buys a hat for.

label: entertainment
translation:
Others went early to Tiole  
I go to Iljapeal to fetch  
I hope for the stallion's strength  
For the stallion’s full step  
For the mare’s gait by Kõrvi.  
The stallion did no plowing for me  
The mare didn’t plow the wet earth  
The stallion didn’t wet the rye stalks.  
Surely that lout forced me  
To plow the start of the land  
Wet land by the hill's edge  
Swamp mud by the bog’s edge  
Still, I plowed a piece in defiance  
I left one furrow for the field  
Plowed one, left another  
Then I got ahead of the others  
By the time of the Tiopäev hearing  
Waiting for food to be brought  
For the white bucket to be carried  
But I saw food being brought  
For the black bucket to be carried  
Immediately my heart fell sad  
My heart started to ache  
Look at the thing I was given  
The food that was brought to me  
The middle grew cold  
Velvetfully listed  
Burnt bread crusts:  
I pick them up and get angry  
Scatter the chaff on the grass  
Scatter the chaff in the yard corner  
I stuck the whip into the corner  
I struck the walls of the sauna  
I myself went to Aru tavern  
Took a few shots of vodka  
Two handfuls from the jug  
A strong mug of beer  
I felt my legs turning  
My legs weakening  
Surely the legs will lead home  
The calves will go to the bed  
The knees will put themselves to sleep  
The soles of the feet into the bed.

label: entertainment
translation:
Juhan Juss killed a cat,  
Made a coat for Kaie,  
A foundation cloth for Anne,  
A quilt for Mari,  
Slippery shoes for Liisu;  
Then he went through our yard,  
Ate our communal food,  
Licked our child's butt.

label: entertainment
translation:
Oh little king, little king  
Why didn’t you come to me last year  
When the commands were carried out  
Five letters were taken  
Six letters were written  
Seven messages were sent  
Now you have come in the time of harvest  
In the light springtime  
In the cool autumn time  
Now you are sewing clothes for the mother  
Mending the neckbands.  
Oh little king, little king  
Give me the poor gold  
The poor gold from my sister’s hands  
My poor neck protection  
These are not for the mother-in-law  
These are not for myself  
I got this for boiling soup  
For beating the priest’s thigh.  
Whose soul is blossoming  
Whose wreath is being placed?  
Liisu’s soul is blossoming  
Liisu’s wreath is being placed  
Cast away your souls, little Liisu  
Cast away your souls, lay down your wreaths  
Throw away those silver curls.

label: entertainment
translation:
The doll was called to the village  
Across the field of oats  
The doll had no time to go  
The doll was in the fabric  
Between fine reeds.  
Lower, lower, doll  
Lower alone two paces  
Already father will die  
Father’s grave is being dug  
A grave deep with an iron bottom  
Nine fathoms deep  
Eight cubits wide  
A cubit plus ten more -  
Lower, lower, doll  
Lower alone two paces  
Already mother will die  
Mother’s grave is being dug  
A grave deep, iron-bottomed  
Nine fathoms deep  
Eight cubits wide  
A cubit plus ten more -  
Lower, lower, doll  
Lower alone two paces  
Already sister will die  
Sister’s grave is being dug  
A grave deep with an iron bottom  
Nine fathoms deep  
Eight cubits wide  
A cubit plus ten more. -  
Lower, lower, doll  
Lower alone two paces  
Already brother will die  
Brother’s grave is being dug  
A grave deep with an iron bottom  
Nine fathoms deep  
Eight cubits wide  
A cubit plus ten more. - - -  
Rise, rise, doll  
Rise alone two paces  
Already father is alive  
Sits on a silk bed  
Golden doll in hand  
Silver flowers around the doll. - - -  
Rise, rise, doll  
Rise alone two paces  
Already mother is alive  
Sits on a silk bed  
Golden doll in hand  
Silver flowers around the doll. - -  
Rise, rise, doll  
Rise alone two paces  
Already sister is alive  
Sits on a silk bed  
Golden doll in hand  
Silver flowers around the doll. -  
Rise, rise, doll  
Rise alone two paces  
Already brother is alive  
Sits on a silk bed  
Golden doll in hand  
Silver flowers around the doll. -

label: entertainment
translation:
We must take by force the troops  
What I give to the troops  
I have not taken the ire sword  
The cat's fur not pulled out  
The rat's intestines not cleaned out  
The pot not brought to the fire  
The scales cold in the cellar  
This I give to the troops  
To these troops.

label: entertainment
translation:
I still drink from a straw,  
Sing with the straw stick,  
Come home from the straw.  
Monday and Tuesday.  
In the middle a fine shepherd.  
Thursday I mow the hay,  
Friday I rake the dry hay,  
Saturday I make a wide pile,  
Sunday I go fishing.

label: entertainment
translation:
Drink, you, bear the neck on the throat,  
Take against the copper breast.  
Surely the legs will carry the tissue,  
The knees will go to bed.  
The shins will set the bed.  
Let the feet trot.  
Move the shins well,  
Burn the knees.  
The thighs travel quickly.  
So that the tissue is ready before dawn,  
The thighs lie down before the day.

label: entertainment
translation:
I went to the edge of the great sea,  
Happened to fall asleep there,  
To see a dream,  
I found a little horn,  
And also a little whistle,  
I started to play the horn,  
Kept blowing the whistle,  
Then came together the Kolga Germans,  
The beautiful girls of Hiio,  
The maiden girls with little brooches,  
The dear ones with twisted necks.

label: entertainment
translation:
Hüia hüia our instrument,  
Laala dear our kannel.  
Feet want to dance.  
The room wants to be swept new,  
The floor wants to be stomped.  
The edges of the walls want to be pressed.  
Little instrument, little joy.  
Dear kannel, little plaything:  
Shall I say it again?  
I sing it back anew:  
No instrument without a master,  
No kannel without companionship.  
The instrument walks to the barn road.  
Searching for beer houses.  
Pulling a load of vodka stench.

label: entertainment
translation:
I still drink even with a straw.  
I drank bulls and horses.  
I drank bulls from the hike,  
Do not ruin the rake.  
I drank the tavern to its ear,  
To the small town to its hall,  
To the market bright red.  
To the linen town road.  
To the water-gray mill road.  
On Monday I drank from under the bow,  
On Tuesday I drank from under the shirt,  
Wednesday was a nice hat,  
On Thursday I drank among them,  
On Friday I drank from the chest of the sled,  
On Saturday I drank a wide belt,  
On Sunday I drank the pants off.  
On Monday I slept my sleep,  
On Tuesday I went to work.  
I set the plows on the edge,  
I plucked the ridge on the furrow,  
Pour the chaff, pour the grain,  
To the row an old red one.

label: entertainment
translation:
Straw Woman Krõõdukene,  
City Woman Liisukene.  
Village Woman Annekene,  
Fashionable Woman Maretukene.  
Are your rooms swept?  
Are your chambers cleaned?  
Are your windows polished?  
Are your chairs in the room?  
Are your benches covered with rushes?  
Silks are coming in,  
To Kalev’s chambers.  
Let me say it again:  
I will sing it once more,  
Soon back to the old tune.  
Straw Woman’s dogs took away,  
They won’t give wine without reason,  
Beer without buying,  
Mead without minding,  
Kvass without pouring,  
Water without whining.

label: entertainment
translation:
I rode a bit through Turkish field,  
Half a verst through Blackberry field,  
A little along Narva road.  
I went through Latvian field.  
At last, I reached the Russian path.  
I did not covet it;  
I saw in the village of Nao,  
In the hayfields of Hillevere,  
In the coppice of Kullevere,  
In the meadows of Varivere.  
Dogs plowed, Bulls barked,  
Girls made sleds,  
Women stretched wheel shafts,  
The pig kneaded dough,  
A woman rummaged through the meadows,  
Cats wove cloth,  
Mice snapped threads.  
The sheep went to the barn to lay eggs,  
The hen brought two little lambs.  
The horse brought a bull-calf,  
The cow brought a cicada calf.

label: entertainment
translation:
Oh king, little king,  
Rich Saxon of Riga.  
Why didn’t you come to us last year?  
When the rivers ran without oil,  
When the old men brewed vodka.  
We brewed kvass in the cellars,  
Beat the ashes for firewood,  
Cleared the streets of mud,  
The village smelled of cumin,  
The village pastures of sulfur,  
Now you come to the white time,  
Now you come to the sad month,  
To the light spring,  
To the noisy autumn,  
To the winter snowfall.  
Now you strip off clothes,  
Break neck chains,  
Large brooches from the chest,  
Golden necklaces from the neck,  
Save the wreath from the head.  
Oh king, little king,  
Rich Saxon of Riga,  
Give me back poor gold,  
Poor gold, poor copper,  
Neither were these your shares,  
Nor were these your precious gifts,  
Nor was a fine feast brought,  
These I earned myself.  
I got the brooch from kneading bread,  
The necklace from boiling broth,  
The belt from beating the brachet,  
I bought myself a dwelling.  
Oh king, little king,  
Rich Saxon of Riga,  
What shall I offer you?  
I have one ox for plowing,  
One horse for raking,  
One cow for milking,  
One sheep in the barn,  
One pig in the sty,  
One hen on the roof,  
What shall I offer you?  
The ox I have for plowing the field,  
The horse for harrowing,  
The cow for milking the family,  
The sheep for shading the family,  
The pig for feeding the family,  
The rooster for crowing in the morning,  
The dog was outside barking.

label: entertainment
translation:
A pies of a pipe, a cloak of grass,
A whip of hay branches,
Who cut the finger?
That lad.
Yes, that lad.
Who leapt into the cradle,
That lad, the boy.
Where did he get the scarf?
He took a neckerchief from around the neck,
Tore apart the chin cloth,
Shattered the headscarf to pieces.
The scarf is gone,
The village lad will buy a new one,
The boy from Viru brings a striped one,
The boy from Sweden brings a rosy one,
The German boy brings a velvet one,
The country boy brings a muddy one.
Where did he get the ribbon?
He took a clogs strap from the calf.
The strap is gone,
The village girl will make a new one,
Make a new wavy one,
Put latticework inside,
Insert ribbon patterns.

label: entertainment
translation:
Go to the corner, young men,  
Under the bench, pipe drinkers,  
Under the table, lazy boys.  
Brother Mino is coming to spar,  
Brother Mino’s swords are crooked.  
The sea foam is white,  
Whiter still is my dear brother.  
The seaweed is straight,  
Straighter still is my dear brother.  
The long reed is long,  
Make it longer still, my dear brother.  
What is my dear brother looking for?  
My dear brother is looking for a bride.  
Where does the brother’s bride stand?  
She stands here among the crowd.  
Who, dear, will take his neck?  
Who, darling, will hold the bridle,  
Who will take the silk on their lap?

label: entertainment
translation:
In front dances the giant,  
Behind dances the powerless.  
Then the pig snorts,  
Then the bull bellows,  
Then the lightning cracks.  
Sometimes a poor man dances.  
The bull dances in the yoke,  
In the yoke and in the bank,  
In Pepermanis rummaging,  
The calf wants to dance.

label: entertainment
translation:
We had a hawk bird  
In our lord's garden.  
It caused quite a fuss,  
For it had some faults.  
It ate all the pepperberries,  
Devoured the best of them,  
Then went itself into the forest,  
To the rich family's woods.  
Some had time to chase after it,  
Some to catch it with nets,  
Some demanded notes,  
Some took a shot with a gun.  
The stewards' boys, the Möldre boys,  
Blacksmiths' sons, stable boys,  
Chamber boys with slipper feet,  
German boys with boot heels.  
They had time to chase after it,  
They caught it with nets,  
They demanded notes,  
They took a shot with a gun.  
One man was there in the forest,  
With an oak leaf on his shoulder.  
He was supposed to shoot the bird,  
Come, hunter, and shoot it down.

label: entertainment
translation:
Swing of the ship’s shine of the ship,  
Move the ship towards the town,  
Swing towards the corner of the swamp.  
Go from the town to bring a ribbon,  
From the shop to bring a gate ribbon.  
From the German box, to the card edge,  
Move the ship below the town,  
From under the town, to Riga,  
From under Riga to Vyborg,  
From Vyborg to the Russian road.  
The watchman calls from the rampart.  
From the shop boy by the door,  
The furnace man at the furnace threshold.  
Long ago Pärnu blessed a cow,  
Sang a speckled rooster in Riga,  
Roared a black bull of the sea.  
Young men, dear brothers,  
Come to buy goods,  
Here is an expensive merchant ship,  
Here men have hats,  
Women have linen handkerchiefs,  
Boys have pipe gate ribbons,  
Girls have blue stones.  
“Five old ones, and six strong ones,  
Seven clear silver coins.”

label: entertainment
translation:
Liisukene lipsukene,  
A little darling with cute lips,  
A little snap upon seeing eyes,  
A little crack upon hearing the ear.  
That was famous in the miller's mind,  
Pleasant in the minds of the manor owners,  
Smooth in the minds of the shepherd boys,  
Very beautiful in the gentleman's mind.  
Liisu went to the tavern to walk,  
Fell down on her back,  
Straight onto the pig's back,  
Eyes shut on the pig's back.  
The poor pig was troubled,  
Beautiful Liisu was showing off.  
The poor pig got a painful blow,  
Beautiful Liisu got a blow to her soul.

label: entertainment
translation:
Let's go, let's go, let's walk, let's walk,  
Let's make tea from the treetop,  
From the ground with liver hair,  
Who came to answer us?  
The white Saxons came to answer,  
The white young gentlemen answered.  
I asked to strike the dog with a whip.  
Could not strike the dog with a whip.  
Sulevipoeg came fiercely,  
Kalevipoeg came stubbornly,  
Ole had a good horse,  
Kalev had an expensive stallion.  
Under the horse was a plow,  
A big body smoked,  
Men thought of forest smoke,  
Boys of tree smoke,  
Girls of brake smoke,  
Women of Narva city smoke.  
The horse of the great man smokes,  
The tall hat scorches,  
Under the plow, a gray stallion.

label: entertainment
translation:
Ask, ask, little frost,  
Strike the winter weather.  
I am freezing at the hand,  
My toes are aching.  
Where has the frost bitten the throat?  
The throat bartered for a coat!  
Standing on the wall of straws,  
Watching at the tavern’s beam,  
Under five distilleries,  
Under two beer mugs.

label: entertainment
translation:
Buy a cat with a curled eye,  
A curled-eyed needle tail,  
In the peel of a bad woman,  
Licked milk from a lazy woman,  
Ate butter from a greedy woman.  
I will beat the cat!  
The cat went to the well in clogs,  
Its long tail was dragging.  
I ran to the village.

label: entertainment
translation:
Here departed many proud mothers,  
The regiment left with rich mothers,  
The flag went to the city soldiers,  
A proper flock left as maidens.  
From here rode great Germans,  
Lords who came late.  
They did not make the roads,  
Nor did they make the land bitter.  
The tall tree of the forest thunders,  
The wide Väila sings songs.  
We are two like little chickens!  
A pair like ducklings.  
We make the road beautiful,  
The beautiful road, the bitter land,  
The tall tree of the forest thunders.  
We alone become poets,  
Poets and singers,  
We write joyful stories,  
We sing the beauty of the wide road.

label: entertainment
translation:
Farts long, long farts,  
Our manor’s men are tall.  
Who is pulling the long farts,  
Who is breaking the broad bellows?  
The broad shirts are sizzling,  
It is the little mischievous boy.  
Who burns the rooster?  
Sings until the wide white dawn,  
Spins until mid-morning,  
So that the young maiden.

label: entertainment
translation:
Mihkel, Mihkel, take me to the forest,  
Carry me on your back to the spruce grove.  
We have many Mihkels:  
Old Mihkel, the resin beard,  
Big Mihkel, the smoky beard,  
Little Mihkel, the milky beard,  
Mihkel-Kihkel, the goat beard.  
If this Mihkel were my brother,  
I would surely know what to do;  
Tie him by the pig’s tail,  
Put a tick on his butt,  
A black bull in the mouth of the pit,  
A gray bull in the mouth of the hole,  
Between the speckled bells.

label: entertainment
translation:
Our men like rascals,  
Our boys like scoundrels;  
We shoot and cheer,  
Scatter the manor's bread,  
Have fun, play tricks,  
Fight each other,  
Carouse and revel,  
Fire shots at Kaie,  
Pellets at sick Anne,  
Down fallen Mai,  
Finally, booze for Rein.

label: entertainment
translation:
Here comes Siim, here Siim’s servant,  
a noble father among all others.  
Here comes the young maiden,  
a beauty with curly hair,  
a spark in her hair,  
a little bird with a linen cap.  
Here sits Siim, here Siim’s servant,  
a noble father among all others.  
Here sits the young maiden,  
a beauty with curly hair,  
a spark in her hair,  
a little bird with a linen cap.  
Here walks Siim, here Siim’s servant,  
a noble father among all others.  
Here walks the young maiden,  
a beauty with curly hair,  
a spark in her hair,  
a little bird with a linen cap.  
Here greets Siim, here Siim’s servant,  
a noble father among all others.  
Silent stands the young maiden,  
a beauty with curly hair,  
a spark in her hair,  
a little bird with a linen cap.  
Siim offers his hand, Siim’s servant’s hand,  
a noble father among all others,  
the young maiden rejects the hand,  
a beauty with curly hair,  
a spark in her hair,  
a little bird with a linen cap.  
Here leaves Siim, here Siim’s servant,  
a noble father among all others.  
Here leaves the young maiden,  
a beauty with curly hair,  
a spark in her hair,  
a little bird with a linen cap.

label: entertainment
translation:
Row the swing, pull the swing,  
Row the swing to the distant land  
Where the spruces turn yellow,  
The aspen leaves turn green  
Alders stand straight and blue,  
White birches flow, –  
Where the roosters eat gold,  
Roosters gold, hens beware  
Geese are greenish silver.

label: entertainment
translation:
I had to go on a journey,  
Long ago set out on the road.  
I set off, it started to rain,  
Snow fell in heavy drifts,  
Water soaked the yoke straps;  
The sled creaked in the Riga style,  
The runners in the Tartu style,  
The shaft poles in the Pärnu style,  
The harness ropes in the Finnish style,  
The lower ones on top,  
The lower shafts,  
The upper sled poles.  
Don’t go astray from the bright path,  
Home to dry bread,  
To tear off the salt herring,  
To lick the leftover lard,  
To babble like a water frog.

label: entertainment
translation:
O king, little king,  
Rich Riga merchant!  
Why did you not come to us last year,  
When the rivers ran without oil,  
The springs flowed with vodka,  
Our cellars brewed beer,  
The city bridges were made of onions,  
The city ramparts of maples?  
Now you come in the time of hardship,  
Now you come in the sad month,  
Now you tear off your clothes,  
Remove the wreath from your head.  
O king, little king,  
Rich Riga merchant!  
Give up the half gold,  
The poor gold, the poor copper,  
That is not yours to have,  
Nor your wife's to have.  
That I myself have obtained:  
I got a buckle from bread sucking,  
A necklace from lime boiling,  
A belt from head shearing,  
In summer from heavy work,  
In winter from stamping flax,  
In spring from spinning.

label: entertainment
translation:
Little raspberry, little raspberry,  
Did you see my orchard?  
Little maiden, little maiden,  
What color is your horse?  
A squirrel's fur,  
The southern lark's feather,  
Bear's fur, covered with dew.  
It went through our yard,  
On its back a blue blanket,  
Wide straps on the saddle,  
A golden rope trailing after,  
Stirrups with curtains on its feet,  
Golden sparks,  
Copper bands on its head.  
Young men of the village,  
Come to buy in the orchard,  
Come to see the little colt;  
Here the horse has eaten barley,  
Eaten barley, grown on oats,  
Played on the flour mat.  
Upwards, Ali, jump to your ears,  
Jump to your ears on the roof,  
Try, Ali, in the garden,  
Was the garden made by men,  
Or was the garden made by women?  
If the garden was made by men,  
It was made from poles,  
Driven together from the beginnings.  
If the garden was made by women,  
It was made from daughters,  
Laid by mother and children,  
Woven from red twigs.

label: entertainment
translation:
Where does it come from, where does it come from  
Ani ani white ani ani white  
Where does it come from, where does it come from  
Idle, idle lynx  
From the seashore, from the seashore  
Ani ani white  
What are they doing there then  
Idle, idle lynx  
Washing Anipoeg  
Ani ani white  
Is it washing my sons  
Idle, idle lynx  
You weren’t even there  
Ani ani white  
Do you want to come through  
Idle, idle lynx  
And we want to come through  
Ani ani white  
We have golden temples  
Idle, idle lynx  
We have copper gates  
Ani ani white.

label: entertainment
translation:
I had a rich godfather  
He gave me a little goat  
A little bell on the goat's neck  
The wolf ate the goat, the bell stayed with me  
I put the bell on the girl’s neck  
I went with the girl to church  
The village girls are smiling  
You are not worthy of smiling like a girl  
Like a young woman worthy of.

label: entertainment
translation:
But I went on the wedding road  
On Black Matsi's wedding road  
An ox was slaughtered for Mats  
But I was called the cook  
I put the meat to cook  
The duck roast to stew  
Along came the cat with quick eyes  
Ate that meat that was cooking  
That duck roast that was stewing  
I went to catch the cat  
The cat ran into the forest  
I went to find a rope  
From Tõnu I brought a tar rope  
Just as well I brought a flax rope  
From the birch I brought a hemp rope  
Then I went to catch the cat  
The hemp ropes tangled  
The flax rope twisted  
The tar rope pulled it out  
The mice laughed in the corner  
Ast ast ast ast little cat  
Where are my six golden sons?  
They are all in the cat's backside  
In Black Mats's belly.

label: entertainment
translation:
Liisakene little ribbon  
A little snap upon seeing the eye  
A little hop upon hearing the ear  
An old sneaker in the shadow  
Liisu heard the sound of an instrument  
She went out shining  
The floor beneath was pounding  
Hopping by the boy's ear  
Liisu heard the sound of a rod  
Clinks hitting the ramp  
Immediately then falling into the warehouse  
Clink escaping into the chest.

label: entertainment
translation:
In the hollow, a pine cone calls into the stream  
A cone crackles into the bush  
In the grassy rye field  
Come here, young men  
Take me to the sack at home  
Set me on the bench by the stove  
Put me on the board to dry  
From there I roll into the cellar  
But I slip into the half-beer glass  
Drift into the beer mug  
Sink into the beer anchor  
Make me a good beer  
That takes away men's senses  
Half of the senses from the boys' heads  
Thanks to wise women's heads  
Men grumble without hats  
Women dance without cloth  
Girls without belts  
Boys with crooked backs  
One drinks from one hand to the other  
Mothers-in-law, mothers with buckets  
Look, I drink from the pail  
I feed my head through the pipe  
Do I drink from the cupboard, or from the jug  
Or do I drink from the colorful cup  
The cone makes the eyes colorful  
The jug makes the neck stiff.

label: entertainment
translation:
Many have gone to the proud mother  
A few lines to the rich mother  
A couple have gone to their families  
They have not traveled the roads,  
Traveled the roads, wandered  
The tall tree in the forest stands.  
I alone, a poor child  
I serve the road  
Travel the roads, wander  
The tall tree in the forest stands.  
Out in the wide meadow  
So that the road will not take me  
Out across the wide fields;  
The tall tree in the forest speaks.  
Let others travel the road  
Across the wide meadow  
The tall tree in the forest speaks.

label: entertainment
translation:
I go to the town to the taverns  
And I go to the shore to the huts  
I am not greeted in the town  
Nor given a handshake in the borough.  
Indeed, the townsfolk mock me  
Some are even hostile.  
Is he the king of Kuuramaa  
Or is he truly from Pärnu?  
That he does not greet in the town  
Nor gives a handshake in the borough.  
I certainly hear and respond.  
Oh, you foolish townsfolk  
You do not recognize the farm boy  
Nor respect the humble soul.  
I seek my own way  
Giving my horse reins in my hand  
With the colt tethered behind.

label: entertainment
translation:
The sprouting grain path was crooked  
The straw woman walked crookedly  
But poured crooked liquor glasses  
Investigation beer tubes  
Slope pots on the slope  
Edge crusts of bread crust.

label: entertainment
translation:
Droplet droplet little needle  
Droplet needle-eye  
The needle did not disappear in the seat  
My needle disappeared into the needles  
Sewing new humming  
Arranging family things  
In the evening I sew sister’s shirt  
At twilight brother’s shirt  
At dawn sweetheart’s shirt  
In darkness father-in-law’s shirt  
In gloom fiancé’s shirt  
The needle disappeared in the heath  
In the woods  
In the golden-eye spruce forest  
In the field of oats  
Young men brothers  
Some were rich in money  
Some were famous for their purses  
Come to demand the needle  
To listen for the golden-eye  
Raise the needle, jump the needle  
Raise the round needle  
Jump the square needle  
Tie the needle’s legs sharp  
You are my soul needle  
You are the smooth sequin needle  
The needle that sparks and sizzles  
Raise the barley bean  
Jump the bear’s oats  
Bring the mountainous beans  
With a bunch of oats

label: entertainment
translation:
We walk through the village  
The horse neighs  
The dusty street rattles  
Even the iron chains creak  
The cuckoo calls from the hollow  
The gray bird from the ridge  
The swallow on the eaves  
The recruit sings on the wagon.

label: entertainment
translation:
On Monday, I drank a new coat  
On Tuesday, I drank a work jacket  
On Wednesday, a nice hat  
On Thursday, I drank a maiden’s apron  
On Friday, I drank the gelding’s thighs  
On Saturday, I drank the cow’s bow  
On Sunday, I drank the pants off  
Then I drank only naked  
The cross-bearer was left without clothes.

label: entertainment
translation:
Let's walk along the meadows of wildflowers  
Let's walk through the blue groves  
So the golden reeds don't sway  
So the silent stems don't bend  
Not a single milk-cap mushroom  
Who has golden reeds  
Our girls have golden reeds  
Who has silent stems  
Our women have silent stems  
Who has milk-cap mushrooms  
Our men have milk-cap mushrooms.

label: entertainment
translation:
The bog contaminates the meadow  
From behind it corrupts the power  
Then here a feather  
In between corrupts the poor man  
The awake drives the dormant  
Dear work and wool work  
Three times around  
Estut sestut sem vem  
Whisk whisk madipu mall  
Around the sheath tongue arrow  
Raise the dance bring the maiden  
Quickly stone under the mortar  
Alle sahkadi sah sah  
Piibe painti piale  
Put paint into the glass

label: entertainment
translation:
Your maidens are coming  
Your maiden has beaten the lieri  
Your mother in the manor  
What shall I give the maiden?  
There is no gold nor silver  
No old copper coins  
There are no small pennies. -  
There is no gold nor silver  
No old copper coins  
There are no small pennies  
I want a young maiden  
Silk fingers, silk thumbs  
Weavers of strong cloth  
Flappers of canvas  
Papershell crackers  
Who put letters into gloves  
Old eyes into canvas  
Shirt tails into shirts

label: entertainment
translation:
The family daughter, a young maiden  
When she hears the sound of an instrument  
She straightens her brow  
And steps outside from the threshing floor.  
Softly, she tiptoes  
Now to dance by the oak tree  
To bend the young spruces  
To sway the apple tree  
To tremble on the rowan tree.  
When I hear the sound of the staff  
Then I walk towards the bed  
Step towards the threshing floor  
There I sleep, my little berry  
My beautiful little flower  
I rest, a little wedding bride.

label: entertainment
translation:
Why are you girls smiling?  
You frighten me too much:  
That I have a shaky horse,  
A colt from a pea stalk.  
I went along the narrow paths,  
The crooked trails.  
The road began to tick,  
The paths began to crack;  
My tin sleigh was ticking,  
My iron horse was cracking.  
A cuckoo fell on the bay horse,  
A swallow on the head,  
A wren on the crest,  
A gray bird on the shaft.  
Village girls were glancing at me,  
Village maidens were laughing at me!  
Where did that fool buy a horse?  
And that fool took a wife:  
A horse from where I bought mine,  
A wife from where I took mine—  
A horse from Oblika Hill,  
A wife from Nappu mill.  
The horse was from Oblika’s Oblika,  
The wife on the May strawberry.  
The horse brings a bunch of Oblika hay,  
The wife brings a handful of May strawberries.

label: entertainment
translation:
Go to the corner, young men,
Pipe men under the bench,
Big jaws under the table,
Sow pigs under the bed,
Tat whiskers behind the wall!
My brother is coming to fence,
The sow pig is coming to pry,
The clog is coming to wash,
The twisted sock is coming to roll,
The nice heel is coming to turn!

label: entertainment
translation:
Oh wonder, or no wonder,
What I saw in Näu village:
Dogs were plowing, oxen were barking,
Flails were carrying water,
Carding boards were boiling lye;
Girls were making sledges,
Women were cutting wheel spokes,
Father was making yoke pieces for the ox,
The old wise man was making beams for the storehouse,
Men were walking to the tavern road,
They were whistling over tavern beer.

label: entertainment
translation:
Be healthy, brewers of beer,  
Brewers of beer and barley beer,  
Makers of angry vodka,  
Who put these three together:  
First, the water is liquid,  
Second, the malt is sweet,  
Third, you are foolish madmen:  
This took the minds from men's heads,  
Half the minds from boys' heads,  
Filled the daughters' bosoms;  
Men made noise without hats,  
Women danced without skirts,  
Boys half drunk.

label: entertainment
translation:
Reach the boat, row the boat,  
Reach the boat to that shore:  
Where those roosters have eaten gold  
Roosters of gold, hens of silver,  
Ducks of shining copper,  
Crows of old brass,  
Nest birds of pennies,  
Wise birds of thalers,  
Where those cabbages have grown  
Cabbages up to the height of the spruce.

label: entertainment
translation:
A slender little girl  
A young maiden  
Let's go on Saturday for a purple petal  
Onto the top of the hill  
What will we find there on the ground  
Six gilded belts  
A hundred German silk shirts  
Where will we put these gold pieces  
We will sew silver threads  
We'll hump them onto the hat  
We'll paint them onto the gate  
There we'll put the gold  
We will sew silver threads  
Oh oh oh oh brother  
Let it be straight by tomorrow  
By next Friday  
By New Year's Eve evening.

label: entertainment
translation:
The rye harvesters are coming  
The rye harvester has struck the field  
The old woman's manor's maid  
The old woman's two chambers  
The old woman's scythe blade  
What can I give the harvester?  
There is no gold nor silver  
No copper, old money  
No small coins at all  
No gold nor silver  
No copper, old money  
No small coins at all  
I wish for a young maiden  
Silky fingers, nimble hands  
Hard fabric weavers  
Paper bangers  
Lecture rattlers  
Who put letters in gloves  
Two letters in fabric  
Herring eyes in canvas  
Perch scales in shirts  
Who knows how to walk fire  
How to cross a bitter fleet  
How to lie without sparks

label: entertainment
entertainment
translation:
Where have they put the throat to the floor,  
Where have they put the windpipe coat?  
At every tavern I drank to the floor,  
To Kapu Cross a coat;  
To the big tavern I drank my socks,  
In the cold the shoes remain.

label: entertainment
translation:
Oh wonder, oh wonder  
What a wonder I saw  
Between Kuksema village  
In the Varivere pine forest  
In the buildings of Olustvere  
Dogs were plowing, oxen were harrowing  
A sheep went to the table to lay eggs  
A hen brought two lambs  
A horse brought a gentleman calf  
A cow brought a blond chick.

label: entertainment
translation:
Young men, tender brothers.  
If you are lowly, buy Mustad,  
If you are noble, buy Kõrvid.  
Buy Oller's horses,  
Leeland’s bays and stallions.  
Ten-ruble hats,  
Hundred-ruble saddles.  
Ride to the wedding at Soare manor.  
To that young lady’s wedding,  
Oh, how I turn my eyes,  
With strength in neck and hands.  
"If only I had a horse of my own,  
My own mare, my own saddle,  
I would ride to the wedding at Soare manor,  
To that young lady’s wedding.  
When the lady invites us to the wedding,  
Then I would ride proudly,  
And step out gallantly."

label: entertainment
translation:
I pour beers from the jugs  
I throw whips to the little whip  
Cap boards to the little bog  
I rush bottoms to the field  
There grew big islands  
Big islands, wide plains  
A wet pine grove  
On every top a titmouse  
On every end a squirrel  
In every treetop a songbird.

label: entertainment
translation:
The beer made me warm  
I make the beer hot  
I heat the coats on the heel  
To the little bear a new shoe  
But the beer made me dizzy  
Moving feet in the city  
It took the minds from men's heads  
Half the minds from boys' heads  
At the gaze of the women’s eyes  
At the sight of the daughters’ grace.

label: entertainment
translation:
Oh, oh, Ots Matsi  
Did you see Kadak Matsi  
Let it come to me as raw meat  
Full of lice flesh  
Bedbug as broth  
Bog as a dry part.

label: entertainment
translation:
Alled sang, Malled sang  
Girls sang down by the village.  
Dear ones killed me  
On the cobblestones.  
Where then did they bury the young maiden  
Under the berry mound in the bog?  
From the maiden grew a dear birch —  
What will be made from that birch?  
They speak of the violin  
Where one can play the kannel (Estonian zither)  
And blow the beautiful instrument?  
Let’s take the kannel to the chamber  
Where can the kannel get its curved sides?  
From the jawbone of a salmon.  
Where can the kannel get its curved strings?  
From the hair of the young maiden.  
Let's try with fingertips  
The hammering of the iron striker,  
Beat with your own stick,  
To put the young maiden to sleep,  
To lull her into a new life.  
The fingerboards whispered,  
The soundboards rumbled,  
Such a child cannot be made —  
A calm soul is needed.

label: entertainment
translation:
We go up to the hill by the meadow  
Among the blue feathers,  
We go shoulder to shoulder - marching ear to ear  
We go shoulder to shoulder towards Riga  
Towards Talli town in the back  
We go to Riga to rob  
To kill in Talli town  
To burn Põltsamaa  
The pig ruins Riga city  
The sheep kills Talli town  
The piglet burns Põltsamaa.  
We will leave salt to bring to Riga  
Money to bang in Talli town  
To bring a comb to Anne  
Ear rings to Krõeda  
Ribbons to Liisu  
Boys to bring tobacco  
Daughters to bring blue stones.

label: entertainment
translation:
Curved one, sexton’s son  
Virve-colored Westerner  
Where do I lay the curved one  
Curved one, sexton’s son  
Virve-colored Westerner?  
Behind the garden fence  
In the furrow of tall stitches  
Among wide leaves  
There he stands unlaid to rest  
Untouched by a dear hand  
Unfelt by a young finger  
Where shall we put the curved one to sleep?  
Right by the stove. In a woolen basket  
A fine boy at the ear,  
Wearing a multicolored jacket.

label: entertainment
translation:
Rise up, old man  
Wash your eyes, old man  
Pants on, old man  
Vest on, old man  
Feet together, old man  
Warm head, old man  
Hat on head, old man  
Scarf on neck, old man  
Sweater on, old man  
Overcoat on, old man  
Belt on waist, old man  
Pipe in mouth, old man  
Gloves on hands, old man  
Seek your old man  
Seek your careful one  
Touch your furry one.  
What is born from your spit  
Fits into a berry basket  
What is better from your mind  
Kinder from your heart  
How your companion.

label: entertainment
translation:
Bloom, piggy pig  
Golden-haired little golden one  
Iron-haired little harnessed one.  
Go to the mountain to root around  
Root the mountains, root the pines.  
Root the spruces on the hills  
Old saunas on the backs  
Bundles on the behinds  
Come, come young men.  
Come to slaughter the pig  
To stick the hooks in the throat  
To hold the kilts tight  
Brothers to take blood  
Sisters to prepare the salt  
Dogs to do the trick  
Bring these pitchforks to the feast

label: entertainment
translation:

Crows with old money.

translation:

The moon with golden rings

With clothes full of stars

Rings with golden sparkle

translation:

label: entertainment

Our two peasants,

For the winter behind Russia.

Carry a corral chapel,  
A long rowan tower,  
A wide tower lantern.

label: entertainment
translation:
Here, here comes Siim,

A noble master  
Among all the others.  
Let us through!

Fix them!

With silk, with thread,  
With old felt yarn.

label: entertainment
translation:
King, little king!

In the harsh autumn rain,  
In the light spring rain.

A squirrel scurries up the mountain  
A cone rattles in the pinecone

From the river, to buzz
