All the village dogs bark  
All the old women stare  
A little neat one for the smith  
A little wreath for Pärtel

label: youth_life
translation:
When the boy died,  
Where was he buried?  
In Kuuramaa under a spruce,  
In Läänemaa under a alder.  
Who visited the boy's grave?  
Every Sunday pagans came,  
Every Friday quarrelsome ones,  
Every Saturday lantern bearers.  
What grew on the boy's grave?  
Thistles and bindweed,  
Junipers and shepherd's staffs.  

When the girl died,  
Where was she buried?  
Under the church on Gold Hill,  
Under the silver tower.  
What grew on the girl's grave?  
Coltsfoot and marsh marigold.  
Who visited the girl's grave?  
Every Sunday lords came,  
Every month kings came,  
Every Friday the Germans from Riga,  
Every Sunday the gentlemen from Pärnu.

label: youth_life
translation:
The maiden goes to the field  
Walks along the edge of the field,  
Behind the corner of the field.  
Her head adorned, hair tied,  
Shoe heels marked.  
The woman goes after the daughter.  
“Come home, young daughter,  
Suitors visited home.”  
“Where did the suitors come from?”  
“The suitors came from Latvia.”  
“No, I will go to Latvia,  
To eat Latvian bread,  
To drink Latvian beer,  
To live in Latvia.”  
The maiden goes to the field,  
Walks along the edge of the field,  
The woman goes after the daughter.  
“Come home, young daughter,  
Suitors visited home.”  
“Where did the suitors come from?”  
“They came from Viisu.”  
“Then I will go to Viisu.  
In Viisu, eat Viisu bread,  
In Viisu, drink Viisu beer,  
In Viisu, live politely.”

label: youth_life
translation:
Be proud, young men,  
Be dashing, buy black ones,  
Wear high ones, buy earrings;  
Buy lace for the whip,  
Silver locks with a locket,  
Copper between the straps.  
Ride to the girls’ homes,  
Visit the maids' households,  
There you will be given food,  
Chairs will be pulled out,  
A seat will be made for you!  

I was a proud young man,  
I was dashing, bought black ones,  
Wore high ones, bought earrings,  
Bought lace for the whip,  
Silver locks with a locket,  
Copper between the straps.  
I rode to the girls’ homes,  
Visited the maids’ households,  
There I was given food,  
Chairs were pulled out for me,  
A seat was made for me,  
I was taken to the chamber to sleep.  

I slept half the night,  
The other half I was thinking,  
The rooster crowed, they didn’t hear it,  
The rooster crowed a second time,  
Neither of us heard it,  
The rooster crowed a third time,  
The girl turned to another lad.  

Then I begin to understand:  
I put on my earrings,  
I put on my coat,  
I shake hands with the gray horseman,  
I speak to the earring horseman,  
I chat with the whip horseman:  
Farewell, maiden,  
I will not come back to you,  
You will be left behind,  
When this pea plant blossoms,  
And puts purple leaves on!  

The girl begins to cry:  
When you walk through Riga town,  
Always stand before me,  
So that no leaf will rustle alone,  
And no straw stalk will whisper.

label: youth_life
translation:
I neither complain nor fear:  
That I was born a beggar's daughter,  
A ragged little child,  
What of the swamp so vast,  
Of five or six brothers even,  
No kin at all to feed me,  
No sisters in the evening hours,  
Still I was chased by rogue boys,  
They wanted me as a servant in Tallinn,  
Some among them manor boys.  

I did not want to be a dancer  
Nor did I want to be a coachman's lass,  
The coachman's tail is dirty,  
I did not want a stable boy,  
Stable boys are clumsy.  

I wanted a peasant lad,  
A peasant lad is wise at work;  
An official lies down to sleep  
An official stands by the wall,  
The farmer lies down to sleep  
Grain grows without him;  
Because I wanted a peasant lad,  
A ploughman, a sower,  
A tiller of black soil.  

What is there in being a fancy man  
Dressed in new clothes and proud:  
A man is pale, his fist is loud.  
His head, big, his fist loud.  
Quick comes the blow of the fist,  
From the harsh man comes a loud punch.  

My man is dark, his mind is wise,  
His flour sack is whiter,  
His oat sack taller,  
His purse heavier.

label: youth_life
translation:
Girls are little birds,  
Snow-necklaces are beauties,  
Let's get together, the three of us,  
We'll hold a council, the four of us:  
Let's leave from this land  
Let's go quietly to Finland,  
For a month or two to Courland.  
There we will build a stone church,  
We'll carry a chapel made of carrageen,  
We'll make a bridge from onions,  
A fence from garlic.  
If there comes to the land a shortage of girls,  
A shortage of maids,  
They will surely search for us on horseback,  
Testing on foal hooves,  
The boys under our prayers:  
Come to the land, maidens!  
We will soon answer,  
Soon respond:  
Is there wild strawberry on the land,  
Blue gooseberries,  
Red hazelnuts?  
If there is no wild strawberry on the land,  
No blue gooseberries,  
No red hazelnuts,  
Then I am a Swedish maiden  
Walking with a elbow in the ditch,  
Marching with a marker on the shoulder,  
Sowing peas in the parish,  
In the district, knitting.

label: youth_life
translation:
A little brother,
I will not come to you,
To your garden fire,
To the horse’s dream,
To the dog’s snout on the face.
Send ships to Germany,
Empty ships to Turkey,
Bring out from there fiercely,
Pull out from the tar vat,
Bring out the arrow noses;
Those who understand drinking but not eating,
Do not really understand how to devour.
I will, of course, become a man,
The son of the barley field,
I have men to the sea,
To Peibu, to the hiding places.
Let time roll the days,
Then Hans will come from Harjumaa,
Kaarel dear from afar,
Peeter from Peibu,
Mart comes from the sea, from the sea lands,
Hans takes Anne to Harjumaa,
Kaarel takes Kaie to the distant place,
Peeter takes Liisu to Peipus,
Mart takes the sea to the sea lands.
Why do you laugh at me so,
With little eyes, you mock me!

label: youth_life
translation:
What do I care about shouting,  
Or do I fear screaming,  
Mine is not here,  
My companion does not grow here,  
Mine is in Holland,  
My companion is among the fish on the shores,  
My fiancé is on the shore of Peipus,  
Now let the mouth just run,  
Let the tongue bark to the limit.  
So let me say it again,  
Let me sing it back again,  
I tilt the words cleverly,  
I roll the words skillfully:  
I have a home with cruel brothers,  
Wise brothers in the back room,  
Words are noticed,  
Whisked and dashed,  
Put on paper.  
Tomorrow they will be laid before me  
When I bring the thought home.

label: youth_life
translation:
I was once a little boy;  
I worked on the manor estate days,  
I did the servant's helper days.  
I was not given food,  
Better things were not offered.  
When the estate days were done;  
The servant's helper days followed.  
Akkan  
Then I put on a gray cap  
With ears hanging high like rings  
Songbirds sang below,  
One on the other's yoke pole.  
Then I went through the villages.  
Rustling man, rustling horse;  
Rustling on the golden hoof!  
Then I went under the gray yard  
Took from the gray yoke-poles;  
From the ears hanging high like rings.  
Songbirds sang below,  
One on the other's yoke pole, too.  
I sat inside on the bench!  
Waiting to be given food,  
Better things were certainly offered.  
I was not given food!  
Better things were not offered.  
Now  
I put my rods through the door  
Girls smiled from the corner:  
“Is this the tail of a mad wolf?  
Or is it the paw of a forest bear?  
I hear and answer,  
""That  
""That is not the tail of a mad wolf;  
""Nor is it the paw of a forest bear.  
""These are clean boys’ rods.  
Now I am going to woo Koiki  
Koiki's bailiff's three daughters:  
One is dear Annekene,  
The second beloved Kaieke,  
The third sweet Mallekene!  
Anne was given to me,  
Kaie’s dowry was bargained.  
I wanted Malleke.  
Malle pays the city of Maali  
Anne’s rare shirt remnants,  
Kaie’s cowbell holes!

label: youth_life
translation:
Dear gentle mother  
Make me a five-wool carpet  
Knit me six new coats  
Seven linen sheets  
Eight pillowcases.  
I am going to a man far away  
To a rich son-in-law  
Where ten pairs plow  
Nine take care of the horse  
Seven wield sickles.  
Be quiet, young daughter  
Yesterday I came from there  
There were mice in the threshing barn  
Rats in the Swedish barn  
Seven poles stand in the field  
There were peas in the granary  
There were sheaves in the barn  
Sheaves at the edge of the stack.

label: youth_life
translation:
Ui, ui, ui, ui, I plowed the valleys,  
I plowed the valleys, rye grew,  
I plowed the hills, pines grew,  
I plowed the swamps, bluebells grew,  
Then the girls went to pick flowers,  
To weave red ribbons.  
White heads to rule;  
Breasts full of baptismal bread,  
Necks full of hearth bread,  
Wrists full of money,  
I went to watch the girls,  
Bent under the spruce,  
By the edge of the alder,  
Is my own among them?  
They are not among my own!  
Girls, girls, do not cry,  
With twisted necks do not complain:  
Mine is not here,  
My match does not grow here.  
My beloved from far away  
A good bride from beyond the rivers,  
May the wind bring him health,  
May the rain send messages.  
As many greetings to him  
As there are sticks in a stick bundle,  
Many-wood good wife,  
Maple white wife,  
Bird cherry strong wife,  
Apple tree good wife.  
From the apple tree, I get a true wife,  
From the maple, a white wife,  
From the bird cherry, a strong wife,  
From the rowan, a tall wife,  
From the hazel, a straight wife,  
From the alder, the shortest.

label: youth_life
translation:
Sister dear Viiukene  
Listen, dear little maiden  
You cannot save the suspender  
Or break the rag string  
Before the man has put on a pair  
The vicar has written

label: youth_life
translation:
Otherwise, would live, otherwise would be
Otherwise, other days would be lived -
Let the evening come on Saturday:
The old woman goes to bed with the old man,
The father goes with his mother,
The brother goes with the young girl,
The sister with her husband,
But I go crying towards the corner,
Towards the empty bed
Where I turn my cheek, I find cold,
I turn my back, I find a wall,
All the boards are cold cheeks,
The edge boards are frosted,
The logs of the wall are mouldy...

label: youth_life
translation:
So far, the meadow is beautiful,  
When the hay has not been mowed,  
So far, the little bow is lovely,  
When the tune has not been taken.  
Young woman, young girl,  
A little girl, a small child,  
Whim, whim of the sock maker,  
Little blue silk bird.

label: youth_life
translation:
If this girl were to die  
where would she be buried?  
In the churchyard under the bell,  
under the silver tower.  
Who visited the girl's grave?  
Every month the kings came,  
every Friday the gentlemen of Riga.  
The prayer was in the middle led by the Germans of Paide,  
every Saturday the gentlemen of Laupa.  

If this boy were to die  
where would the boy be buried?  
In the swamp under a large spruce,  
in the forest under a wide alder.  
Who then visited the boy's grave?  
Every month the devils came,  
every Friday the dogs of Riga,  
every Saturday the dogs of Laupa,  
the prayer was in the middle led by the dogs of Paide.

label: youth_life
translation:
What are you old women thinking about?
Old women are arguing
I cannot bring a woman here.
This parish will not age
This place will not gather
I will bring a woman to Narva road
A slippery woman to the city road
A suitable woman to the Paide road
I will bring Hans from Harju County
And Jaan will come from Järva County
Hans brings money for the horse
And a ring for the finger on the edge of the forest
Jaan brings shoes with high heels
The moon will shine on their heels
The sun will shine under their soles
Hans made juniper wooden containers
Rowanwood milk pails
And made spruce butter churns.
Juniper wooden containers,
They were good for greening.
Rowanwood milk pails,
They were swift for churning
Spruce butter churns,
They were easy to rinse.

label: youth_life
translation:
What are you staring at, old boy?  
Why don’t you sometimes take a wife?  
Take an old girl from town.  
Chasing after a servant from the start  
It wears you out sometimes  
Turns the dew-soaked hay.  
Father goes to bed with his mother  
Brother goes with a young maiden  
I go crying to the corner  
Towards the empty bed:  
All the sideboards were cold,  
The wall logs were covered in fungus,  
I fumble for the old coat  
Oh, you old coat.  
It was good to walk along with the ox’s catch,  
Beautiful to walk with the herd’s catch,  
Even better to sleep on the barn floor.

label: youth_life
translation:
Paleness comes because of mercy,  
Weeping comes because of the young maiden,  
Tonight must be endured,  
There is no maiden to hold,  
With whom I speak:  
We have fun with the bedbug,  
I speak with the louse;  
I turn my side, find coldness  
I turn my eyes, find the wall.

label: youth_life
translation:
Virgin girl, young maiden,  
Do not go to a young man as a husband,  
To an ungrown mate.  
You think he will help you grow,  
You think he will help you grow,  
But he gives only a man’s mind?  
A mate does not help growth,  
But a man takes away your mind;  
A mate asks for cloth from a weaver,  
But a man asks for clothes from a tailor:  
Every month he wants a new hat,  
Every week he wants four shirts,  
Every day he wants something fine,  
Every noon he wants linen.  
If you do not give it to him,  
Then you shall feel the whip,  
And you shall taste the rod:  
The man warns with his arm –  
You respond with your leg,  
Your mouth to your big toe:  
"Oh, legs, keep moving, legs,  
Keep me from beating,  
Keep me from the lash of the whip!"

label: youth_life
translation:
"Oh, you deceitful boy,  
Clever to walk as a companion,  
You deceived the father-in-law, deceived the mother-in-law,  
You deceived the whole household, the fine young maiden:  
'Maiden, young girl,  
Darling, come to me,  
I will make you three pairs of shoes:  
One slippery, another wooden,  
The third a bitter pair of shoes.  
I will make slippery ones from snow shoes,  
Wooden ones from wedding shoes,  
Bitter ones from church shoes.'  
He became your servant,  
You again became his supporter—  
One pair of shoes was donated,  
Their toes made of soft leather,  
Heels of cat leather,  
In the middle patchy dog leather—  
You let the servant carry burdens,  
The hired boy to tie ribbons:  
The servant made big burdens,  
The hired boy thick ribbons—  
Those were then my three pairs of shoes."

label: youth_life
translation:
A young virgin girl  
A slender figure  
Do not go to a young man  
Who has no grown-up bride  
You think the bride grows up with him  
But he only gives the man's mind  
A bride does not grow up  
But a man takes the mind  
The bride asks for cloth  
The man for garments  
Every month he wants new jackets  
Every week he wants four shirts  
Every day he wants a fine one  
Every noon a meal  
If you cannot give this to her  
Then you will feel the whip’s blow  
Then you will taste the rod’s sting  
The man informs his boss  
You inform your foot  
With your mouth to the big toe  
Oh legs, move swiftly, legs  
Oh toes, wag your toes  
Hold me, but stop it  
Save me from the whip’s lash.

label: youth_life
translation:
King, little king,  
Rich lord of Riga:  
But why didn't you come to us last year,  
When the orders were carried out  
Five or six jugs of spirits,  
Seven or eight jugs of beer.  
Beer could be drunk from the trough,  
Ale could be drunk by all the livestock.  
The squire grabbed by the hair,  
I grabbed the squire by the chest,  
But I struck the squire against the walls.  
The pigs got to eat dung,  
While all the livestock could drink.

label: youth_life
translation:
What’s wrong with becoming a prostitute,
Then you can go to the city as a barmaid.
My head wears a lace cap,
My feet new clog shoes,
Legs silk stockings,
Hips a shop apron.

label: youth_life
translation:
I heard, I heard, crazy brothers,  
I heard the clatter of rascals,  
the silver raindrop’s pattering,  
the tin roof’s clinking.  
Bring that fire to the room,  
the bellows’ blaze to the floor;  
bring me silk stockings,  
silk stockings, thread stockings,  
thread stockings, high shoes.  
So I can go out to the dance,  
and wrap my arms around his neck.

label: youth_life
translation:
My sister, a beautiful girl,
sits on a linden leaf,
dances on an oak branch,
boys kneel below.
Fall down, golden doll,
a hundred German apples fall down.
Fall onto my pillar,
let a wide hat fall on it,
on the edge of the wide hat.
I will not fall onto the pillar,
let a wide hat fall on it,
on the edge of the wide hat.
The devil falls onto the pillar,
I send him tall in a silk bed,
the devil swells in the pillowcase.

label: youth_life
translation:
I just wanted to elope  
couldn't go secretly  
I watched through the keyhole  
the girl was dozing against the guard  
the old lady again leaning against the post  
the clean lines were burning  
there was nowhere a fire extinguisher

label: youth_life
translation:
Girls like snowdrops,  
Beautiful as rosebuds,  
They would sneak into boys' hearts,  
Slip under their skirts,  
Without chasing a boy,  
Without asking for a promise,  
Without trying a loving hand.

label: youth_life
translation:
The evening comes, twilight arrives:  
the young woman goes to bed with the old man,  
the brother goes with the young maiden,  
the sister goes with her husband.  
Oh, poor me, always alone!  
I took the lice to talk to,  
the bedbug to amuse myself.  
The louse was shy, did not talk,  
the bedbug was talkative, but said nothing.  
My edges froze,  
my sideboards chilled,  
my pillows got moldy.

label: youth_life
translation:
If I were Olev,
I would wear the cloak of Kalev,
I would carry a long saber:
I fear touching heels,
stretching out on the street,
getting caught by the crowd.
I would take a young wife:
I fear her young weeping,
bringing secrets into the room,
putting a bow by the edge.
Secrets are troublesome in a room,
a bow is used to poke the eye.
She did not poke the father-in-law's eye,
she did not poke the mother-in-law's eye.

label: youth_life
translation:
... I had a home with three sheds:  
one for cracking flax,  
another for storing goods,  
the third . . . .  
You had a home with three sheds:  
one for mice to jump,  
another for cats to roar,  
the third for dogs to roam ...

label: youth_life
translation:
There was no broom on the table,  
no timid one tending the fire.  
Maggots crawled with stalks in their mouths,  
lice went to the corner with bundles on their backs,  
bedbugs dragged the trough.

label: youth_life
translation:
I still go where it is created,  
Where the buildings might be dilapidated,  
And the cattle barns on a slope,  
A room supported by beams,  
And the stove resting on brackets,  
Long ago with a half-faced cow,  
In a yard full of fences,  
A woman would milk beside her hip,  
In an earthen floor barn,  
I still go where it is created.

label: youth_life
translation:
Aidu, raiu, with wheels,  
before me I play with tussocks,  
I jump with birch stumps,  
before with those maidens,  
who are half-promised,  
loved beforehand,  
brought to the beer table,  
tasted on a bread roll.

label: youth_life
translation:
Mari granny, Mari grandma,  
Mari strawberry on the hill,  
called the boys to the spruce forest,  
tricked them into the long-leaved forest.

label: youth_life
translation:
Beautiful girl, beautiful girl,  
white maiden,  
do you promise, do you promise  
to come to me.  
To come to me, to come to me,  
to be mine.  
I have no wealth, I have no wealth;  
I have no lack of bread, I have no lack of bread.  
I will make a granary, I will make a granary  
from goose meat,  
a roof on it, a roof on it  
from chicken meat;  
I will make walls, I will make walls  
from pig meat,  
a floor below, a floor below  
from piglet meat,  
a house in front, a house in front  
from frog meat.  
Inside I will put, inside I will put  
a silk bed,  
a silk bed, a silk bed,  
a silk bed.  
At the foot I will put, at the foot I will put  
junkru boy...

label: youth_life
translation:
The bachelor’s miserable fate,  
Always must he wander,  
Sleep on a haystack  
And fall down from the roof.  
He sits under the haystack,  
An old pipe in hand,  
Coal inside it,  
Waiting to blow luck.  
If only I had a woman’s embrace,  
Surely it would be dear to me.  
There would be no wandering at night,  
No sleeping on the haystack,  
No falling down from the roof.  
I will go sleep on the loft.  
I rummage in the old sheepskin.  
Even better to sleep on the loft.

label: youth_life
translation:
I drove a grey horse, I gave water to the grey horse.  
I went riding on the grey horse.  
The night is full of pain, the moon is full of pain,  
The sky is covered with stars.  
A girl came towards me,  
A maiden from the group of girls.  
I asked the girls:  
Are these girls for sale?  
Are the hens being traded?  
From the girls came the answer:  
Oh, you foolish man!  
Oh, you crazy young man!  
Outside there is plenty of merchandise,  
On the street there is all kinds of goods.  
There are foals for sale by the aunt.  
Maiden goods on the bench,  
Under the hill there is whore merchandise,  
Prostitute goods even in the barn.

label: youth_life
translation:
Call back, little sacred grove,  
Sing back, little forest clearing.  
To my good voice,  
To the deeper throat.  
If it used to call well before,  
Deceive not with false sounds,  
Hide the German horn sounds.  
The kannel’s sound was heard.  
There were also many of us,  
We also had many groups.  
They wandered like herds of horses,  
Rolled like herds of cattle.  
Now the herds have ended.  
And the flock has disappeared.  
From here the boys of Viru have gone,  
Beloved by the Hans of Harju,  
The coachmen of Kuie courted (them).  
If they have gone, let them go,  
If they have been taken, let them be taken.  
We have Kaia staying to grow,  
Leena to slide on top.  
We have Mai with berry heads,  
We have Kaia with cardigans.  
Ann remains a gray spruce,  
Leena remains with flaxen locks.

label: youth_life
translation:
Little Hellak, little brother!  
Wake me up from my sleep.  
What I saw in the dream;  
The fig tree was in our yard,  
The yellow tree was in front of the hut.  
The shawl tree was on the sauna road,  
The birch was in the room.  
The alder was on the wide market road.  
I understand the dream:  
From the fig tree drinks are drunk,  
From the yellow tree come marriages.  
From the shawl tree are eaten breads.  
The birch is a lover,  
The alder is a child's reconciler.

label: youth_life
translation:
Little boy, little lad!  
Why are you standing at the edge of the table,  
And why are you looking through the window?  
Is there no ear of rye nearby,  
Or no white field opposite,  
Is there not a beautiful body,  
Or a face not red,  
Or lips not more shapely,  
Ears more elevated.  
Where must I go?  
Where must I lay my head?  
I myself will lie down in the mouse’s box,  
My head I will lay on the bed of bites.  
My legs I will save for the mosquito bed.  
Girls, little birds,  
Lovely with slender necks!  
Do you know where you will go,  
Where you will finally be taken,  
Where you will be placed afterward,  
Where you drift in the crowd,  
Where you sink in the territory.  
To the beggar, to the scavenger,  
To the buyer of barley sacks,  
To the filler of oats sacks,  
To the city’s floaters,  
To the wearer of hats,  
To the destroyer of new huts.

label: youth_life
translation:
Oh, you little deceitful boy!  
You deceived the fine girl of the family.  
In the village cold in the barn,  
In the heated building.  
Neither told the father was there.  
Nor told the mother was there.  
Nor told the brother was around.  
It became your own doing,  
It stayed your own doing.  
There was a father, there was a mother,  
There was a wise little brother,  
Also two beautiful sisters.  
Like a hunchbacked fox,  
Pecking in the stove.  
Looking for torn clothes,  
Wretchedly shabby rags.

label: youth_life
translation:
Sister, darling, first I told!
Naughty, young, first I scolded!
I am not a young man,
Nor an unripe wife!
A wife does not make one grow,
A man has no desire to take one,
The wife asks for the linen store,
The man has no desire for clothes.
If he could not have her,
Then there was brandishing of a whip,
And noisy scolding hand in hand.

label: youth_life
translation:
I have, I have a little brother,  
he is a weather-wise one,  
he makes a bonfire into waves,  
he turns ropes into aganasta,  
throws a spear into the sky,  
to the other Jordan river,  
pulls rocks out of the cliff,  
ties knots into eggs;  
he makes gusts from the winds,  
prepares a cart from snow,  
rides across the Finnish bridge,  
along the arcs of the rainbow,  
the sky arches get tangled,  
the pillars of the world creak,  
when my little brother rides,  
the weather-wise one rushes on the path.

label: youth_life
translation:
We eat from one, we drink from one,  
Together we sleep through the night,  
We wear one embrace;  
One silk shirt on the back.  
But we do not take one wife,  
One takes another's wife,  
Another takes another old woman's daughter.

label: youth_life
translation:
Mother made five twisted socks  
I knitted six wedding socks  
Then I went to Kolka to ask for a bride  
To the daughter of the Kolka blacksmith.  
One was naked on the stove  
Another in bed without a shirt  
The third had a bare buttocks by the door.

label: youth_life
translation:
Tiidu, Tiidu, Tiiu's thighs  
The wolf had torn Kaie’s thighs,  
The wolf had bitten Anne,  
The bear had scratched Kaie.

label: youth_life
translation:
Before I throw a stone to the stone  
To the stone, to the stump  
Before the crazy boy  
The stone does not pull, the stump does not try  
The boy does not leave untouched  
The girl, however, is not undressed at the chest  
The hand cunningly untried  
Before I play with turf  
But joke with women  
Before those girls  
Who are engaged  
On the outside a fine young lady  
Underneath long since a woman.

label: youth_life
translation:
Our Maied, our Kaied  
They were lively girls  
They wanted to share from the sky  
To scatter little clouds  
But then Maie would disappear without Kaie  
Then the clatter from the barnyard would vanish  
The laughter rolling from the alder grove  
The boys’ shouting from the spruce stand  
The boys’ jokes from the fields  
Mai was a fond young maiden  
She tended to give gifts to her man  
But she left the gifts on top of the coffin  
The stockings on the big table  
The shoes on the echoing path.

label: youth_life
translation:
Put beads around Heide's neck  
Pearls on Pärts's neck  
Money but wide coins around Laugu's neck  
Rubles on the steed  
Before this girl's neck  
Who has been half-promised  
Loved too early  
Else my black mare could run  
Could neigh under the saddle  
The boat could circle the quay  
The chimney could smoke  
Before it would quiver and twitch  
Through the town's brothel  
Across the islands' crossroads  
Behind Paide's palm tree.

label: youth_life
translation:
Dear little brother, dear little one,  
Do not take a woman from the manor.  
In the manor there are certain ones,  
Beautiful beneath the windows,  
Delicate and slender above the sill.  
How many men have they had,  
How many boys have they slept with,  
A hundred Martis they have slept with,  
A thousand known Thomases.  
Yet they remain innocent,  
Standing upright,  
Growing mold on the hill.  
They do not know how to weave fabric,  
How to stretch the fine thread,  
How to weave on the loom,  
How to twist the linen thread,  
How to flash the copper combs.  
Dear little woolen one, dear little one,  
Take instead the village outcasts,  
The servants from the end of the village.  
They know how to weave fabric,  
How to stretch the fine thread,  
How to weave on the loom,  
How to twist the linen thread,  
How to flash copper combs.  
They may go to the fire,  
Light the bed without sparks,  
Milk the cow without a lamp,  
By moonlight strain the milk,  
In the village buzz of beauty,  
On the forehead of the horned ox under the sun.

label: youth_life
translation:
Boy, what wandering are you looking for here?  
Or are you watching aimlessly here?  
There are no strays of wandering here,  
Or lazy ones worthy of it.  
Here are sorrowful dark girls,  
The poor little children of the county.  
Go along the beaten paths,  
Walk through the shaggy bushes.

label: youth_life
translation:
Who went down to the meadow?  
Jaan went down to the meadow.  
Kaare lets the other mow.  
What is there under Kaare's side?  
An eagle under Kaare's side.  
What is there under the eagle's wing?  
An axe under the eagle's wing.  
What is there under the axe's eye?  
Shavings under the axe's eye.  
What are those shavings made into?  
Jaan's house.  
What should be put inside the room?  
Three young maidens.  
One of them weaves golden thread,  
Another braids silk ribbons—  
The third weeps for a young brother.  
Why do you weep, maiden?  
Why do you weep for the young brother?  
He is already seen coming:  
His head appears above the forest,  
His legs below the forest,  
His body from the middle through the forest.

label: youth_life
translation:
The young men of our village,  
Leaving for Midsummer at the church,  
Under the horse like the oven,  
On top like the day?  
A hat like the moon’s servant,  
A belt like the rainbow of rain.

label: youth_life
translation:
If I were the present  
If I wore the helmets  
If I had a long spear  
I would fear touching the heels  
Stabbing the toes  
Marking the calves  
I do not know how to hold a rifle  
Nor how to handle a wise spear.

label: youth_life
translation:
Mistress, little woman,  
Do not laugh at women’s children,  
Do not let others’ children wander.  
You have a herd growing,  
A roomful is rising.  
A scabby head is in a diaper,  
A crusty head is hidden inside,  
A bloody one rolls in the cradle.  
You do not know what will become of them,  
Whether they will be able to saw wood,  
To saw wood, to carry a load,  
For fathers’ wives to sew,  
For wives to spin.

label: youth_life
translation:
We, the beautiful girls, walk,
We make noise as we walk,
The empty one knows it a second time.
Will the rain drive us away,
Or will the dew carry us,
Snow orders new gates,
Hail orders new power.
Let me say, I will respond immediately:
Neither will the rain drive us away
Nor will the dew carry us,
Snow orders new gates
Hail orders new power,
But we are driven by the little brother,
Carried by the farm boy,
Warming the earth in the melting season.
I belong to the servant
To the cunning farm boy,
A woman created for the servant.
The servant buys me with barley,
The farm boy with oats,
A servant in the summer melt.
A lady, a woman,
Immediately hears and answers back:
"Where is the servant’s barley field,
The farm boy’s oat field?"
I hear and answer back:
"In the swamp is the servant’s barley field,
The farm boy’s oat field.
In the swamp roams the servant’s wife,
In the heath the farm boy’s wife."
A lady, a woman,
Immediately hears and answers back:
"The wolf eats the servant’s wife,
The bear eats the farm boy’s wife."
I hear and answer back:
"The wolf eats the bought geldings,
The bear the combed horses.
Linen bundles, wild garlic.
Mouse fur, greyish,
Barn hair ears.
White, well sheared,
Fat iron-gray horses."

label: youth_life
translation:
The old woman lied  
Said my rune-carved one  
I have been a stallion until today  
Bachelor tomorrow until morning.

label: youth_life
translation:
Mari grandma, Mari granny,  
Mari strawberry on the hill!  
The bullfinch in the spruce forest;  
The bluebell in the alder grove.  
Surely you were caught by the boys in breeches,  
Loved by the boys of Harju.  
You were not caught with a gun;  
Nor taken with a net,  
You were happy to wander.  
Exploring the shore.  
Ants listened in the wasteland;  
Jaan Jaak in the hayfield  
Peeter in the long rowan;  
He was fit to be a smallholder;  
A husband for a farmer's daughter!  
For a fingered glove,  
A neighbor like Kuldanaast.  
Some kind of man  
Some man keeps close watch;  
Some chooses the barn,  
Some works in the kiln;  
Because of that young maiden  
Because of that long whip:  
Because of that wide strike.

label: youth_life
translation:
The sister went to bed with the man,  
The brother went with the young maiden.  
With whom shall I go?  
I go crying to the corner,  
Striking the wall with my face.  
I fumble in the old fur coat.  
I turn around, I find coldness,  
I turn my back, I find the wall.  
All were cold sideboards,  
Frost-covered were the edgeboards.

label: youth_life
translation:
Iiu-tiiu Tiiu’s thighs,  
The bear had bitten Kaie’s thighs,  
The wolf had bitten Anne.

label: youth_life
translation:
Maiden, young girl,  
Do not marry a young man,  
An immature husband:  
A husband does not make you grow,  
A man does not want to take a wife;  
A wife asks for cloth,  
A man desires fine clothes;  
Every month he wants a new coat,  
Every week he wants four shirts,  
Every quarter he wants tailored pants,  
Every year two fur coats.  
If he does not earn them,  
He cannot have a new coat each month,  
Four shirts each week,  
Tailored pants every quarter,  
Two fur coats each year,  
Then he starts flailing around,  
Clutching and growling.  
Your fist is square-shaped,  
The material is overfurnished;  
You have a scold,  
A hen to pester.

label: youth_life
translation:
Virgin girl, young maid,
Come to me, I have a visit;
Come to my visit, a shelter,
Let’s look after the early crops.
I will put the work to the willow:
I will put a yoke to your mouth,
To find the head for the day,
I will make the breads ready,
I will make the oats for the roof,
The barley under its own courtyard.
But the maiden understands, replies:
I can be yours to be,
Again I remain yours,
You make the oats far away,
The linens halfway to town,
The barley down in the valleys.

label: youth_life
translation:
Girls, do you hear,  
What do you think of yourselves,  
That you despise boys,  
Leave men behind?!  
Later you come to the boy’s request,  
The sheet flutters in the hand,  
Pillows shifted to the side:  
Dear one, brother,  
Come to my arms to sleep;  
I will lay down sweet fern  
Under your head parsley,  
Under your feet St. John's wort. -  
The boy understands again, answers:  
- Before I throw a stone into a deep place,  
A stone into the depths, a stump into the depths,  
Before this girl’s depths,  
Who is half engaged,  
Excessively loved,  
Immoderately played with;  
Before I drag (her) to the peach cottage,  
Through Narva to the wells’ cottage,  
Before those girls,  
Who had too many loose ways,  
Who had half the hangman’s ways  
And yet had whore’s ways.

label: youth_life
translation:
With sparrow-bird wheels,  
Before I play with mosses,  
I jump with birch stumps,  
Before those girls,  
Who were half-promised,  
Loved too early,  
Boys' hands had fondled,  
Boys' penises had fondled.

label: youth_life
translation:
Which of us swung in the cherry tree,  
And which of us rocked in the apple tree?  
The mill watch Maija maiden,  
She was the one who swung in the cherry tree,  
And rocked in the apple tree.  
Sass from Mäeküla was a boy,  
He went down to the prayer place,  
Spread the sheets loosely,  
Beat the pillows soft:  
Fall down, little Maija,  
Step onto my shoulders,  
So you don’t break your leg,  
You'll surely break your skull.

label: youth_life
translation:
A girl is trapped, a girl is screaming,  
Trapped in custody,  
Screaming in the town hall.  
There was her town hall, standing still,  
She turned her mouth towards the boy,  
Began to ask the boy:  
"What is buzzing in your pants?  
Trembling below the waistband?  
Can I give the girl into your hand,  
And place the girl in your palm?"  
Then the boy understands, replies:  
"You cannot give the girl into my hand,  
Let him put a couple of coins,  
Sign the wide-waisted certificate,  
Let the parish priest announce,  
And the blue coat persuade,  
Then you can give the girl into my hand  
And place the girl in my palm."

label: youth_life
translation:
Virgin girl, young maiden,  
Do not go to the young man,  
Unmature companions  
Do not make a companion mature,  
A man does not intend to take a wife  
If he must ask a fabric shopkeeper for a wife.  
Every month he demands six new coats,  
Every week he demands four shirts,  
Every quarter he demands felted trousers,  
Every year two fur coats.  
If not, if not, virgin girl,  
If he does not get six coats a month,  
Four shirts a week,  
Felted trousers every quarter,  
Two fur coats a year,  
Then the drummer will come to strike,  
Hand in hand to quarrel.  
Your fist is checkered,  
Your jacket woolly,  
The drummer is your water carrier,  
The calf is the wife carrier.

label: youth_life
translation:
Virgin girl, young maiden,  
Come to me, I have a visit,  
Come to my home to keep watch,  
To watch after the evening hours.  
I will set the flax to work.  
I will put the mouth to give,  
To seek the head for the day;  
For the year to set the place.  
I will make barley on the roof,  
I will lay flax nearby.  
I will place oats under the yard.  
The maiden answers to the visitor:  
"I can be yours, I have gotten,  
Again I will remain yours,  
You make barley far away  
Flax halfway to the town,  
Oats in the mountain valleys.  
I will go when it is time.  
If his buildings were hills,  
Cowsheds on slopes,  
A room leaning on supports.  
If I get a willing husband;  
A beloved spouse,  
I will make a big mess,  
Would cause a neck-breaking harm,  
Still he strokes my head,  
Tries on my necklace."

label: youth_life
translation:
Ann went down to the hayfield,
Mowed the swaths for the third time,
What is under the swaths there?
An eagle under the swaths.
What is under the eagle's wing?
An axe under the eagle's wing,
What is under the axe's eye?
A wooden shaving under the axe's eye.
What is carved from that shaving?
Jaan's barn is made.
What is put inside there?
Beds are put inside,
What is put on the beds?
Boards are put on,
What is put on the boards?
Straw is put on,
What is put on the straw?
Planks are put on,
What is put on those planks,
Four young maidens.
One wove gold
Another cast copper.

label: youth_life
translation:
Do not rush to get married  
or become a young widow.  
What use is a crazy husband,  
to ungrown wives?  
A man does not like liking,  
a wife does not make grown.  
A man wants clothes to the ground,  
a wife asks for fine fabric,  
every month wants new skirts,  
every week wants four shirts,  
two fur coats a year.  
If he does not get this from you,  
then he feels the whip,  
knocks on the household goods,  
tastes the sweetness of plates.

label: youth_life
translation:
A little scoundrel,
when you deceived me,
You lingered in the room and at the door,
In the room and behind the door.
On your knees and in the pantry,
Without hat, without gloves,
Without a copper belt, without saddlebags.
You promised to keep me at the instrument,
promised to raise me on the kannel.
I go to sleep in the evening,
Put the instrument by the window,
The kannel by the chamber ceiling.
I wake you up in the morning,
Take the instrument from the window,
The kannel from the chamber ceiling.
You get up to milk the cow, Lilli,
White head, nurse the calf,
Then I became yours,
I remained your remnant.
You take the whip to keep me,
To raise me in the chamber.
You get up in the morning,
Take the whip from the window,
From the chamber ceiling, —
"Get up, bitch, milk the cow,
Old whore, nurse the calf,
I'll bring you an apron red
To the ground, with wolf fur,
Probably bringing striped ones,
Quickly bringing checkered ones,
With mustard’s paw prints.
The whip is red aprons,
The quiver is striped,
The comb has cat’s paw prints.
I have quilts with capercaillie patterns,
The blankets have duck patterns,
I have pillows with border patterns,
Pillow shams with lace.
These could have rotted
And become moldy under the cover.
If you spend badly,
The evil man scolds.
The evil could have endured living,
The bad could have slept in the willow.

label: youth_life
translation:
There was cold, there was hunger  
There was drought, there was heat  
But still not that hunger  
That was the hunger of the girls  
And there was emptiness of the girls  
The boys kneeled down  
Bowed without hats  
In the village street in Külleli  
At the Persel family gate  
Juniper berries in the hand  
Rowan berries in the palm  
Let’s bring down the tulips to the shoulder  
Pastry jugs on the bench  
Come to me, maiden  
Come to me and pull  
Get to me and ask  
The maiden heard and answered  
I still won’t come to you  
Your yard is muddy  
The cattle pen is full of holes  
The suitor heard and answered  
I have bulls to thresh  
Fat cows are sleeping  
Surely you’ll walk past the barn  
You’ll step along the edge of the garden  
Along the fences and reeds  
Until the bridge is made  
The foundation board is laid  
Bridges are made here from onions  
Logs are laid from carrots

label: youth_life
translation:
I went to walk in the forest  
And look for bird nests  
I found a boy under a bush.  
His underside was moldy  
And his top side was sunburned.  
I threw him over my shoulder  
And went back for a piece  
There I scrubbed him with sand  
And dried him with a sack.  
Then I threw him over my shoulder  
And took him to the Viitna fair  
There I traded him for a rooster  
And a mottled sack.

label: youth_life
translation:
Once I went wandering in the forest  
There I found a boy under a bush.  
His underside was moldy  
And his upper side had sunblotch.  
I threw him over my shoulder  
And carried him to the river.  
There I scrubbed and rubbed  
And dried him with a sack.  
Then I threw him over my shoulder  
And took him to Paide fair.

label: youth_life
translation:
Other days I would live as usual,  
I would spend the peak days,  
When a blissful little evening comes,  
A little wandering one rolls by:  
The maiden goes to bed with the old man,  
The sister goes with her husband,  
The brother goes with a young maiden,  
With whom, poor me,  
With whom, little plain one!  
But I, crying, towards the corner,  
Towards the empty bed,  
Old coat on the hanger,  
Old sixpence in hand,  
The flea was proud, did not buzz,  
The louse did not bring joy,  
I turned my back – I found the wall,  
I turned to my side – I found cold.

label: youth_life
translation:
Here I have boys, six boys,  
Their horse has turned gray in front,  
The man has sunburned on top,  
A thin strip of leather belt,  
Hat on the head like a mushroom,  
Look at the boys, our boys,  
The horse in front like an oven,  
The man on top like the sun,  
Belt around the waist like a rainbow,  
Hat on the head like the moon.  
Look where the boy is across the county,  
Across Koeru parish.

label: youth_life
translation:
Little maiden, thin and slender,  
If you want to come to me,  
To me, a young man,  
A red bull?  
If you don't come – I won't want you.  
Stay home to stew,  
By the stream to mildew,  
By the wall to gather mushrooms,  
The maiden responded with a refusal:  
I will not come to you,  
To you, the sow,  
To the horse’s dream,  
To the dog’s clumsy paw,  
The boy then replied,  
But I do not want a lazy one,  
You wash the pot with your backside,  
You crouch to heat the stove,  
While lurking you look for a broom,  
When napping you sweep the room.

label: youth_life
translation:
I went to Kadi's village,  
Got lost on Emu hill.  
From there I found Salla's trap,  
Rushed to Ruuna's house.  
There I had a woman to bid farewell,  
At Kilimitu, at Riga's rack,  
There were three ashes’ daughters.  
Mouse-gray was on the oven,  
Old silver was on the distaff,  
One was dozing with a safety pin;  
A piece of trousers was under the head,  
A window plug was over the hole.

label: youth_life
translation:
Before, little mother,  
Put this daughter to a husband,  
Who walks around the yard,  
Foghead, foghair,  
Nice sleeves on her hands.  
If you don’t put her - don’t ask.  
Let her stay home knocking,  
By the fence picking mushrooms,  
By the garden wilting,  
A birch grows on her neck,  
A spruce grows over her eyebrow,  
A bird cherry on her eyelashes,  
A juniper among the hairs.

label: youth_life
translation:
The evening comes through happiness,  
Through the fruit of twilight,  
The evening brings straw to the barn,  
Puts the straw on the threshing floor,  
Straws side by side,  
Each partner by the neck,  
Whoever has a partner, take the cat,  
The rat from the tuft of grass,  
The mole from the molehill.

label: youth_life
translation:
Liiva-Liis's little bird,  
Kalmu-Hans's little companion,  
Come to me, you to me;  
I will build a barnyard,  
Make the walls from pork,  
The floor from pig fat,  
Shelves from bread rolls,  
The ceiling from pike fish,  
My cattle pen from fabric.  
If you go wandering outside,  
Bring pike fish from the ceiling,  
Pig fat from the floor,  
Pork from the walls.

label: youth_life
translation:
Virgin girl, young maiden  
Cutting in the field, on the hill  
Between the garden beds.  
Brother called out:  
"Come home, my sister,  
You have suitors at home!"  
"Where did these suitors come from?"  
"Suitors came from Kuur."  
Did not want to go to Kuur  
To eat the bitter bread of Kuur.

label: youth_life
translation:
We are three sisters,  
In the field, three stalks,  
Our home has three suitors.  
One was a clever one from Viljandi,  
The second a wise one from Tammiku,  
The third from our own village.  
From our village's high ground,  
Our parish's fair area,  
Our family's fine estate.

label: youth_life
translation:
If this man had me,  
This man would have to take me.  
Who rides along the road,  
Rides along the paths,  
Chases along the edge of the fence  
Under the horse like to the oven,  
On the man like to the day,  
A hat like the church bell,  
A belt like a rainy rainbow.  
If this man does not take me,  
Let the horse under him grow moldy,  
The man still gets suntanned,  
The hat turns yellow on the head,  
The belt rots on the waist.

label: youth_life
translation:
I can’t find the girl, where has she gone,  
Her footprints have vanished from here,  
She had tied the sandal straps.  
Now I have caught the girl again.  
Why do you hesitate when coming to us,  
In our yard, the apple trees,  
In the grass garden, the little roses,  
By our gate, the tall birches.

label: youth_life
translation:
Little Toomas from Turu  
Brother from Järva-Jaani  
Went to Koigi to woo,  
To Koigi cobbler's daughters.  
One was slippery little Liisuke,  
The other dear little Annake.  
I used to be a young man  
I jumped over a horse  
Over a creaking log boat  
Over a hazelwood sled.  
Now I have grown old and weakened  
I cannot anymore  
Over a creaking log boat  
Over a hazelwood sled  
Over a little piglet’s sow.  
Why didn’t you come to me last year?  
Last year I could not come to you.  
I would have long ago built barns  
Barns built even from eggs,  
Roofs from chicken skin,  
Stone bridges to the church,  
Priest’s streets from limestone.  
Otherwise my black could have run  
Otherwise my stallion could have ridden empty  
Kimme could have hauled stones  
Boat  
Before I grew old,  
I played on a rotten chest.

label: youth_life
translation:
I saw a hawk growing  
Rising from the ground like a berry  
I took to hold the horse  
I took the spark in the fire.  
Horse, you are beautiful  
May your mane be smooth  
I ride to see the girl  
To look at the girl  
Whether she is healthy or sick  
Or has long been ill.  
I rode to father-in-law’s doorstep  
Greeted the father-in-law:  
Is your girl at home?  
The girls went to fetch water.  
May I ride to the well’s path?  
Certainly, you may ride to the well’s path.  
I greeted the girls:  
“Hello famous home hens.”  
“Are you a suitor?”  
No, I am not a suitor  
I am a poor traveler.  
A messenger of German affairs.”  
“If you are not a suitor,  
Why is your horse groomed,  
And the horse’s tail tied?”

label: youth_life
translation:
Iiu, tiiu, Tiiu’s thighs,  
The bear had bitten Kaie’s thighs,  
The wolf had long ago taken Anne,  
And the snake had tasted Marit.

label: youth_life
translation:
Beautiful girl, beautiful girl,  
white maiden,  
Do you promise, do you promise  
to come to me?  
To come to me, to come to me,  
to be mine?  
I have no wealth, no wealth,  
I do not have,  
I will not suffer from lack of bread,  
I will not suffer from lack of bread.  
I made a granary, I made a granary  
of elk meat,  
A roof over it, a roof over it  
of chicken meat.

label: youth_life
translation:
Oh, you deceitful young lad,  
a companion for playing cards,  
you deceived your father-in-law, you deceived your mother-in-law,  
you deceived the young maiden in the household.  
"Young maiden, young girl,  
darling, come to me!  
I will make you three pairs of shoes:  
one pair slippery, another wooden,  
the third pair of stone shoes.  
The slippery ones I make as snow shoes,  
the wooden ones as wedding shoes,  
the stone ones as church shoes."  
I received for you dried peas,  
and again for you dried peas,  
one pair of shoes I donated,  
even those with scarce stitching,  
their tips made of thin leather,  
heels at the back of cat leather,  
and the middle part of patchy dog leather.  
I gave the servant to braid,  
and the hired boy to lace.  
My servant made big braids,  
the hired boy made thick laces.  
Those were my three pairs of shoes.

label: youth_life
translation:
Virgin girl, young maiden,  
delicate to the writing board!  
Do not go to a young man,  
to unripe companions.  
You think that they will nurture you together,  
but they only please the man.  
The companion does not cause growth,  
but the man takes away the mind.  
The companion only asks for fabric,  
the man for garments,  
every month wants a new coat,  
every week wants four shirts,  
every day wants something delicate,  
every noon wants linen.  
If you do not give this to him,  
then you will feel the whip,  
and you will taste the rod.  
The man advises the arm,  
you advise the leg,  
but the mouth to the big toe:  
Oh legs, go forth, legs!  
Oh toes, move, toes!  
Keep me off the hooks,  
save me from the lash’s thongs.

label: youth_life
translation:
I came from work, tired,  
I came from the pub, weary,  
I refused to rest on the porch;  
my tools were left hanging,  
left visible through the window.  
The mistress came from the chamber,  
happened to see this:  
Could it be the tail of a wolf  
or perhaps the foot of a hare?  
It is not the tail of a wolf,  
nor the foot of a hare;  
these are the boy's genitals,  
fully grown man's testicles.

label: youth_life
translation:
Mother, dear mother,  
give your daughter in marriage here!  
If you do not give her, I will not ask.  
Let her stay at home knocking,  
mushroom picking by the wall,  
tending the garden's edge.  
A birch will grow on her neck,  
a spruce over her eyebrow,  
a willow over her breast,  
a juniper among her hairs!

label: youth_life
translation:
Where did you get the hedgehog's eyes,
to come to our land,
to our great family,
to the dear people,
to the family of money coins?
We have the sea at our doorstep,
golden fish inside,
silvery little roaches,
and little bream in the rushes.

label: youth_life
translation:
I am mowing on a mountain meadow,
between the garden beds,
in the middle of six fields.
Who came home calling?
My own brother:
"Come home, my sister,
suitors have visited the home."
I then asked my brother:
"Dear brother!
Where have the suitors been?"
The suitors came from Latvia.
If they have come, let them come on!
I will not go to Latvia,
to eat Latvian bread,
to drink Latvian beer,
to live in Latvia.
- -
I am mowing on a mountain meadow,
between the garden beds,
in the middle of six fields.
Who came home calling?
My brother came home calling:
"Come home, my sister!
Suitors have visited the home."
Where have the suitors been?
The suitors came from Viisu.
Maybe I will go to Viisu,
to eat Viisu bread,
to live in Viisu.

label: youth_life
translation:
I sing, why wouldn’t I sing.  
I sing a song about an apple,  
put a walnut on its top,  
ears made of oak leaves,  
eyes made of heavenly stars,  
legs made of birch,  
irons made of branches,  
tail made of foodstuffs,  
body made of food-stuffs.  
Then I go to Sõrve’s land,  
to see the maidens of Sõrve,  
a maiden gazes through the fence,  
through the gate of the fence.  
If only that man were mine,  
the one riding along the road,  
along the road, along the land,  
riding along the paths.  
Apple to him like the oven,  
head like the day,  
belt like the rainbow,  
hat like a king’s crown.  
Go past me, man,  
go through, cunning boy,  
pay attention to this road,  
mark the paths in the book,  
mark the writings on the gloves!  
Come back in autumn,  
take me from the rainflows,  
redeem me from the snowfall,  
stop the winter weather,  
from Viru’s scythe blow,  
from Arju’s plough cranes.

label: youth_life
translation:
If you want to go to the sauna,  
invite me to be a listener,  
choose me to be a viewer;  
I know a dull girl,  
I guess a naive girl.  
Dull with tangled hair,  
naive with rough hands,  
lazy with wide shirt sleeves,  
the tall one goes to sleep on the bench.  
Take a very tiny one,  
a tiny one, a little grain,  
a little wild one, a little diligent one.

label: youth_life
translation:
Anne has been a horn for a long time,  
Kaie has been a bear's horn.

label: youth_life
translation:
I came home from work tired,  
weary from the manor’s courtyard.  
I went into the hot parlor,  
life’s tools left hanging,  
through the parlor’s window.  
Maids were smiling in the corner.  
The housekeeper came out of the room.  
“Girls, why are you laughing?  
That is the tail of a dumb wolf,  
the leg of a hare from Jändrik,  
or the paw of a bear from the wilderness.”  
The housekeeper then replied:  
“That is not the tail of a dumb wolf  
nor the leg of a hare from Jändrik  
nor the paw of a bear from the wilderness.  
That is the tip of a teopoiss (tea boy)  
and the finger of a spirit boy.”  
- - -  
From there he went to the shirt hedgehogs,  
but disappeared into the sixfold folds.  
From there he traveled along the journey,  
reached the source of life,  
there he warmed himself in the cozy spot.

label: youth_life
translation:
The dull girl’s bangs were long,  
the lazy girl’s braid was long,  
the cradle’s belt was wet,  
the slender heart was watery.

label: youth_life
translation:
Iiut-tiiut Tiina’s thighs,  
the bear had torn Kaie’s thighs,  
the snake had bitten Maie’s thighs,  
the wolf had gnawed Anne’s.

label: youth_life
translation:
Mother dear, granny dear,  
granny dear, mother dear,  
Put this daughter to a husband,  
who walks along the streets,  
fog-headed, fog-haired,  
handsome little hands in hers.  
If you don't put her, don’t plead!  
Let her stay knocking at home,  
picking mushrooms by the wall,  
let  
a birch grow on her neck,  
a willow on her forehead,  
a spruce on her brow,  
a juniper among her hairs.

label: youth_life
translation:
/Beautiful girl, beautiful girl, white young lady:/  
/Do you promise, do you promise to come to me:/  
/To come to me, to come to me, to be with me:/  
/I will build a barn, I will build a barn out of meat:/  
/A roof on top, a roof on top made from a hen’s egg:/  
/I will put inside, I will put inside a silk bed:/  
/Into the bed, into the bed a silk cover:/  
/Around it, around it a garland of bride’s roses:/  
/At the root, at the root I will put a young man:/  
/Sit down, sit down on the bench:/  
/The boy’s hand, the boy’s hand on your neck:/  
/As soft as, as soft as a pillow:/

label: youth_life
translation:
Taiut, taiut, to Tammik,
Taiut to the Tammik path,
There was bad boy merchandise there:
Five received an old song in return,
Six received a dry shoe in return,
Seven received a boot leg in return,
A hundred received an old whip in return.
They were used to fence the herd yard,
To spread in the barn.
From them a bridge was made in the swamp,
A fence was made in the meadow.
Yet the crooks did not end,
The old boys from Tammik either.
Their horses are gray in front,
The men are sunburned on top,
Pea stalks as small ropes,
Bean stalks as cigar ribbons.
Look where the Moe boys are then:
The horse in front is like an oven;
The man on top is like the day,
They have silver small ropes,
Cigar ribbons made of fox tail.

label: youth_life
translation:
Aiut, to Taiut in Tammik
Taiut to the village of Tammik
From there comes
Five to the old visa
Six to the dry shoe
Seven to the wall log
Eight to the coat
Nine to the horse
Ten to the plow ox.

label: youth_life
translation:
Where are the three of us going,  
Over the field with five!  
To the meadow under St. John's Day.  
I took the bow, left the other,  
Started to take the third one,  
What did I find there then?  
I found an eagle under the bow.  
What does the eagle have under its wing?  
An axe under the eagle’s wing.  
What is at the end of the axe?  
A shaving at the end of the axe.  
What is being chopped from that shaving?  
Base logs are being chopped.  
What is being chopped from that log?  
St. John's Day's barn is being chopped.  
What is inside that barn?  
A lock is inside the barn.  
What is inside the lock?  
A bed is inside the lock.  
What is inside the bed?  
Straw below, hay above.  
What is above the hay?  
A plank above the hay.  
What is above the plank?  
A pillow above the plank.  
What is above the pillow?  
Four young maidens.  
One is leaning on a golden belt,  
The second wears green,  
The third beats a hamstring,  
The fourth weeps for a young man.  
Don't you cry, little maiden,  
He is already seen coming,  
His head peeks above the forest,  
His feet rarely below the forest,  
His body twists through the middle of the forest.

label: youth_life
translation:
Come to me, be mine,  
I will put you to easy work –  
To learn how to be strong,  
To seek a head for the day,  
To make a place for the year.

label: youth_life
translation:
Little Riinukene sister  
Who told you to walk so prettily  
Across the beautiful yard  
Over the straight bridge  
You looked at our shy lad  
If only that man were mine  
I would stand without eating  
Winter without fuel.  
Oh, you frost devils  
Half the rascals of Põltsamaa  
What do you have against my sister?  
Put a wreath on her head  
A slave's leaf in front of her forehead  
A singing leaf on her bald head—

label: youth_life
translation:
Oh, you deceitful shepherd boy  
You loved your wife  
Promised to bring three pairs of shoes  
One pair smooth, gray wooden  
The third pair rocky shoes  
Smooth shoes for having fun  
Wooden shoes for carrying wood  
Rocky shoes for going to church.  
I got there,  
And I stayed there  
They gave me a blow on the crown of my head  
It was at the doorstep of the cellar  
They struck my knees  
They broke my money pouch  
That was the pay of the deceitful shepherd  
The wife’s lover.

label: youth_life
translation:
I went out wandering in the evening,  
Looking for a girl.  
The girls did not want to go,  
Because I didn’t have a silk vest on,  
A silk vest, calico shirt.  
On my feet were German boots,  
At night no store bags,  
Around my neck a kerchief.  
Then I went home with a sad mind,  
With a sad mind, with mourning on my lips.  
The maiden came to meet me at the gate,  
The old man came to meet me on the street,  
They began to ask me.  
Why do you weep, young boy?  
Why do I weep, old lady?  
And why do I mourn, old man?  
The girls did not want to go,  
Because I didn’t have a silk vest on,  
A silk vest, calico shirt.  
On my feet were German boots,  
At night no store bags,  
Around my neck a kerchief.  
"No, no, no, no, young boy,  
Tomorrow we’ll go to Huus’s store,  
From there I’ll bring you a silk vest,  
A silk vest, calico shirt.  
On your feet German boots,  
At night store bags,  
Around your neck a kerchief."

label: youth_life
translation:
Hooves, hooves on Tiiu's thighs  
The bear had attacked Kaie's thighs  
The wolf had bitten Anne  
The bear had chased Kaie away.

label: youth_life
translation:
Who went down to the hayfield?  
Jaan went down to the hayfield,  
Kaare stayed behind, mowing the other,  
what is there under Kaare's side?  
An eagle under Kaare's side,  
What is there under the eagle's wing?  
An axe under the eagle's wing.  
What is there under the axe's blade?  
Shavings under the axe's blade.  
What are those shavings made into?  
A house is built for Jaan,  
What is put inside the chamber?  
A bed is put inside the chamber?  
What is put inside the bed?  
Straw below, hay above.  
What is placed on top of the hay?  
A pillow below, a coverlet above.  
What is put on top of the coverlet?  
Three young maidens.  
One weaves golden thread,  
the second binds a silk ribbon,  
the third cries for the young brother.  
Why are you crying, maiden,  
why are you crying for the young brother?  
He is already coming:  
his head appears above the forest,  
his feet beneath the forest,  
his body turning in the forest.

label: youth_life
translation:
I had only one son alone,  
he vowed to live without a wife,  
to live without a partner.  
He started living, he existed,  
he could neither live without a wife  
nor thrive without a partner.  
But he went from home to seek a bride,  
for a little while on a maiden’s path.  
He returned from the bride-seeking,  
then went to the room behind,  
placed his hat on the table,  
gloves on the edge of the hat,  
while himself began to cry;  
the father then asked the son:  
"Why are you crying, young son?"  
"Why should I not cry, dear father?  
I cannot live without a wife,  
cannot thrive without a partner.  
I went just briefly to seek a bride,  
a little while on a maiden’s path;  
the girls did not like me,  
started to bark at me.  
You don’t have a chintz shirt on,  
a chintz shirt, a silk vest,  
lace ribbons around your neck,  
German boots on your feet."  
The father then understood, responded:  
"Don’t cry, young son,  
let’s go to Riga to buy clothes,  
we will buy a chintz shirt to wear,  
a chintz shirt, a silk vest,  
lace ribbons for your neck,  
German boots for your feet."  
I went again to seek a bride,  
for a little while on the maiden’s path,  
then the girls loved me,  
they kissed me sweetly,  
embraced me dearly.  
Then I came from bride-seeking back home,  
brought a bride with me,  
from across the gate,  
her chest shone with rubies,  
apron with splendid lace.

label: youth_life
translation:
Swamp I plowed – the piglets  
Field I plowed – the crows I watered  
Then I let the girls go picking  
Who was quick to pick  
Quick to throw the sheaf  
That girl for my name  
And a wreath on my tongue  
Then I started feeding the horse  
So I could ride the horse up close  
In a pile, I carried oats  
In the shade, I fetched water  
Flour in my pocket, I endured  
Then I rode straight to my father-in-law’s house  
Then I rode straight to my mother-in-law’s house  
Hello father-in-law, boot tops  
Hello mother-in-law, boiled neck  
Are the girls at home,  
Our girl by the well  
At the well, watering the herd  
I rode again to the well  
Hello girl, boiled neck  
Bring water to the calves,  
Bring water to my horses  
Let me pour water down  
Mouth black and rough  
Ear to ear linked  
I am a poor traveler  
Traveler, land measurer  
Messenger of kings  
Handler of German affairs  
Writer of big letters  
The girl heard again, the voice said  
You are not a poor traveler  
Traveler, land measurer  
Messenger of kings  
Handler of German affairs  
Writer of big letters  
You are a cheating lad  
Why do you have spurs on your whip  
And silver buckles on your strap  
And a horse’s tail in a braid.

label: youth_life
translation:
I went to Laar for a song,  
Down to the meadow below Aru.  
I began to gather the song,  
To pick the hay stalks.  
I found an eagle under a bow.  
What is under the eagle's wing?  
An axe under the eagle's wing.  
What is on the axe's blade?  
A shaving on the axe's blade.  
What is made from that shaving?  
Jaan’s barn is built.  
What is inside Jaan’s barn?  
Four young maidens.  
One of them wears a golden belt,  
Another has a tail of alder,  
The third wears a green dress,  
The fourth weeps for a young man.

label: youth_life
translation:
We are clean bachelors  
and demand to go courting.  
And none of us has a man's wisdom  
nor any desire for marriage.  
We are going to court Koigi.  
Koigi's steward has three daughters:  
One is Anne, the second Kaie,  
the third is Litter-Liisukene.  
Anne was naked like a stove,  
Kai was in rags,  
Liisu was at the pot,  
a little pipe in her fist  
and a small ladle in hand.  
He searches but completely ignorantly:  
whatever was bigger, he put in his mouth,  
whatever was smaller, he threw away,  
whatever was just right, he put in the pot.

label: youth_life
translation:
Mari was fond of strawberries,  
called the boys to the spruce grove,  
behind the room to the oak grove.  
The linden tree, how beautiful it was,  
Mari already knew that.  
On top of it went her swing,  
letting the linden branches move.  
Then the boys' eyes turned red  
as if they were seeing different worlds.  
Fall down, little Mari,  
Fall on my six-string,  
lay on my wide ribbon.  
If you don’t fall, I won’t call you.  
Pull your back like a cat,  
Mari’s bed is at the top of the linden.

label: youth_life
translation:
I rode to my father-in-law, I rode to my mother-in-law.  
I rode to my father-in-law's doorstep.  
Under the meadow near the pond,  
Under the table by the door,  
Under the thick post of the boat.  
I myself was watching the doorstep,  
The hole of the doorstep's stick.  
The daughter was dozing on the chair,  
The old woman under the stove,  
The old man was watching the end of the rod.  
The fire began to die down,  
The stoves began to go out;  
The old woman said to the daughter,  
"Go sleep in the stable,"  
Then the daughter took a wild mood,  
And went to sleep in the stable.  
.......... .......... ......... .......  
Then grumbling behind the backside.....  
I took the gray one out from under the pond,  
Under the table by the door,  
Under the thick post of the boat.  
Then I rode out from under the pond,  
I rode down to Andrekse.  
There were marten daughters,  
And vesihall sisters.  
There I was invited inside,  
And a chair was given to me.  
A chair was given to me,  
And a table was set before me.

label: youth_life
translation:
Aim for the woman behind the sickle,  
watch from behind the rod,  
take the stroke of the scythe.  
Do not lurk on the church path,  
there all are proud and beautiful.

label: youth_life
translation:
Ants was a man from Harju, Joak was a man from Järva.  
Ants was a humble man from Harju,  
Joak was a stout man from Järva.  
Ants bought a horse from Harju  
and a saddle from a Saare German,  
rode across Saare bridge,  
the bridge planks creaked.  
The girls of Saare smiled,  
secretly they watched.  
If only that suitor were mine,  
the one who rides across the bridge there.  
His horse is as strong as a stove,  
he himself is as bright as the day,  
a hat like a church bell,  
a belt like the flag of Riga city.  
Then I heard, I answered back:  
Beautiful girls are seen from afar,  
lovely girls are seen from a distance,  
only an empty one knows a girl’s heart,  
maybe there is a bug inside.  
A special one under the teeth,  
a bee on the mind.

label: youth_life
translation:
Girls, little birds,  
Little doves in braids,  
Linen cloth little birds,  
Beautiful wreath-wearers!  
Do you know where you will go?  
In what group will you swim,  
Where will you stop in company?  
Some will end up in the dry spruce forest,  
Some in the wet pine forest,  
Some rarely in the aspen forest,  
Some flying into the alder forest,  
Some in the wise oak forest.  
Who ends up in the dry spruce forest,  
Will get a bad man.  
Who ends up in the wet pine forest,  
Will get a drinking man.  
Who gets the dear birch forest,  
Will get a dear companion.  
Who gets the wise oak forest,  
Will manage a farm.  
Who flies into the alder forest,  
Will worry about bread.  
Who gets the bad aspen forest,  
Will get a bad fate.

label: youth_life
translation:
I went to the village barn roof,  
The girls did not want to go,  
They started barking at me.  
You don’t have a chintz shirt on your back,  
A chintz shirt, a silk vest,  
Around your neck a calico scarf,  
On your feet German boots.  
I went home crying,  
Home to the cabin.  
Then I put a hat on the table,  
Gloves on the edge of the hat.  
Then an old woman came into the room,  
And an old man came into the room.  
Why are you crying, young boy?  
Why am I crying, old woman?  
Why am I crying, old man?  
I went to the village barn roof,  
The girls did not want to go,  
There I got bad treatment,  
Jeering from the girls.  
Don’t cry, young boy,  
Tomorrow we’ll go to the new store,  
From there I’ll bring you a chintz shirt,  
A chintz shirt, a silk vest,  
Around your neck a calico scarf,  
On your feet German boots,  
On your back a German tailcoat.

label: youth_life
translation:
Let's go down to the meadow  
I mowed a swath, I mowed two  
I cut a third for the threshing floor  
I found an eagle under the swath  
A whole feather under the eagle's wing  
What's whole there?  
A splinter is stuck right in the nose.  
What is cut from that splinter?  
They cut a St. John's Day hay rake  
What to put into that rake?  
Four young maidens.  
One is shaping a golden belt  
The second ties a silk ribbon  
The third is weaving a wave pattern  
The fourth is crying for a young man.

label: youth_life
translation:
Oh you gentle little brother,
Do not take a tall wife!
The tall one goes to sleep on the bench,
But the shins stick up against the wall,
The knee bones against the doorframe,
And the head against the beam’s edge.
Take a short wife:
The short one milks the cow,
Drives the herd far away,
Far away to the hayfield,
The bulls to the golden barn,
The calves to the rook’s hill.

label: youth_life
translation:
We are three sisters,
Three ears of grain in the field,
Three suitors for the home:
One was clever from Viljandi,
The second wise from Tammiku,
The third from our own village.
From our village's high heart,
From our parish's fair heart,
From our family's fine heart.

label: youth_life
translation:
I can't find the girl, where she has gone.  
From here the tracks have gone straight,  
Having tied the shoestrings.  
Now I have found the girl again.  
Why did you resist coming to us,  
In our yard beneath the apple trees,  
In the grassy garden with little roses,  
At the gate we have tall birch trees.

label: youth_life
translation:
A young maiden, a young girl,  
Went to the meadow on the hill,  
Between the garden patches,  
"Come," called her little brother,  
"Come home, my sister,  
You have suitors at home!"  
Where did these suitors come from?  
Suitors came from Kuura,  
I do not want to go to Kuura,  
In Kuura, one eats harsh bread.

label: youth_life
translation:
If I were Olev  
I would wear the helmets,  
I would carry the long sword.  
I am afraid to wear the helmet,  
To fall into the comb,  
To reach the street.  
I would take a young wife  
I am afraid of young weeping,  
Suddenly  
To put a bow on the duck.  
Suddenly it becomes troublesome,  
To put an arrow in the eye.  
Do not put it in father-in-law’s eye,  
Do not put it in mother-in-law’s eye.

label: youth_life
translation:
I went into the forest, fell asleep,  
Under the porch to rest.  
The wind came, raised a storm,  
Carried my oars away,  
Filled my bucket with water.  
I hung the bucket to dry,  
To the top of a birch tree to chirp.  
Came the cruel claws of the goldfinch,  
Took it away from drying,  
From chirping on the birch tree.  
The village boy was left crying,  
Crying, longing.  
Oh, that wicked little goldfinch,  
Where he took my little bucket,  
A pretty little toy.

label: youth_life
translation:
I went to the forest for hazelnuts,  
But up the hill for strawberries.  
I went to the forest, fell asleep,  
Resting under the bush.  
The wind came and stirred a storm,  
And broke my oars in two.  
One took one oar,  
Another took the other oar,  
The third one took everything away.  
The village boy got free from wandering,  
From roaming on a dark night.

label: youth_life
translation:
I wanted to go to the sauna.  
I looked through the keyhole:  
My daughter was dozing with a soft face,  
The peers were burning cleanly.  
I took up a brave spirit,  
I stepped boldly into the room.  
Anne was given to me,  
Kaie was traded to me.  
Father-in-law started scolding me,  
Mother-in-law began reproaching me:  
"How could you dare come to the sauna,  
You have nothing of your own!  
You have a vest from other brothers,  
A knife from other young men,  
A sheath from other acquaintances,  
An apple from the village heard about,  
A gift sent from the village."  
But I understood, I answered again:  
"Oh, oh, oh, dear father-in-law,  
Oh, oh, oh, dear mother-in-law!  
Surely here in the sauna there would be no sketching,  
And on the new one, no crawling,  
First, I should come to the sauna for you.  
The mites are dancing on the floor,  
The lice go to the corner with a broom strapped on.  
Who made your breads?  
The cows made your breads.  
The oxen drove the fire to the oven."  
"Where is the sign then?"  
"The ox's horns are doughy,  
The cow's hooves are ashes."

label: youth_life
translation:
I had a little blackbird,  
A speck of flax cloth.  
I fed it, I gave it water,  
I was tending it for myself.  
With it, I go to the western Kõpu peninsula,  
With it, I take the sleeper from the room,  
From under the blood sausage bed,  
I take the sleeper from on top of the stove.

label: youth_life
translation:
Dear brother,
Do not take a wife from the manor.
In the manor, there are certain women,
Beautiful from below the windows,
Finer from above the sill.
Take the enemy's children from the parish,
Next to a slave from the village,
Who knows how to work with fire,
Milk the cow without a pail.

label: youth_life
translation:
A blissful little evening comes,  
a miserable little twilight,  
then those loud quarrels arise,  
the barnyard ducks argue.

label: youth_life
translation:
Listen, dear little daughter,  
don't believe the wolf's story.  
The wolf has those crazy tales,  
the bear has cunning words.  
But he promises to bring slippers,  
a bunch of clog shoes;  
he will live, he will be,  
then there will be spinning,  
the mitten immediately yapping.

label: youth_life
translation:
If you start to take a woman,  
then invite me as the matchmaker;  
I know a dull maiden,  
I consider bad maidens.  
Dull with tangled hair,  
angry, watery eyes,  
angry faces red.  
Do not take a big woman,  
a big one will make your throat silent,  
a tall one will sleep on the bench,  
take a quite small one,  
small and sharp.

label: youth_life
translation:
Mother, dear little mother,  
Marry that daughter off,  
The one who walks along the yard,  
Foghead, fog-haired,  
Nice, strong sleeves.  
If you don't marry her off, don't ask,  
Let her stay at home chopping wood,  
Picking mushrooms by the garden edge.  
A birch tree around her neck,  
An alder on the rye,  
A spruce on the eyebrow corner.

label: youth_life
translation:
Boys, boys, bright-eyed,
Boys, boys, ring-collared,
Do not laugh at the maidens,
Do not tease the girls.
You will surely suffer a bride shortage,
A lack of brides, a shortage of women.
You squat on the village street,
You loiter at the farmyard gate,
Looking for a girl there,
Begging for a bride there:
"Dear master of the household,
Kind mistress of the family!
Give me that daughter,
The one swung on the swing,
Rocked softly in the cradle."
The mistress listens and replies:
"I will not give you my daughter.
She may stay at home with me,
Sit by the stove,
Pick mushrooms by the wall,
Before I give her to you."

label: youth_life
translation:
Why didn’t you come to us last year,  
The year before that you didn’t come either,  
When rivers ran without oil,  
Springs flowed with vodka,  
And the garden bed was peppery?  
Now you have come to the sour eel,  
To this sad month,  
Now there are no more peers in the family,  
No village comes to the sauna.

label: youth_life
translation:
I set out walking,  
When a maiden came towards me,  
A maiden, like a flock of sheep.  
In front were quarrelsome lads,  
Behind were quarrelsome young men,  
In the middle, lovely maidens.  
I carefully watched,  
I am neither in a crowd,  
Nor in a row,  
Nor among companions.  
My sweetheart,  
A good bride beyond the seas,  
The wind carries her health,  
Willows bow in prayer,  
Clouds stretch long and wide;  
So many greetings to her,  
As many trees are in the grove,  
Straight and tall maples,  
White birch trees;  
In every treetop a titmouse,  
On every branch a squirrel,  
In every crown singing birds,  
All branches filled with squirrels,  
All leaves filled with birds,  
So many greetings to her.

label: youth_life
translation:
I am not allowed to prove singing,  
Not allowed to proclaim loudly –  
There are listeners in the spruce woods;  
Speakers in the young forest,  
All the forests are full of men,  
Wastelands full of walkers,  
Groves full of underbrush breakers,  
Sharpeners of spears;  
Some are perhaps looking to buy,  
Some are watching to sell,  
Some are aiming for maidens:  
If I had a bow, I would ask for a maiden,  
If I had a gun, I would try to shoot,  
If I had a net, I would catch.  
But I hear, I answer back:  
Hear, dear young men,  
A bird is caught by a gun,  
A fish is caught with a bow,  
A fish is caught in a net,  
A maiden is caught with an arrow,  
Send her with bread,  
Bring her with beer,  
Test her with a bun.

label: youth_life
translation:
Listen, dear young man,  
If you are going to take a wife in the west,  
Then take me with you:  
I am a dull girl to you,  
The last angry girl –  
A dull girl with long hair,  
A lazy girl with long braids,  
A slender waist.  
You surely rode to the marriage proposals,  
You surely wanted to have one –  
You rode to Viru's farm,  
You visited Harju crosses,  
You sent for West’s bride,  
But you did not find one to have.  
Look at the women along the church roads:  
All you see are churchways,  
Girls among other peoples;  
Aim for a woman even without dowry,  
Look at women from other villages,  
Try even from places unknown.  
Do not look for a wife from the manor;  
There are all sorts at the manor,  
The beautiful ones beneath the windows;  
But seek from the orphans –  
There you will find maidens in the granary,  
At the front of the granary are lively ones,  
At the back of the granary serious ones;  
There stand poor children,  
Find one from there for yourself:  
She knows how to walk around the fire,  
Sets the bed without sparks,  
Cooks the broth without scum,  
Warms the room without smoke.  
If you take a farm girl –  
She will tease you out of spite,  
Torture you out of anger;  
When she returns to the child’s home,  
If she teases you out of spite,  
She will pretend to be fond of a groom –  
The fire will not end in the house,  
No spark in the bedpost,  
Fruits will not ripen on the tree:  
But seek a woman from the dangers,  
A taker of young tears.

label: youth_life
translation:
Mari was a girl, Mari was a woman,
