She gave soap to make clearer.  
To make foam whiter  
The day gave time to wash the head  
The moon to dry the hair  
I put the spruce to dry  
To sway in the apple tree  
To shine in the pines  
The spruce dried with golden hair  
The apple tree with silver hair  
The pine with gray hair  
The boys of Albu barked  
The boys of Sõidla rode around  
They thought the moon would shine  
The day gently shine  
The stars sparkle in the sky  
Those were my white hairs  
They wanted to crop my head  
To shorten the flaxen hair  
I gave to crop the head  
To shorten the flaxen hair  
Now Hans comes from Harju too  
Now Jaak from Järva too  
Peeter from long Piibe too  
They have scissors in hand  
Shears in the pocket too  
But they crop my head  
Shorten the flaxen hair  
Hans brings shoes with hooks  
Jaan brings shoes with leather straps  
Siim brings shoes with spikes  
I throw Hans’s shoes into the oven  
I throw Siim’s shoes in the shit  
I put Jaan’s shoes on my feet  
Then westward with shoes to the church  
Shoes click underfoot  
Laces snap behind  
Hair stands on the head  
Goes up to the armpits  
Sways over the shoulders  
I pass through the men’s men  
I slip also through the boys  
Albu boys are kind brothers  
Don’t think  
That I will become a bad woman  
Become one bad, stay one bad  
Become a kind one or maybe old  
Not even a whole parish  
I will become a woman on the Narva road  
A slippery woman on the city road  
A suitable woman in Paide  
My husband over the seas  
Drinks there at river’s edge  
Under the bluish-gray bridge  
Under the watery-gray mill  
Under the church of lavender  
I cannot ride to say  
To make a place for him  
To turn at the pillowcase  
The wind takes him entirely away  
The cloud pulls him  
What a life I have  
The life of a mistress I have  
The daughter of a lady’s lap  
She comes with a carriage after me  
Rides a sledge at seven  
Drives the horse at nine  
Already from that we get by three  
That we started well  
Let us finish comfortably

label: youth_life
translation:
This girl is even crazy  
Foolish in her head  
Who marries young  
Without gaining skill,  
Thinks to charm the man  
Thinks to raise skill.  
The man puts in mad work  
The skill weaves the fabric.  
If you don’t tend the fabric storeroom,  
The husband’s clothes storeroom,  
And your own jewelry storeroom,  
Then you will face the whip of the hearth;  
Then you will soon get fists  
Swift on your face.

label: youth_life
translation:
What was it for  
That I walk near the villages  
My own is not here  
My companion does not grow here  
My own is on their own path  
My companion is far away  
A good man across the seas  
A dear companion across the waters  
There he swings in the hidden forest  
Bends the flexible bow  
Sways under the net  
Ties under the strap  
Now I want to talk to him  
Nights do not pass sleeping together  
Nor whispering close to the ear  
May the wind carry greetings to him  
May the rains send messages  
May the clouds linger and watch.  
So many greetings to him  
As there are wood bushes  
Straight hazel  
Fine rowan  
Proper apple tree,  
White maple.  
Proper apple trees in the grove  
My fiancé's true mother  
Maples white on the mountain  
My fiancé's white mother  
There was cunning fish in the sea  
My fiancé more cunning.

label: youth_life
translation:
These are the men we have  
Try to stay away if you are in Järvamaa  
They don’t hesitate to resist  
To chatter like a milker  
To lie down on the bench  
To give a good whip to the bucket.  
Into the peat bog grows a forest  
A row grows by the alder grove  
Tall trees go into stacks  
The foundations of the barns  
Without young men and men  
Without sharpening the scythe.

label: youth_life
translation:
We used to have a whole bunch
A big amount of goods.
There was quite a flock of maidens.
Now there are many gone
The herd has disappeared
The brood has been scattered
The stock has been separated.
Now I am left alone to tend the goods,
To call the chicks,
To pick flax seeds,
To separate the seeds of the clothes,
Among the beans,
In the middle of the nice seeds.

label: youth_life
translation:
I cut the meadow hill  
I turn the center of the fields  
I cry at the edge of the meadow.  
Who is coming home to call?  
For my own brother.  
Come home, my sister,  
Your suitors have come to the house  
Five vodkas, six suitors.  
I hear it, I respond again:  
Dear brother  
If they have come, let them come  
The gate post does not tire  
Break the room's digging cake,  
The workbench is not for the landowner  
Holding the suitor’s horse,  
Carrying the field's aid,  
Surely the pressure on the ring's aid  
To stab behind the wall  
Who must keep the suitor’s horses  
Carries the suitor’s field aid.

label: youth_life
translation:
Taurus  
When the hay was not mowed  
Taurus  
When the song was not sung  
Taurus  
When the berry was not picked  
Taurus  
When the boy was untouched.

label: youth_life
translation:
The evening of Saturday is coming  
A little Sunday day.  
The girl goes to bed with the child,  
The brother goes with the young sapling,  
I go crying to the corner  
I poke towards the empty bed.  
I turned my feet and found Juan,  
I turned the sail and found the wall  
I turned to the side and found cold  
Where I stood the walls were wet  
Where I cried the corners were wet.  
The cold water was flowing down the side  
The dark water under the carpet.

label: youth_life
translation:
I know a girl with a pointed hat  
A girl with a black lock of hair  
Then came a widower in response  
With widow’s gloves on hand  
With widow’s letters in gloves  
Immediately asking me:  
Young maiden, young girl  
Will you come to me  
To be mine, my own  
To look after early  
To milk five cows  
To feed five pigs  
To do the work under the stove  
To lay out the carpet?  
I surely hear and answer back  
I will not come to you  
To you, the widower  
To your dream of a horse  
Better I know a girl with a pointed hat  
A girl with a black lock of hair.  

Now came a young man in response  
A young man, a plump boy  
Immediately asking me:  
Hello, young maiden  
Beautiful, plump and petite  
Will you perhaps come to me?  
To be mine, my own  
To look after early  
To milk two cows  
To feed two pigs  
To weave my fabric  
To sew the shirt border  
To do the work under the stove  
To lay out the carpet. –  
I surely hear and answer back  
Yes, I will come to you  
To be yours, my own  
To look after early  
To milk two cows  
To feed two pigs  
To weave your fabric  
To sew the shirt border  
To do the work under the stove  
To lay out the carpet.

label: youth_life
translation:
In our village several young men  
About forty lads  
Went to the drinking place  
To wet their throats  
Swimming across the lake  
Dancing behind the lake.  
Then came from the maiden group  
Two from a distant herd.  
Some of you were young men  
Some of you were young and foolish  
Outside is market goods  
In the street are seller's goods  
Maiden goods in the chamber  
Maidservant goods in the household  
Foal goods in the pasture.

label: youth_life
translation:
The moon shines from the Kuura river,
The day from the Pärnu spring.
But I am among the girls,
Between two girls,
Under the shoulders of five girls,
Under the blanket of six girls.
The moon shone along my side,
The day wheel hit along,
The stars stood at the edges.

label: youth_life
translation:
Oh my little brother Ella  
If you want to marry a woman  
If you want a whip  
If you want a blue flower  
Do not look at the shadows!  
Do not look at the thorns.  
Look at those with braided hair  
Know those with wild hair  
Look at those with combed hair.  
The braided-haired one goes to cut  
The combed one goes to weave cloth  
The wild-haired one goes to work.  
Oh my little brother Ella  
Let me sing the words back,  
Take the enemy's patch  
Cut off the slave’s tail  
They know how to walk in fire  
They lie without sparks  
They milk the cow without a chandelier  
They strain milk in the moonlight  
They stew soup without herbs.

label: youth_life
translation:
I am not a bully out of spite  
Out of spite bullying the shores  
But my mouth is for cursing inside  
Backside for slandering  
The fool laughs at me, the rogue praises me  
My own man always takes me.  
My own is not here  
My barley does not grow here.  
My own is in Holland  
Where there were fishing shores  
My own man across the seas  
A handsome man across the waves.

label: youth_life
translation:
Virulasi five-six  
Arjakaid seven-eight  
Still a Järva boy alone  
And also a Järva herdsman boy  
One ribbon to this ribbon  
I put one ribbon on the ribbon  
I throw it into the pear tree.

label: youth_life
translation:
Oh, oh, oh, oh, lover’s scarf  
Early I took the weary scarf  
Early I confirmed the engagement  
Early I exchanged the rings  
Without the old woman’s knowledge  
Without the mother’s knowledge  
Without the elder’s consent  
Without the dear one’s hearing.  
They caught me, sharp Jüris  
They wanted the children of the house  
The girl neither gave nor allowed  
Nor did I even go  
The girl gave no kiss  
Nor allowed any touch  
Seeing the hunger in the eye  
The girl gave not a single one  
Nor allowed any caress  
I myself did not go, little flower.

label: youth_life
translation:
Waves-waves weddings on the beach  
For some men weddings in the forest  
The trees are tall wedding guests  
The alders wide beggars  
The feeding piece is a feeding table  
The field edge is a bench.

label: youth_life
translation:
Juotme  
The women went to the meadow.  
They made a wedding in the garden.  
Who did they invite to the wedding?  
The crane with the golden spur  
The crow with the copper sabers  
The titmouse angrily went without oil  
The sparrow tried to pull  
The dung beetle put in the fools.  
Who went to try fishing?  
The hen went to try fishing  
The rooster went to run to the threshing floor.

label: youth_life
translation:
Let the young girls have fun,  
Let the wise women frolic –  
God commands to enjoy pleasure,  
The Heavenly Father to celebrate.  
Pleasure is to eat, pleasure is to drink,  
Pleasure is to live for pleasure;  
There is no pleasure in doing work,  
Pleasure is to go on a ramble,  
With dear crutches.  
The soldier does not tie this knot,  
Nor does the warrior paint it,  
Nor do they put it on a raft.  
The soldier ties the knots whole,  
The warrior paints them white,  
The well-fed were put on the raft.

label: youth_life
translation:
Be proud, young men,  
Be proud, go to the hills,  
Be bold, buy black ones,  
Go to the hills, buy ears;  
Buy laces for the whip's handle,  
Lovely bows for the whip's handle,  
Copper between the joints.  
Ride to the maidens' homes,  
To the families of the eel girls –  
There you will have food on the table,  
There you will be lifted down,  
Placed below the seat;  
Taken to the chamber to sleep  
Half the night by the brother,  
Half the night you slept,  
The other half you thought –  
The rooster crowed, the maiden did not hear,  
The rooster crowed a second time,  
The maiden heard neither;  
The rooster crowed a third time,  
The maiden turned to the other side.  
The suitor began to think –  
To think – to speak:  
I sit by my road’s edge,  
I jump by my ear’s edge,  
I let my song run along;  
I offer my hand from the road’s edge,  
I speak from the ear’s edge –  
I tell tales from the clearing’s edge:  
Farewell, maiden,  
You will fall behind me,  
I won’t leave you,  
As long as the flower blooms,  
The purpling leaves flourish.

label: youth_life
translation:
The girls were milking on the hill  
I am milking behind the hill  
Golden scissors in hand  
Bright border rails  
Why does the girl limit me?  
I pay with a branch base  
I throw the bundles to the bottom of the pond  
Golden buckles on the skull cap  
But I take the bundles to Germany  
Golden buckles to Courland

label: youth_life
translation:
My dear little brother  
You've been to see a girl from this land  
From these villages  
Between the parishes  
From the center of the district  
Ships sailed, ships sailed  
Ships went to Germany  
Half of the ships to Finland  
Push the little boats into the sea  
Send the tar boats after them  
Row down to the city of Riga  
There are three rows of girls  
One is the row of rich ladies  
The second row of poor ladies  
The third row of servants  
The row of rich ladies  
Have fields to tend  
The row of servants  
Have fields to tend  
I took in the poor child in between  
The prettiest in the middle  
She started coming home  
A big gate was hung at Olevi  
At Nigula it clanked sharply  
The bell of Tuompia beat a big drum  
The girls' ribbons stayed in the town  
The girl's things stayed in the small borough  
The brooch stayed on the friend's table  
The daughter stayed in the stone oven  
The knives stayed in the German box.

label: youth_life
translation:
What I was doing at the fair  
I refused to lift the hay  
I have no time to listen  
The bridegroom is hiding his eyes  
My time is far away  
My bridegroom is in Peipus  
He is across the sea  
A white sail in the Viru bay  
A wavy sail in Kadi village  
The wind will bring greetings  
The rain will carry the messages  
So many greetings to him  
So many words in between  
So many good words  
Straight as hazelwood  
Small as rowanberries  
True as apple trees  
White as maples.

label: youth_life
translation:
A young virgin maiden  
Do you want to come to me  
If I come to woo you  
Will you accept my answer with pride  
Or reject me angrily  
If you reject me angrily  
Then out of spite I will sing  
Spitefully praise myself  
Even criticize you  
I still have many brides in Muskus  
I still have another bride in Tartu  
A beautiful flock of stepsisters  
Rings in their ears, skirts flowing  
The rings in their ears are jingling  
The skirts flowing are rustling  
Idut-tiidut, I have wings  
If those wings take me there  
From here I will take a young wife  
A kind-hearted wife  
A passionate one from the other side.

label: youth_life
translation:
Beautiful Senni maiden  
Fair Senni beloved  
When the meadow is unmowed  
Slim Senni cows  
When the summer pasture is not yet begun  
Wretched Senni pile  
When there is no livestock in the pile  
Young Senni maiden  
When untouched by a boy  
Untouched by a dear hand  
Yet has touched a boy  
Has felt the dear hand  
Soon begins to wither  
To bear the maiden’s name.

label: youth_life
translation:
Girls are dill tips  
Dill tips are coltsfoot buds  
Beautiful as rosebuds  
Straight German sigurs  
They are made because of boys  
Halfheartedly worried for boys  
To please the men  
Then men didn’t go to sleep  
Boys were lulled to sleep  
Men slept in the forest  
Under the alder grove  
Under the spruce they bowed.

label: youth_life
translation:
I slept by Mary’s meadow  
Among the bluebells  
Between the meadowsweet  
In the middle of the globeflowers  
And even while sleeping I saw a dream  
Fig trees behind the fence  
Rowan trees behind the fence  
An apple tree was in the middle of the yard  
A big hazel tree by the path  
My grandmother’s life  
Understand this dream  
I slept by Mary’s meadow  
Among the bluebells  
Between the meadowsweet  
In the middle of the globeflowers  
And even while sleeping I saw a dream  
Fig trees behind the fence  
Rowan trees behind the fence  
An apple tree was in the middle of the yard  
A big hazel tree by the path  
Grandmother immediately heard and said  
What are you trying to riddle about?  
This has already been figured out before  
Told half the world  
You drank vodka under the fig tree  
Suitors came by the rowan tree  
The apple tree was the beer keg  
The big hazel tree is the matchmaker.

label: youth_life
translation:
A young maiden, a young man  
Let’s leave this place  
Let’s go to Finland for the summer  
For half a year to Pohla land  
For the winter already to Alutaguse  
Let’s build a stone church  
Let’s put a floor of boards  
Let’s drive in iron crosses  
Iron crosses with golden crowns  
A little altar in the corner  
Golden locks on the skull. -  
Then comes here the young maiden  
The young maiden without a girl  
Then comes the search for a groom  
Traveling on the seat plank  
Checking the foal’s hooves  
The fire cuts the groom’s shoulders  
Sparks fly from the seat plank  
The foal’s hooves flash like lightning  
The suitor’s shoes cut sparks  
Looking for a young maiden  
Trying to touch the sweetheart  
Come to me, young maiden  
Come to me and call  
The maiden hears and answers  
I will not come to you  
I will neither come nor call  
Come, indeed, young maiden  
Come to me, my blooming one  
Come to watch my wealth  
Come to tend my money  
Come to be my pig feeder  
Come to beat my pillow  
Come to separate my linen. -  
I will neither come nor call  
The suitor hears and answers  
Come, indeed, young maiden  
The maiden hears and answers again  
I will not come nor call  
The suitor hears and answers  
Why don’t you come to me?  
Because you do not come to me  
Because the yard is muddy  
The cattle pen full of holes  
Young maiden, young man  
There is much stirring on the seat plank  
The cows have slept thickly  
The bulls have fouled the haylofts  
The stallions have circled the cows  
The maiden hears and answers  
Would if only the yard were planked  
The cattle pen woven from cloth  
The bundles from fine flax  
The bridges from silk thread  
Still I will not come to you  
To you, the vague desire  
The groom’s dream  
To the face of Kuera’s hut  
There I go where created  
Where my creator has made a place  
Where Mary has given a home  
Where my blood has drawn  
Where my luck has been counted;  
Where my strength has been followed  
Would if only there were a pillar in the yard too  
A hundred bundles of pillars  
Still I go where created  
Where my blood has drawn  
Where my color has entered.

label: youth_life
translation:
Sisters, dear ones  
Now let's gather as three  
We must consult as four  
Let's go away from here, elsewhere  
Let's go to Finland for the summer  
And to Hiiumaa for the autumn  
For the winter beyond the seas  
There is no hay to mow there  
Nor meadow to take  
But there the girl mows the nirki  
The little mare takes the load  
The cuckoo sings on the pile  
We will not return from there  
Until a girl’s hunger comes to us  
A girl’s hunger, lack of cloth  
A void among the girls  
When we are sought at the orchard  
And driven from the meadow  
The foal trots on its hoof  
So that fire strikes the doorways  
Sparks fly around the cabins  
The mare’s harnesses are bloody  
You seek maidens  
Listening at the braided neck  
Sitting in the brooch’s embrace.

label: youth_life
translation:
Ann was a shy maiden  
Sitting on the Arju barn roof  
On top of Viru distillery  
Holding a golden stick  
The boys below hold their knees  
Without hats, without gloves  
Without a teacher's belt, without a hairpin  
Without a tin belt, without a drop  
Fall down, golden little one  
Let the wide ribbon fall down  
Fall like an apple from an apple tree  
Drop like a berry from a berry bush  
Don't fall on the stone  
On the stone, on the pot  
Make your beloved stay true  
Fall on my forehead  
Roll onto my vest  
Fall onto my hat  
I will take you to the chamber  
Into a bed of silk  
I will place many pillows  
You will grow in the chamber  
You will straighten in the silk bed  
You will swell among the pillows.

label: youth_life
translation:
Oh, my life is boring  
Oh, my party is dark  
Weepy youth  
It is worn by sorrow  
It is sunk by noise  
From wicked life into the evening  
From darkness into clouds  
Sunk down low  
At other times I would live differently  
At other hours they would come differently  
Comes that blessed little evening  
Miserable little twilight  
Father goes with mother  
Brother goes with a young girl  
I go crying to the corner  
Warming by the stove  
Regretting in the room  
I hug the old fur coat  
Oh, you old fur coat  
You are fit for wandering  
Fit for sleeping on a patchwork  
Not suitable for going to church.

label: youth_life
translation:
Before I believe a snake's tongue  
A snake's tongue, a snake's mind  
Before a young boy's tongue,  
A boy's tongue, a boy's mind.  
A boy is born a deceiver  
A deceiver and a tricker.  
He deceived the family mother  
And the poor family mother,  
Deceived the family's fine girl.  
But he promised to buy a new hat,  
A new hat, new lace,  
Proud lace with a beautiful ribbon.  
He got his punishment  
A couple of days, then a year.  
Then from the swamp he brought warm rods,  
From the willow he brought those burning rods.  
He beat the back blue,  
And twisted the neck twice.  
"That is for your new hat,  
New hat's proud lace,  
Proud lace with a beautiful ribbon!"

label: youth_life
translation:
One of us eats to eat,  
One of us drinks to drink,  
One of us buys items,  
Margu pays the money.  
You cannot take one wife,  
Another takes another wife,  
Another takes another sister.  
Then we are all linked together.  
One eats and one drinks,  
Somewhere under the oil,  
The bridegroom drinks under the bench,  
Like a hundred-year-old tail,  
One of us helps the other.

label: youth_life
translation:
The young maiden daughter,  
Be diligent in the morning,  
Earlier than the white dawn;  
Clean the room, set the table,  
Sweep under the windows;  
Silk ships are coming in,  
Merchant ships are sailing by,  
Passing by proud coaches,  
Suitors are coming in,  
Young men, lads.

label: youth_life
translation:
What is the reason for the nap,  
That my groom is a little weak?  
At the village, he also grows thin,  
Sprouts in a silk bed,  
Swells among pillows.  
He does not grow without a heel,  
Does not grow without leg meat,  
Swelling does not thicken without milk!

label: youth_life
translation:
Family boys are deceitful,  
The father-in-law deceives, the mother-in-law deceives,  
The fine young lady of the family deceives!  
In the cold village house,  
In the ugly building,  
He promised to bring a silk hat,  
He promised to bring a calico apron,  
Green with little roses,  
Down to the waist, with chestnut-colored hair.  
He will be, he will live!  
His fist is checkered,  
With faint stripes,  
Mattar with chestnut-colored hair.

label: youth_life
translation:
What suits a frantic man,
Ungrown beans?
Beans do not grow,
A man is not willing to take.
The bean asks the fabric woman,
The man desires the cloth woman;
Every day wants fine things,
Morning silk clothes,
Every noon linen,
Evening silk bedding.
If that cannot be afforded;
Then the torso feels rowan berries;
Shoulder blades of the apple tree,
Fingers of the currant bush branches.

label: youth_life
translation:
Our men like wild bulls,  
The gray oxen of Harju Jaan:  
They were fierce to fight,  
To scatter the manor boys,  
To shake the village bulls.

label: youth_life
translation:
Oh stupid and even more stupid,  
What I saw last year:  
I went to the family as a suitor,  
The family gate was a latch,  
The door below was ajar;  
The daughter of the family was in the chamber,  
In the chamber and in the cupboard,  
The cupboard door was locked,  
The key was in the old woman's pocket.

label: youth_life
translation:
Girls, little birds,  
Lovely pearl necklaces,  
Maiden with a tin curl:  
Do you know where you are flying?  
Where will you finally be taken?  
Some fly among the pigs,  
Some fly among the barnyards,  
Some roll among the cattle,  
Some find a place of bread,  
Some fly to the place of bread rolls,  
Some know to the spring shoots,  
Some notice the mountains,  
Find the place of bread,  
But fly to the place of bread rolls —  
Some got under a dry spruce,  
Some got under a wide alder,  
Some got under a dear birch,  
Some got under a slim pine,  
Some got under a wet pine.  
Who got under a dry spruce:  
That one got a bachelor man,  
Who got under a wide alder:  
That one got a widower man,  
The widow’s widow grieving,  
Choosing poor children,  
Who got under a dear birch:  
That one got a young man,  
Who got under a slim pine:  
That one got an old man,  
Who got under a wet pine:  
That one got a drunkard man.

label: youth_life
translation:
I saw the girl growing,  
Rising from the cradle,  
Immediately I went to guard,  
Feeding the pitch-black one,  
Giving rye to the gray one.  
Under the oil, I gave meals,  
Carrying rye in heaps,  
In the shade, I carried water.  
I fed the gray one for Anne,  
For Linalakk Liisu,  
For Kõrv Krõeda,  
I fed the black one to run otherwise.  
Neither the old woman’s soul knew this,  
Nor the room’s soul knew this.

label: youth_life
translation:
Virulasi five-six,  
Harjakaid seven-eight:  
From them alone come Järva men –  
Järva herdsman boy!

label: youth_life
translation:
Virgin pretty young girl  
Slender scribe  
Come to me and hasten  
I will set the sleeve to work  
No, I will not take you into the rain  
Nor send you into the storms.

label: youth_life
translation:
Virgin young maiden  
Slender at her writing desk  
Why do you hesitate when coming to me  
Coming to me; coming to me  
To me, a young man  
To me, proud of my good genes  
To the copper belt, white dawn  
Because you hesitate when coming to me  
Coming to me; being with us  
To me, a young man  
To me, proud of my good genes  
To the copper belt, white dawn  
That our yard is muddy  
The cowsheds full of holes  
Oxen treading in our yard  
The cows have slept heavily  
Foals playfully running around  
The maiden walks with the ox  
The maiden walks on the dry heath  
Walk along the edge of the garden  
Until you come to our yard  
Because you hesitate when coming to me  
Coming to me; being with us  
To me, a young man  
To me, proud of my good genes  
To the copper belt, white dawn  
That our wells are far away  
Water five versts (3.3 km each) away  
Do not complain, maiden  
The oxen will bring the water  
The reins will pull the cart  
Servants will bring the tub  
Will put the kettle on the fire  
Because you hesitate when coming to me  
Coming to me; being with us  
To me, a young man  
To me, proud of my good genes  
To the copper belt, white dawn  
That you have many debts  
More than pearl beads  
You think to pawn them  
To borrow bread  
To waste money  
To take grains  
To send salt  
You will not pawn those  
No bread will be borrowed  
No salt will be sent  
We will be thirsty at the foot  
When the harvest is poor  
The man’s gun will bring catch  
Do not hesitate when coming to me  
Coming to me; being with us  
We have large fields in the fields  
And wide strips in the forest  
Edges run down to the brook  
Sides reach the sea  
Corners to the gray meadow  
If you are, if you are a maiden  
If you are quick to pick  
Swift to take by hands  
Then your crown will carry gold  
Your head will carry a lace cap  
Your neck will carry a golden necklace  
Crown with golden ribbons  
Shoulders with pearl beads  
Hips with a half skirt  
Shins with silk stockings  
Feet with new shoes  
If you are, if you are a maiden  
If you are quick to pick  
Swift to take by hands  
Then you will feel the thimbleberries  
Your side will feel the rowans  
Shoulder blades the apple trees  
Forearms the maples  
Thighs like rowan bushes.

label: youth_life
translation:
Why are you laughing at me,  
With your narrow eyes mocking me,  
You are not worth a smile,  
Nor is the girl with the narrow eyes.  
The boy went to the manor court,  
The girl went to eavesdrop,  
Whose right would prevail,  
Whose right would rise.  
The maiden’s right prevailed,  
The boy’s right declined.  
Where did that maiden herself end up?  
The maiden herself died.  
Where was that maiden buried?  
In the churchyard of Kullamaa.  
Who buried that maiden?  
There were five clever men from the manor,  
Five had gray scarves,  
Six wore golden earrings,  
Seven had star-shaped marks on their shins.  
What grew on that maiden’s grave?  
Peony reeds, lily leaves,  
Straighter German onions.  
Where is that boy now?  
The boy himself died.  
Where was that boy buried?  
Behind the room in the slaughter yard,  
Above the urine buckets,  
Between the pig baths.  
Who buried that boy?  
There were six Krants dogs from the village.  
What grew on that boy’s grave?  
Dog thistles, club leaves.

label: youth_life
translation:
Boys, young lads  
Do not make the girls laugh  
Girls should not be untamed  
Surely you sometimes crave girls  
Crave a bride  
Surely you go from village to village  
And visit house to house  
You ask from the family mother  
And ask from the family housekeeper  
Give me the daughter  
Who swings in your arms  
And sways on a silver rein  
Faints into weak water  
And under the ribbons of the skirt.

label: youth_life
translation:
Let other men not do  
What I myself have done  
With my foolish drinking,  
With my silly thinking.  
I took an old woman,  
I bought an old horse,  
I took an old little dog.  
When I come home from the tavern,  
Neither does the old dog bark,  
Nor does the old horse neigh.  
Boys, lads,  
Take wives from the maidens,  
Buy horses from the foals.  
Take dogs from the puppies.  
When you come home from the tavern,  
The foal neighs,  
The woman laughs from the maidens,  
Your mother made you warm socks,  
Your mother made you wise shoes,  
She told you to walk nicely,  
Across the yard properly,  
Across the bridge straight,  
Across the field clearly,  
Across the yard prettily.  
So the man leads our maiden,  
Like the shoots on the walnut tree,  
Hazel in the blue forest,  
Roses in the herb garden.  
But then comes the trickster boy,  
The cunning rogue,  
He takes the shoots from the walnut tree,  
The hazel from the blue forest,  
The roses from the herb garden.

label: youth_life
translation:
Awake on the pine forest trail  
The rooster crowed like a young girl  
Five met an old tune  
Six met a dried shoe  
Seven met a shoemaker's apprentice  
A hundred met an old series  
A thousand met the wind vane.

label: youth_life
translation:
Our men are beer drinkers  
Beer drinkers, fishing neighbors.  
They hear the horse urinating  
The foal throwing water  
They think of running to drink vodka  
Rising beer barrels.

label: youth_life
translation:
Why do men hate me  
Why did boys despise me  
The blue-collars dug at me  
The sailors cursed me  
The black-collars proclaimed?  
I did according to the men's wishes  
Following the boys' lead.  
I did according to the maiden's wishes  
Following the shepherd's lead.  
Then I was dear in the maiden's eyes  
Then I was dear in the shepherd's eyes  
I was dear to two sisters  
I was well-behaved in the eyes of five brothers.

label: youth_life
translation:
My grandmother was a pearl necklace:
She got daughters married,
Sons took wives.
My grandmother was a horn necklace,
An old, crafty woman’s daughter;
She brought a handsome young man,
Brought a capable one from elsewhere.
My dear gold twisted necklace:
She had three suitors.
All were from craftsmen’s families,
All were from wise households,
From the richest of the rich,
From families with gold coins,
From households with copper coins.
One was a ploughman,
A wielder of a broad axe.
He was skilled at measuring,
Had seven sickles,
Nine planes at home.
The second was a blacksmith's apprentice;
He was a smelter of iron.
A maker of copper wagons.
An old hitter of nails,
A tapper of small coins.
The third was a weaver:
He made blankets with capercaillie patterns,
Pillowcases with duck patterns,
Sheets with atlas patterns,
Tablecloths with ribbons,
Handkerchiefs with woodpecker patterns.
The old rune was a strict necklace:
She brought sour cream with butter,
She poured five vats of vodka.
The old cow was a cud-chewer necklace:
Because she got Võru butter.
The old pig was a silk necklace:
Because she got lard even for the table,
She could eat on a saw horse.
The old sheep was a fleece necklace:
Because she could knit cubes,
Make a baby’s cradle,
Weave leg straps.
The old dog was a snarling necklace,
She was the evening herald outside,
Announcing the arrival of the suitors.

label: youth_life
translation:
Grandma kindly told me to go,  
proudly across the yard.  
When coming, bring firewood to the stove,  
when leaving, take food to the cattle...

label: youth_life
translation:
This girl is my namesake,  
This wreath is my crown  
Whose coat is gold-decorated  
But whose wreath is made of fur.  
I do not want Anneke,  
Nor do I want Kaieke.  
Anne has torn shirt tails,  
Kaie has worn-out sleeves.  
But I will take Mari, the berry-bringer,  
The berry-bringer, the herder.  
Mari is plump, Mari is sweet,  
Mari has a fashionable mouth.  
She misleads boys into the spruce forest,  
To the edge of the ravine,  
Young men to the meadow,  
Old men to the hunter’s hut.

label: youth_life
translation:
I don’t have German women by birth,  
But I do have German women by birth,  
Poepoiss’s little bride.  
Poepoiss calls me inside,  
Into the red yard,  
"From whom do you buy silver?  
From whom do you exchange copper?  
From whom do you listen to the little gold chain?"

label: youth_life
translation:
I had to go to Pilli  
To tease Pinni Pilli girl  
To charm Maidu Anne  
To pull at Kõrtsi Kaie’s neck  
To hustle Suigu Salme;  
But I ended up falling asleep with Malle  
Malle’s kisses were sweeter,  
Than Pilli’s milk cakes  
Than Anne’s fragrant breads  
Than Kaie’s chicken eggs  
And Salme’s warm milk.

label: youth_life
translation:
My sister was taken to a place of fortune
Where there are long milk cans
Where there are tall cream tops
And also wide bread tables
The room was made of turf dust
The stove made of goose jawbones
The hearth from chicken eggshells
The roof from pea pods
The eaves from meat
When the wind blows, it rattles
When the sun shines, it roars
When it rains, it clatters against it.

label: youth_life
translation:
Father said a death reaction in the ground,  
Mother a soul's annex:  
Girls are little birds,  
If you start to walk away,  
Start to walk to the meadow:  
Then take sleeves into your fists.  
Handkerchiefs down the shoulder.  
If you meet a crowd of men,  
A crowd of men, a gang of boys.  
Pull the boy’s head down.  
A married woman pulls her face!  
Knock both eyebrows.  
Do you want a man from me?  
Go through Kalevipoeg,  
What is your concern with me?  
Let me be a little donkey,  
Grow into a little herdboy,  
Rise into an acorn.  
There will be plenty of seekers on that donkey,  
Wanting on the acorn—  
Demanding on the heath girl.

label: youth_life
translation:
Go away, family boy.  
The family boy is deceitful!  
He deceives a lot, beats a lot,  
Steals and lies a lot.  
He quarrels a lot to bring:  
Many worthless gifts,  
A hundred useless slippers.  
When I had to deal with madness,  
And had to live with life,  
I didn't finally get five gifts.  
I didn't sneak through the bark of the pine!  
Like here, before six months,  
Old then five woolen carpets.  
Now you want to grow big.  
Into the purse of the people's treasure.  
To the family of the schoolmaster -  
To the farm of the old tanner.  
Where there are big dining tables  
And long benches to sit on.  
Wide bread paddles;  
Very tall birch trunks.  
Then go under the mother-in-law's foot,  
Then go under the father-in-law's foot.  
Stir the milk churn,  
Then take the golden club,  
The schoolmaster's whip.  
Warm the father-in-law's sides with a stick,  
Warm the mother-in-law's sides with a stick.  
From the cheeks hit the mark,  
Sell the vodka skin.

label: youth_life
translation:
Virgin maiden, young man,
Why do you resist when I come to you?
To me, a young man,
With a flushed, rosy cheek?
Tomorrow I am going to Germany.
From there I will bring three crowns,
Green - braided ones.
I got to live, I got to be: -
A fist brings a braided one,
A whip brought blood-red, -
A farmer with a matted head.
Then I brought rods to lash
Willow rods - to whip.
I brought rods for spanking
These go along the skin of a woman.
Thin twigs along
Delicate shoulders along.

label: youth_life
translation:
Oh, if only I had seen it in a dream  
If only I had thought of it while sleeping.  
Dozing, it came to my mind:  
That I had received an angry sweetheart  
A quarrelsome second wife -  
A sorrowful young woman!  
Then I would have built a new barn here  
A barn with a lintel,  
Walls made of pork.  
A roof made of chicken eggs.  
Inside I would have placed a silk bed  
A silk bed, a thread game  
For the young son to sleep  
To lull the new sweetheart to sleep  
To quiet the old sweetheart.

label: youth_life
translation:
I am Maie, I am a berry  
I am a strawberry on the hill.  
In the bluebell grove  
In the wood pigeon copse  
In the red willow grove  
In the meadowsweet thicket  
Let the boys come to pick me  
To find the bluebells  
To gather the wood pigeons  
To harvest the meadowsweet  
I slept, Mari, on the hill  
Among the meadowsweets  
In the bluebell grove  
In the red willow grove  
And I saw a dream while sleeping:  
"In front of the fig tree  
Behind the gold tree  
In the chamber of the alder  
The bog myrtle was inside the sauna  
The apple tree was in the yard.  
Village girls, little old women!  
Understand this dream  
That I saw while sleeping:  
'In front of the fig tree  
Behind the gold tree  
In the chamber of the alder  
The bog myrtle was inside the sauna  
The apple tree was also in the yard.  
You drink spirits under the fig tree  
Suitors come from the gold tree  
The alder is a female companion  
The bog myrtle is a lady of the sauna  
The apple tree is the one at the wedding.'"

label: youth_life
translation:
My dear little brother!  
If you are going to take a wife,  
If you are going to get a wreath,  
If you are going to row a boat:  
Do not take a wife from the manor.  
In the manor, they are somewhat  
Beautiful under the windows,  
With red balconies above,  
Polished stone cellars,  
The master’s wedding chambers.  
They do not know how to walk with fire,  
How to set a shirt without sparks,  
How to milk a cow without a chandelier.  
How to cook broth without bitterness.  
Watch the woman at the distaff,  
Aim the woman with the sickle,  
Try her on the loom.  
The woman at the sickle is smooth,  
The woman at the distaff is nimble,  
The woman at the loom is patient,  
The one in the hay barn is tender.  
Do not take a wife from the tavern.  
All are above even the stalks,  
Fine for going to church.

label: youth_life
translation:
Girls, little birds  
Cheese locks, neat ones  
Sweethearts, smooth ones  
Wreath heads, pretty ones!  
Do you know where you will go?  
Where will you be finally taken?  
Some will go to the sad spruce forest,  
Some to the bright open forest,  
Some to the wet pine forest,  
Some to the dear birch forest,  
Some to the wise oak forest,  
Some flew to the alder forest.  
Who goes to the bad spruce forest  
Goes to a bad man.  
Who goes to the wet pine forest  
Goes to a man who drinks heavily.  
Who goes to the dear birch forest  
Goes to a dear embrace.  
Who goes to the wise oak forest?  
Goes to tend the farm.  
Who goes to the bright open forest?  
Goes to the white plain.  
Who flew to the alder forest?  
Goes to beg for bread.  
Girls, little birds,  
Sweethearts, smooth ones!  
Ask your Gods!  
That they do not drink heavily  
Nor become tavern-goers.  
A drunkard drank to the tavern's end  
To Kuie's tavern in Kuie,  
To Kase's tavern in Kasuka.

label: youth_life
translation:
I would go to the man, the man would not take me,  
I would stay home, the boy would not stay.  
Neither would he leave me  
Nor would the little mad one forget.  
If I get angry, where can I lay it down?  
If I go mad, where do I forget?  
I'm not going to be a bull to be killed,  
Nor a horse to be exchanged,  
Nor a mule to be abandoned,  
Nor food to be fed.  
When I come home from the threshing floor,  
I may not live indoors,  
In the room, by the door.  
I jumped into the barnyard,  
I may not be there either.  
From there I step into the barn,  
I may not be there either.  
I went back inside after all,  
Watching secretly myself,  
Head poked through a crack,  
Feet beneath the window.  
He was angry, fallen into bed,  
Badly sunk onto the pillow,  
I sit under the cradle  
Beginning to cry softly,  
Calling for my foster parents.  
Mother-in-law came to ask me,  
Mother-in-law came to ask me,  
Speaking despite the stove,  
Laughing near the window.  
I heard, soon I answer:  
Oh you father-in-law, with sparse beard,  
You stoke the stove without tongs.  
Oh you mother-in-law, with a crooked jaw,  
You boil broth with a ladle.  
Or you stove, with a curved back,  
You carry ashes without a bag,  
Or you window, with a tattered curtain,  
You sweep the room without a broom. -  
What can a woman do with an empty pocket,  
A person with an empty bag,  
A farm girl with a runny nose,  
A house girl with a sore mouth. -  
If only I had seen in a dream,  
While dozing the thought came to me,  
While sleeping I imagined,  
That I am being courted by the bad one,  
Given to a cruel one,  
Drunken with angry spirits,  
Fed with bitter bread:  
If at least the six-stripy ones were gathered,  
Between the edges of the carpet,  
Join these two linen pieces,  
Let these men go past,  
Let the suitors walk by.  
There would be time to be with my beloved,  
To grow with gentian,  
To prepare in the copper age.

label: youth_life
translation:
What is beneath our yard?  
The sea is beneath our yard.  
What is in the middle of the sea?  
A well is in the middle of the sea.  
What is in the middle of the well?  
A pillar is in the middle of the well.  
What is on the top of the pillar?  
A sieve is on the top of the pillar.  
What is at the bottom of the sieve?  
Soot is at the bottom of the sieve.  
What is on the hands of the soot?  
A child is on the hands of the soot.  
What is on the child’s chest?  
A brooch is on the child’s chest.  
What is on the edge of the brooch?  
A ring is on the edge of the brooch.  
Where did you get that ring?  
From the finger bones of soldiers,  
From the collarbones of merchants,  
From the knee bones of shop boys.

label: youth_life
translation:
If the boy died,  
Where was he buried?  
In Kuuramaa under a spruce,  
In Pärnumaa under a poplar,  
In Läänemaa under a alder.  
What plants grow on the boy’s grave?  
Groundsel, burdock leaves,  
Garden-edge nettles.  
Who visited the boy’s grave?  
Every month the devils came,  
Every Friday the quarrelsome ones.  

If the girl died,  
Where was she buried?  
In Kullamäe churchyard,  
Under the slender tower.  
What plants grow on the girl’s grave?  
Coltsfoot, cranesbills,  
Long-necked foxgloves,  
German edible onions.  
Who visited the girl’s grave?  
Every month the kings came,  
Every Friday the lords of Riga.

label: youth_life
translation:
I plowed the swamp, the bluebells grew,  
I plowed the ridges, the heathers grew.  
Then I sent the girls to pick hay.  
Who was quick to pick hay,  
Swift to toss the bundle,  
That girl was mine in name,  
The wreath-bride at my side.  
Here I began feeding the horse,  
So it could grow strong for riding.  
I carried bundles of oats,  
Drew water from the shade,  
Carried flour in my pocket.  
Then I rode straight to my father-in-law’s house,  
To my father-in-law’s house, to mother-in-law’s house.  
Hello father-in-law, boot top!  
Hello mother-in-law, cooking neck!  
Are the girls at home?  
Our girl is by the well,  
At the well to water the herd.  
I rode straight to the well.  
Hello girl, cooking neck!  
To the one who makes calves drink,  
To the one who makes my horses drink,  
Give the grey one a saddle,  
Let the black one nibble,  
And let the ears hang one over the other.  
I am a poor traveler,  
A traveler, a land measurer,  
A messenger of kings,  
A handler of German affairs,  
A writer of large letters.  
The girl heard and answered:  
You are not a poor traveler,  
A traveler, a land measurer,  
A messenger of kings,  
A handler of German affairs,  
A writer of large letters;  
You are a scoundrel, young man!  
Why do you have kicks on your whip,  
Braided straps on your jacket,  
And a braided tail on your horse!

label: youth_life
translation:
I went to visit under the village barn,  
The girls didn’t want to go,  
They started barking at me:  
You don’t have a calico shirt on your back,  
A calico shirt, a silk vest,  
Beads around your neck,  
German boots on your feet.  

I cried by the stream,  
I put my cap on the table,  
And the cap on the bottom.  

A girl came to ask me:  
Why are you crying, young lad?  
I replied back:  
Why should I cry, young lad?  

I went to visit under the village barn,  
The girls didn’t want to go,  
They started barking at me:  
You don’t have a calico shirt on your back,  
A calico shirt, a silk vest,  
Beads around your neck,  
German boots on your feet.  

The girl heard and replied back:  
Wait, wait young lad!  
Tomorrow we’ll go to the town of Paide,  
Paide town, to Ohmann’s shop,  
There you can get a calico shirt,  
A calico shirt, a silk vest,  
Beads around your neck,  
German boots on your feet.  

Then go under the village barn:  
The girls will want you then.  
Some will think you are the manor’s son,  
Or a farm worker,  
Or a steward,  
Or a groom following behind.

label: youth_life
translation:
Maiden, young maiden,  
Come to me and drive!  
I will not take you into the rain,  
Nor carry you into the dew —  
I will bring the oats into the chamber,  
The barley to the edge of the oven,  
The flax to the threshing floor.  
Maiden, young maiden,  
Come now and drive!  

Come to my village, caretaker,  
To manage my property,  
To milk a single cow.  

We have three barns outside:  
One is for threshing wheat,  
Another for threshing rye,  
The third for threshing barley.  

Be true, do not lie!  
I was at your place yesterday,  
I did come to you.  

You have three barns outside:  
One for mice to jump on,  
Another for cats to roar,  
The third for rats to crawl.  

Maiden, young maiden,  
Come now and drive!  

We have dun mares,  
We have bays in the harness,  
Chestnuts with spotted coats.  

Be true, do not lie!  
You had mice in the dun mares,  
You had rats in the bays,  
Cats in the chestnuts’ harness.

label: youth_life
translation:
Virgin girl, young maiden,  
Come to me and hasten!  
I will bring tunes in the apron basket:  
One I bring is silk blue,  
Another is apron red,  
The third is checkered,  
The fourth is mare’s hair,  
The fifth is golden-striped.  
Ellakene, little brother,  
I have become yours,  
I have remained yours,  
Then you bring the checkered fist,  
The mare’s hair headscarf,  
The striped coat,  
The golden-buttoned jacket.  
Ellakene, little brother!  
First I will sit in the river,  
In the running river water,  
In the cold village spring—  
Before I get into your carriage,  
Your poor wagon,  
The shabby man’s coach.

label: youth_life
translation:
Virgins, young girls!  
What are you building for yourselves,  
Dressing up finely,  
Twisting wreaths on your heads!  
Yet I will not take you,  
I will not come as a suitor to the gathering.  
I have three girls at home,  
Who dangle stockings for me,  
Slip through my hands:  
The marten jumps into the hole,  
Foam jumps into the bowl,  
Tears to another household.

label: youth_life
translation:
Father is going with his wife  
Brother is going with a young girl  
I go crying towards the corner  
I wander towards the empty bed  
I grope in the old fur coat.

label: youth_life
translation:
If only my grandmother knew  
If only my grandfather knew  
If only my other half knew  
If only my spouse knew  
If only my young men understood  
If only they truly knew my sorrow  
Yearning in this world  
Worrying elsewhere  
They would run with ears pricked up  
Let the stallions run freely  
They would come after me  
Take my beloved home  
Take my berries to the house  
Take flowers to the porch  
A pretty jug to the chamber  
Take gifts to my father-in-law  
Take gifts to my mother-in-law  
Bring joy to my husband  
And comfort to my neighbors

label: youth_life
translation:
Village girls, little old women;  
Village men, little old men,  
Help me understand  
Give a little advice  
Should I leave soon, or should I stay soon  
Or should I soon give a promise? -  
Rings on the autumn finger;  
Clasp on the table,  
I am a girl today! -  
A maiden until tomorrow morning,  
I keep my honor and grow for a long time,  
And will soon have a good wreath of years;  
A wreath of straight hair  
A wreath of white sleeves  
I have ten suitors;  
Nine admirers  
When I begin to consider:  
One was: Ants, rarely near the boat;  
Second: Lauri with a broad jaw,  
Third: Mihkel with a thin mustache  
Fourth: a worthy maiden;  
Fifth: a servant of a torch,  
Sixth: Jaan from the spruce forest;  
Seventh: that one, better  
Eighth: a fisherman’s son  
Ninth: beyond the seas  
Tenth: a groom from the village

label: youth_life
youth_life
translation:
If that man were mine  
Who rides past you  
Rides along the road  
Does he have a rainbow’s belt  
A hat on his head like a wreath?  
Riding past the Finnish bridge  
Over Curonian mountains  
Near the soft Finnish bridge.  
Curonian mountains roaring  
Fallen under the water  
He struck my brother in the water!  
My brother went under the water  
My brother’s wreath remained on top of the water  
I am going to look for my brother;  
Who will come back to me?  
The moon came from Curonia.  
I greet the moon:  
Hello moon from Curonia!  
You walk high above,  
You aim straight,  
You watch from the light.  
Did you see my brother?  
Rowing on the river  
Rowing in the sea bay  
In the small pilot boat there  
With a white sail in the middle  
The moon answered me:  
I did not see your brother,  
Rowing on the river:  
Rowing in the sea bay.  
In the small pilot boat there  
With a white sail in the middle.  
I am going to look for my brother,  
Who will come back to me?  
He came from Pärnu region.  
I greet the one from Pärnu  
Hello from the Pärnu region.  
You walk high above,  
You aim straight,  
You watch from the light  
Did you see my brother  
Rowing on the river  
Rowing in the sea bay  
In the small pilot boat there  
With a white sail in the middle?  
The one from Pärnu answered me:  
I did not see your brother  
Rowing on the river  
Rowing in the sea bay  
In the small pilot boat there  
With a white sail in the middle.  
I am going to look for my brother  
Who will come back to me?  
A second man came from the stars:  
I greet the man from the stars  
Hello man from the stars  
You aim straight  
You watch from the light  
You walk high above,  
Did you see my brother  
Rowing on the river  
Rowing in the sea bay  
In the small pilot boat there  
With a white sail in the middle?  
The star answered me:  
I did not see your brother  
Rowing on the river  
Rowing in the sea bay  
In the small pilot boat there  
With a white sail in the middle.  
I will start to cry for my brother  
The moon, I cried for my brother  
The one from Pärnu, I cried for my brother’s wreath  
The year will bury my brother.

label: youth_life
translation:
Essu lessu leaves were wide  
The boys of our parish were tall  
They went to the heath to drive  
The apple was under the stove  
They themselves were bright as the day  
Their hat like a king's crown  
A belt on their waist like a city ribbon  
Boots shining on their feet  
Gloves colorful on their hands  
Essu lessu leaves were wide  
The boys of the other parish were tall  
They went to the heath to drive  
The apple had fallen down  
They themselves were bright as the day  
Their hat had wilted  
The belt on their waist had rusted  
Boots muddy on their feet  
Gloves worn on their hands

label: youth_life
translation:
If there were a man for me,
Who rides along the road there,
Rides along the trail,
A rainbow belt around his waist,
A hat on his head like a wreath,
Rides along the Finnish bridge,
Along the Curonian mountain.
Along the Finnish bridge he bent,
The Curonian mountain roared,
Fell under the horse:
He struck my brother down.
My brother went under the water,
My brother's wreath stayed above the water.
I go to look for my brother.
Who will answer me?
The moon came from Curonia.
I greeted the moon:
"Hello, moon from Curonia!
You walk high,
You aim straight,
You watch over the light:
Have you seen my brother
By the river idling,
Rowing on a sea island,
In Luisa's boat,
In the middle of Puise's sail?"
The moon answered me:
"I did not see your brother
Idle by the river,
Rowing on a sea island,
In Luisa's boat,
In the middle of Puise's sail."
I go to look for my brother,
Who will answer me?
The sun came from Pärnu land.
I greeted the sun:
"Hello, sun from Pärnu land!
You walk high,
You aim straight,
You watch over the light:
Have you seen my brother
By the river idling,
Rowing on a sea island,
In Luisa's boat,
In the middle of Puise's sail?"
The sun answered me:
"I did not see your brother
Idle by the river,
Rowing on a sea island,
In Luisa's boat,
In the middle of Puise's sail."
I go to look for my brother,
Who will answer me?
The stars, the other men, came.
I greeted the stars:
"Hello, stars, the other men!
You aim straight,
You walk high:
Have you seen my brother
Idle by the river,
Rowing on a sea island,
In Luisa's boat,
In the middle of Puise's sail?"
The stars answered me:
"I did not see your brother
Idle by the river,
Rowing on a sea island,
In Luisa's boat,
In the middle of Puise's sail."
I begin to weep for my brother,
The moon I wept for my brother's death,
The sun I wept for my brother's wreath,
The year for my brother's resting place.

label: youth_life
translation:
The leaves of the Essu-Lessu were broad,  
The boys of our parish were tall,  
They went to the heath to ride:  
The horse was harnessed beneath,  
The rider himself in the daylight,  
A hat like a king's crown,  
A belt on their waist like a city ribbon,  
Boots shining on their feet,  
Gloves brightly patterned on their hands.  

The leaves of the Essu-Lessu were broad,  
The boys of another parish were tall,  
They went to the heath to ride:  
The horse had become moldy beneath,  
The rider himself had aged in the daylight,  
The hat on his head had grown moldy,  
His belt had rusted at the buckle,  
His boots muddy on his feet,  
His gloves worn on his hands.

label: youth_life
translation:
If only I had seen it in a dream.
Came to mind even while dozing,
I would have long ago built the barns
Barns built from rye straw,
Walls made from pig meat,
Roof from chicken eggs.
Doors out of eyelids
Locks from the jawbone.

label: youth_life
translation:
Mine is not here.  
My companion does not grow here.  
I am mine in Oandi  
My companion far away,  
The man across the sea,  
The wind may carry health,  
To ask in prayer for bad weather,  
May hail not destroy the crops,  
May clouds not last long.  
Heaven, grant wise mind.  
If healthy, let him work,  
If sick, may God help!

label: youth_life
translation:
My fiancé Peibesessa,  
Accompanies the young far away,  
Neither moonlight is heard by me,  
Nor the week is seen by me,  
Nor is it proper to offer a hand.  
In summer, it is not appropriate to talk,  
When coming to visit home  
He then brings money for the horse.  
At the edge of the sieve, rings  
And old talents are secured.

label: youth_life
translation:
Before I play with the tufts  
Around the wheels,  
Before with those girls,  
What was half-finished at Kis,  
Loved too soon.

label: youth_life
translation:
What the mud horse does
The woman annoys the youth
The madman goes wandering to the village
The woman goes crying towards the corner
In the barns towards the stove
Pecking towards the empty bed
Rustling old coats
Oh you old coat
It was hard to walk
Even better to sleep on the ridge pole
Look, the famous woman of our farmstead
A rich woman with thick thighs
They went to the spruce trees to relieve themselves
To the chaff to fart
The floor stuck in the butt
A needle at the edge of the hole
The stove pulled even the claws
The nest on all four paws
Her own man in the crotch.

label: youth_life
translation:
And those strong Raua boys  
Will go to the church on Midsummer  
Seven pigs in front of the sleigh  
There’s pig dung in the pipe  
Tatirida in front of the line  
Wooden turn in front of the pants

label: youth_life
translation:
My mother made woven stockings  
My father made clever shoes  
Daughter, daughter, walk nicely  
Across the yard right steps  
Across the garden white steps  
Across the field light steps  
Men peeked from the shadows  
From under the fence, quietly  
If only that girl were mine  
If only she were my wife from the farm  
Who is walking along the road  
Across the field nicely  
I do not have the courage to approach  
I do not have the heart to take her into my arms  
If I had a purse of gold  
If I had a rich dowry  
Then I would dare to approach  
And take her into my heart

label: youth_life
translation:
Little Juan, little squeeze,  
Make me a little wheelbarrow.  
In summer I roll on the grass,  
In winter by the stove’s glow.

label: youth_life
translation:
Village old women, little old women.  
Help me understand,  
Give me a little advice.  
I had three suitors:  
One was a wolf, another a bear,  
The third was a beautiful lynx,  
The fourth was a handsome fox.  
The wolf brought me great boars,  
The bear brought two necklaces.  
The lynx brought silver without end,  
The fox brought broad crosses.  
Help me understand,  
Give me a little advice,  
How should I sleep with the wolf,  
Breathe with the lynx.  
I have a small little rug,  
A tiny little patch,  
My feet peeked out from under the rug,  
My legs from the wolf’s bed,  
The stirrups from the bedposts.

label: youth_life
translation:
In the forest, I got a husband  
Up in the tree, I held a wedding  
In the top of the birch, a veil fluttered  
In the willow bush, a ring was placed  
The trees were long wedding guests  
The birches were white bridesmaids  
A bite was at the feeding table  
The field's edge was a bench  
Stubborn, stubborn old woman  
Stubborn to eat foreign bread  
Ale to eat in holes  
Ugly to eat crusts  
Hard is to eat, sworn old woman  
Oh, my hardship, slave child  
Like pushing and pulling  
A village well's bucket  
Water was drawn out.  
The farmer's daughter born lazy  
Born lazy, become lazy  
Sleeping without a belt in bed  
Much footwork  
I, poor slave child  
Rise up from the mud  
Wash piles of dishes  
Work is put in the box  
The old sprightly spirits  
Then I go plowing to the village  
A furrow goes to the feast  
You hold the harness straps  
The oxen are harnessed at the yoke  
The father is following behind.

label: youth_life
translation:
Let other girls not become  
Accidental third parties  
I feared boys would disappear  
Men drown at sea  
I went to the forest to get a husband  
I went to the barn to herd  
I got a husband, a sea devil  
A strangler at the barn door  
But he beat me with his fist  
And also beat the thumb flower  
And also scratched the knuckle flower  
He put me to sleep on the floor  
Under the stove to warm me up  
To burn the junipers.

label: youth_life
translation:
Four maiden girls,
Five of them livelier,
Six of them taller,
Went out into the field to reap,
Reaped two rows of rye,
Laid down for a nap,
To rest a little,
Oh, an eagle came from the forest,
Shot onto our barn,
Flew onto the granary roof,
Then began to proclaim there,
Dear boys, dear brothers,
Go out to the field,
See what is done in the field,
I found the girls sleeping,
They had gone underneath to rest,
They had gone on top to brighten,
Ants had eaten their eyes away,
Different souls inside,
Moles had nibbled their lips,
I took the girls to the sauna,
Brought them home to the market house,
I myself lay on the hay,
Placed my head on a pillow,
Put my arm around the girls’ necks,
Got up in the morning;
Thought about leaving the girls behind,
The girls drive away in a cart,
With a small whip,
To the blacksmith's shop in the meadow,
From there she buys syrups,
Ten pounds of cake dough,
Makes the boys fry it,
Boys turn the roast,
Gives it to the young maiden to eat
Whose face blushed
Because she had been touched by the boys,
The boys’ hands had fiddled with her.

label: youth_life
translation:
The wind comes on Saturday evening,  
Sunday’s little day,  
The girl goes to sleep with the old man,  
The sister goes with her husband,  
The brother goes with a young maiden,  
I go crying towards the corner,  
Turning towards the empty bed,  
All were cold sideboards,  
The benches were edge tables,  
The end boards were misty,  
The wall logs were like mushrooms,  
I turn to the side, find coldness,  
I turn my back, find the wall.

label: youth_life
translation:
The fire comes, the bonfire sings,
I drive the herd, the girl makes a cake,
Where I would drive the herd,
Drive the herd to Kaunissaare,
I myself went to Hülissaare,
Made a fire at Tulissaare,
The cat came to my fire,
The boy came to my fire,
I had a stone in my glove,
An iron rod in my hand,
I hit the boy on the head,
Knocked on both eyebrows,
The boy went to the manor court,
Which court will judge,
The court would judge in my favor,
The boy would be beaten on the behind.

label: youth_life
translation:
If I were Olevik  
If I wore the Kalev shoes  
I would have a wise mind.  
I fear stepping on thorn bushes  
Pricking my toes bloody  
Marking my shins  
I do not know how to hold a gun  
To trample a wise blade.

label: youth_life
translation:
Mother dear,  
Marry this daughter off.  
If you do not marry her off, do not ask either,  
Let her stay home to comb wool,  
To thresh by the riverbank,  
To gather mushrooms by the wall.  
Let a birch tree grow on her neck,  
A buckthorn on her head,  
A juniper among her hair.

label: youth_life
translation:
Mother Ella granny,
Spin me long threads,
Long threads, fine threads,
From which I will make three scarves.
One I will make with a long striped pattern,
The second wide and patchy,
The third with a cat's paw pattern.
Maybe for a lame man,
For a poor unmarried man.
I will lend the first one as bread,
Send the second one with salt,
Wear the third one around my neck.
The one with the long stripes,
I will lend as bread.
The one wide and patchy,
I will send with salt.
The one with the cat's paw pattern,
I will wear around my neck.

label: youth_life
translation:
Mother, oh dear granny,  
Give that girl to me,  
Who rocks in the cradle,  
Sways in the silver reins,  
Faints in the weak carriage.  
She is very tiny.  
Come back another time,  
Then the young girl will be ready,  
The modest young maiden will be ready.

label: youth_life
translation:
I saw the girl growing,  
Rising from the ground like a berry.  
I began to take care of the hay.  
Under my arm, I carried the hay,  
In a bundle, I carried the oats.  
Then I gained full strength,  
I went to the father-in-law’s door.  
The father-in-law came outside to look,  
The mother-in-law came outside to look.  
Hello, father-in-law, hello, mother-in-law.  
The horse was driven into the yard,  
Hay was given in front,  
Oats were carried in front,  
I was invited inside,  
They gave me food.  
I did not come to eat afterward,  
Nor did I come to drink,  
I came for the sake of the house,  
I came to see the girl.

label: youth_life
translation:
King, little king,  
Why didn’t you come to us last year?  
When rivers ran without oil,  
Springs flowed with vodka.  
From the yard ran beer veins,  
From the gate ran vodka veins,  
From the well path ran rock veins.  
Now you come to a bad swamp,  
The year after year begins.  
Now I strip off the clothes,  
Cut off the plague necklace,  
Save the wreath head from misery.

label: youth_life
translation:
Kessi's swing - rowan tree  
Girl  
Who went down to the prayer place  
Was Jüri's little boy  
He went down to the prayer place  
Don't fall, maiden  
On a stone, on a stump  
Fall on my hat  
Put a cap on it too  
Then I will give you a gift  
A big brooch

label: youth_life
translation:
A little old woman, a little auntie
Buys a golden dog for the yard
To the iron rack at the gate!
Who lets the men pass by
Without a dowry, going far away.
Her head wears a lace cap
Her belly wears a straw apron
Her shoulders sewn, she would walk,
Wearing silk stockings
Her hips with store skirts.

label: youth_life
translation:
When the old bachelor dies  
Then the boy's bell is rung  
The pig cries its eyes out  
Both his bastards are his own.  
Both his bastards are his own  
Old Kulti of the hills.

label: youth_life
translation:
Other days I should otherwise  
Other times I otherwise would drive  
Comes that blessed little evening  
Wretched little twilight  
All the children go to sleep  
Father goes with his mother  
Brother goes with the young girl  
Sister goes with her husband  
The guy goes with a girl  
I stay alone  
I go crying to the corner  
Toward the empty bed  
I take the crab to talk  
To hold a flea's gratitude  
To the louse a little fun  
The crab is an easy jumper  
The flea is a wise dancer  
The louse slides flying

label: youth_life
translation:
What is there below our yard?  
The sea is below our yard.  
What is there in the middle of the sea?  
There is a well in the middle of the sea.  
What is there under the well's shore?  
A pillar is under the well's shore.  
What is on top of the pillar?  
A sieve is on top of the pillar.  
What is at the bottom of the sieve?  
A cuckoo is at the bottom of the sieve.  
What is on the cuckoo's hands?  
A child is on the cuckoo's hands.  
What is on the child's chest?  
A brooch is on the child's chest.  
What is on the eye of the brooch?  
A ring is on the eye of the brooch.  
Where did this ring come from?  
What is this ring made of?  
From the finger bone of a soldier,  
From the neck bone of a merchant,  
From the tail bone of a sailor,  
That is where this ring comes from.

label: youth_life
translation:
What use is your empty boasting  
Wasting your own time  
There are few of you, many of us  
We are still more  
Outside we have a group of boys  
At the gate a crowd of men  
If you want to fight  
Or pull a billy club  
Or wrestle bear-style  
Then come inside, rope-pullers  
And all you potato hurlers  
With big thick noses  
And sparse teeth, thick upper lips  
With noses like worms that pull  
And gather birch bark.

label: youth_life
translation:
I plowed the valleys, the oats grew,
I plowed the hills, the pines grew,
I plowed the swamps, the bluebells grew.
Then I sent the girls to pick
And to weave red aprons.-
I watched from the shade myself:
Is he plowing well.-
But my bride is tiny,
Tiny and upright,
Crossing thin twigs,
She never finishes the southern bread,
No difference in the little counts lost
Among the stone oaks.-
The horse I bought from there,
The girl I took from there.
The horse from Obliqa field
The girl from Strawberry hill,
I took the girl, I buried the other.
I paid honest grave money,
Beautiful soul money,
Handsome clock money,
Pleasant man money.

label: youth_life
translation:
There were many of us before,  
A beautiful herd grew up,  
Wandering like a flock of geese,  
Stretching like a herd of cattle,  
Smooth like that flight of wild geese.  
Now the flock has come to an end,  
The herd has disappeared,  
The flocks of wild geese are scattered widely,  
The flock of twite.  
Now the wanderers have become a crowd,  
And became a row of travelers,  
The troop has become an army from the tower,  
Separating the flock of wild geese,  
Scattering the flock of twite.  
Now I am left alone to hoe,  
Left to gather chicken chicks,  
To sow flaxseed.

label: youth_life
translation:
Oh, you little deceiver  
Clever little companion!  
You deceived the father-in-law, you deceived the mother-in-law,  
You deceived the family's fine young lady,  
You said you were coming to visit to eat,  
To visit to eat, to visit to drink,  
To visit to eat in the kitchen,  
To eat downstairs in the cellar,  
To eat fish in the chamber.  
Even more so in the living room.  
I got to live, I got to be,  
There was plenty of crying in the kitchen,  
Crying all the way to the cellar,  
Twice as much in the chamber,  
Even more in the living room.  
Oh, you little deceiver  
Clever little companion!

label: youth_life
translation:
Voiu and Mari the short one  
Loans but little Liisukene  
When the orders were delivered  
Five vodkas, six mugs  
What do you fear, what do you grieve  
When coming to us, when arriving to us  
To me, a young man  
To the top of the hat  
To the leather belt, to the white one  
That we have far Karelia stores  
Water five versts away  
Village boys carry water  
Runes push carts  
I make gutters under the horse’s belly  
And make new granaries in the yard  
I make walls from pork fat  
Floors from pork lard  
Roof from cured meat  
Rafters from dried meat.

label: youth_life
translation:
Ghostly mist, little breath  
Take me a wife soon,  
Whisper to me a golden moon!  
If you don't take, don't ask.  
I go heating the village,  
To the cold village granary,  
To the unheated building.  
There lie little houses on the road,  
Malformed ones on the yard,  
Children on the granary floor.  
In the rustling swamps,  
In the gray woods,  
In the broken gate,  
Upon father and mother's souls,  
Upon the black cat's neck.  
Daughters are like little houses,  
Sons are like pot makers.

label: youth_life
translation:
Ellakene, little brother  
If you go to ask for a bride  
To court the home hen;  
Invite me also as a suitor  
I know the maidens.  
From the tuft know the dull maiden  
From the lock know the lazy maiden.  
The dull tuft was unrecognizable  
The lazy lock was not combed.  
Angry eyes watery  
Angry black eyebrows.  
Fierce cheeks red.  
Quick hands were scabbed.

label: youth_life
translation:
I saw the maiden growing;
By the blue fence
Swelling with a red wreath;
Rising in a tin crown.
I, from the stables;
From the coal-black haven,
From the window I gave barley,
In the shadows I carried water;
Without the old woman's knowledge,
Without the old man's knowledge,
That I gained the horse's strength.
In front I put sturdy irons;
Behind irons from the threshing floor.
Then I harnessed the horse.
After that I put on the bridle,
On top I put a playful bow,
Eyes into silk reins,
Eyebrows into golden rings,
Tail into a braid,
Brushed the mane to one side.
I rode to the father-in-law's door,
I rode to the mother-in-law's door:
"Hello, father-in-law! Boot-tops,
Hello, mother-in-law! Neck of the kettle,
Are your maidens at home?"
The mother-in-law understood, answered:
"Our daughters are at the well,
Drawing water at the well."
I ride to the well road:
"Hello, dear maiden!
Drawing water with the bucket,
To water all the village's herd;
To water my horse at the well.
Let my black one paw,
Let my gray one sway,
Let my dappled one tug,
Move on the linen cloth.
I, a poor wayfarer,
Wayfarer, knower of lands;
Lord of matters,
Messenger of kings,
Keeper of the town council's book,
A postman from St. Petersburg."
The maiden hears, answers again:
"You are not a poor wayfarer,
Wayfarer, knower of lands,
Lord of matters,
Messenger of kings,
Keeper of the town council's book,
Postman from St. Petersburg.
You are an evil suitor,
And a deceitful groom:
Why is your horse harnessed?
Brushed mane and swayed tail?
Why do you have locks on the bridle?
Why do you have an eagle's skull?
A headgear in the harness?
A sparrow in the reins?"
I heard, answered again,
"I have at home an old father
Who makes the locks on the bridle.
I have at home a little brother
Who is my horse's groom,
Brushed mane and swayed tail.
He puts the tail in a braid,
Eyes in silk reins,
Ears in golden rings.
I have at home a little sister
Who makes the letters on gloves
Who makes lace on the whip..."

label: youth_life
translation:
Marikene little berry  
Mari berry little maiden  
Mari brought berries from other lands  
Purple ones she brought from the city street  
Mari brought Matt's strawberries  
Half a cup of lingonberries  
Then she went up to Harju's granary  
To the Viru distillery  
The boys down to the prayer room  
Down fell a little doll  
Fell on my hat.

label: youth_life
translation:
I go crying towards the corner  
I head towards the empty bed  
I turn over and find cold  
I turn my back and find the wall  
I fumble with an old fur coat  
A furry little coat  
It was good to go to the slave's hall  
To go among others  
Sometimes among the hunt people.

label: youth_life
translation:
I made a wedding feast in the swamp  
Games on the hillock  
Who was invited to the wedding?  
The bear was invited to the wedding  
The wolf came with a gray fur coat  
The titmouse with a tin whistle  
The crow came with copper boots  
Who was invited as the cook?  
The cuckoo was invited as the cook  
The cuckoo boiled boiling broth  
Added angelica for flavor  
Added bile for herbs  
The meadow went to the feast  
The roosters went crowing.

label: youth_life
translation:
Indeed, the stable boys wanted me,  
The lords of Viru enticed me,  
The riders of Riga quarrelled,  
The Hans of Harju pursued me long ago.  
I did not want to be a stable boy,  
Nor be enticed by the lords of Viru.  
My heart did not call to the coachman,  
My mind did not long for the manor’s mood.

label: youth_life
translation:
One is from one family  
Another is from another family  
One does not want to name the other  
One does not call the other by name  
Calls tenderly, calls darling  
Calls tenderly her beloved  
Calls her golden curls  
Names her wheat-colored  
Complains about hairy seeds  
I already understand, I respond  
Calls tenderly, calls darling  
That we are not sisters  
That we are not sisters-in-law  
Let our hands be sisters-in-law  
That we are not brothers  
Let our toes be brothers  
That we are not siblings  
Let our fingers be siblings.

label: youth_life
translation:
What do I care about the flower,
Or what do I fear the scream.
Mine is not here,
My companion is not useful here.
Mine is in Holland,
My companion is in the fish nets,
My fiancé is from the shores of Peipus.
Now let the mouth run its course.
I cannot bear to shout the tongue.
Maybe if I say it roughly again
Let me sing the words back.
I favor cunning words.
I knock down low feet,
I have angry brothers at home,
Wise brothers in the back room
Words are taken seriously.
With a scratch and a flutter,
They are put on paper.
Tomorrow they will be presented
When I come into the room.
Still, onto the dining table,
Onto unwashed hands.

label: youth_life
translation:
Sit on the edge of the fence.  
Nicely onto the side of the boat,  
Give the order to the sailor:  
Row the feathers, fly to the leaves,  
Sail, boy, to that land  
Where my dear father-in-law is,  
Dear father-in-law, dear mother-in-law,  
Silver maiden of youth.  
My father-in-law used to drink a flask of vodka,  
My mother-in-law used to drink another flask,  
I with the maiden, the fourth.

label: youth_life
translation:
If this maiden dies  
Who will accompany the maiden?  
Germans accompany the maiden  
Ladies build  
Kings are listening  
What grows on the maiden’s grave?  
Buttercups, golden tops –  
If this boy dies  
Who will accompany the boy?  
A pig accompanies the boy  
An old boar is listening  
What grows on the boy’s grave?  
Dog fennel, burdock leaves  
Old sparse meadowsweet  
Old twisted nettles

label: youth_life
translation:
Why should I care about the shouts  
Why should I fear the cries  
For I have no one here of my own  
My own is Harju County  
The groom’s five versts away  
From there I searched, from there I found  
When I went to stroll there  
Into the grassy forest  
There was joy for both of us  
When our hearts felt joy  
The bride wondered if she should leave him behind  
The groom looked with a sorrowful eye  
They gave each other their hands  
With a kiss.

label: youth_life
translation:
Aiti raiti with wheels  
Before I play with tufts of grass  
I strike with bursts of laughter  
I jump with birch stumps  
But when it comes to those girls.

label: youth_life
translation:
A little virgin, a young girl  
A slender figure in writing  
Why didn’t you come to me last year  
When the orders were being carried out?  
The fifth were the vodka carriers  
The sixth were the betrothed  
The hundredth were the bread makers? -  
Still, I will not come to you  
Maybe you would have a precious face  
Bluer eye sockets  
Golden eyebrow hairs  
You surely walked in a silk dress  
White stockings, black shoes  
When you walked along the road  
Then the crowd stared at you  
You were beautiful like a painting there on the highway  
You kept going and said goodbye to everyone  
A large spruce gate came opposite  
There he sat under the spruce  
There tears began to drop from his eyes  
The young man went to him  
Why do you sit here with your pale face?  
I have lost my way on the roads.....

label: youth_life
translation:
Old boy, why are you still watching  
If you don’t take a young woman?  
Your mouth has been burned,  
Your beard has turned gray.  
Your mouth runs smoke water,  
Your beard runs gray healing water.

label: youth_life
translation:
Sister Ella Annekene,  
Your shoes hurt,  
Your laces begged,  
The bullhides groaned,  
The goat hides led;  
Women waited to die,  
Men to remain widowers,  
Children to remain orphans;  
So you could become a mother to the children,  
A leader over the family,  
Hands to carry the ladle,  
Mouth to taste the soup.

label: youth_life
translation:
If only you knew my other half,  
My poor husband would think,  
If only my deed existed,  
It would bring fire to me,  
It would carry my old furs,  
It would take me from the rain streams,  
It would redeem me from the snowdrifts,  
Behind the Harju plows,  
From the strike of the Viru scythe.

label: youth_life
translation:
Let other girls not do
What I foolishly did
I went to a young man
Without having a dowry.
I thought he was a considerate man,
A loving husband.
The man was like a sea devil,
A servant of coastal demons,
He ate the flesh off my back,
Sucked the blood from my chest.

label: youth_life
translation:
Old boy, old devil  
Sits on the leelõuk  
Pipe stick in his mouth  
Asks forgiveness for sin  
How many young ones have been made to cry  
How many old ones silenced.

label: youth_life
translation:
Before, I throw a stone by the edge  
By the edge of a stone, by the edge of a stump,  
Before going to the crazy boy.  
The stone does not pull, the stump does not touch,  
The boy does not leave untouched  
The skin hair untested.  
A good boy sleeps with good ones  
But puts his clothes on his thigh  
His shirt on his shin.  
A bad boy sleeps with the bad ones  
But pulls his clothes off his thigh  
His shirt off his shin.

label: youth_life
translation:
Where do I know the dull girl from?  
From Tukas, I know the dull girl,  
From Laka, I know the lazy girl,  
The lazy girl from Laka is tall,  
The dull one has tangled hair,  
And a low curvy waist.

label: youth_life
translation:
May was a sweet maiden  
She called the boys to the spruce forest  
She made peace with them in the alder grove  
She annoyed them in the meadow  
She had seven sprats in her purse  
Eight herring in her scarf.

label: youth_life
translation:
Oh you boys, budding eyes  
Budding eyes, ring-necked  
Don’t make the girls laugh  
Don’t insult the girls with dimples  
Don’t slander the money-chests  
You will surely suffer from a lack of girls  
A lack of girls, a shortage of brides  
You will surely go from village to village  
Also from farm to farm
