Squatting in the village street  
Sitting bare-bottomed at the family gate  
I have a grandmother, a little old lady  
I have a grandfather, a little old man  
Give me the daughter  
Who swings in your arms  
Sways with a gentle pull  
With ribbons under the skirt  
While the girls watch secretly  
If only that fiancé were mine

label: youth_life
translation:
What is there beneath our yard  
The sea beneath our yard  
What is in the middle of the sea  
A pillar in the middle of the sea  
What is at the end of the pillar  
A sieve at the end of the pillar  
What is inside the sieve  
A ring inside the sieve  
What is inside the ring  
A cuckoo inside the ring  
What does the cuckoo bring us  
It brings news of war  
Whose turn is it to go to war  
Will father go, or will mother go  
Or will the one who is swinging hidden go  
Sister went to teach brother  
Ride to the middle of the war  
The first are thrown out  
The last are killed  
The middle ones come home

label: youth_life
translation:
One of me was shouting  
Two of me were afraid while screaming  
A little when speaking out  
My own is not here  
My companion does not grow here  
My own is in Holland  
My companion far away  
A good man over the seas  
A good companion over the fish  
Sings by the lake shore  
Where he jumps by the shore  
There he leaps by the building  
Where he dances by the shore  
There he dances in the stable  
Where he spins by the shore  
There the church spins  
I go through the masculine forest  
Through the boyish street  
Do not stick your head out anywhere  
Do not put your hand in a glove  
Do not press your hair down into a shadow  
I am going home to the old lady’s yard -  
If the good lady does not stop me  
Then the wise old man will stop me  
If the wise old man does not stop me  
Then my sister will stop me  
If my little sister does not stop me  
Then the young brother will stop me  
If the young brother does not stop me  
Then the secret man will stop me  
If the secret man does not stop me  
Then the dear companion will stop me  
If the dear companion does not stop me  
Let the hair be washed to the cup  
Let the night be slept until dawn

label: youth_life
translation:
Hello there, little brother  
There were quite a few of us before  
There were quite a few who went with the herd  
It was like a group from Hoosta  
Moved like a village gang of rascals  
Now the group has come to an end  
The flock has been driven to a place  
Where did they go – where did they stay  
Did rainstorms carry them away  
Or did windstorms bring them  
Or was there hail here  
Rainstorms did not carry them away  
Nor did windstorms bring them  
Nor was there hail here  
From here, boys of Viru have taken them  
Boys of Harju have loved them  
Viru "kimmelid" have led them  
Swedish stallions have trotted around  
Horse backs were struck with fire  
Sparks from their rascals’ shins  
The foal’s hooves cast lightning  
Even when walking on maiden paths  
Or going on a bride-seeking errand

label: youth_life
translation:
Young men are gentle brothers  
Let's harness the steeds to the yoke  
Gray in silver beads  
Blue eyes in rings  
Then we go through the villages  
Through the trodden street  
The golden nails click in the harness  
Behind it rattles the iron plow  
A maiden watches from the side  
The chamberlain calls along  
If only this man were mine  
Who goes through the villages  
Through the trodden street  
The horse shines with beads  
The stone-paved street thunders  
The golden nails click in the harness  
Behind it rattles the iron plow  
I would wash his head  
And comb his neck  
I would rinse the stockings and gloves  
I would drip them through the waters  
Öivo, Võivo, victorious shoes  
Mother-in-law’s shoes without grease  
Edges sharp without tearing  
Soles without fat

label: youth_life
translation:
Sister dear, did I say  
Many young ones, did I scold  
Dear wife, did I say  
Friend dear, did I ride  

Oh, go to the young man  
Unmature wife  
The wife does not grow (mature)  
The man is unwilling to marry  
The wife, however, inherits the linen shed  
The man, however, prefers clothes  

Every noon a meal  
Every month wants a new cap  
Every day wants a white shirt.

label: youth_life
translation:
Let's go take Maie as a wife  
The second takes another wife  
The second takes another old woman's daughter  
You get Kaie, I get Maie  
Kai was stout for work  
Mai was chubby for the leg

label: youth_life
translation:
Oh, our one little sister  
Oh, our two little hands  
The sparkles of one room  
The little birds of one bread  
Together we eat, together we drink  
Together we sleep through the nights  
Together the head on the pillow  
Together the feet under the carpet

label: youth_life
translation:
My brothers are like these spires  
Cousins on my uncle’s side are like these parts  
Cousins on my aunt’s side are grown men  
They did not take debt, nor steal  
Did no harm to anyone  
Not more than anyone  
The German did not send me to the same place  
The parish did not send me to court  
Other brothers, unlike these frogs  
Took on debt and stole  
The German already sent them to the same place  
The parish already sent them to court

label: youth_life
translation:
What is here beneath our yard  
The sea beneath our yard  
What is in the middle of the sea  
A well in the middle of the sea  
What is on the edge of the well  
A post on the edge of the well  
What is at the very end of the post  
A sieve at the very end of the post  
What is on the edge of the sieve  
A cuckoo on the edge of the sieve  
What is on the cuckoo's hands  
A child was on the cuckoo's hands  
What is on the child's chest  
A brooch on the child's chest  
What is on the edge of the brooch  
A ring on the edge of the brooch  
Even this is a soldier's ring  
How did it come to this land  
From the knees of a chimney sweep boy  
From the shin bones of a German soldier

label: youth_life
translation:
In the corner, in the corner, young men  
In the dark tobacco pouches  
Lake maidens are coming  
Their mouths sealed shut  
Their heads crowned with feathers  
Their necks curled with lice  
Snow-white gloves on  
Blue-gray mustache  
Dark black six-button jacket  
Fish-scaled stockings on their legs  
Cherry leather shoes  
Cork soles made from spiny oak  
Silver glass patches underneath  
When he turns, he glances  
When he steps, he shines.

label: youth_life
translation:
Oh, but the harvest festival in Tammiku,  
There was bad girl merchandise there,  
And there was a broad girl without permission.  
They all came together there  
Probably from Harjumaa,  
Undivided from Järvamaa.  
They stand there on Siim's hill,  
The sails were against Siim's garden,  
Their bellies faced the sexton's yard.  
Then they were counted off—  
Some went to Siim,  
The bowlegged one went to the sexton;  
Some mad one went to the new tavern.  
When the night had now passed,  
A letter came from Kehras,  
The third book from Raasik:  
Girls needed for work,  
Some old ones to go as spirits,  
Proper cattle herds,  
Whores to milk cows,  
Harlots to pick apples.  
What were they given to eat there?  
Kaalileent and cabbage stew!  
The whores ate apple soup,  
The women ate sweet soup.  
When the night had now passed,  
Then when they took them to town,  
To be pricked by the town doctor,  
To be rubbed with kolostrohv,  
To have syrup put in the wound.  
The syrup dripped under the bridge,  
The kolostrohv in the home room,  
The syrup dripped from wet eyes,  
Kolostrohv on wet eyebrows,  
At Rotermann the jaws wide open.

label: youth_life
translation:
I fed the stallion, I gave the stallion to drink...  
I went to the German's matchmaker,  
I sent the Germans to Saaremaa,  
The lords to Hiiumaa,  
Half the gentlemen to Poland.  
I started coming home,  
I found a tavern down a lane.  
I went to take a drink,  
I took one drink, I took two,  
I went to take a third drink,  
A thief came from the grove,  
Another from outside the yard,  
They took my good horses,  
A ten-ruble hat,  
A hundred-ruble saddle.  
I came home crying,  
Weeping outside in the yard;  
The woman was there, the man was there,  
Both the old ones answered.  
"Why do you cry, young son?  
We have three stallions at home,  
One is a gold-maned stallion,  
The second is silver-maned,  
The third bronze maned."  
"Well, we will give them for you,  
Redeem you from this trouble."  
...  
I fed the stallion, I gave the stallion to drink,  
The stallion gained strength indeed.  
I went to Koigi to court,  
To the smith Koigi’s daughters  
Were quite famous maidens.  
One was Anne, another Kaie,  
The third a sweet Maiekene.  
Anne was given to me,  
Kaie was bargained for me.  
Ann was naked by the stove,  
Kai was bare bottomed by the rack,  
Mai was on the threshing floor,  
A sack underneath her, and a sack on top,  
A piece of sack by her side,  
No way to bring her home.  
I came home crying,  
The woman was there, the man was there,  
Both the old ones answered.  
"Why do you cry, young son?  
- Why not cry, old woman!  
Why not cry, old man!  
I fed the stallion, I gave it to drink,  
The stallion gained strength and stamina.  
I went to Koigi to court,  
To the smith Koigi’s daughters  
Cannot bring them home,  
I left them out as wild ones,  
The garden barn as helpers!"  
...  
The woman was there, the man was there,  
Both the old ones answered.  
"Why do you cry, young son?  
Bring home the announced wife!  
Set her on the table!  
If not, she will take the lower place,  
She will manage the household affairs,  
She will rinse the spoon handle."

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
I went to the meadow,
Singing across the wide clearing.
A herdsman came from Kuura's side,
Helpers from Arude's side,
A young man running from the manor's side,
A youth from Kiima's barn side.
He gave me a large piece:
A large piece, a wide piece,
Swamp from the bog, swampy land,
Stream from the river, white land,
Marsh from the lake, wet land;
I plowed until my horses were tired,
Blades worn out from hard work.
I let the horses rest at noon,
Under the hayloft to graze,
Under the heathland to roam.
A wolf came from the great forest,
With wide paws even from the hayloft,
It broke my black horse,
Tore my gray horse,
Ate both foolishly.
I wept bitterly:
An old woman was there, an old lady was there.
"Why do you cry, young one?"
"Why do I cry, old lady,
Or why do I cry, little lady?
Be quiet, young one,
Let the wolf come, the wolf's kin:
He lets the wolf from the great forest,
Wide-pawed from the hayloft forest."

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
I do not belong among the great;
Nor fit in the house of the rich!
To sit on a high ear.
I sit especially.
Among other burdensome troubles;
Among the common people.
I speak plainly with the lowly!
Soon I will speak with the weary.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
The frog went with three districts  
The flea went with two parts,  
But I went with the chief.  
I went to Harju street,  
There were two gray ones in front.  
There stood the court lords opposite,  
Court lords, governors.  
But the lord shouted from the stairs,  
"On whom is this hornbag?"  
On me is this hornbag!  
"How did this grain get wet?  
The grain got wet from rain,  
It was covered with fog,  
Wet barns were struck.  
It is not my fault,  
Nor is it the fault of the poor parish.  
It is the fault of the evil commissioner,  
It is the fault of the club servant."

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Maiden, young girl!  
The fish darted from under the stone  
At the crab's bright mountain:  
This girl is my namesake  
My wreath-head beside me  
Who has knots in her shoelaces  
No young woman laughed at me!  
The girl fluttered strongly.  
Lazy woman laughed at me;  
The girl fluttered fiercely.  
Hello, brother!  
Take a whip from your pants;  
Pay the women laughter wages  
The girl’s flutter wages.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Widows, I would become a widower,  
Would broad aprons fall?  
But I say to the widows:  
O widows, go away from me,  
Let broad aprons fall.  
But I will take Epuke,  
At Epuke’s place, pearl-like beads.  
A maiden, a young girl,  
So let me say once again:  
The usual one is already drowsy,  
A hand that works, a foot that walks;  
Who will buy me out of slavery?  
Redeem me from the snowfall?  
Take me away from the rain showers,  
From the Viru sickle’s blade,  
Behind the Järva plows,  
From Harju’s ard cranes.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh, we poor gentlemen  
Ladies with golden crowns  
Let us rise up from our seats  
Let us go up to the hall  
Let us step onto the window frame  
Look at the poor parish  
How this parish is tormented  
The small ones are tormented  
The bigger ones are killed  
Oh, our poor manorial spirits  
Late spirits of the lord  
The most unfortunate servants  
Oh, we poor road walkers  
Road walkers, land measurers  
Managers of German affairs  
Parish letter bearers  
Readers of the municipal book.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
My dear old grandmother!  
She heard me coming home,  
Beyond Väila,  
Beyond the forest's edge,  
She immediately said to her daughter:  
Jump, Anne, leap, Kaie;  
Then take the gate from the fence,  
Close the doors tightly;  
Home is coming a golden bird,  
Coming in a silk bird,  
Then light the stove;  
Heat the stove for the cumin;  
Honor to the whisk of branches,  
Then the branch goes to the whisk:  
The goose is going to the ditch,  
The duck is going to wash knees,  
The pig is going to wash the piglets!  
In her fist are whip strokes;  
On her neck are rod strokes,  
Whip marks between the belt.  
Who had struck the cruel servant,  
Set the strong village chief,  
Knocked on the wicked Kilter;  
Kilter had a stone stick,  
The Junker had a five-striped,  
The servant a six-twisted,  
The barn had a toothed one.  
This went straight through;  
Along the thin shoulder,  
Along the small arm!

label: songs about social relationships
songs about social relationships
translation:
May the harvest come in the year of heaven!  
May it rain in the year of the rod;  
May hail fall like iron,  
There must always be a slave,  
A servant to do the work,  
To keep things running properly.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Mother, dear little woman!  
Stoke the stove with kitchen firewood.  
Honor the whisk for Virve,  
I will take the whisk to Virve,  
To sew the hem of Aniluida:  
Whip strikes from the hip;  
Whip strikes from the neck,  
Blue marks on the back!  
Oh, this poor Esna parish,  
Among other parishes,  
In the middle of the district;  
Whip lashes were heard from Laiuse  
Whip lashes to Paide!  
Torment from Alutaguse;  
The maiden's crying in the meadow!  
I cried before, I cried yesterday,  
Again I cry today!  
*  
Why did the golden eyebrows dry up,  
Why did the eyes straighten?  
Into the rough village,  
To the border of Esna parish.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh, God, dear God!  
Take away the poor children  
Gather up the immoral ones;  
Take into your arms the guilty  
Put in your bosom the despised beasts  
Pollute the rest who are rich  
Shoot the daughters of the family  
Swear at the free women.  
The rich curse me as a farmer  
As a money-driven taxi  
As a gold-plated carriage.  
Let me live without a necklace  
Without a growing collar  
Without rings to row:  
While living, I get a bead  
While growing, I get a neck-bead  
Take the rich landowner away  
Not the money-driven taxi  
Not the gold-plated carriage  
Not the free woman's carriage.  
Let the poor go to hell  
The golden ones to the devil  
The paupers to the demon  
The great rye of the swamp  
I will stay living without a necklace  
Without a growing collar.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Our noble little gold one  
The boldly patterned little bird  
The helper man with a silver cap.  
The silver bell waver  
The gold stick swinger  
Let the children go to lunch  
Sisters in the evening!  
The children ask for lunch  
Sisters in the evening.  
Surely comes from the black manor field  
From the blue grove inside.  
Between gray gardens.  
Now comes the nodder  
Now appears the pincher  
The complainer of five girls,  
The dropper of six girls.  
I will put the gentlemen to the oxen  
The lads into the words  
The bold ones into the tassels  
Ladies with headscarves;  
Myself behind the plowman.  
Plow the barn, pour into the field  
The furrow’s track, old red  
Lift to the land, the dark ox.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
I was a slave, I tended the herd  
I was in the Dutch service  
In the fields of Lehila's sheep  
Holland made a new dome  
Lehila land a wide coat.  
Oh, poor me, a prisoner of children  
Complained from the hiding place!  
Nights I am imprisoned, nights I am saved.  
Nights I keep watch over my father’s herd  
I protect the herd of my brother  
At the river mouth, at the lake mouth  
In the middle of the river’s whirlpool  
Between the river’s currents.  
Two merchants came  
Two merchant servants  
Both had swords at their belts  
Both had spurs on their feet.  
"Maiden, young girl  
In embroidered clothing, slender,  
Sell me father’s horse  
Trade for brother’s saddle."  
"I will not sell father’s herd  
I will not trade brother’s saddle  
Father has a good horse,  
Brother has a dear saddle."  
"Sell me the sword at your belt  
Trade for the spurs on your feet."  
"I will not sell the sword at my belt  
I will not trade the spurs on my feet  
Maiden, young girl  
Allow me to come to you,  
To come to you until death  
To be with you until the end of life.  
I will put you to easy work:  
Beating rye stalks  
Treading on oat husks.  
In summer I keep smoke away  
In winter I lift dust away.  
In summer I feed you sugar rushes  
In winter buckwheat tangles,  
A year's goose meat.  
I protect the herd with walnut cores."  
"I hear, I answer:  
Salt cellars you have for sugar  
Pumpkins for goose meat."  
"Allow me to come  
To come to you, to stay with you."  
"Maybe you would bake me in gold  
Spin silk threads  
Sew with silver thread.  
Maybe there would be a silver yard  
An iron-forged gate  
Stone in the corral,  
Still I will not come to you.  
For you a pigsty  
A horse’s nightmare,  
A dog’s snout with a stick in it  
A mouth like a poor man’s hole  
Face like a paper sack  
Teeth like cattle gates  
Jaws like that of a tongs.  
I will go where it is created  
Where the Creator has made a place  
Mary has given a home.  
Where my blood has carried  
Where my color has taken me  
Where my little luck shares in.  
Maybe there would be an oily yard  
Maybe a fenced garden  
Gates forged from twigs,  
Maybe there would be a pillar in the yard  
In the corral stone stakes  
Still I go where it is created,  
Where the Creator has made a place,  
Mary has given a home.  
Where my blood has carried  
Where my color has taken me  
Where my little luck shares in."

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh, our handsome gentlemen  
And our slender Germans  
Young gentlemen with golden hair  
Ladies in silver lace.  
Rise up onto the chair  
Step onto the windowsill;  
Look upon the poor parish  
Upon the whole district,  
When this parish is afflicted  
The district is troubled.  
The bulls still eat  
The poor horses are confined  
Men dressed in their jackets.  
The bulls groan with their horns  
The horses toss their chests around.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
When I have to go to Tapa
To the dust of Tapa, from the soil of Tapa
From the evil place of Tapa.
From under the German scoundrel
From under the loud old gentleman
From under the bitter soldier
From under the cruel master.
I would look back sorrowfully,
The dog would turn its head from the load,
Before ruin to the home
Before berries to the house,
Under the beloved man's yard.
Then I would look back a little
Turn my head a bit:
"Where the hell is the place,
Where the damn spot.
The windows of hell are burning
The towers of ghosts are foolish
Heating up the evil spirit
Where I was beaten with a whip
Where my arms were tormented,
Where the finger bones were scolded.
If only the wrists were rowan-berry red
The forearms maple-colored
I had thin wrists
Thin shoulder buds."

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh, I am a poor purchased slave!  
Purchased slave, crowned with a wreath,  
A pledged servant.  
Who will buy me, and crown me?  
Who will buy me from slavery  
And crown me with a wreath,  
Redeem me from the snowfall?  
Take us away from the rain showers.  
Viru Peter, a young lad,  
He will buy us an ox yoke,  
A tall apron for the belly,  
A wide ribbon for the head,  
Ruffled cuffs for the hands,  
New buttoned shoes for the feet.  
He will buy us from slavery  
And crown us with days  
Redeem us from the snowfall,  
Take us away from the rain showers.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Who waits for me at home?  
The dog waits for me at home.  
Who urges me into the house?  
The cat urges me into the house.  
The dog waits for crusts,  
The cat for crumbs of bread.  
I have no other waiters,  
The dog is dear, the cat is precious.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh, this poor Tapa parish,  
The hungry Näu village,  
Where I don’t dare to walk in the manor,  
I don’t flash before the lord:  
I don’t even have a barley cake in my pocket,  
Nor any oat porridge in my pan.  
Salt is scarce inside the box,  
And beer is thin in the neck.  
Women walk the manor roads  
Wearing egg mittens.  
Pairs of chickens in the stall,  
Pairs of geese under the hem.  
Thread scarves in their hands,  
The court’s sheep on the hilltop  
Are led out into the manor yard  
To the old lord on the rampart.  
From there the lord comes grunting:  
“Look where the poor sheep stands.  
Take it home to the dogs,  
Give it to the hound!  
Bring me a fatty from the barn,  
A pretty one from the herd  
To carry to the manor’s sheepfold.”  
When the people go to work:  
The coachman goes like a devil,  
The young lord like Judas behind;  
The parish like a prisoner in the middle.  
Then you hear the coachman’s voice,  
The old lord’s cursing.  
There the rowan struggles,  
And then the fir tree moves  
And there the bird cherry staggers  
Over the shoulder of the apple tree.  
But it strikes past the fine coat,  
Past the thin shoulders,  
Past the long sleeves.  
The tenant sighs in slave bondage,  
A tear in his eye.  
The coachman is called hell,  
The young lord is sent after,  
The old lord to watch.  
Tables are set in place,  
Chairs are brought to the table,  
Fire and tar also brought:  
Eat, coachman, drink, steward,  
This poor parish’s toil,  
Its tiny pain-blood.  
If you tormented the parish,  
If you tormented the little ones.  
Oh, this golden Kuruda,  
Silver Roosnaida,  
When the people went to work:  
The coachman like the moon,  
The young lord like God behind,  
The parish like copper in the middle.  
No fir moves there,  
Nor does the rowan struggle.  
No bird cherry staggers there,  
Over the shoulder of the apple tree.  
No sound of the coachman’s voice,  
Nor the steward’s whining,  
Nor the old lord’s cursing.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh, we poor spirits of the parish,
The demons, the other spirits,
The proper third ones,
The auxiliary spirits the fourth,
The drunkards the fifth:
The pain of the night, the pain of the moon,
The pain of God's fire
Golden rakes in hand
Silver plow handles:
I hunted a hundred head for the Saxon,
Six piles for the king.
The piles appeared in Courland,
The herds appeared in Germany,
The flocks seemed to Narva!

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Master, little master,  
Mistress, little lady,  
Pay the servant's wage,  
Reward the poor child's toil!  
If you do not pay the servant's wage,  
Nor reward the poor child's toil,  
Then you will pay in the afterlife,  
Pay to Maria's house:  
You will walk to the gallows tree,  
Clothes rolled in bundles,  
You will seek your little servant,  
Beg for someone to pay wages:  
"Come servant, take your due,  
Come poor one, take your toil!"  
Then I will understand, reply in return:  
Dear miss and little sir,  
Surely you have paid there, in the land,  
Where my path is one of torment,  
An aching road of hardship;  
I do not want to go to the afterlife,  
Among the blue clouds,  
Between the white clouds,  
At the midpoint of the three dawns  
To accept the poor one's toil!

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Our parish, captive parish,  
Coming parish, tar parish,  
Parish of white huts,  
Bulls are eating into the yoke,  
Runes have withered into branches,  
Young men went into the tree,  
Poor spirits went into the poles,  
Rogues were beaten into the pillar,  
The poor into the prison house.  
Women wept in front of the door,  
Wearing egg mittens,  
A fat wheel under the apron,  
Went to the gentleman's petition,  
Went to the lady's petition:  
"Oh, my pea gentleman,  
Golden crown lady,  
Silver button young gentlemen,  
Copper button old gentlemen,  
Rise up onto the chair,  
Sit on the edge of the sofa,  
Look at the poor parish,  
How this parish is tormented,  
The bigger ones are killed,  
The stronger ones are carried away,  
The bigger ones are killed,  
The stronger ones are carried away,  
Do not walk to the bog."  
The lady turned her head.  
"Go home, poor woman,  
From the swamp I will bring those warm switches,  
From the willow I will bring proper switches,  
From the aspen I will bring softer ones:  
Beat the leaves, beating men.  
Lift up the oak roots,  
Switches rough in the hand,  
The ends of the switch will blister,  
The ends of the stick will splinter."

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
I went home wandering,
To see the old woman,
I heard the old woman crying,
Mourning the deceased.
I asked the old woman:
"Why are you crying, old woman?"
The old woman heard, replied:
"Why do you cry, young daughter?
You still wander the manor,
You rock before the swing,
You shout in the middle of the courtyard,
Roaming among spirits!
I am afraid, I am afraid, young daughter,
Afraid of the fine shirts betraying me,
Of being buried beneath the husband's coat,
Covered by the worn fur coat!"
I heard, replied:
"Not me, not me, old woman,
The fine shirts do not betray me,
The husband's coat
Covers the worn fur coat;
But me, but me, old woman,
I am hidden by fine sand
And buried by black soil,
Covered by the worn church,
Concealed by the white little tower."

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh, we poor tiumehed  
When we come from the wind  
And we are wet  
Where do we dry ourselves  
Let's go to Rein's thigh,  
What do we put in our oven?  
Kubja's shanks, the constable's gloves  
We both help the fields  
We put these in our oven  
And then dry ourselves.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
If I were in charge  
If I were in control  
I would turn the oxen into horses  
The ladies into sticks  
The braids on the ears into earrings  
The lads into companions for the girls

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Listen, dear old granny  
Listen, dear old grandpa  
Throw a bundle of twigs into the stove  
An honor birch whisk for whipping  
I go to whip the miserable  
I go to chase the geese  
That had beaten the angry groom  
The angry groom, the brave young man  
Even louder the manor lords  
Would be my existence  
Would be my doing  
I would know what I would do  
I would turn the gentlemen into bulls  
The young men into stories  
The grooms behind bars  
And the maidens into bald heads  
I myself would sit on the saddle  
A long whip in my hand  
Plowing the yard, turning the field  
Wow, old red one  
The plow plows, the back bends  
Plowing the field, the tail swishes  
Our day blazes into noon  
Turns to the middle of the day  
We have nothing to eat  
Neither given nor offered without asking  
If I get angry  
I leave the bulls right there  
I myself go where the devils  
Then I go to the forest as a breaker  
Then I break the bulls  
I kill the lambs in the barn.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
The master was angry with me  
The mistress was loud with me  
I am good to the oxen  
Good matches for them  
I tended the oxen well  
Gently harnessed the horses  
I plowed the sod land  
Did not spoil the horn roots  
Threw willow without a family  
The housewife was angry with me  
Sprinkled salt among the coarse salt  
Added straw to the hay  
Poured water into the milk.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Slave labor is sought  
A poor child is seen  
If not changed, forced to carry mud  
To beat clods in the field  
To carry stones together.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Brother invited to the wedding  
I don't have time to go  
I’m going to town tomorrow  
With the church gentleman  
With the old gentleman of the parish  
I will become the parish carpenter  
The trial bag will be on me  
I, the poor stable boy  
The gentleman of the parish’s spiritual boy  
When they go through Kiu  
I go through Tond’s straw  
But here comes a German  
Hello, hello, parish carpenter  
Who has the trial bag on  
Open the trial bag.  
Listen, you parish carpenter  
Why is the rye wet?  
That’s not my fault  
Nor the poor parish’s fault  
It is the evil carpenter’s fault  
Grain was wind-sifted in the blizzard  
Grain was carried in the rain  
Grain was caught in the hail  
The barn roof keeps breaking  
Oh, I, the poor stable boy  
The gentleman of the parish’s servant boy.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
In the ancient times, the daughter cries  
It is not for nothing that the daughter cries  
The daughter has a quarrel coming  
And is weighing the rods  
The fire does not extinguish  
The woman does not argue with the youth  
The horse does not belong to the gray harness  
There is no spark in the bedding stakes  
Illu-lillu pregnant gray  
In our yard several stalls  
In each stall seven gray ones  
They neigh and make a ruckus  
All of them wanted payments  
Settlements with silver manes  
Rates with golden combs  
Tender caresses  
I could not pay them  
Could not settle with silver manes  
Could not rate with golden combs  
Could not caress them more tenderly  
Then had to be beaten with a whip  
Pulled by a tarred rope  
But I managed to get away poor  
Skirting along the field.  
Then I was caught with a rope  
And chased mercilessly  
See, the rope was a thousand fathoms long  
And within the rope were a hundred knots.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
The landlady tricked me  
She promised to cook cat soup.  
She cooked soup from an old shoe  
Threw in a piece of song.  
The master thought: a piece of bacon  
The servant thought: a piece of bone  
The children: a piece of lamb meat  
The old man: a heel.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
The devil dug in the spruce forest,  
The pagan hammered on the sapwood,  
Made the wheelwright’s barn  
An old gentleman’s carriage.  
The rims rusted from the iron,  
The spokes from wolf bones,  
The side boards from forest trees.  
The hub was made of pine,  
The hoops cast from brass,  
Boards broken from logs,  
End pieces from teeth,  
The breasts from ladders,  
Legs considered as shafts,  
A plug rod made of dill,  
The back beam of a pine tree.  
Tail base for the tail end.  
The horse was placed in front;  
The gentleman between the shafts,  
The coachman’s ears, the bell on the tilt,  
The gentleman’s ears by the shafts. –  
The lady with a whip on the bench,  
The young lord with a running foot.  
Misses tarred the carriage skin,  
Nailing the coach’s hide.  
Then the Germans were sent to hell,  
The peasants to heaven.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Investigate, investigate, what are you investigating  
Investigate a new thigh  
Boundary on a long border  
Let it be on a wide board  
There is pitch water of reeds  
Five buckets of cracked water  
Six buckets of devil’s urine  
There the investigators swim  
Washing their heads with borders.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
I was a slave, I tended the herd  
I was a Dutch servant,  
A shepherd boy from the land of souls,  
What was my wage for the dyke path?  
An old coat, an old fur coat,  
Are you satisfied with that?  
And are you satisfied with us?  
I do not agree to that  
Nor am I satisfied with you.  
If I serve, I will serve still  
A rich man and the well-mannered.  

I was a slave, I tended the herd  
I was a Dutch servant,  
A shepherd boy from the land of souls,  
What was my wage for the dyke path?  
An old rag on a shriveled branch,  
An old bundle at the edge of the forest,  
Do you agree to that?  
And are you satisfied with us?  
I do not agree to that  
Nor am I satisfied with you.  
If I serve, I will serve still  
A rich man and the well-mannered.  

I was a slave, I tended the herd  
I was a Dutch servant,  
A shepherd boy from the land of souls,  
What was my wage for the dyke path?  
A sheep with a lamb,  
A pig with a hundred piglets,  
Do you agree to that?  
And are you satisfied with us?  
I am not satisfied with that  
Nor do I agree with you.  
If I serve, I will serve still  
A rich man and the well-mannered.  

I was a slave, I tended the herd  
I was a Dutch servant,  
A shepherd boy from the land of souls,  
What was my wage for the dyke path?  
A horse with the largest bridle,  
A barn with a hundred horned heads,  
Do you agree, do you agree with that?  
And are you satisfied with us?  
I do not agree to that  
Nor am I satisfied with you.  
If I serve, I will serve still  
A rich man and the well-mannered.  

I was a slave, I tended the herd  
I was a Dutch servant,  
A shepherd boy from the land of souls,  
What was my wage for the dyke path?  
From Tallinn to the roads of Tartu,  
The big cities of the land of Finland,  
Do you agree to that?  
And are you satisfied with us?  
I do not agree to that  
Nor am I satisfied with you.  
If I serve, I will serve still  
A rich man and the well-mannered.  

I was a slave, I tended the herd  
I was a Dutch servant,  
A shepherd boy from the land of souls,  
What was my wage for the dyke path?  
A virgin's bed of gold,  
Supply all the house tools,  
Do you agree to that?  
And are you satisfied with us?  
Yes, I agree to that  
And I am satisfied with you.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Loori-loori chant  
The chief bird, the little swallow  
Sang a song from the eaves, little bird  
The rich man killed a great bull  
I am the enemy, a crow  
Meat was eaten, meat was sold  
The hide went to Narva to the tanners  
The head went to the chief of Pärnu  
From the beak I got a blowhorn  
From the tuft I got a snow cap  
From the tail I got a woolen hat  
Then I went to the town to roam  
To Paide to steal ribbons  
The manor lords were baffled  
The town masters wondered  
Where has this man come from?  
He has come from afar  
He is a rich man from Riga  
Or is he the real lord of Pärnu  
Or is he the king of Courland  
I heard, I answered in turn:  
I am not a rich man from Riga  
Nor the real lord of Pärnu  
Nor the king of Courland  
I am a poor servant boy  
A spirit boy from the parish of Hallik

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Now beautiful Viru's water  
Lovely to sing on the shores  
Viru rolls the words  
Dear beloved to speak  
Dew carries the voice box  
The aal carries the voice to Harjumaa  
Dew carries the voice far away  
Harju women to bark  
Viru women to roll  
To follow the daughters of Järva.  
Harju woman to bite the crust  
Viru woman with a fierce back  
Western woman with a lame leg  
Do not eat my heart  
Drink the good voice box  
I am great to set the pot  
To spread widely on the table  
Easy to cook the kettle  
White to set on the platter  
To place the dish on the board.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Mari from Magas  
Among the bluebells  
Beneath the buttercups  
Between the meadowsweet  
The bluebells are seeding  
The buttercups are yellowing  
The meadowsweet is turning gray  
The grass weakens the young ones  
I weep for the young grass  
I was once a gentleman's boy  
A stick-bearer’s servant  
Now I am the servant’s slave  
Of the thirty dog boys  
The overseers had large runes  
Wide clearings, thick boats  
They wanted to work in the summer  
To cultivate the iron furrow  
To tend the golden comb  
If I had been able to work in the summer  
To tend the golden comb  
Then they would have beaten me with a whip  
Driven me по the dog rose  
Led me по the bull’s path.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
To wander the leg for an hour  
To stumble slightly on the leg  
I had a wide belt woven  
To twist it from coarse yarn  
To lay it from fine yarn  
To fasten my stomach  
To pull from the belly’s hardship.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
We had a damn blacksmith  
The bitter shit was a constable  
The thief was the parish leader  
This meadow was for spirits  
Timber men for whips  
Young men for blades  
The old gentleman for hell's tobacco  
Was from a crueler blacksmith  
Of a stronger parish leader  
Pulled together, pulled the constable  
Imprisoned the parish leader  
"Listen, blacksmith, darling  
Manor lord, little calf  
Constable, spotted little bird  
Let the sisters go to the evening  
The sisters are diligent in the morning  
Before dawn, the crows  
Before the rooster crows  
Before the second capercaillies  
Before the day’s swallows"

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Our groom, the golden one  
The manor lord, the lowland one  
You have surely felt the feeling  
You have surely guessed the time  
No need to discuss further  
Already has Virus eaten lunch  
Of course, from Alutaguse  
A thousand times from Turkey  
A hundred times from Germany  
Our servants without pride  
Geese always without a meal  
Blueberries without lunch  
Cuckoos without a morning

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
What are you scurrying for, little Siim  
Are you watching the crow, little Jaagu  
Are you guarding the pigsty, little Hans  
The garden is not yours to have  
Nor the valuable land  
Among the pigs it is yours to have  
In the flock your companion  
In the barn your little child.  
Among the pigs it is growing up  
In the flock it is growing  
In the barn the child is being taken care of  
At home they are waiting for me  
They are watching at the gate  
To see if the bringer of fire is coming  
Or the water carrier is rolling by  
The kitty is waiting for me at home  
Or maybe watching me at the gate  
The dog is waiting for me at home  
The cat is watching at the gate  
The dog is waiting for scraps  
The hen for fish heads  
The sheep for bread crusts.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Our captain, little gold one,  
Dainty, colorful little bird,  
Let the children go to lunch,  
Sisters to evening,  
Boys to mid-afternoon.  
Now it is children's lunchtime,  
Sisters' evening time,  
Boys' mid-afternoon time.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Is Kessi waiting for me at home?  
The dog is waiting for me at home.  
Is Kessi coaxing at home?  
The cat is coaxing at home.  
The dog is waiting with little barking dogs  
The cat with little bread crumbs.  
That slave is waiting at home.  
The slave is looking for work  
The channel is being tested for work  
If nothing else, to carry mud  
To gather firewood.  
A bit of these days  
Thinking of those times  
Even if the slave is praised  
As a son-in-law in jest.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Come together, young children  
Let's go see the manor  
What is understood in the manor  
In the manor, people get beaten  
Meat is soaked in bones  
Bloodletting is done  
"Dear hunchback, stop, hunchback  
Don't hit me, I'm short  
Don't beat me, I'm small  
Shoes worn out on the barn floor  
Brother's worn shoe soles  
Sister's sewn shoes.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh, I, a bought slave,  
A bought slave, head-dressed with a wreath,  
A pledged servant,  
Who will buy me from slavery  
Who will free me from bondage  
But carries me away from the rain showers  
Redeems me from the snowfall  
A brotherly Russian  
A sailor, a lowly boy  
He will buy me from slavery  
He will free me from bondage  
Redeems me from the snowfall  
He will gather me under the spruce  
Hide me under a woolen blanket  
Under a striped cover.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh God, oh little God  
Throw down the ropes of scum,  
Push down the cords of tar  
Pull me into heaven  
Among the rich of others,  
Among the poor of others;  
I am not born among the great  
Nor fit into the house of the rich  
Nor to sit on a high ear.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Iitus-tiitus, a pregnant Hall,  
In our yard several stables,  
Seven Halls in each stable,  
Neighing and making fiends.  
They all wanted payments,  
Settlements on silver ridge,  
Yardings on golden comb,  
Tender caresses more delicate.  
I could not manage to pay them,  
Nor to settle on silver ridge,  
Nor to yard on golden comb,  
Nor to caress more delicately.  
Then they had to whip me with a whip,  
Pull me with a tarred rope.  
Then I, poor man, had to shed  
Socks in my mouth and rags under my arm,  
A skirt between my teeth.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
The village calls me to visit,
To visit and eat,
To visit and drink.
Oh, how I understand, I immediately respond,
I would answer with a verse:
"For how long would I eat at the village,
Or why would I run to the village:
I eat the ox without eating,
I drink the barrel without drinking.
What is there to eat from the ox?
The bone is inside, the skin is on top —
A chunk of lean meat.
What is there to drink from the barrel?
The yeast is down, the foam is on top —
A drop of dark beer."

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh, I, poor wife of a free man,  
A wretched little sauna woman!  
I pace around the mistress,  
I walk around the maid,  
I ask her for a little pot,  
I beg for the corner of a linen cloth.  
I have to carry the broth,  
I have to cook the beans,  
I have to walk on tiptoe,  
I have to scoop ashes with a ladle,  
I myself get beaten,  
The wretched little one is so scolded,  
I ask for a strip of the field,  
Where I may sow cabbage,  
But meanwhile I look around,  
To see how they dig for gold.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Now it is time for the court to go home,  
the right to go to the evening gathering;  
Now it is time to milk the cow,  
the calves' drinking time,  
the young noblemen's drinking time.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
If it were tomorrow,
The coming Friday,
Then I would know what I would do:
I would turn socks into trousers,
Gentlemen into oxen,
Caps into storks,
Kilts into wedges,
Young ladies into calves.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Our little golden cub,
A jaunty, colorful little bird,
Lets the children go to lunch,
The right time to the evening.
The children are diligent in the morning,
Early before dawn,
Before the sun has risen,
Before the dawn, they have gathered.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
The village calls me to visit  
They eat in the village, they drink in the village  
When I understand, I immediately reply  
Soon I will respond to them  
How many villages would I eat at  
Or at which village would I run  
I eat the ox altogether  
And drink beer from the barrel altogether  
What is there to eat from that ox  
Or to drink from that beer barrel  
The ox has skin on  
Skin on, bone underneath  
A chunk of beef  
Or to drink from that beer barrel  
Yeast settles, foam stays on top  
A drop of dark beer.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
I was diligent, I tended the flock,  
I was Hollard's servant,  
Lieberland's shepherd boy.  
What was I paid?  
A sheep with two lambs.  
I did not agree to that,  
I was not satisfied with that lamb.  
I was diligent, I tended the flock,  
I was Hollard's servant,  
Lieberland's shepherd boy.  
What was I paid?  
A horse colt.  
I did not agree to that,  
I was not satisfied with that colt.  
I was diligent, I tended the flock,  
I was Hollard's servant,  
Lieberland's shepherd boy.  
What was I paid?  
A fur coat and a six-year-old (horse).  
I did not agree to that,  
I was not satisfied with the six-year-old.  
I was diligent, I tended the flock,  
I was Hollard's servant,  
Lieberland's shepherd boy.  
What was I paid?  
A pig with seven piglets.  
I did not agree to that,  
I was not satisfied with the piglets.  
I was diligent, I tended the flock,  
I was Hollard's servant,  
Lieberland's shepherd boy.  
What was I paid?  
The landowner's daughter with a farm,  
With that I am satisfied.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Master, little master,  
Mistress, little mistress:  
Pay the servant well,  
Reward the poor child's toil.  
If you do not pay in this world,  
Surely you will pay in heaven,  
You will pay before Mary.  
Surely you will walk to the stocks,  
March to the whipping post,  
The fabric to the broad loom.  
Come, then, pay the servant wages,  
The servant’s summer wages,  
A day’s full day’s wages.  
Then I understand, I reply:  
I do not want to go to heaven  
If I was not paid in that world,  
Where the breastbone was broken,  
The neckbone snapped,  
And many other bones broken.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh, that poor Väätse parish:
The parish is sluggish ahead,
Humpbacked like the devil from behind.
Oh, that good Kerna parish:
The parish is strong as copper ahead,
Humpbacked golden from behind.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Hello, dear gentleman,  
Lady of the Golden Crown,  
Rise up onto the chair,  
Step onto the window frame,  
Look upon the poor parish,  
Upon the wicked deanery,  
How the parish is tormented,  
The little ones are punished,  
The bigger ones are killed,  
The deanery is harassed.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
It would be my being,  
for another my doing.  
If only I knew what I would do,  
I would turn gentlemen into oxen,  
young ladies into headscarves,  
old ladies into plough handles,  
myself at the back calling out:  
"Plow the furrow, pour the seed,  
A'a furrow the old red one,  
lift the earth a little,  
turn the earth a little."

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Master, little master,  
Mistress, little lady,  
Pay well the servant’s wage,  
Compensate the poor child’s toil.  
If you do not pay in this world,  
Then you will pay in heaven,  
(You pay before Mary)  
You will be at the mercy of the elbow tree,  
You will march to the shoulder of the whip tree,  
The cloth to wide tension.  

"Come now, servant, take your pay,  
Servant—winter pay,  
Day laborer—daily wage."  

Then I understand, I answer:  
"I do not want to go to heaven,  
If I was not paid in that world,  
Where the ribs were broken,  
Where the neck bones were fractured,  
And many other bones were broken too."

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh, that poor Väätsa parish:  
the parish is miserable,  
hunched like the devil afterwards.  
Oh, that good Kerna  
parish is like a copper entity,  
hunched golden afterwards.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Mother, dear little mother,  
stoke the stove with kitchen herbs,  
honor will be bound to Virve.  
I am coming, Virve, to whisk the birch branches,  
I am coming, goose, to break twigs,  
swallow, to wash your head.  
I have on my back whip blows,  
on my neck rod blows,  
wooden rod blows under my skirt.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
If it were for my being,  
for my doing,  
I would know what I would do.  
I would make the skirts into petticoats,  
the carts into wagons,  
the huts into cranes,  
the ditches into wedges.  
Then the plow would come to the village,  
furrow breaking the fields.  
I myself am muddy to the crown,  
my body wet to the clock.  
The mud, however, enriched the crown,  
The nest washed the clock.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
The rich man killed a great bull,  
A great bull, a black bull.  
Could neither eat it, nor sell it,  
Could not take the meat to town.  
I, the poor man, killed a raven,  
An old and gray raven;  
From there I got to eat, from there I got to sell,  
From there I got meat to take to town.  
From the hornbeam, I got a hornpipe,  
From the tuft, I got a snow hat,  
From the tail, a fur coat;  
From the shin bone, I got bedposts,  
From the kneecap bone, I got main boards,  
From the collarbone, I got side boards.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Study, study, what are you studying,  
Study on the new thigh,  
Border on the long border,  
Let it on the wide board.  
There is tar water from a broom,  
Five vats of virutis water.  
Six vats of the devil's piss.  
There the investigators swim,  
Borders wash their heads.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Master, little master!  
Mistress, little mistress!  
Said to eat a lot,  
Eat a lot, drink a lot.  
Put a lot in place.  
What will I eat at the village!  
What will I drink at the village!  
What will I put in place at the village!  
The ox eats even while eating,  
Drinks from the vat even while drinking.  
What can I eat from the ox!  
What can I drink from the ox!  
The skin is outside and the bone is inside.  
What can I drink from the vat!  
The yeast is below and the foam is above,  
A drop of red beer,  
I won't go, I won't rush,  
I leave this place.  
I pour to the other room.  
I give the place to others,  
Let the better ones come to the place,  
The more honest to the place,  
Let the most famous be at the door's side.  
I will come to see tomorrow,  
Then I will come back again.  
The order was where I left,  
The chair was where I raised,  
The bench was where I stayed.  
Sweep the room to the corner,  
Split kindling for the stove,  
The broom cried like a whisk.  
The clogs asked for cleaning,  
Spoons burned in the fire,  
The ladle handles got hot.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Now the beautiful Viru without water  
Is lovely to sing to the shores.  
Viru rolls the words.  
Dear is the speech below.  
The dew carries the vocal cords.  
The eel takes the voice to Harjumaa,  
The dew carries the voice to far away.  
Harju women bark,  
Viru women roll,  
Järva daughters divide.  
Harju woman [is] toothy,  
Viru woman [has] a vengeful back,  
Western woman [has] slippery feet.  
Do not eat my heart,  
Eat the good vocal cords.  
I am great to set the pot on the stove,  
To lay it wide on the table,  
Easy to cook in the kettle,  
White to put on the plate,  
Want to put on the platter.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
The devil dug in the spruce forest,  
The pagan hammered in the willow.  
He made a cart's wheelhouse,  
An old gentleman's wagon,  
Rims rusted from iron,  
Spokes like a wolf pack.  
Rungs like ladders.  
Toe boards placed on the head beam,  
Cast brass hitches,  
Axles broken from jaws.  
End rods without teeth.  
Side parts of ear wood.  
Feet considered shafts.  
Backbeam load of harness wood.  
A rod made of dill-like wood.  
The horse's yoke in front,  
The gentleman between the shafts,  
A bunch of ears, a jaunty jingle.  
The gentleman's ear on the shaft.  
The lady with a whip on the bench,  
The maids on the cart to tar,  
Nailing the carriage hide.  
Then the Saxons were sent to hell.  
The peasants to heaven.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Lõõri-lõõri swallows,
daybird sparrow.
Sang the bird under the eaves:
A rich man killed a great ox.
I am the enemy, the carrion.
Got meat to eat, got meat to sell,
The hide went to Narva’s tanner.
The head went to the Pärnu chief.
From the beak, I got a snuff horn,
From the tuft, I got a woolen cap.
From the tail, I got a hundred-cap.
Then I went to roam the town.
To Paide parish to wander.
The manor Germans pondered,
The town lords wondered:
Where did this man come from?
He has come from afar.
Is he a rich lord of Riga,
Or is he a true lord of Pärnu?
Or is he the king of Courland?
I heard, I replied.
I am not a rich Riga lord,
Nor the true lord of Pärnu,
Nor the king of Courland.
I am a poor stable boy,
A servant boy of the Alliku parish.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
I was a slave, I herded the flock.
I was a Dutch servant,
A sheep boy from England.
What was my reward?
An old coat, an old sheepskin.
Do you accept this,
And are you satisfied with us?
I do not accept this,
Nor am I satisfied with you.
If I serve, I serve still
A rich man and a decent one.
I was a slave, I herded the flock.
I was a Dutch servant.
A sheep boy from England.
What was my reward?
An old crooked back,
An old worn-out foot.
Do you accept this,
And are you satisfied with us?
I do not accept this,
Nor am I satisfied with you.
If I serve, I serve still
A rich man and a decent one.
I was a slave, I herded the flock,
I was a Dutch servant,
A sheep boy from England.
What was my reward?
A sheep with a lamb,
A pig with a hundred piglets.
Do you accept this,
And are you satisfied with us?
I do not accept this,
Nor am I satisfied with you.
If I serve, I serve still
A rich man and a decent one.
I was a slave, I herded the flock.
I was a Dutch servant,
A sheep boy from England.
What was my reward?
A horse with the finest harness,
A hundred-horned calf in the barn.
Do you accept this,
And are you satisfied with us?
I do not accept this,
Nor am I satisfied with you.
If I serve, I serve still
A rich man and a decent one.
I was a slave, I herded the flock.
I was a Dutch servant,
A sheep boy from England.
What was my reward?
From Tallinn to Tartu roads,
From Finland to the big cities.
Do you accept this,
And are you satisfied with us?
I do not accept this,
Nor am I satisfied with you.
I was a slave, I herded the flock.
I was a Dutch servant,
A sheep boy from England.
What was my reward?
A virgin with a golden braid,
All the house utensils gold-plated.
Do you accept this,
And are you satisfied with us?
Yes, I accept this,
And I am satisfied with you.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
I used to be a large mountain,
Among the bluebells,
Above the globeflowers
Between the meadowsweet.
The bluebells fade,
The globeflowers yellow,
The meadowsweet turns gray.
The grass grows weak and young.
I weep for the young grass:
I was once the master’s boy,
The stick-bearer, a hen’s keeper.
Now I am a forced servant.
The master had big hooves,
Wide eyelids, thick boats,
They wanted to furrow in summer.
To iron the ridge.
To comb the golden comb.
If you couldn’t furrow in summer,
Comb the golden comb—
Then they would beat me with a whip,
Feed me as dog’s food,
Drive me as ox’s fodder.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
I am not born among the great,  
to fit into a rich man's house,  
the rich take against the rich,  
the wealthy against another wealthy,  
I am born in the corner of the sauna,  
among the poor and middle-aged.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh, we poor manor spirits  
Other poor laborers  
Ordinary third ones  
Helper spirits fourth  
Drinkers fifth  
Were driven to howl at night  
To march across the land  
To walk across the desert.  
Night is painful, moon is painful  
God’s fire is painful  
Night is painful, I cut the hay  
Moon is painful, I cut the stack  
God’s fire is painful,  
Golden rakes in the shed  
Silver sickle handles  
When will I escape the manor's year?  
The manor’s year is a hellish year.  
I escape as if from under your mouth  
Between the jaws of a lion.  
Between the teeth of a monkey  
Now I look back carefully  
On my dog’s load I turn my head.  
Before the home gate  
Before father’s barn door,  
Before brother’s chamber threshold  
Then I look over the ridge  
Towards the worse side,  
See how the hell looks  
The underworlds blaze  
Hell’s windows glow red  
Ghost towers stand idle  
Life seems a joke.  
There are large German fields  
Bottomless lady’s fields.  
There our feathers melt  
Silver ornaments straighten out.  
Wallets grow empty.  
There on the big field  
On the bottomless field.  
On the angular meadow.  
Now I say again in reverse.  
To sing again in Danish  
I turn the words upside down.  
There fall on the back of the German  
Break the mistress’s neck  
Lady’s hip bones fall apart  
Virgin’s limbs twist  
Our backs become whole  
Our scythes sharp  
Our necks stiff.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Our manor’s prisoner manor  
The spiritual destruction of people  
A poor refuge for children  
The bulls keep eating  
Runes, weak ones, in harness  
Men in chest clothes  
Women walk the manor road  
Gloves on hands  
A fat wheel in a kerchief,  
Oh, you are a gentleman.  
A maiden with silver lace.  
Young gentlemen with golden buttons,  
Let us rise onto the chair,  
Step onto the window table,  
Step onto the window table,  
Let us look upon the poor parish.  
How this parish is tormented  
The little ones are tortured.  
Women are cursed,  
The swamp comes from the black manor side  
Gray comes from between the gardens  
Blue from behind the grove  
Oh, I am a poor farmhand:  
I plow all day  
Towards the blessed evening  
May the devil take this steward.  
Scratch both hands  
Bring me a big piece  
A big piece from the bottom of the pond.  
Wet earth from under the hill  
I plow but cannot reach.  
I keep staring towards the manor.  
Our steward, a dear one  
Manor man, Madalukene  
Roller of the silver rod  
Spinner of the golden staff,  
Let the children go to the noon meal  
Sisters to the evening meal.  
Already the day rolls in Viru  
Already noon long ago in Harju.  
Our noon not exhaled  
Fish not cut up,  
Cauldron not filled with gold  
Silver handle not tempered.  
Dear little brother  
Come to us to carve pike perch  
To cut fish into pieces  
To split the roach.  
The pike roaring into the sea  
Fish singing on the shore  
But throwing a splash into the wave.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
The Hellish Mistress  
Boiled me some shoe-leather  
Put some apnemaie in the oven  
Kept the keriksele boiling  
And leesimaie under the flame.  
The shields were washing their behinds  
The pigs rinsed their piggy snouts,  
The servant ate a large amount  
During the long daytime,  
I, poor, all year round.  
The mistress twisted her neck  
Twisted the neck of the string  
Tied the string to the dog's neck  
And the other end to the servant's neck  
She made me stand outside  
To watch the gate,  
The hole for the three-legged dog.  
The milkmaid rubbed her horn,  
The milker's ear was sore,  
A little milk in the vessel  
A bit of soot inside  
A little butter upfront,  
Oh, that first living!  
Couldn't get bread with butter  
Couldn't touch a chicken egg  
Nor tear any meat,  
The housemaid was a pepper sack  
A pepper sack of buckwheat  
She walked the way to the barn  
Switching between two chambers  
Ripping the blacksmith's thighs  
And breaking the neck of a cake.  
Pinched the end of the sausage.  
The housemaid, a young maiden  
Certainly could eat in the kitchen  
Secretly could eat in the sauna  
Even more in the chimney corner  
Twice as much in the chamber  
Her knife even stretched from hanging  
The other one broke at the phallus  
The third broke from a dear nail,  
Always to the butter dish,  
Took a bite of cake.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
I do not belong to the great ranks  
Nor fit in a rich man’s house  
I have no shame of honest parents  
Nor of rich garments  
I sit especially  
Among other poor people  
Amidst mediocre children.  
Let me pour words back  
I do not care for the proud ones  
I fear breaking the rich ones  
I break long planks to splinters  
Thick pieces to chips  
Wide boards to shavings.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
The devil's den  
Look, there the hellpit appears  
The smaller ones are tortured there,  
The bigger ones are killed there  
If I escape from the manor,  
Then I escape from hell.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
If I were in charge,  
And it were up to me to act,  
I would tear the Germans to shreds,  
And turn the gentlemen into oxen,  
The Junkers into chatterboxes,  
The ladies into sticks,  
And the peasants into cranes.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
When we come from work  
And if we then also get wet,  
Where can we dry ourselves?  
Let's go by the manor's threshing barn.  
What will we find there by the oven?  
The cooper's legs, the miller's boots,  
We will help both of the lads.  
The cooper came from the sack side  
And the miller from the chaff side.  
A stick bundle was on the shoulder strap  
A switch bundle was tucked into the belt,  
Then I begin to wonder,  
What kind of forest is closest,  
The birch forest was far away,  
And the willow forest grassy,  
The aspen forest was the closest.  
Then I run to the aspen grove,  
Jump down into the birch grove.  
I knocked the cooper over.  
And the miller face down.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh, I am a poor servant girl,  
A little wretch, a servant girl!  
I have water instead of long-lasting milk,  
Fire hay instead of enough tobacco,  
Dugout cake instead of enough kvass,  
Oh, I am a poor servant mother,  
A little wretch, a sauna mother!  
I spin around the mistress,  
I walk around the German woman,  
I break the corner of the flax roll,  
I ask for my own little pot,  
I have broth to push the flaxes,  
I have broth for the tand (a kind of footwear),  
I have pea broth for punishment,  
I stir coal into the ladle,  
They beat me themselves,  
They thrash this little wretch.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
If it were up to me,  
And my doing besides,  
I would surely know what I would do.  
I would turn the gentlemen into oxen,  
The old ladies into iron slags,  
The German children into clods,  
The peasants into backwoodsmen,  
And myself into their overseer.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
I was in the barn, I went to the herd,  
I was in Holland tying up,  
Linder in the sheepfold by the lamb.  
What will you pay as a wage  
And also as a price for the gift?  
The church with the parish,  
The manor with the entire estate.  
Do you agree with this,  
And are you satisfied with us?  
No, I do not agree with this,  
Nor am I satisfied with you,  
I want two thousand money  
And to buy expensive clothes too,  
Then I will agree with this  
And be satisfied with you.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
The rich man killed a big bull,  
A big bull, a draft bull,  
I, a poor old wretch,  
Because I got to eat, because I got to sell,  
Because I could still take meat to the town,  
Because I made a lot of things,  
I made a pouch from the skin,  
I made a pouch from the snout,  
I made a walking stick from the thigh bone,  
I made a bedpost from the shin bone,  
I made a bedspread from the wings,  
I made a big pillow from the feathers.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
I was a slave, I herded cattle,  
I was a servant of the Ollender,  
In the service of Tillermann.  
Reinu had big horses,  
Tall ears, thick boats,  
They wanted to mate in summer,  
In winter to work with an iron plow.  
I, a lazy boy,  
Did not bother to mate in summer,  
Or to work with the iron plow in winter.  
They had to beat me with a whip,  
Strike me with an iron rod.  
I became an enemy, a cattle driver,  
And a knickerbocker...

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
But I was drowsy, roaming in the herd,  
I was a servant of Ol´lan´di,  
Enchanted by Leeverlan´di.  
Ol´lan´t made me a new jacket,  
Leeverlan´t a wide coat,  
From Al´li cat skins  
And colorful goat legs,  
Hedgehog hides of pig skin  
And old hat made of piña cloth.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
If I were to exist,  
Secondly, my doing:  
I would make otters into otter-like beings,  
Horned cranes into crane-like beings,  
Sparrows into sparrow-like beings.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
The village calls me to the village to eat,  
to eat in the village, to drink in the village.  
Oh, how I understand, I will answer soon,  
I will reply to you shortly:  
How many villages would I eat at  
or to which village would I run.  
I eat the ox while eating,  
drink a keg of beer while drinking.  
What good is the ox to me to eat?  
What good is the keg of beer to drink?  
The ox has its hide on,  
the hide on, the bone underneath,  
a little tender meat.  
Or to drink from the keg of beer?  
The yeast is beneath, the foam on top,  
a little drop of dark beer.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
I was a slave, I tended the herd,  
I was Ollard's servant.  
Ollart made a new coat,  
Leemert a wide jacket. -  
I watch over the old woman's sheep,  
I protect the large flock of the village.  
The old woman makes me a new coat,  
a warm coat of white wool.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Come, slave, take what is yours,  
come, poor one, take the hardship!  
...The long feast of Kuinarpuu,  
the loom's sling on the shoulder...  
I don’t want to go to heaven,  
when you are living on earth.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
If only I knew what I would do:  
I would turn the mares into mares with foals  
and the young ladies into sticks!

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
I am a traveler,
who has widely traveled the world,
my scissors, curling iron, needle case,
all together in my pouch.
My work is delicate and precise.
Where wedding guests gather,
I am always brought there
and honored
and carried in hands.
He asked in great anger:
What is your name, old crone?
I am tailor Jüri Ants,
who has widely traveled the world.
Then he let me shear,
and pile a thousand backs.
My back then became straighter
and my legs became lighter.
Then I cursed the Germans:
let the Germans perish,
let the cane-bearers disappear,
let the masters suffer famine,
today alone, tomorrow two,
the day after tomorrow five or six.
May God grant us many Antsus,
may there be many Siimuses,
may the Jüris vanish to the roots,
may the Mardis fall to the ground.

label: songs about social relationships
songs about social relationships
translation:
Here where the hellish pit shines,  
where the devil's chapel rings;  
there my cheeks are tormented,  
the knuckles are afflicted,  
young fingers are scolded.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
If it were up to me,
if it were my doing,
then I would know what I would do:
I would turn lazy people into diligent ones,
dogs into sled dogs,
louts into talkers.
I would call on everyone:
Plow for Kiitu, sow for Lauk,
go to battle, old Red!
I would have ten pairs of ploughs,
the ninth saved one.
Seven sickles cut in Väila.
The eighth mowed with a scythe.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
But I was a slave, I tended the herd,
I was Olland’s servant,
Liiberland’s shepherd boy.
Ollan´t made a new coat,
Liiberlant a wide cloak
from scraps, from patches,
from the colorful legs of a patchwork dog.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
But I was a slave, I tended the herd,
I was a servant of Olland,
a pauper of Leeverland.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh, we poor night slaves  
Night slaves, crowned with wreaths  
Springtime slaves left at home.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
I was a slave, I tended the herd
I was a servant at Holstre manor.
There were tall rye stalks,
Tall rye stalks, thick boats
I had to comb them with a rake,
Brush them with an iron comb.
I did not want to comb them,
Brush them with an iron comb,
Then I had to be whipped with a whip,
Swept through the rye.
Then I had to cast a spell of enmity,
Weave breeches.
I ran along the village meadow,
Along the plowed fields of ten villages,
The breeches were tucked under my armpits.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh my dear little gentleman  
Little iron nail of gold  
Little reindeer of Sicily  
Sweet as honey, little glutton  
Look at this poor parish  
How this parish is tormented  
The greater ones are killed  
The weak ones on the tip of a needle  
The clever ones on the tip of a rod  
The tiny ones on the tip of a thorn.  
Now it’s no longer a joke  
When it is the painful fate of a slave.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
How many slaves are on the land?  
Six slaves are on the land.  
One is the slave workman  
The second is the slave workhorse  
The third is the regular slave  
The fourth is the young slave maiden  
The fifth is the Russian slave  
The sixth is the manor’s coachman.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
If only I were alive  
If only I were real  
Then I would know what I would do  
I would make the nobles beg  
Make the peasants dance,  
Make the lords sing  
Make the ladies mow the grass  
Make the servants plow the land  
Make the serfs whip the wagon  
Make the old gentlemen guard the gate.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
If I were to exist  
if my doing were otherwise  
I would make gentlemen into oxen  
and ladies into little sticks.  
Kilts beneath wedges  
young men in front as stories.  
I myself went after as a driver.  
Turn the stove, pour into the hollow  
A furrow of a fault, old red.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
When we come from the sea
and we are wet, –
where do we dry ourselves?
We go to the manor houses,
to the threshing floors of the manor,
we lay the drying rack,
we stretch it over the back,
on clean barley straw,
down to the floor of the barn.
Who among us arrives first,
ahead of the others, before the others,
asks the barn keeper,
the dusty barn keeper,
to take us under the eaves,
under the warm barn floor of the room...

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
The devil dug in the pine grove  
The old devil in the willows

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Behold where the hellpit glows,  
The devil's house shines,  
The whore’s tower is blooming green,  
Where the poor are tormented,  
The little ones are tortured,  
The finger gets cursed,  
The whip cracks until dark,  
At dusk the bull’s whip,  
At dawn the bailiff’s little stick.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
If it were up to me  
if it were my doing  
I would turn gentlemen into forks  
coppers into ear plugs  
ladies into skirts  
and chamber boys into poles.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh my dear gentleman doctor  
Lady of the golden crown  
Let us rise onto the chair  
Let us step onto the window frame.  
Let us look at the poor parish  
How this parish is tormented  
The smaller ones are tortured  
The bigger ones are killed  
The horse was golden in front  
Its hooves were in the stable

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
The devil was hammering in the spruce forest,  
The devil was banging in the grove,  
He made a wagon wheel barn,  
With which to take the Saxon to hell,  
The lords also into the fire.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Why the hell are you studying me,  
a snake sprawling wide upon me,  
a long-ass fence enclosing me.  
Study on the new thigh,  
enclose on the long stick;  
There is a tar barrel filled with pitch,  
six barrels of devil's piss,  
there those examiners swim,  
the enclosers wash their heads.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh, we poor night slaves,  
Night slaves, crowned with wreaths,  
Fastened servants,  
We must serve others.  
Serve the German for a hundred years.  
The German's four silk coats  
The poor child has an old quarrel.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
The others went to work on Monday,  
I went on Tuesday to follow.  
I put the plowshare on the plow,  
Suddenly it turned aside.  
The smith came from the manor,  
I to the smith’s plea.  
Dear smith, dear smith,  
measure me a tiny piece,  
a tiny and narrow piece,  
pleasant land from beneath the hill.  
The smith took the dog’s mind,  
measured me a large piece,  
a large piece, a long piece  
from the hilltop mound,  
from the swamp’s hollow.  
I plowed that day,  
that blessed little evening,  
then I let the oxen rest,  
I myself went walking in the wilderness.  
From the wilderness came a spotted dog,  
it tore Kriimu, broke Must,  
from the forest came a wide paw,  
both ate at once crazily.  
I went to the lord to plead,  
then I got a thousand on the back,  
seven hundred on the shoulders.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
If I were in charge  
Secondly, if it were up to me  
I would make the gentlemen oxen  
The ladies wear bonnets  
Put the boys into stories  
And give the girls whips.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
If it were up to me,  
If it were my doing,  
I would surely know what I would do:  
I would make men into guards,  
Ladies into gossiping cranes,  
Misses into full jays,  
Young men into winter guards.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh, we poor theorists,  
Bound servants,  
Imprisoned wage slaves.  
We must enslave others,  
Torment ourselves,  
Wet by day, slaves by night.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh farrier, devil’s skin!
Black boots’ kisser.
Took steak from my ass,
From there got lean meat,
From the groin got lard.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
If it were up to me,  
if it were my doing,  
I would make the nobles beg  
and the peasants dance.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh I am a bright little thorn,
Lady with a golden crown,
Let the children go to lunch!

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh we poor night slaves,
Night slaves, wreath-crowned,
Clenched servants,
Wage workers in chains!
We must serve others,
Wear ourselves out early.
Serve the German for a hundred years -
The German on his silken coat,
The poor child in old clothes,
The little slave in their own clothes.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Our chief little ram,  
A quirky, colorful little bird,  
Lets the children go to their noon meal,  
At the right time to their evening meal.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Shit falls from Jüri’s mouth,  
to the bottom sucking filth,  
from the top the tongue chews wool;  
Gold falls from Liisu’s mouth,  
to the bottom sucking nectar,  
from the top the tongue boils milk.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Where did our goat go?
The old nanny goat went,
her belly ran along the ground,
her back ran along the roof.
There were barrels of tar water,
five barrels of virsa water,
six barrels were the devil's urine.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
The niece created laziness!  
She didn't bother to bring water,  
peed on the stove,  
eyelashes stuck to her chest,  
tears on her head.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
If tomorrow were Saturday,
the coming Friday,
then I would know what to do.
I would put the boots on shaggy,
the gentlemen in front as grooms,
the sheepskin coats behind as cranes,
the kilts inside as wedges,
the ladles behind as handles.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Our bright little ram,  
A brightly colored little bird,  
Lets the children to lunch,  
At the right time to dinner.  
The children are industrious at work,  
Early before the day is light,  
Their heads washed before daylight,  
Their backs washed before dawn.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
If it were up to me,  
if it were my doing,  
I would know what I would do.  
I would make Germans into sacks,  
wolfhounds into oxen,  
hearts into cranes,  
buckles into wedges.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
I was a slave, I tended the herd,  
I was Olland's servant,  
A shepherd boy from Lööveland,  
Olland made a new hoe,  
Lööveland a wide coat.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
(But) the rich man kills the big bull,  
The big bull, the straight bull;  
I am a poor old crow.  
The meat was eaten, the hide was sold,  
The meat went to the birds of the city,  
The hide went to the Narva conscript,  
Some stays in their own houses,  
The dung becomes food for the pigs;  
From the scrap, I get a tuque hat,  
From the beak, I get a nose horn,  
From the shinbone, I get a bed post.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Now it is time to go home,  
It is time to count the household;  
There was time for the father, there was time for the mother-in-law,  
There was time for the family daughter.  
When the time comes to my home,  
And the cat awaits me at home—  
The dog awaits me at home;  
The dog, however, awaits the puppies,  
The cat awaits the crumbs of bread.  
The home is spoken of in ill terms,  
Harsh words are given,  
Bad words are offered.  
They speak against someone,  
Harsh words are given to someone  
Someone else, not me.  
When I go home,  
No one asks for a splinter of firewood,  
Nor gathers kindling in a row,  
The straw stalks do not speak;  
The mother-in-law is angry with me,  
The father-in-law is angry with me,  
Even the loud family elders—  
They do not even offer me food,  
Nor offer me a little bit;  
It is not allowed to enter the room,  
Nor to light a fire under the hearth.  
But I take a handful of twigs from the pile,  
Pull tinder from the room’s ceiling,  
Snatch splinters from the firewood—  
Then I make a fire under the hearth,  
There I warm my soup.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
If it were my being,
if it were my being

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Mother, dear,
Wash my fine shirts,
Whiter than whale's cuffs,
Then I will go to the beautiful hayfield,
To the slender German field.
But mother understood, replied:
Fine shirts will deceive you!
Before you are deceived, fine sand,
The golden plague of the church.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Little piece of sand, sauna woman,  
I would ask for a pot,  
A corner of a nook for broth,  
I have broth for the soup,  
I have broth for the stew,  
To put the pot outside,  
To fill the ladle with ashes,  
To beat myself upon.  
I, a poor poor woman,  
Would ask for a row of fields,  
Where I could sow garlic.  
Father would watch around  
How those gold pieces would grow.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
The village calls me to eat at the village,  
To eat at the village, to drink at the village.  
How many villages would I eat at,  
Or at which village would I drink?  
I eat the bull in the eating hall,  
Drink barrel beer in the drinking hall.  
Oh, when I understand, I will answer soon,  
I will respond to you shortly:  
What is there to eat from that bull,  
The bone was inside, the skin was on top,  
A strip of lean meat;  
Or to drink from that barrel of beer,
