Then the pain began to come.
The mistress, the hellion,
Boils the shoes, dresses the straps,
Feeds the slave with shoes.
So the slave thought: chunks of ossi!
And the family thought: chunks of beatings!
These were the mistress's shoe trials.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Thus sing the boys of Lalli,  
The boys of Uuemõisa Oti:  
"Who is waiting for us at home?  
A cat is waiting for us at home,  
A dog is waiting for us at home.  
The cat wants to cover the bottom of the box,  
The dog, however, is waiting for scraps."

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
For I am truly sorry  
That my bride walks with a wreath,  
That she walks among others,  
A spirit with the poor people.  
And then she goes out by the manor,  
Often even plowing the furrows  
And digging the ditches.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
I have certainly seen days of hunger,  
Some nights I was sleepless,  
Some days without lunch,  
At night I could not sleep,  
Could not lay my head on a pillow.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Our crooked little gold one  
Quirky spotted little bird  
Let the children go to lunch  
Little sisters to the evening  
The children ask for lunch  
The sisters wait for the evening,  
If you don't let them, don't ask,  
May it, may it be damned  
May the coercers die  
May the stick-bearers disappear  
Today one alone, tomorrow two,  
The day after tomorrow five or six  
In a week seven or eight  
Now the devil is placed crooked  
The eyes turn askew.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
When we come back from work
And we are wet
Where do we dry ourselves?
Let's go to Rae's barn
There the spot is long ready
Sheets spread wide in the barn
Pillows beaten soft
There was straw up to the knees
Tangle up to the shin of the boot
Scab to the heel of the shoe
Lice to the ointment on the leg
Scabs walked with stems in their mouths
The louse went to the corner, the young one stayed on the back.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
If it were up to me  
And my doing as well  
I would surely know what to do  
I would put the gentlemen on the oxen  
The ladies behind the plows  
Kilts behind the earlocks  
German children in the stables  
The gentlemen on the sledge runners  
The gentleman ran, his head trembled  
The pants stayed with Saint George  
The buttons to Heikki in the corner

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
It’s raining by the rod’s length  
Fire and tar in the sky’s length  
A slave still must be  
Properly going soon  
Who will save us from shadows  
Heal from daily troubles  
Redeem from the snowfall  
Take us from the rain berries!  
The church in Juani was a little boy  
Peter a tall little tower  
He will save us from shadows  
Heal from daily troubles  
Redeem from the snowfall  
Take us from the rain berries.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Where the devil's house is  
Where the cursed place is  
Hell's windows are burning  
Ghosts and spirits are stirring  
Where the children play  
Where the daughters tylt  
Where the young women cry  
Better to dwell in hell  
Than in Tapa manor  
The Oxen do not eat  
The Runes fade away  
Men dress on their chests  
Girls go to work  
The Oxen groan with horns  
Men suffer in confession  
The Runes circle the chest  
Boys are on knees  
Women do housework  
Girls keep the sacred nests  
Unmarried women guard their feet!  
I praise the Brown Maiden  
Brown Maiden, Brown Lady  
Lowly lands  
Open lands  
The Brown estate goes its way:  
The smith like the moon inside  
The nobleman like God beside  
The estate like a copper plate in between. -  
But the Tapa estate goes its way:  
The smith like the devil inside  
The nobleman like Judas beside  
The estate like a prison cell in between!

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Not all home dogs  
Fathers work outdoors  
Brothers’ collars are iron chains  
What kind of hooliganism is done at the barn  
At the barn poles is shown  
At the manor thoughts are pondered  
Something is searched for  
Something is demanded  
Dogs are at home  
They smell the coming  
The scent of a spark reaches even here  
Swiftness brings it to the shoes.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Already past midnight  
The other half not yet gone  
Already roosters crowed once  
Hens clucked eight times  
Birds sang melodies.  
Now is the German eating time  
The young men’s drinking time  
The men’s sleeping time  
Our poor ones’ walking time.  
Our poor manor spirits  
Late masters’ spirits  
Spirits of the old lord  
Created to wander the night  
In the moonlight to wander  
To cut hay by night light  
To make haystacks in moonlight  
To carry large stacks to the swamp  
To the meadow thin cows  
To the field bright sheep  
To me the joyful little hills.  
Juhan has a strong cow  
Muaria a hefty heifer  
They carry large stacks from the swamp  
From the meadow thin cows  
From the field joyful little hills  
From the village high stacks.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Listen, dear gentleman  
Silver lace young lady  
Golden dolls young gentlemen  
Rise up from your chair  
Step onto the window frame  
Look at the poor parish  
How the parish is tormented  
The little ones are tortured  
The weaker ones are wasted  
Those the size of a finger are being killed.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
A slave was sought for work  
A servant was forced,  
When there was no other mud to carry  
To gather the dung.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Master, little master,  
The little room was the little house.  
Anna the Estonian slave to eat,  
The slave feeds the bull to eat.  
The bull carries the straw to the field,  
The field swells to the edge of the swamp,  
The barn swells to the corner of the yard,  
And the purse swells to a pile of money.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh, oh, Kaie Otsa,  
Otherwise a plump mistress,  
A kind caretaker of children.  
But your manners have long been heard,  
And your ways have been exposed.  
How do you feed your servant?  
You take the milk pail for yourself,  
And give the servant a water dipper.  
You pour from the milk pail,  
The servant pours from the water dipper,  
Dripping into the tar barrel.  
Oh, oh, Kaie Otsa!  
Otherwise a plump mistress,  
A kind caretaker of children.  
But your manners have long been heard,  
And your ways have been exposed.  
How do you pay your servant?  
You knit socks with a large needle.  
Gloves with a fuss,  
Ribbons in bad temper,  
Surely in the end you get blamed,  
In court days contested.  
Then you dance in the street of heaven  
Holding a long whip,  
Wearing broad cloth.  
There you call the servants:  
Come, servants, take your pay!  
The servant hears and replies:  
"If you didn’t pay me a wage,  
There’s no need for pay in heaven.  
If I did your work,  
Did the work, suffered hardships,  
Broken my neck bones,  
Dented my breast bones,  
Ribs were like handcuffs,  
Bladders between thumbs.  
If I asked for shoes,  
Barefoot I asked,  
I bent down to you deep!  
With your big buckets,  
Wide water buckets,  
Long milk pail."

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh, that young gentleman of Ärtu,  
Miss Õbeportu,  
The young Lord of Kuldnukk,  
The German with the silk finger.  
Let us rise from the chair  
Let us rise from the table  
Let us step onto the window sill.  
Let us shout over the poor parish,  
Over the whole parish!  
How the parish is tormented,  
The parish is harassed!

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Tiny little birds,  
Let's go blossom, little flowers.  
At the cattle gathering, the hoofs.  
We are justified in blooming.  
At the cattle gathering, there is shouting!  
At the bloom, the beer is red.  
At the cattle gathering, the kvass is sour.  
Where are we going, the six of us,  
Over the field - five of us,  
Over the meadow, four of us.  
In front is a long boundary forest,  
Behind a wide board forest,  
In between, a maple tree forest,  
The sky is wide and open,  
The night is long and dark. –  
Young girls, young men:  
Let's go over the five fields,  
There sits a beautiful chamberlain,  
A white veiled chamber,  
The wind sweeps the chamber doors.  
There are many German houses,  
Many young gentlemen's houses,  
They wanted to make a bed there,  
To put pillows for sleeping.  
From there I secretly came out,  
A little sneaky – a little sneaking,  
I gave the door an elbow,  
Whistled a tune for the kvass.  
So that the doors wouldn't open,  
The birch twigs shouted,  
I ran home myself.  
Who met me on the way?  
Met were the Germans of Valga,  
Met were the old gentlemen of Valga.  
In front of them were burrows, little tunnels,  
Among them old hares –  
Behind them iron carts.  
In the middle, the handsome foxes.  
I asked for a whip to hit the dog,  
To tear the collar away. –  
They did not give a whip to hit the dog,  
Did not allow to tear the collar.  
Then I took a long rowan twig,  
A little bird cherry stick.  
At the front, I struck the burrows, the tunnels,  
Among them the old hares,  
From behind the iron carts.  
I ran home myself,  
I was not allowed to sleep at home,  
While I was at the feast –  
For two nights I slept on the oat straw.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Today is a day for fun and frolic  
Tomorrow one can sleep  
Tuesday is for going to work  
Saturday evening for coming from the fields  
I myself make fasting days  
I myself trudged through spirit days  
I myself make correction weeks!  
Spirit days are poor indeed  
Angry fasting weeks!  
Spirits torment us  
Fasting is enforced.  
Maidens are tormented  
Proper ones are peeled!  
Our steward is a harsh man,  
The bailiff has cruel hawk eyes  
Angry titmouse eyes.  
The bailiff has a crooked stick  
A coniferous tree – twiggy –  
The staff is made of thorny wood  
The whip’s handle is made of reed stalk  
The whip goes along the maiden’s waist  
Along the woman’s skin –  
Along the ploughmen’s sides.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh, poor soul maid,
Whistled farm girl!
They whistle at me,
Regretting the herding.
The herding boy whistles at me,
The herder is an ill-tempered fellow!
The herding boy whistles, becoming smelly,
The herder calls him a little cat.
Why do they whistle at me,
Why do they often whistle?
Because I hit the herder's eyebrow,
The herding boy's nose.
When they hugged me,
They nuzzled gently.
They called me to the spruce grove,
To the spruce thicket - to the windfall.
But I did not go to the spruce grove,
To the spruce thicket, to the windfall.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh, we beautiful gentlemen  
And our slender gentlemen  
Golden-doll young gentlemen  
Lace-pretty misses.  
Rise up onto the chair  
Step onto the window frame  
Look upon the poor parish  
Upon the entire parish  
How this parish is tormented.  
The parish is harassed  
Oxen still eat  
The weak horses are yoked  
Men dress in the chest.  
Oxen groan with their horns  
Horses paw at the chest.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Don’t rush away to the west,  
I will leave this place standing.  
I won’t give my place to anyone else,  
I won’t rush to another place.  
Let better ones come to the spot,  
More honorable ones take my place.  
More famous ones to the position,  
Those closest to the wall more respected.  
Then I will come back tomorrow  
To see if there are better ones in the place,  
More honorable ones in the position.  
More famous ones at the spot,  
Those nearest to the wall more respected?  
There were no better ones in the place.  
The next was where I left off,  
The chair was where I lifted it,  
The table was where I placed it,  
The spoons were burning on the stove,  
The ladle handles were heating,  
The room to be swept into the corners,  
The stove to be split into logs,  
The ember crying ashes,  
The stone cupboard to be cleaned,  
The water buckets to be carried.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
When I go home  
I step into the house  
I roll onto the wooden floor.  
Neither straws speak to me,  
Nor the beams tell stories –  
Speak back to the speaker.  
I begin to think  
The wheel’s gathering words  
What are you waiting for, servant,  
Or what are you guarding from the enemy children?  
Surely you will rise,  
Surely you will lean on the chair –  
Sit by the stove.  
Stick your butt on the bench.  
I heard and answered back  
Soon I responded:  
You cannot just rise up,  
You cannot just lean on the chair,  
Stick your butt on the bench.  
I have come to be a servant,  
A walkway walker,  
To handle family matters.  
I stir the porridge,  
I fetch the water bucket,  
I leap onto the neck collar.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
The axe did not tolerate a woman for me,  
The lord did not give good care,  
The sister did not help with the glove,  
The brother did not help with the brass,  
I took it in hand and got angry,  
I went to the grove of the leaf,  
There were three good helpers,  
One was the beautiful grey spirit of the sacred grove,  
The second was dear to the wilderness of the forest,  
The third was the field stallion of the grove,  
He even had a saddle on his back.  
I stepped onto the grey spirit of the sacred grove,  
Let the field stallion work,  
With the grey I plow from below,  
With the ears I plow from above during the day,  
Behind the sky is red,  
Then I strike the mark into the turf,  
Into the arrow of the wound,  
Across Riga's rod,  
It cracks, it creaks in the clouds,  
Who wants to chase after,  
I take the mark from the turf,  
From the arrow of the wound,  
From Riga's rod.  
It cracks, it creaks from the clouds,  
Then I drive down the weather.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Who is coughing in the spruce forest there  
Hammering there on the bark  
The devil is coughing in the spruce forest  
The fiend is hammering on the bark.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
I was a servant in Olland  
A shepherd boy in Leeverland  
Olland made a new hat  
Leeverland a wide coat  
Then I went on a marriage journey  
Fog ruined my new hat  
Rain ruined the sled letters  
That was the woman we got  
That was a woman to weave dough  
New Riga’s breastplate.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
I was the only slave in the world  
The stable boy was the second slave  
The orderly was the third slave  
The maiden in the manor was the fourth slave  
The distiller was the fifth slave  
The cooper in the manor was the sixth slave  
The little blacksmith was the seventh slave  
The herdsman was the eighth slave  
The night watchman was the ninth slave  
The plowman was the tenth slave.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Let's start going  
Home, to our waiting place  
To the gate view.  
Who is waiting for us at home?  
The dog is waiting for us at home  
The cat is chasing us behind  
The dog waits for puppies  
The cat for kittens in the box  
Evening comes unexpectedly  
Twilight comes uninvited  
The day goes down without hope  
What else do I worry about  
What harm do I regret  
Worrying breaks the mind  
Regretting breaks the neck  
It ruins the curly hair.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh, poor me, a servant woman  
A little wretched sauna woman  
I go around the mistress  
I go around the housekeeper  
I ask her for a pot  
I grumble for a corner of a cloth  
I have broth pushed away from me  
I have the beans taken away from me  
I have the dregs pushed away from me  
I spoon up ashes  
I beat myself up  
I brush away the little wretched cloth.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Mother Ella, dear granny!  
Heat the village's cold saunas,  
Heat the stove for the kitchen flower,  
Honor the whisk under the birch.  
Take me to the whisking in the sauna,  
And to the washing with a broom.  
Whisking strikes on the head like whip lashes,  
On the neck like cane blows,  
On the forearm like rod blows:  
What evil hump has struck,  
What harsh district chief has laid down,  
What bitter spite has troubled.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
My old Ella grandmother
Heard me coming home.
Väila
Behind the forest to the glade
Immediately she said to the daughter-flower:
Jump Anne, jump Kaie
Then take the gate from the prison
Close the doors with a ring
Home is coming a golden bird
A silk bird is coming inside
Then put the stove to heat
Heat the stove with caraway
Honor the whisk on the branch
Then go brush the branch
Quickly go to the well
The duck goes to wash its knees
The pig goes to wash the piglets
In hand are whip strokes
On the neck are stick blows
Whip harnesses between the belt
That the bad Kubjas struck
The chief of the village struck
The rough one knocked harshly
The rough one has a stone stick
The Junker has five stripes
Kubjas has six twists
Let's help him, the ambulance
It went along the path straight
Along the thin shoulder
Along the small arm.
***
Let it be, let me swear
Bitter death will come to the rough one
Ale death will come to the howler
Bad death will come to the swearer
A tongue was put on the stove
Teeth directly into the oven
Jaws to the edge of the oven.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Vao parish, troubled parish!  
Norra parish, weeping parish;  
Preedi parish, frozen parish.  
Oh, this dear Kapu parish.  
And this good Ärvit parish  
Love Aruküla.  
There on the instrument, the thigh is beaten,  
At the dance, the sole is stamped,  
At the song, the boards are struck,  
In Preedi, the whip is used to beat,  
At the beat, the boards are struck.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Maybe I could come from the year of heaven  
Turn into a rain of rods  
Let hail fall from the iron sky  
Still, one must be a slave  
A servant must really do  
Immediately start properly.

label: songs about social relationships
songs about social relationships
translation:
So be it, so be it, I curse;
What do I wish upon the oppressor -
Shall I give to the letter carrier? -
Wolves upon his herd;
Buzzards upon his chickens,
Bears upon the entire flock! -
Sheep upon the forest herds.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Ellakene, little brother  
Don’t you become a drunkard  
Don’t become a farmhand  
Bitter death is for a drunkard  
Slow death is for a farmhand  
Fine death is for a swearer  
If he would die  
As if a stove was placed on the hearth  
Under the poor hay roof  
Teeth under the tongue.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Mother, dear little woman,  
Heating the stove in the kitchen,  
Grave—  
I take the torch to light the chaff,  
But the birch broom is left to simmer.  
I feel the whip blows on my palm,  
Blue marks on my back. –  
Oh, that poor Esna parish.  
Among other parishes;  
In the middle of the district:  
Whip strokes were heard in Laius,  
Whip lashes in Paide,  
Misery in Alutaguse,  
A girl’s crying over the meadow!  
I cried before, I cried yesterday,  
I cry again, I cry today!  
The eyebrows of Milla have dried up,  
The eyes have hardened and straightened,  
In the harsh village, between  
The graves of Esna parish?!

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
My tender old grandmother  
Heard me coming home,  
Was out searching.  
Behind the grove, singing,  
Immediately she said to her daughters:  
Jump Anne, leap Kaie,  
Take then the gate from the fence,  
Close the door tight—  
Home is coming the golden bird,  
Entering the silk bird.  
Then light the stove,  
Heat the stove with cumin,  
Prepare the birch whisk for the sauna,  
Then the birch whisk will begin to beat,  
Also the bones will begin to bathe,  
The duck will wash its knees,  
The mosquito will rinse its legs.  
In its hand are whip strokes,  
On its neck are club strokes,  
Whip folds under the belt—  
What the evil corporal struck,  
What the troop leader put on,  
The crooked one cursed wildly.  
In the crooked one’s hand is a stone stick,  
In the Junker’s, a five-striped one,  
On the corporal, a six-twisted one,  
On the aide, a toothy one:  
It went along the forehead,  
Along the thin shoulder,  
Along the slender arm.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
German children pages  
Gentlemen children, naughty children,  
Would give a nursing mother to endure  
The careless brats.  
To tend the wet nurse,  
To raise the housemaids.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
German children, squire children  
The lord's children are scoundrels  
The maiden's children are weaklings  
The whore has suckled milk  
The debauched whore has  
The peasant has wise children  
The old woman's milk is suckled  
The old man's cock is raised  
The cow has suckled.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
The hostess deceived me  
She put water into the milk  
Hagan mixed bread in the granary  
The meadow made me plow the field  
But I deceive the hostess  
I leave the stubble to another  
We let the plow share go  
The sled can slide to the clay.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Our steward, dear golden one  
Kilter Ella, dear brother  
Helper, fair one  
Let the children go to lunch  
To the nice midday meal  
To the sisters in the evening  
Our servants without rank  
Ellas without a meal  
The boss goes to lunch  
Turns to the midday meal  
To eat, dear heart  
To drink, dear throat  
I wait for the food to be brought  
To run after the drink  
To carry after the fish  
To send the bread  
I received news from Tuli Tuul  
That the food bringer has died  
The fish carrier is gone  
The bread sender has left  
If the steward is dead  
If the messenger is gone  
The socks stay in the grave  
The shoes went with Kersto  
The skirt stayed on another woman  
The belt stayed on another woman’s waist.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh, this good Aavere parish  
Went to town with a bit of liquor  
The old gentleman with vodka.  
Hunchbacked like the moon in front  
Kilter danced in the middle  
Young man like God behind.  
Oh, this bad Kuie parish  
Went to town with a bit of liquor  
The old gentleman with vodka:  
Hunchbacked like the devil in front  
Kilter [a term for a rogue or trickster] in the middle  
Young man like Judas behind.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Our trooper little gold,
Helper honest one,
Quirky speckled little bird.
You start to guess,
To feel the hours.
That in Harju it has long been noon,
The virus last eaten.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
I was the one who acted, I broke the planks,  
I did not break the ox’s horns,  
The sturdy horses are down. -

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Is the cat waiting for me at home?  
The dog is waiting for me at home.  
Is the cat guarding my house?  
The cat is guarding my house,  
The dog is waiting for crusts,  
The cat for bread crumbs.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
What era in hell it is,  
That era in Liigvala,  
Liigvala the captive land,  
That land the Siberian land,  
With the whip the threshing is done,  
With the bagpipe the wind is played,  
With the whip the grain is carried,  
On the kantik the bars are rung.  
Oh, that good Hallikuda  
Or that famous Kuksimäe,  
Mesista beyond the forest,  
With the fiddle the threshing is done,  
With the bagpipe the wind is played,  
With the violin the grain was carried,  
On the kannel the bars are rung.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh my noble sir  
Lady with a golden crown  
Young gentlemen with silver buttons  
Old gentlemen with brass buttons  
Rise up onto the chair  
Get up into the hall  
Step onto the window frame  
Look upon the poor parish  
How this parish is afflicted  
Some are killed more  
Some are afflicted less  
Some are tormented the least  
Every Friday they are scourged  
Every Saturday they are lashed  
Blood is shed in the procession

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
I never walk on the field  
I never linger in the manor  
Under the spear of the five-tined harrow  
Under the stick of the six-pronged fork  
When it cuts along the side  
Along the side, against the edge  
Across the broad shoulder  
It strikes so that the bone is visible  
Down to the skin’s edge  
For the sake of the blood to the toes. -

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Our strong little gold one  
A colorful little bird  
Let the children have lunch  
At the right time in the evening  
Others eat for the second time  
The householders for the third time  
Us without a meal  
Without cutting the fish  
Our salmon unbroken. -

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Why Väetsa became poor,
Kurjavere disappeared,
Because there was a manor in the village,
A parasite in the parish,
He made the village pay tenfold.
He put a barrel on the girl,
A vat on the old women,
Half a vat on the boy,
The pig had seven piglets,
They were taken to the German as pork,
The sheep brought a lamb,
It was taken to the German's table,
Because Väetsa became poor,
Kurjavere disappeared.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Let the rain roll down from the sky,  
Let the storm come from the heavens:  
Still I must go,  
Still I must not be a slave,  
Still I must not wander in poverty.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh, we poor manor spirits  
The second ones are poor servants  
The third ones are regular workers  
The fourth are assistant spirits  
The fifth are the liquor men.  
They were driven to howl at night  
To march along the roads  
To walk through the wilderness  
The pain of the night, the pain of the moon  
The pain of God's fire  
We struck the pain of the night  
We struck the pile of the moon's pain  
The pain of God's fire.  
Golden rakes in hand  
Sharp sickle shafts.  
When then shall I leave the manor  
Leave the manor, leave for hell  
Shall I leave from your mouth  
Between the jaws of the lion  
Between the pipes of the monkey.  
I cannot turn away  
With a load of dogwood, not turn my head  
Before the home gate  
Before father's granary door  
On brother's chamber threshold.  
Then I look over the edge  
From the worse side.  
See how hell’s place shines  
Evil flames blaze  
The windows of hell are burning.  
The towers of ghosts stand tall.  
Life seems to smile. -  
There are large German estates  
Bottomless lady’s fields  
There we will melt our feathers  
There we will catch our fish  
True fellow servants will wander  
Money pitchers will break  
On that large estate  
On the bottomless field  
On the cornered meadow  
Now I say again  
To sing the Danish song again  
I turn words upside down.  
There the Germans perish on their backs  
May the lady’s neck break  
May the lady’s hip bones crumble  
May the maiden’s ribs be dislocated  
May our backs stay whole  
May our scythes be quick  
May our necks be strong. -

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Perhaps the father is wealthy,
The mother wrapped in silk,
The brother kept as a darling,
The sister with a hundred coins,
But if he were to die,
The land would remain the wealthy father,
The mother wrapped in silk,
The brother kept as a darling,
The sister with a hundred coins.
No riches are laid in money,
No king’s gold is buried.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Where is it as it is for us  
When it is at our manor's estate  
The whip cracks, the fiddle plays. -  
The fiddle is round  
The whip crackles like rowan  
The stick beats like an oak.  
The stick moans like a maple.  
It strikes the girl along the way  
Along the young maiden's skin  
Along the sister's shoulders.  
The whip cracks against the waist  
It snaps against the maiden's skin,  
From the sorrow then comes crying  
From the bitterness then comes screaming,  
Blood flows out  
Then ran home quickly  
Playing to the father's farmhouse  
Give mercy, old lady  
Give mercy, old man.  
You cannot give young daughters  
You cannot give mercy to yourself.  
You must be a serf at the manor  
And pray to the Lord of Heaven.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
The Hellish Mistress  
Boiled shoe lye for me  
Put the stove to burn  
To the chimney to boil  
Under the fire to simmer  
Shields wash their behinds  
Pigs washed the pigsty  
The servant ate a large amount  
The mottled one stays long  
I, poor, around the bean  
The mistress turned her neck  
Tied a string to the dog's neck  
To the other end, to another dog's neck  
Made me hole out in the yard  
To watch the gate.  
A hole dog on two legs,  
Milk the girl with a scabbed paw.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
God be born, great Saxons,  
Let the hungry lords be seen:  
Who were sent to wander at night,  
To walk in the moonlight,  
The nights are long and dark,  
The roads are black and muddy.  
The nights are indeed long, I thresh the threshing floors,  
By day I cut the sheaves.  
At night the body is alive,  
By day, the back is beaten.  
Some complain of the sad day,  
Some lament the evening.  
I lament at home,  
Sensing pain in my bed,  
My father helps me sigh,  
My mother cares with love.  
Where can I complain, where grumble!  
Before me all are noble lords,  
Around me all are hungry scoundrels;  
But I, a poor spirit child,  
A small walking boy.  
I have no court anywhere,  
No righteous judges—  
But I must suffer on my knees,  
Sleep on my calves.  
I would cry big lakes,  
Perhaps deep rivers from my eyes!  
No one hears the lament,  
Nor the cries of distress!  
Grandfather is merciful,  
Taarataat, a wise man:  
Repay the proud lord,  
Repay the cruel bailiff,  
The tormentor, the tormentor.  
Repay before nightfall,  
Before going to the grave.  
In the earth, change is born;  
In the earth, no crushing is seen,  
In the grave no mercy is seen,  
Where could one find true testimony,  
Where could Taarataat be known  
And give justice.  
The lord is skilled in words,  
The bailiff evil in arguing.  
But I, a poor servant child,  
A small lost boy.  
I have no pleasant thought,  
No skillful word.  
For I remain without justice,  
Until then sighing,  
Lamenting with love:  
Until Kalev comes home  
To see his tired brother,  
But Kalev breaks the iron,  
While I break my chest straps,  
My back blue from stripes.  
He wears a shield on his neck,  
Green swords on his hips.  
Why do the tormentors talk nonsense,  
The long tormentors flee.  
"Then life will be ours in the front,  
We will live on Taaramäe  
In service to the steel."

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Master is the little master,
Mistress is the little mistress,
Give the servant good food.
The servant feeds the ox,
The ox takes the straw to the field barn.
The field will become strong to the bottom,
The barn will suffice for a while.
How many barns are under the yard?
There were three barns under the yard!
One waters the wheat,
The second threshes the rye,
The third rakes the barley.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Our little golden chief,  
Lanky, sharp little brother,  
Look out for the day for a moment.  
The day had long since gone down.  
Let us into the evening of Saturday.  
Already the moon is in front of the hut,  
Already the sieve stands on its edge. -

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Now the eating days are over  
Now the drinking days are over  
We ate the bull in the eating place  
We drank the barrel in the drinking place  
What could be drunk from that beer  
The yeast settled down, the foam was on top  
Beer itself for the mid-tongue  
What could be eaten from that bull  
What was left behind  
The tail remained and the horns remain  
The horns remained as new ornaments  
The tail remained for the sheath to burst

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh my dear young gentleman  
Young men with silver buttons  
Young ladies with silver lace  
Stand up on the chair  
Look at the poor parish  
How this parish is troubled  
The parish is being harassed.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
I don’t care even because of this  
That a widow laughed at me  
The girl from Teuta was shaky  
Cursed with foul words  
Keeper of straw benches  
Stacker of straw roofs

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Little Sisters, Little Birds  
Where are we going, the six of us?  
Where will we swim that crowd?  
Where will we place that flock?  
In front is the long peat forest  
Behind is the wide plank forest  
In the middle is the beautiful spruce forest  
Sometimes the old deciduous forest.  

Let’s go over five fields  
Let’s go over four meadows  
There sits a lovely room  
And a white wall watches from the chamber  
And a white wall watches from the chamber  
The wind sweeps through the rooms.  

There were many Saxons there  
They laid down in the beds  
Placed in a pot to sleep  
Still, I managed to come secretly  
I gave the door some oil  
And sent some beer to the forks  
So that the new doors wouldn’t creak.  

The creaking forks shouted  
I set off on the road to walk,  
What met me on the road?  
Old Valga Saxons came against me  
Old gentlemen of Valga came against me  
In front of them were iron fences  
Behind iron shackles  
Among them the old hares  
In the middle the beautiful foxes.  

I took a twig to strike my dog  
To shake the harness straps  
I took a long rowan twig  
And a nice little stick.  

In front of me I struck wild dogs  
Behind iron shackles  
In the middle the beautiful foxes  
Between them the old foxes.  

I myself ran homeward  
I was not allowed to sleep indoors  
That night I was in the barn  
Two nights in the oat field.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
I was a slave, I herded sheep,  
I was a servant in Holland,  
A lamb's shepherd in Leerland.  
Holland made me a new coat,  
Leerland a wide jacket  
Made of flags and patches,  
Colorful goat skins. -  
On Monday I ate herrings,  
On Tuesday I ate smelts,  
On Wednesday good pikes,  
On Thursday large perches,  
On Friday Riga flounders,  
On Saturday broad breams,  
On Sunday pike-perches.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
The man was angry with me,
The woman of the house was loud with me;
They made me plow early in the season,
But early I was made to take the yoke,
The head of the plow, however, was the cooking head.
By dawn I plowed three furrows,
By sunrise a long field,
By noon I spread out a wide field:
I wait for food to be brought
Carried after the plow.
What food have I produced
That is carried after the plow?
Dead nettles, burdock leaves,
Old cursed nettles,
Sprat shins, small seeds,
Moss those more suitable thighs.
Those are the foods I have produced
Carried after the plow.
Then I swore in anger
With a big mouth I scolded...
Plow the head, step into the furrow,
Make the old red furrow straight!

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
I do not serve a rich man  
A rich man and a wise man.  
What will be my wage, the road toll?  
A horse with all its foals.  
I did not take, I did not want to.  
I do not serve a rich man.  
A rich man and a wise man.  
What will be my wage, the road toll?  
A cow with all its calves.  
I did not take, I did not want to.  
I do not serve a rich man.  
A rich man and a wise man.  
What will be my wage, the road toll?  
A pig with seven piglets.  
I did not take, I did not want to.  
I do not serve a rich man,  
A rich man and a wise man.  
What will be my wage, the road toll?  
A hen with eight chicks.  
I did not take, I did not want to.  
I do not serve a rich man,  
A rich man and a wise man.  
What will be my wage, the road toll?  
The village’s fair-haired girl.  
This is what my thighs rejoice in,  
This is what my customs love.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh our honorable sir  
Lady of the golden crown  
Young gentlemen with silver buttons  
Let us rise onto the chair  
Let us step onto the windowsill  
Let us look upon the poor parish  
How this parish is tormented  
The smaller ones are persecuted  
The bigger ones are put to death  
Two are pillars to the manor  
Three are rings on the pillar  
Where women are taken away  
Little boys are sold  
The beauty of the golden ones was chased away.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Is a cat waiting for me at home?  
A dog is waiting for me at home.  
The cat is coaxed inside the house.  
The dog is waiting for crumbs,  
The cat for crumbs of bread.  
It waits for the servant to come home.  
Work is sought for the servant.  
The henhouse is called to work.  
If nothing else, to carry mud.  
To gather manure...  
When the servant is given an end  
To be put on the head of a day laborer.  
To be taken a little during the day,  
To think about a maiden during the day,  
If only the servant is praised.  
A daughter-in-law never.  
The son's wife is always joking.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
If only my existence  
Were someone else’s doing  
I would make gentlemen into oxen  
Ladies into sticks  
Spades into wedges  
Hoods into cranes  
Brooms into shovels.  
Now the gentleman goes ai-ai-aaa  
Behind me there’s trai-rai-raaa

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Here, our masters,  
Lady of the golden crown,  
Young scissors with silver knobs.  
Let us rise onto the chair,  
Step onto the window frame,  
Look upon the poor parish:  
How this parish is tormented,  
The smaller ones are tortured,  
The greater ones are killed.  
There are two pillars in the manor,  
Three are the rings on the pillar:  
Where those women are snatched,  
The boys are pawned,  
The daughters' beauty is taken away. -

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
If it were my being,  
And secondly my doing,  
I would surely know what I would know:  
I would make the oxen into oxen,  
The horses into horses,  
The helpers into fathers,  
The boys into proud cranes,  
The girls into blossoms...  
I myself would be in the field,  
Plowing the furrow in the meadow,  
Letting the songs ring out,  
And the words be lovely to hear.  
Then the village would listen,  
The parish would watch closely,  
The forest would roar back,  
The grove would respond,  
Young women would smile,  
Men would ponder their thoughts,  
Children would quietly spy,  
Squatting by the village gate,  
Near the backyard of the household.  
Oh! If only it were my being,  
And secondly my doing;  
Surely I would know what I would know.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
The Mistress, a bad woman  
Woke me up early,  
To do the household chores.  
I answered, begging:  
- Please, my mistress,  
Delicate mistress!  
Let me laze a little,  
Doze by the door of sleep,  
Stretch my back:  
My sides are burning from plowing,  
My palms ache from the harvest.  
The mistress scorned my plea.  
Kept sending me to the chores.  
When I cunningly understood,  
The lady of the house’s intentions,  
I set a trap under the door latch,  
Laid ribbons on the floor.  
The baking pan got caught in the ribbons.  
The mistress came to beg,  
To soften her mood:  
"Good boy, dear boy,  
Undo the ribbons from my pan,  
I’ll let you lie down till noon,  
I’ll give you beer to drink."  
The fair maiden,  
The household daughter,  
When she went to feel the latch,  
It caught her chin.  
She begged fiercely,  
Trying to coax me:  
"Good boy, dear boy,  
Release my chin from the latch,  
Undo the ribbons:  
I’ll be a better servant below the stove,  
I’ll bring you softer blankets,  
I’ll obey, I’ll hold you in my arms."

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Oh, we poor chimney sweeps  
When we get ourselves wet  
Where do we dry ourselves  
Down there in the barn sauna  
There we dry ourselves  
What then in the oven chamber  
The blacksmith's legs, the miller's thighs  
The farmhand's shoulders both  
The barn priest's thigh bones  
There we then dry them in the oven  
There we dry ourselves indeed

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
Don't kill the gentleman  
Don't kill the lady  
I got a little lamb  
What I fed her was  
Sheep's marrow and rooster gizzard  
Grandma's broth and swan meat  
This is my poor possession

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
I was a slave, I tended the flock  
I was a servant of the Hoolender  
A shepherd boy of Liiderland  
The Hoolender made a new jacket  
A wide coat of Liiderland  
Made from flags and patches  
And from doghide legs

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
If it were tomorrow  
If it were next Friday  
I would know what I would do  
I would put boots on my feet  
Gentlemen in front as horses  
Wedges inside the saddlebags  
The young lady behind as a swan.

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
The hedgehog came from the manor,  
The weevil from the new thigh,  
Gathered sticks in a bunch,  
A baton shaft in the bundle,  
Brought me a measuring tape.  
Measured me a large piece,  
A bog but hollow inside,  
Under the mountain, a clump of moss,  
I plow and worry myself,  
I watch the stake myself,  
Plowing hills into furrows,  
Clumps between the furrows.  
The hedgehog came to plow the furrow,  
Found hills inside the furrow,  
Clumps between the furrows.  
They beat my blue sail,  
My sides scraped and scratched,  
The backside pure filth.  
Wait, wait, little hedgehog!  
Let Saturday evening come,  
The hedgehog will come to the village!  
Saturday evening came,  
And a message followed:  
"Come, come, young men!"  
And the hedgehog came to the village.  
I took rowan branch from the heap,  
Juniper from the cart,  
Bird cherry from behind the house.  
Juniper walked along the road,  
Bird cherry moved past the back.  
Then I escaped from the hedgehog’s grip,  
At last it was over!  
What became of that hedgehog’s body?  
It ended up as the devil’s nutshell!

label: songs about social relationships
translation:
There are those Harju ridges,  
Near the city of the wealthy mother,  
They sit on Irumäe,  
Pipes smoking in their mouths,  
Mosses on the wall inside,  
Waiting for a mare’s urine  
To be thrown into the water.  
Virumaa has five or six,  
Harjumaa has seven or eight ridges.  
Those will be over the sedge,  
I will put a ribbon on one,  
Threw it at a margapuu (a kind of fence),  
Then there will be a Järva boy alone,  
Still a pig boy,  
Alone a Järva herdsman.  
A man from Virumaa was a grain bull,  
A man from Harjumaa was a chaff bull,  
A little bull boy from Järva.

label: nature
translation:
Little rooster, little hen.  
They are rushing off in a race.  
The rooster went under the rich man's leg,  
The hen went to the poor barn.  
The rooster got one barley seed,  
The hen got two oat grains.  
They put the money on the table,  
Rolled it to the miller,  
Paid master miller,  
And to another village man.  
They started making beer.  
Got a horn full of beer,  
A womb full of earwax.

label: nature
translation:
Cuckoo, cuckoo, little cuckoo.  
The cuckoo will not cuckoo to me,  
The cuckoo cuckoos to the herdsman.  
The cuckoo cuckooed in the spruce forest.  
I play in the pine forest,  
I keep daughters in the house,  
And boys under my heart.  
The cuckoo came to ask me:  
Give me my children!  
Tomorrow I will go toward the town,  
From there I will bring you three pairs of shoes:  
One pair will be loose and floppy,  
Another pair will be firm and sturdy,  
The third pair will be stony shoes.  
The loose ones are your snow shoes,  
The sturdy ones are your wedding shoes,  
The stony ones are church shoes.

label: nature
translation:
Surely I know the father-in-law's yard  
Surely I know the mother-in-law's yard  
A miserable cow mooing  
An ugly dog barking  
A pig whining with a fierce eye  
A rooster crowing with a dry tail  
Wait-wait, pig; no-no, pig;  
In summer you were grand  
Surely you will give it back in winter.  
Surely you howl at the door  
Surely you beg behind the sauna:  
Master, little master  
Mistress, little mistress  
Cook me some barley porridge  
Give me some bran porridge  
Then you’ll get meat in the broth  
Wedding meat in halves  
Shoulder meat on a dish  
Then the young men got to eat  
The boys got to marry  
The old people got the shoulders.

label: nature
translation:
What is under our yard?  
The sea is under our yard.  
What is in the middle of the sea?  
A lake is in the middle of the sea.  
What is under the lake's shore?  
A well is under the lake's shore.  
What is under the well's shore?  
A post is under the well's shore.  
What is on the edge of the post?  
A bundle is on the edge of the post.  
What is on the bottom of the bundle?  
A sieve is on the bottom of the bundle.  
What is on the edge of the sieve?  
A cuckoo is on the edge of the sieve.  
What is on the hands of the cuckoo?  
A child is on the hands of the cuckoo.  
What is on the child's chest?  
A brooch is on the child's chest.  
What is in the eye of the brooch?  
A ring is in the eye of the brooch.

label: nature
translation:
Ellakene, little brother!  
I am cutting down dry spruces,  
Dry spruces, wet pines:  
I leave the birches to grow;  
The little branches to moan  
The little leaves to mourn!  
Branches moan for their father  
Flowers mourn for their mother,  
On every top there is a titmouse  
In every treetop a songbird.

label: nature
translation:
Ride, pig, stud, piglet  
Tiny, red piglet  
Do not go to the rye field  
One comes carrying rye on the shoulder  
Another comes carrying a staff on the shoulder  
The third comes, followed by a dog.

label: nature
translation:
What are you neighing, Hiiumaa grey,  
Or what are the Swedes shouting at the ears?

There they grow into fish,
breed into pigs,
decay into bream.
The pigs are big, the sails black,
the holes big, the ponds wide,
the bream have hunched backs.
Tin was for making matches,
iron was hard to shake,
copper was loud to drain.
My soul armor is pierced,
my neck armor bruised,
my blood shedders are ready. -
These upon my tender soul
these upon my golden neck.

label: nature
translation:
The fox had a proud wedding:
The rooster wore golden spurs,
The crow wore copper boots,
The titmouse wore tin shoes.

label: nature
translation:
Sots pig, sow, boar,  
Little red piglet,  
Spotted golden piglet  
Lied to the old sow:  
Off to Tuusti, you must feed,  
Don’t go to the neighbor’s grain field,  
One neighbor is coming with a sheaf on his back,  
Another neighbor with a pole on his back,  
A third one is coming with a dog behind.  
Jaan, come to tend the feet,  
Kusta to tend the throat,  
Mart, come to take down,  
Women to move the blood.

label: nature
translation:
But we are both woodmen,
Above all
We cut down wet pines,
Wet pines, dry spruces,
We carry the beans.
From the rowan tree I get a long pile,
From the bird cherry I get whip twigs,
From the hazel I get a forked sled.
The birches remain growing,
Birch branches do not groan,
Birch leaves do not mourn.
Branches groan for the father,
Leaves mourn for the mother,
Shavings for the sons, daughters.

label: nature
translation:
Wait, wait, pig with silk eyes,  
Young golden yellow moon,  
You have grown in summer,  
Surely you will fight back in winter,  
Surely you howl behind the door,  
Surely you beg behind the stove,  
Surely you stand behind the wall:  
Master, little master,  
Mistress, little mistress,  
Cook me kie  
Honor to me a porridge of chaff,  
Knead the eating time of dung;  
From me comes meat into the broth,  
Wedding meat goes into the sack,  
Shoulder meat onto the plate,  
From there  
Daughters can go marry.

label: nature
translation:
Rooster, hen.  
You go to sift the grain,  
One under the other's granary.  
The rooster found a grain of sand,  
The hen two oats.  
I put a plate on top  
And roll it to the mill,  
Still I make your bread without oil,  
I call together the sad birds,  
I gather the noisy birds,  
I call the lords of Hiiumaa,  
The young Saxons from behind Narva,  
I leave the hawk uninvited –  
The hawk is a cruel predator,  
It tore the fur coat,  
The alder bird’s wide bow,  
The sacred bird’s long pants.

label: nature
translation:
The mouse's daughter married  
Nirgi's young son;  
They had proud bridesmaids;  
The rooster drank from a golden cup,  
The hen from a golden bowl,  
The pig from a silk soy cup,  
The crow from a copper chariot,  
The titmouse from a tin teapot.

label: nature
translation:
Cuckoo, cuckoo, little cuckoo,  
Sing, little eavesbird!  
The cuckoo does not cuckoo for us -  
The cuckoo cuckoos for the herdsman,  
Clucks for the milker,  
Sleeps for the thread-spinner,  
Knocks for the willow basket maker -  
Little cuckoo, little treasure.

label: nature
translation:
The cat rises blue from the bog,  
Blue from the bog, red from the ground,  
Round over the forest,  
Through the forest.  
The moon rises blue from the bog,  
Blue from the bog, red from the ground,  
Round over the forest,  
Through the grove.

label: nature
translation:
Over, over, rain showers!  
Over the shower, I wait.  
I endure the dew shower.  
Take the rain to Vigala land,  
Send the rain to Harju land,  
For the cattle of Vigala to drink,  
For the women of Harju to wash their hands,  
To wash their hands, to wash their scarves.  
In Harju land the men are dark,  
Men are dark, women are dark,  
Girls fiery,  
Boys with curly hair,  
Children like little flames.  
In our land the men are fair,  
Men are fair, women are fair,  
Girls very beautiful,  
Boys with golden hair,  
Children like cowslips.

label: nature
translation:
A hundred rainfalls on the Germans,  
But don’t rain on us.  
We don’t have a home dryer,  
Nor a white shirt bleacher.  
German home dryers,  
White shirt bleachers,  
Fine robe washers.

label: nature
translation:
Cuckoo, cuckoo, little cuckoo,  
Helgi, gentle little bird.  
The cuckoo does not cuckoo to others,  
The cuckoo cuckoos to the herdsman,  
To Helgi, the hayfield worker,  
To the one who takes the cattle,  
To the one who cuts the grass,  
To the one who digs ditches.

label: nature
translation:
The cuckoo calls on the top of the spruce  
Sings on the top of the broadleaf aspen  
I play on the top of the pine  
The titmouse dances on the top of the oak.

label: nature
translation:
Who was beautifully blooming?
The pea was beautifully blooming,
The flower blossomed beautifully.
Who was round alone?
The pea was round alone.
Who was a bit elongated?
The bean was a bit elongated.
Who was lens-shaped?
The lentil was lens-shaped.
Who wore long trousers?
The oat wore long trousers.
Who had reddish hair?
The barley had reddish hair.
Who was naked?
The wheat was naked.
Who wore a silk shirt on their back?
The rye wore a silk shirt on its back.

label: nature
translation:
Rui, rui, rui, rui Ruti's wedding  
The mouse's daughter got married,  
To Nirgi's youngest son.  
The wedding guests were so proud!  
The rooster had golden spurs,  
The crow had copper boots,  
The titmouse had a tin tail,  
The magpies were grey birds,  
The crows were poor birds.

label: nature
translation:
What are you worried about for nothing? -  
Rye heads are already visible,  
Barley ears are turning green,  
Oat ears cover the ground,  
Peas decorate the clothesline,  
Beans bloom proudly on the clothesline,  
Cabbage grows on bright sunny days.  
Turnip spreads its leaves.

label: nature
translation:
Mother Eltse, daughter Kaie,  
Come outside to look!  
The sky is dancing, the earth is rumbling,  
A rainbow strikes the violin,  
The stars play dice,  
The moon is a golden ring.

label: nature
translation:
In the forest, the birch grows well green  
Among the pine twigs.  
From there a rich man gets firewood,  
A bailiff gets a cartload,  
A poor man gets a wagonload.  
I cut down the wet pines,  
I knock on the spruces,  
I leave the birches to grow,  
The aspens to mourn the serf,  
The straight alders to the blue.

label: nature
translation:
Is the cat plowing in Võõbu meadow?  
The pig is plowing, the wind is rushing,  
the crow is ready to sow oil,  
the crane is fiercely harvesting oil,  
the curlew is gathering,  
the wagtail is stacking the hay,  
the nightingale is raking around the rice field;  
the swallow put the dishes on the table,  
the bug is pulling inside,  
the hare is a huntsman;  
the duck is eager, the young drake,  
the fox is eager, the old fox,  
the otter was an experienced helper in the barn,  
the bear was a quick writer!

label: nature
translation:
The cuckoo calls, the spruce bends  
I sing, the treetop moves  
The boys walk in drought  
The girls walk in hand  
The cuckoo, go with a prayer  
Dear daughter, young maiden,  
Farm daughter, little plant  
Give my boys strength  
Bring my daughters home  
Four children to the table  
I will go to the city road tomorrow  
I will bring you three pairs of clogs  
One pair for carrying bones, another for stacking wood,  
The third pair for going to church.

label: nature
translation:
The little red pig  
Said to the big pig  
He lied to the white one  
How there was barley bread  
How there was oats in the bag.  
Let's go rummaging in the garden  
We rummage the spruces sideways  
Then the junipers on the slope.

label: nature
translation:
Why are our boys sad  
Why are the girls of our parish silent  
Mourning linen hair  
Because, because there are dear brothers  
That have caught cold from the frost  
Driven by the hail.  
The field is written with lightning  
Because the bride was not taken  
The dear horse remained unbought.

label: nature
translation:
Let's go to the sheaf, foxes  
In the grain sheaf, squirrels  
The fox is in the sheaf bag  
The magpie was a trading fellow  
The duck was a ware packet  
The lizard pushed us in  
The wolf was the fast runner  
The bear was strong at writing  
Understood the estate's crops  
Sent big crops to the granary.

label: nature
translation:
The river flowed beneath the roots  
Goldfish in the river  
The pike had large spots on the tip  
The bullheads had colorful sides.

label: nature
translation:
The lord praised the sacred grove  
The king, indeed, the golden summer  
I praise the fertile soil  
The rotten thicket becomes moist.  
He plows the pieces, carries the stems  
This leads the girls to become wives  
Carries the girls to be young brides  
The elders indeed become leaders.

label: nature
translation:
If only I existed  
If only I were made  
I would know what I would do  
I would make a wooden horse  
That does not neigh at hayfields  
Nor shout at grainfields  
It neighs at riders on its back  
It shouts at those who lean on its back.

label: nature
translation:
Hüpelik is my horse  
Täpelik was a little mare  
Hüpelik is the gray one of the sacred grove  
My path was time-bound  
Time-bound, full of obstacles  
Rocky, hilly  
Mountainous, tufted with moss.

label: nature
translation:
The landlady beat the cat  
The maid cursed the cat  
What bad thing did the cat do  
The cat was pulled by another cat.  
Between two rooms  
In front of the new barn door.

label: nature
translation:
The wolf was Uila's stable boy  
The bear was Kõrve's herdsman  
The fox was Riia's leg servant.

label: nature
translation:
Neigh, neigh, O sacred grove  
Bellow, bellow, O merchant beetle  
Why do you neigh at the sacred grove  
Or why do you bellow at the market heap  
You neigh at those who sit on your back  
You bellow at those who jump on your back  
You bellow loudly from the granary  
Did you see my foal?  
What color is your horse  
In the morning squirrel-colored  
At sunrise dark-colored  
At midday salmon-colored  
In the evening my own color.

label: nature
translation:
Why are the young men weak  
Silence, the boys of our parish  
Sad, tall hats  
Because, because, little brother  
Because the young men are weak  
Silence, the boys of our parish  
Sad, tall hats  
Because the firewood was taken cold  
Hay was driven away by frost  
The field was written by lightning  
Because the horse remained unbought  
The young woman remained unmarried  
Ribbons remain in the town’s maiden’s hair  
The girl’s gates remain in the shop  
Kalevs remained in the German cupboard  
The brooch remained on the friend's table  
The kettles remained in the stone cellar  
The knife remained on the corner of the shop  
Clog shoes remained on the door.

label: nature
translation:
What is there under our window?  
The sea under our window.  
What is there in the middle of the sea?  
A well in the middle of the sea.  
A post on the edge of the well.  
What is on top of the post?  
A sieve on top of the post.  
What is on the bottom of the sieve?  
A cuckoo on the bottom of the sieve.  
What is on the cuckoo’s hand?  
A child is on the cuckoo’s hand.  
What is on the child's chest?  
A brooch on the child's chest.  
What is in the middle of the brooch?  
A ring in the middle of the brooch.  
Where did this ring come from?  
From the fingers of soldiers,  
From the necks of merchants,  
From the ears of shop boys.  
I am going to cut an oak tree,  
From the crown will come a singing board,  
From the middle will come a spinning stool,  
From the root will come after God.  
What will the shavings be used for?  
They will become the sister’s praise chest.  
It fastens even while leaving,  
Sings children while making too,  
Fastens like a church bell,  
Sings like the only one on the ship.

label: nature
translation:
Cuckoo, cuckoo little cuckoo  
Since we got the beach money  
My throat can't take it  
The Murga children are singing  
Planting apple trees  
Growing a vegetable garden.

label: nature
translation:
Feed the pig, the sow, the piglet  
Dear gray-banded one  
Golden-maned little male pig  
Iron-maned little working pig  
Go to the forest to walk  
Walk the hills, walk the pines  
Walk the spruces on the ridge  
Booted ones on the backside  
Come home for Christmas  
Quickly bring the white meat  
A cubit of lard to the backside.

label: nature
translation:
Sisters bloom on the hill  
Already a leaf waves in the tree  
A leaf in the tree, grass in the ground  
Green hay ripples  
Already a rye head is visible  
Wheat comes from the ear  
Oat spikelet covers the ground  
Barley spikelet turns green  
Beans are flooding with flowers  
Peas nod on the stalk  
Tails turn blue for the pig  
A horse neighs in the grove  
A foal calls to the market  
A deer bends in the heath  
A birch foot swings in the bog  
Let time pass, let the day roll  
The horse from the grove sleeps deeply  
A bear from the market’s foal  
A knife from the heath’s deer  
An axe from the bog’s birch foot.

label: nature
translation:
The cuckoo calls, the spruce bends  
I play, the pine bends  
I have cuckoo chicks in my hand  
Cuckoo daughters on my lap  
The cuckoo comes to my prayer  
Give me my children on my hands  
I am going to town tomorrow  
I will bring three pairs of shoes from town  
One pair will be new ankle boots  
The others afterwards.

label: nature
translation:
Virgins, young girls
What are you thinking about for so long
How long will you make noise
The rye head already appears
The barley ear is greening
The wheat ear is coming out of the sheath
The oat ear covers the ground
The pea is growing pods
The bean blooms proudly
The cabbage grows heads
The lentils are growing pods.

label: nature
translation:
Bring the rain, water the rye
Bring the rain towards Vigala
Drive the speed towards Harju
To water the cattle of Vigala
To wash the hands of the women of Harju
To wash the hands, to wash the kerchiefs
Women of Harju, gray women
Gray women, black men
The girls became angry
The boys, half pagans
In our land, men are stupid
Men are stupid, women are stubborn
The girls became beautiful,
The boys are half Germans.

label: nature
translation:
The mouse faced the bottom of the wall  
Started threatening the cat  
Wait-wait, cat, well-well cat  
Where is my little spruce boy  
My five little nephews  
The cat heard, an answer sounded  
From the black cat’s hole in the mouth  
From the gray cat’s hole in the mouth  
Between the speckled bells.

label: nature
translation:
Owl owl little boy  
Who was running along the sand  
The hare was running along the sand  
Owl owl little boy  
Who was sneaking through the swamp  
The wolf was sneaking through the swamp  
Owl owl little boy  
Who was stumbling along the road  
The horse was stumbling along the road  
Owl owl little boy  
Who flew into the alder grove  
The foal flew into the alder grove.

label: nature
translation:
Do you remember last year  
Where last year we ate food  
Ate food, drank water  
With a knife, a silver plate  
With a gold fork  
In the town I forget the knife  
I use the gold fork  
There grew a sleepy forest  
A golden fly in the sleepy forest  
You have a brother, I have another  
I put my brother to cut wood  
You put your brother to plow  
He cuts  
He plows the middle fields  
We fed pieces to the pigs  
Then we tenderly come together  
Tenderly to sleep together  
To weave golden belts together.

label: nature
translation:
I will make a honey drink  
I will make a spirit jar  
Then I will put it in the garden shed  
The crooked one thought the moon was shining  
The old man blushed during the day  
My ladles were glowing  
My honey boards were shining  
Then I go to Miku's room  
What will be done in that room  
Bear baked fish  
The little mill broke wood  
The miller moaned in his head.

label: nature
translation:
Our little workboys,  
If these are little oak stumps.  
Wall beaters, tree cutters,  
Shakers of the whole forest,  
We cut down wet pines,  
Wet pines, dry spruces;  
We leave the birches growing,  
Birch branches groaning  
Branches groan like a father  
Leaves mourn like a mother.  
Break the branches, maiden,  
Break the branches, plague two,  
Then leave the tops for the birds to fly,  
For the birds to fly, for the pigeons to come,  
For the swallow to fly over,  
For the capercaillie to make its nest early.

label: nature
translation:
The horse runs because of the reins,
Because of the thin whip,
Because of the broad lash.
Let me say it again,
Let me sing it back again:
The horse does not run because of the reins,
Nor because of the thin whip,
Nor because of the broad lash—
The horse runs because of the hay,
It leaps because of the barley,
Because of the young man's spirit.

label: nature
translation:
I am a sailor's son,  
A dear man, a fisherman's son,  
I look for dill under the cabbage,  
Under the shirt of the seasoned ones.  
I put the bigger one in my mouth,  
And throw the smaller one into the water.

label: nature
translation:
Row the swing, pull the swing,  
Row across three forests;  
There were three forests side by side:  
One was the golden spruce forest,  
The second the precious birch forest,  
The third the forest with apple trees.  
The one that was the golden spruce forest  
Was the forest of young men.  
The one that was the precious birch forest  
Was the forest of young women.  
The one that was the forest with apple trees  
Was the forest of young girls.

label: nature
translation:
Row the swing, row the swing,
Row beyond the three fields;
There were three fields in a row:
One was the rye field with ergot,
The second was the dear oat field,
The third was the beautiful wheat.
The one with the rye field with ergot
Was the field of young women.
The one with the dear oat field
Was the field of young men.
The one with the beautiful wheat
Was the field of young girls.

label: nature
translation:
Understand, understand, my little sisters,  
What can be seen from the hill?  
An apple tree can be seen from the hill.  
How many branches does the apple tree have?  
The apple tree had three branches.  
How many blossoms does the top branch have?  
The top branch had three blossoms.  
How many apples does the blossom have?  
The blossom had three apples.  
One was the apple of young men,  
The second the apple of young women,  
The third my own apple.  
With this I deceive the hidden ones,  
I pick the young men,  
I try to follow customs  
Whether there is a hint of whisky,  
Or a slender plate of bread,  
A cunning beer jug.

label: nature
translation:
Swing smiths, brothers alive,  
Where have they made the swing?  
They made the swing below the village,  
By the guests’ resting places,  
By the village boys’ stick places.  
Where was this swing brought from?  
Swing brought from Kei  
Kei village, Pei homestead.  
Posts brought from Ammutasta  
Beams from Sinisalusta  
Axles brought from Võhmutalta.  
Swing smiths, brothers alive,  
Little sisters, little ladies.  
Pearl earrings glistening.  
Let’s go to swing,  
The boy comes to row the swing,  
To sing the swing song,  
Rows from the high place, reaches the swift,  
So that I would be noticed for a long time  
Be talked about a lot, be remembered long,  
So that I would be noticed across the forest:  
Across three spruce forests.  
Three forests were side by side:  
One was an apple tree forest  
It belonged to the young youths,  
The second a dear birch forest  
It belonged to the young maiden,  
The third a precious spruce forest  
It belonged to the young men.

label: nature
translation:
The crow is a gentle little bird  
Under our soil,  
Under the wall of Aganik.

label: nature
translation:
What is there under our yard?  
What is there under the seashore?  
A column under the seashore!  
What is on the end of the column?  
A brooch was on the end of the column!  
What is on the edge of the brooch?  
A ring on the edge of the brooch!  
Where did this ring come from?  
The ring came from the war,  
From the finger of a soldier.

label: nature
translation:
Jüri told me  
That he had been in the moose field,  
And the bear was at the haystack.  
I took the rifle from the attic,  
The horn from under the eaves,  
I went to watch for the moose.  
The moose went into the forest here and there,  
The bear followed in pairs.

label: nature
translation:
The sky danced, the earth thudded,  
Clouds whistled and blew.

label: nature
translation:
Sisters, darlings,  
Young maidens,  
Where last year we sowed flax,  
Sowed flax, drank honey,  
There grew a buttery forest,  
A buttery forest, golden spruce,  
Silver birches.  
Listen, brothers, listen, kinsmen,  
In healthy bodies, a sharp blade,  
Make a strike sharp as fire,  
Cut down the buttery forest,  
The buttery forest, golden spruce,  
Silver birches.  
Then make buttery plows,  
Buttery plows, golden oats,  
Silver rye ears.

label: nature
translation:
The fox was a thigh-stabber  
The wren was a wind-chaser  
The sun was a sweeper  
The ghost was a sack-stuffer.

label: nature
translation:
The flax wears a silk shirt  
Oats wear long pants  
Barley has a prickly crown on its head  
Rye has rust-colored hair  
Pea is busy sowing  
Lentils tie around the leg  
Cabbage swirls on top of the hill  
Let's go to steal the flax  
To pull gold from the sack  
We steal linseed in clusters  
Burdens in six embraces  
We take it home to the grandmother  
The woman makes the box sink  
To grow under the lid  
It grew for one month, it grew for two  
Three quarters of a month  
A quarter of five months.

label: nature
translation:
The cold chills me  
I am cold in my hand  
My toe hurts  
Wait-wait, cold, no-no, cold  
Let my room be made  
But the home is still being knocked on  
And the house is still being painted  
Then I sit in the sauna  
You howl outside the door  
You shout between the rooms.

label: nature
translation:
Row the swing, swing the rowboat  
Row over three forests  
One was a fir forest  
It was the forest of young men  
The second was a birch forest  
It was the forest of young women  
The third was an apple forest  
It was the forest of young maidens.

label: nature
translation:
What are you mooing, old cow  
You are mooing, you are a pregnant cow  
You are talking, old red one  
You are mooing like crazy bullocks  
From the blue pea manure  
From the red pullet's dung heap.

label: nature
translation:
Crow, quiet little bird  
Laid eggs in the hollow below  
Called the maiden to pick them  
The maiden picked a full sip  
Piret a full long apron  
Maret a full Mardi's shirt  
Villager a full hat.

label: nature
translation:
Cuckoo, cuckoo, little cuckoo  
Helgi's hay bird  
My cuckoo does not cuckoo  
The cuckoo cuckoos to the shepherd boy  
To Helgi, the hay cutter  
To the willow branch cracker  
To the one who takes the meadow  
Why do you chirp, little bug  
Filthy fly, so dirty  
You are servant of the bug  
Son of the filthy fly  
From your mouth drips urine  
Below is the row of teeth  
Above is the long tongue  
Let me sing the flax song  
From my mouth drips gold  
Below is silver of teeth  
Above is the fine skin of the tongue  
Where did this singer come from  
Came from here, got from here  
Came from the pigsty  
From the pig’s barn with straw  
Where did the child get these songs,  
I took the stories from the suckerfish’s mouth  
From between the teeth of the pike.  
Tunes from a crooked tail  
A girl went to some wedding  
Rode to the seventh (village)  
Carried me under the belt  
Kept the apron strings  
He drank from the cupboard, drank from the pitcher  
From the bottom of the flute  
From the pipe-maker’s cup  
He drank himself, gave me some  
Because I became a singer  
Stories from the girl closing the door  
Words tangled in knots  
I was told to close the reading  
The singer was my father  
The singer was my mother  
Both singer sisters.

label: nature
translation:
What is beneath our yard  
The sea is beneath our yard  
What is in the middle of the sea  
There was a well in the middle of the sea  
What is in the middle of the well  
A pillar in the middle of the well  
What swayed on the top of the pillar  
A cuckoo swayed on the top of the pillar.

label: nature
translation:
The crow, a meek little bird  
Laid an egg under our yard  
I pick a full sip  
The village boy a full hat  
The village wife a small full.

label: nature
translation:
Row the swing, row the swing  
Row the swing to that land  
Where the log forest shines  
Where the alder shrubby forest rises  
Where the pine board forest grows  
There are many fish in the river  
Big graylings, black-backed  
Wide salmon, with broken tails.

label: nature
translation:
The heads were bulls, big bulls  
They go with sledges to the village  
The sledge carries bundles of firewood  
The heads were bulls, big bulls,  
Even more bulls pulled  
A hundred fathoms of fir wood  
A thousand fathoms of pine wood.  
Even more bulls pulled.

label: nature
translation:
Our little woodcutters  
These little oak stumps  
Haymakers, wood carriers  
The greatest forest swingers  
We cut down the wet pines  
Wet pines, sad spruces

Calling out beyond the three forests
One was in the spruce forest
The second was in the pine forest
The third was in the birch forest
There grow the crooked birches
From there I cut wheel wood
For father, ox yoke wood
For brother, strong horse wood
For sister, club wood
Why aren’t you sisters calling out here?
Often I do not slip up either
Sing so that the ceiling rattles
The ceiling rattles, the rafters clap
I toss the verses, or is it pity
For the black spruce in the hot stove.
Sisters, you hear
And brothers, pay attention
What a dreadful story in hell
How the rich burn inside hell
The poor watch from the shadows
As the rich ride recklessly
And the wealthy recklessly
The poor watch from the shadows.

And you fish of the kabala

Noon shots into the waves  
In the evening you boil in the kettle  
But you fry, sir, on the pan  
And old sir in the bath.

translation:
Little Goat Maiden  
The kid was a little plant

Branch hay from the aspen grove  
Golden daisies from the spruce forest  
But the wolf waited in the valley  
Come here, little goat  
I will bring you a red apron  
I will bring you a dear necklace  
I will bring new clog shoes  
The fox shouted from the brushwood  
Little Goat Maiden  
Don't be silly to believe  
The lip is ready to lie  
Blood is the red apron  
Lungs and liver are the neck ornament  
The skin is your dear necklace  
New clogs for hooves  
Intestines like silk ribbons.

translation:
The crow flew into the maple,  
Its tail touched the rowan,  
I asked my apple to die  
On the linen field,  
On the oat field.

translation:
The Master was at the wedding  
At the wedding and the wedding,  
The Mistress was on guard,  
On guard and on guard;  
A pig is wallowing in the garden  
In the garden and in the garden,  
Three forks on its back,  
On its back and on its back,  
The hen is screeching in the wall,  
In the wall and in the wall,  
The yoke is staring at the raven,  
At the raven and at the raven,  
The mare is neighing in the stable  
In the stable and in the stable,  
Wants to go riding  
Go and go;  
Why did you neigh so early,  
Or why are you shouting into the wolf’s ear?  
Did you neigh like a lone one,  
Or are you shouting like a curved one?  
I did not neigh like a lone one,  
Nor do I shout like a curved one,  
I neigh from a dying age,  
I shout from a dying sorrow.

translation:

The mare was a wise little plant

The wolf called out from the meadow:  
"Come here, little goat!  
Little scratched goat  
I will bring new shoes  
I will put on red ribbons  
Inside I will tie silk straps  
Underneath there are beautiful hooves."  
The bird sang in the alder grove:  
"Little goat, little scratched one!  
Do not be foolish to believe  
Do not be weak to take advice  
The new shoes are made of skin  
Inside are silk straps  
Blood on the red ribbons  
Hooves are beautiful."

translation:

The people are rusted iron.

The sky is soot-haired  
The people are rusted iron  
The godchildren's quarrels are large:  
The fathers' oaths are broad,  
The listeners' minds are sad,  
The viewers' minds are painful.

translation:
I am a man, the son of a sailor,  
A handsome man, the son of a fisherman,  
I sit by the sea shore,  
Picking full from the eelgrass.  
The bigger ones I put in my mouth,  
The smaller ones I throw away.  
From there come the big plants,  
Big plants, dark backs,  
Leaves wide at the blade ends.  
They stood at the edges into the sea,  
Rustling in the waves.

translation:

Flax wears a silk shirt.

Spruce has a golden hat.

Birch has a fur coat.

Rowan’s head is red.

Alder wears a mourning dress.

Broom was the shepherd of the wilderness.

The wolf was the lamb of the forest.

The hare is the desert ruler.

The capercaillie is the black rooster of the forest.

The cuckoo is the king of the spruce grove.

translation:

Sing it back once more,  
Soon in the old order again.  
Ernes was round alone,  
Uba was slightly lanky,  
Leats was broad and lumpy,  
Tatar was triangular,  
Nisu wore a silk shirt on their back,  
Kaer had long pants on their legs,  
Oder had a Moorish hat on their head,  
Rukkil had curly hair.

translation:
Understand, understand, young men,  
Know, know, wise women,  
Guess, eager boys,  
Why don’t I understand the youth?  
What walks along the fence?  
Steps along the edge of time,  
A little bee, a little bird.  
Understand, understand, young men,  
Know, know, wise women,  
What draws water from the river?  
Touches the village wells,  
Why don’t I understand the youth:  
A rainbow draws from the river.  
Touches the village wells,  
Understand, understand, young men,  
Know, know, wise women,  
Guess, eager boys.  
What comes mooing from the meadow?  
Stepping through the blue grass,  
Rain comes mooing from the meadow,  
Stepping through the blue grass,  
Rustling from the grove.
